live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|59:8: And the root of wisdom, and the riches of understanding, and the fount of knowledge: And the height of the air, and the greatness of Paradise, and the consummation of the ages, and the beginning of the day of judgement:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|59:9: And the number of the offerings, and the earths which have not yet come:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|59:11: And the likeness of future torment, and the multitude of innumerable angels, and the flaming hosts, and the splendour of the lightnings, and the voice of the thunders, and the orders of the chiefs of the angels, and the treasuries of light, and the changes of the times, and the investigations of the law.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|59:12: These are the bright fourth waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|60:1: 'And the black fifth waters which thou hast seen raining are the works which the Amorites wrought, and the spells of their incantations which they wrought, and the wickedness of their mysteries, and the mingling of their pollution.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|60:2: But even Yashar'el (Israel) was then polluted by sins in the days of the judges, though they saw many signs which were from Him who made them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:1: 'And the bright sixth waters which thou didst see, this is the time in which David and Solomon were born.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:2: And there was at that time the building of Zion, And the dedication of the sanctuary, And the shedding of much blood of the nations that sinned then, And many offerings which were offered then in the dedication of the sanctuary.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:3: And peace and tranquillity existed at that time,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:4: And wisdom was heard in the assembly: And the riches of understanding were magnified in the congregations,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:5: And the holy festivals were fulfilled in blessedness and in much joy.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:6: And the judgement of the rulers was then seen to be without guile, And the righteousness of the precepts of the Mighty One was accomplished with truth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:7: And the land [which] was then beloved by Yahuah (Lord), And because its inhabitants sinned not, it was glorified beyond all lands, And the city Zion ruled then over all lands and regions.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|61:8: These are the bright waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:1: 'And the black seventh waters which thou hast seen, this is the perversion (brought about) by the counsel of Jeroboam, who took counsel to make two calves of gold:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:2: And all the iniquities which kings who were after him iniquitously wrought.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:3: And the curse of Jezebel and the worship of idols which Yashar'el (Israel) practised at that time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:4: And the withholding of rain, and the famines which occurred until women eat the fruit of their wombs.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:5: And the time of their captivity which came upon the nine tribes and a half, because they were in many sins.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:6: And Salmanasar king of Assyria came and led them away captive.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:7: But regarding the Gentiles it were tedious to tell how they always wrought impiety and wickedness, and never wrought righteousness.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|62:8: These are the black seventh waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:4: "Behold, for lo! Sennacherib is prepared to destroy us, and he will be boastful and uplifted when he has destroyed Zion."
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:5: And the Mighty One heard him, for Hezekiah was wise, And He had respect unto his prayer, because he was righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:1: 'And the bright eighth waters which thou hast seen, this is the rectitude and uprightness of Hezekiah king of Yahudah (Judah) and the grace (of God) which came upon him.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:2: For when Sennacherib was stirred up in order that he might perish, and his wrath troubled him in order that he might thereby perish, for the multitude also of the nations which were with him.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:3: When, moreover, Hezekiah the king heard those things which the king of Assyria was devising, (i.e.) to come and seize him and destroy his people, the two and a half tribes which remained: nay, more he wished to overthrow Zion also: then Hezekiah trusted in his works, and had hope in his righteousness, and spake with the Mighty One and said:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:6: And thereupon the Mighty One commanded Ramiel His angel who speaks with thee.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:7: And I went forth and destroyed their multitude, the number of whose chiefs only was a hundred and eighty-five thousand, and each one of them had an equal number (at his command).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:8: And at that time I burned their bodies within, but their raiment and arms I preserved outwardly, in order that the still more wonderful deeds of the Mighty One might appear, and that thereby His name might be spoken of throughout the whole earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:9: And Zion was saved and Jerusalem delivered: Yashar'el (Israel) also was freed from tribulation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:10: And all those who were in the holy land rejoiced, and the name of the Mighty One was glorified so that it was spoken of.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|63:11: These are the bright waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:1: 'And the black ninth waters which thou hast seen, this is all the wickedness which was in the days of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:2: For he wrought much impiety, and he slew the righteous, and he wrested judgement, and he shed the blood of the innocent, and wedded women he violently polluted, and he overturned the altars, and destroyed their offerings, and drove forth their priests lest they should minister in the sanctuary.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:3: And he made an image with five faces: four of them looked to the four winds, and the fifth on the summit of the image as an adversary of the zeal of the Mighty One.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:4: And then wrath went forth from the presence of the Mighty One to the intent that Zion should be rooted out, as also it befell in your days.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:5: But also against the two tribes and a half went forth a decree that they should also be led away captive, as thou hast now seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:6: And to such a degree did the impiety of Manasseh increase, that it removed the praise of the El Elyon (Most High) from the sanctuary.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:7: On this account Manasseh was at that time named "the impious", and finally his abode was in the fire.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:8: For though his prayer was heard with the El Elyon (Most High), finally, when he was cast into the brazen horse and the brazen horse was melted, it served as a sign unto him for the hour.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:9: For he had not lived perfectly, for he was not worthy—but that thenceforward he might know by whom finally he should be tormented.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|64:10: For he who is able to benefit is also able to torment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|65:1: 'Thus, moreover, did Manasseh act impiously, and thought that in his time the Mighty One would not inquire into these things.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|65:2: These are the black ninth waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:1: 'And the bright tenth waters which thou hast seen: this is the purity of the generations of Josiah king of Yahudah (Judah), who was the only one at the time who submitted himself to the Mighty One with all his heart and with all his soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:2: And he cleansed the land from idols, and hallowed all the vessels which had been polluted, and restored the offerings to the altar, and raised the horn of the holy, and exalted the righteous, and honoured all that were wise in understanding, and brought back the priests to their ministry, and destroyed and removed the magicians and enchanters and necromancers from the land.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:3: And not only did he slay the impious that were living, but they also took from the sepulchres the bones of the dead and burned them with fire.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:4: [And the festivals and the sabbaths he established in their sanctity], and their polluted ones he burnt in the fire, and the lying prophets which deceived the people, these also he burnt in the fire, and the people who listened to them when they were living, he cast them into the brook Cedron, and heaped stones upon them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:5: And he was zealous with zeal for the Mighty One with all his soul, and he alone was firm in the law at that time, so that he left none that was uncircumcised, or that wrought impiety in all the land, all the days of his life.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:6: Therefore he shall receive an eternal reward, and he shall be glorified with the Mighty One beyond many at a later time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:7: For on his account and on account of those who are like him were the honourable glories, of which thou wast told before, created and prepared.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|66:8: These are the bright waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:1: 'And the black eleventh waters which thou hast seen: this is the calamity which is now befalling Zion.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:2: Dost thou think that there is no anguish to the angels in the presence of the Mighty One, That Zion was so delivered up, And that lo! the Gentiles boast in their hearts, And assemble before their idols and say, "She is trodden down who ofttimes trod down, And she has been reduced to servitude who reduced (others)"?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:3: Dost thou think that in these things the El Elyon (Most High) rejoices, Or that His name is glorified?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:4: [But how will it serve towards His righteous judgement?]
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:5: Yet after these things shall the dispersed among the Gentiles be taken hold of by tribulation, And in shame shall they dwell in every place.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:6: Because so far as Zion is delivered up And Jerusalem laid waste, Shall idols prosper in the cities of the Gentiles, And the vapour of the smoke of the incense of the righteousness which is by the law is extinguished in Zion, And in the region of Zion in every place lo! there is the smoke of impiety.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:7: But the king of Babylon will arise who has now destroyed Zion, And he will boast over the people, And he will speak great things in his heart in the presence of the El Elyon (Most High).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|67:8: But he also shall fall at last. These are the black waters.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:1: 'And the bright twelfth waters which thou hast seen: this is the word.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:2: For after these things a time will come when thy people shall fall into distress, so that they shall all run the risk of perishing together.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:3: Nevertheless, they will be saved, and their enemies will fall in their presence.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:4: And they will have in (due) time much joy.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:5: And at that time after a little interval Zion will again be builded, and its offerings will again be restored, and the priests will return to their ministry, and also the Gentiles will come to glorify it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:6: Nevertheless, not fully as in the beginning.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:7: But it will come to pass after these things that there will be the fall of many nations.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|68:8: These are the bright waters which thou hast seen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|69:5: On his account there were not black waters with black, nor bright with bright; for it is the consummation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|69:4: And of the good works of the righteous which should be accomplished before Him, He foresaw six kinds of them, beyond those which He should work at the consummation of the age.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|69:1: 'For the last waters which thou hast seen which were darker than all that were before them, those which were after the twelfth number, which were collected together, belong to the whole world.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|69:2: For the El Elyon (Most High) made division from the beginning, because He alone knows what will befall.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|69:3: For as to the enormities and the impieties which should be wrought before Him, He foresaw six kinds of them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:1: 'Hear therefore the interpretation of the last black waters which are to come [after the black]: this is the word.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:2: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:3: And they shall hate one another, And provoke one another to fight, And the mean shall rule over the honourable, And those of low degree shall be extolled above the famous.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:4: And the many shall be delivered into the hands of the few, And those who were nothing shall rule over the strong, And the poor shall have abundance beyond the rich, And the impious shall exalt themselves above the heroic.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:5: And the wise shall be silent, And the foolish shall speak, Neither shall the thought of men be then confirmed, Nor the counsel of the mighty, Nor shall the hope of those who hope be confirmed.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:6: And when those things which were predicted have come to pass, Then shall confusion fall upon all men, And some of them shall fall in battle, And some of them shall perish in anguish,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:7: And some of them shall be destroyed by their own. Then the El Elyon (Most High) will reveal those peoples whom He has prepared before, And they shall come and make war with the leaders that shall then be left.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:8: And it shall come to pass that whosoever gets safe out of the war shall die in the earthquake, And whosoever gets safe out of the earthquake shall be burned by the fire, And whosoever gets safe out of the fire shall be destroyed by famine.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:9: [And it shall come to pass that whosoever of the victors and the vanquished gets safe out of and escapes all these things aforesaid will be delivered into the hands of My servant Messiah.]
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|70:10: For all the earth shall devour its inhabitants.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|71:1: 'And the holy land shall have mercy on its own, And it shall protect its inhabiters at that time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|71:2: This is the vision which thou hast seen, and this is the interpretation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|71:3: For I have come to tell thee these things, because thy prayer has been heard with the El Elyon (Most High).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:1: 'Hear now also regarding the bright lightning which is to come at the consummation after these black (waters): this is the word.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:2: After the signs have come, of which thou wast told before, when the nations become turbulent, and the time of My Messiah is come, he shall both summon all the nations, and some of them he shall spare, and some of them he shall slay.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:3: These things therefore shall come upon the nations which are to be spared by Him.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:4: Every nation, which knows not Yashar'el (Israel) and has not trodden down the seed of Jacob, shall indeed be spared.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:5: And this because some out of every nation shall be subjected to thy people.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|72:6: But all those who have ruled over you, or have known you, shall be given up to the sword.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:1: 'And it shall come to pass, when He has brought low everything that is in the world, And has sat down in peace for the age on the throne of His kingdom, That joy shall then be revealed, And rest shall appear.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:2: And then healing shall descend in dew, And disease shall withdraw, And anxiety and anguish and lamentation pass from amongst men, And gladness proceed through the whole earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:3: And no one shall again die untimely, Nor shall any adversity suddenly befall.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:4: And judgements, and revilings, and contentions, and revenges, And blood, and passions, and envy, and hatred, And whatsoever things are like these shall go into condemnation when they are removed.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:5: For it is these very things which have filled this world with evils, And on account of these the life of man has been greatly troubled.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:6: And wild beasts shall come from the forest and minister unto men, And asps and dragons shall come forth from their holes to submit themselves to a little child.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|73:7: And women shall no longer then have pain when they bear, Nor shall they suffer torment when they yield the fruit of the womb.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|74:1: 'And it shall come to pass in those days that the reapers shall not grow weary, Nor those that build be toilworn; For the works shall of themselves speedily advance Together with those who do them in much tranquillity.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|74:2: For that time is the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|74:3: Therefore those things which were predicted shall belong to it: Therefore it is far away from evils, and near to those things which die not.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|74:4: This is the bright lightning which came after the last dark waters.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:1: And I answered and said: 'Who can understand, O Yahuah (Lord), Thy goodness? For it is incomprehensible.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:2: Or who can search into thy compassions, Which are infinite?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:3: Or who can comprehend Thy intelligence?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:4: Or who is able to recount the thoughts of Thy mind?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:5: Or who of those who are born can hope to come to those things, Unless he is one to whom Thou art merciful and gracious?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:6: Because, if assuredly Thou didst not have compassion on man, Those who are under Thy right hand, They could not come to those things, But those who are in the numbers named can be called.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:7: But if, indeed, we who exist know wherefore we have come, And submit ourselves to Him who brought us out of Egypt, We shall come again and remember those things which have passed, And shall rejoice regarding that which has been.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|75:8: But if now we know not wherefore we have come, And recognize not the principate of Him who brought us up out of Egypt, We shall come again and seek after those things which have been now, And be grieved with pain because of those things which have befallen.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|76:1: And He answered and said unto me: ['Inasmuch as the revelation of this vision has been interpreted to thee as thou besoughtest], hear the word of the El Elyon (Most High) that thou mayst know what is to befall thee after these things.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|76:2: For thou shalt surely depart from this earth, nevertheless not unto death, but thou shalt be preserved unto the consummation of the times.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|76:3: Go up therefore to the top of that mountain, and there shall pass before thee all the regions of that land, and the figure of the inhabited world, and the top(s) of the mountains, and the depth(s) of the valleys, and the depths of the seas, and the number of the rivers, that thou mayst see what thou art leaving, and whither thou art going.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|76:4: Now this shall befall after forty days. Go now therefore during these days and instruct the people so far as thou art able, that they may learn so as not to die at the last time, but may learn in order that they may live at the last times.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:3: For to you and to your fathers Yahuah (Lord) gave a law more excellent than to all peoples.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:1: And I, Baruch, went thence and came to the people, and assembled them together from the greatest to the least, and said unto them:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:2: 'Hear, ye children of Yashar'el (Israel), behold how many ye are who remain of the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:4: And because your brethren transgressed the commandments of the El Elyon (Most High), He brought vengeance upon you and upon them, And He spared not the former, And the latter also He gave into captivity: And He left not a residue of them, But behold! ye are here with me.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:6: If, therefore, ye direct your ways aright, Ye also shall not depart as your brethren departed, But they shall come to you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:7: For He is merciful whom ye worship, And He is gracious in whom ye hope, And He is true, so that He shall do good and not evil.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:8: Have ye not seen here what has befallen Zion?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:9: Or do ye perchance think that the place had sinned, And that on this account it was overthrown? Or that the land had wrought foolishness, And that therefore it was delivered up?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:10: And know ye not that on account of you who did sin, That which sinned not was overthrown, And, on account of those who wrought wickedly, That which wrought not foolishness was delivered up to (its) enemies?'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:11: And the whole people answered and said unto me: 'So far as we can recall the good things which the Mighty One has done unto us, we do recall them; and those things which we do not remember He in His mercy knows.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:12: Nevertheless, do this for us thy people: write also to our brethren in Babylon an epistle of doctrine and a scroll of hope, that thou mayst confirm them also before thou dost depart from us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:13: For the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel) have perished, And the lamps which gave light are extinguished, And the fountains have withheld their stream whence we used to drink.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:14: And we are left in the darkness, And amid the [trees of the forest], And the thirst of the wilderness.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:15: And I answered and said unto them: 'Shepherds and lamps and fountains come from the law: And though we depart, yet the law abideth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:16: If therefore ye have respect to the law, And are intent upon wisdom, A lamp will not be wanting, And a shepherd will not fail, And a fountain will not dry up.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:17: Nevertheless, as ye said unto me, I will write also unto your brethren in Babylon, and I will send by means of men, and I will write in like manner to the nine tribes and a half, and send by means of a bird.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:18: And it came to pass on the one and twentieth day in the eighth month that I, Baruch, came and sat down under the oak under the shadow of the branches, and no man was with me, but I was alone.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:19: And I wrote these two epistles: one I sent by an eagle to the nine and a half tribes; and the other I sent to those that were at Babylon by means of three men.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:20: And I called the eagle and spake these words unto it:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:21: 'The El Elyon (Most High) hath made thee that thou shouldst be higher than all birds.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:22: And now go and tarry not in (any) place, nor enter a nest, nor settle upon any tree, till thou hast passed over the breadth of the many waters of the river Euphrates, and hast gone to the people that dwell there, and cast down to them this epistle.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:23: Remember, moreover, that, at the time of the deluge, Noah received from a dove the fruit of the olive, when he sent it forth from the ark.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:24: Yea, also the ravens ministered to Elijah, bearing him food, as they had been commanded.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:25: Solomon also, in the time of his kingdom, whithersoever he wished to send or seek for anything, commanded a bird (to go thither), and it obeyed him as he commanded it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|77:26: And now let it not weary thee, and turn not to the right hand nor the left, but fly and go by a direct way, that thou mayst preserve the command of the Mighty One, according as I said unto thee.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:1: These are the words of that epistle which Baruch the son of Neriah sent to the nine and a half tribes, which were across the river Euphrates, in which these things were written.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:2: Thus saith Baruch the son of Neriah to the brethren carried into captivity: 'Mercy and peace. I bear in mind, my brethren, the love of Him who created us, who loved us from of old, and never hated us, but above all educated us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:3: And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:4: Wherefore I have been the more careful to leave you the words of this epistle before I die, that ye may be comforted regarding the evils which have come upon you, and that ye may be grieved also regarding the evil that has befallen your brethren; and again, also, that ye may justify His judgement which He has decreed against you that ye should be carried away captive—for what ye have suffered is disproportioned to what ye have done—in order
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:5: that, at the last times, ye may be found worthy of your fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:6: Therefore, if ye consider that ye have now suffered those things for your good, that ye may not finally be condemned and tormented, then ye will receive eternal hope; if above all ye destroy from your heart vain error, on account of which ye departed hence.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|78:7: For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:1: Now, my brethren, learn first what befell Zion: how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against us.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:2: For we have sinned against Him who made us, and we have not kept the commandments which he commanded us, yet he hath not chastened us as we deserved.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|79:3: For what befell you we also suffer in a pre-eminent degree, for it befell us also.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:1: And now, my brethren, I make known unto you that when the enemy had surrounded the city, the angels of the El Elyon (Most High) were sent, and they overthrew the fortifications of the strong wall, and they destroyed the firm iron corners, which could not be rooted out.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:2: Nevertheless, they hid all the vessels of the sanctuary, lest the enemy should get possession of them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:3: And when they had done these things, they delivered thereupon to the enemy the overthrown wall, and the plundered house, and the burnt temple, and the people who were overcome because they were delivered up, lest the enemy should boast and say: 'Thus by force have we been able to lay waste even the house of the El Elyon (Most High) in war.'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:4: Your brethren also have they bound and led away to Babylon, and have caused them to dwell there.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:5: But we have been left here, being very few.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:6: This is the tribulation about which I wrote to you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|80:7: For assuredly I know that (the consolation of) the inhabitants of Zion consoleth you: so far as ye knew that it was prospered (your consolation) was greater than the tribulation which ye endured in having to depart from it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:1: But regarding consolation, hear ye the word.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:2: For I was mourning regarding Zion, and I prayed for mercy from the El Elyon (Most High), and I said:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:3: 'How long will these things endure for us? And will these evils come upon us always?'
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|81:4: And the Mighty One did according to the multitude of His mercies, And the El Elyon (Most High) according to the greatness of His compassion, And He revealed unto me the word, that I might receive consolation, And He showed me visions that I should not again endure anguish, And He made known to me the mystery of the times, And the advent of the hours he showed me.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:1: Therefore, my brethren, I have written to you, that ye may comfort yourselves regarding the multitude of your tribulations.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:2: For know ye that our Maker will assuredly avenge us on all our enemies, according to all that they have done to us, also that the consummation which the El Elyon (Most High) will make is very nigh, and His mercy that is coming, and the consummation of His judgement, is by no means far off.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:3: For lo! we see now the multitude of the prosperity of the Gentiles, Though they act impiously, But they shall be like a vapour:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:4: And we behold the multitude of their power, Though they do wickedly, But they shall be made like unto a drop:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:5: And we see the firmness of their might, Though they resist the Mighty One every hour, But they shall be accounted as spittle.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:6: And we consider the glory of their greatness, Though they do not keep the statutes of the El Elyon (Most High), But as smoke shall they pass away.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:7: And we meditate on the beauty of their gracefulness, Though they have to do with pollutions, But as grass that withers shall they fade away.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:8: And we consider the strength of their cruelty, Though they remember not the end (thereof), But as a wave that passes shall they be broken.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|82:9: And we remark the boastfulness of their might, Though they deny the beneficence of Elohim (God), who gave (it) to them, But they shall pass away as a passing cloud.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:1: [For the El Elyon (Most High) will assuredly hasten His times, And He will assuredly bring on His hours.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:2: And He will assuredly judge those who are in His world, And will visit in truth all things by means of all their hidden works.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:3: And He will assuredly examine the secret thoughts, And that which is laid up in the secret chambers of all the members of man, And will make (them) manifest in the presence of all with reproof.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:4: Let none therefore of these present things ascend into your hearts, but above all let us be expectant, because that which is promised to us shall come.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:5: And let us not now look unto the delights of the Gentiles in the present, but let us remember what has been promised to us in the end.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:6: For the ends of the times and of the seasons and whatsoever is with them shall assuredly pass by together.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:7: The consummation, moreover, of the age shall then show the great might of its ruler, when all things come to judgement.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:8: Do ye therefore prepare your hearts for that which before ye believed, lest ye come to be in bondage in both worlds, so that ye be led away captive here and be tormented there.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:9: For that which exists now or which has passed away, or which is to come, in all these things, neither is the evil fully evil, nor again the good fully good.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:10: For all healthinesses of this time are turning into diseases,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:11: And all might of this time is turning into weakness, And all the force of this time is turning into impotence,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:12: And every energy of youth is turning into old age and consummation, And every beauty of gracefulness of this time is turning faded and hateful,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:13: And every proud dominion of the present is turning into humiliation and shame,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:14: And every praise of the glory of this time is turning into the shame of silence, And every vain splendour and insolence of this time is turning into voiceless ruin.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:15: And every delight and joy of this time is turning to worms and corruption,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:16: And every clamour of the pride of this time is turning into dust and stillness.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:17: And every possession of riches of this time is being turned into Sheol alone,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:18: And all the rapine of passion of this time is turning into involuntary death, And every passion of the lusts of this time is turning into a judgement of torment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:19: And every artifice and craftiness of this time is turning into a proof of the truth,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:20: And every sweetness of unguents of this time is turning into judgement and condemnation,
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:21: And every love of lying is turning to contumely through truth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-baruch|83:22: Since therefore all these things are done now, does anyone think that they will not be avenged? But the consummation of all things will come to the truth.]

cards.note: *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2). Baruch looks ahead to the time when the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, and the Mighty One brings bewilderment on the earth and its rulers. Yahusha (Jesus), looking at the crowds, says the harvest truly is plenteous, and the labourers are few. What Baruch placed at the end of the age, Yahusha (Jesus) says is already at hand. Both speak of a harvest of two kinds of seed, which is why the sorting matters and why labourers are wanted.
cards.s_text: Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
cards.t_text: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.

cards.note: *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38) *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sees the crowds and tells his disciples to ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest for labourers, because the harvest is standing ready. Baruch had already been told what that harvest is: the time of the age ripens, and what was sown in it, evil seed and good seed alike, has come up. The one Baruch calls the Mighty One is the owner of that field, so the prayer in Matthew is a prayer prayed inside that ripening time, and the next chapter sends the twelve out as the answer.
cards.s_text: Pray you therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
cards.t_text: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.

cards.note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* (2 Baruch 78:3) Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the multitudes and finds them scattered and without a shepherd, which is a picture of a people and not of a crowd of strangers. Baruch writes to the brethren in captivity and says who that people is: the twelve tribes, bound by one bond because they are born from one father. However far they have been carried, they are one flock by birth, and that is what moves Yahusha (Jesus) to compassion.
cards.s_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.t_text: And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.

cards.note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* (2 Baruch 78:7) Yahusha (Jesus) is moved with compassion at sheep scattered abroad with no shepherd. Baruch closes his letter to the scattered tribes with the promise that answers it: Yahuah (Lord) will never forget or forsake them, and with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed. The compassion in Matthew and the mercy in Baruch are one mercy, and its work is the gathering.

cards.note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). *And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.* (2 Baruch 6:7). The veil is torn from the top to the bottom, which is a tearing from above. In 2 Baruch the hand from above also acts upon the veil: the angel descends into the Holy of Holies and takes from there the veil, the ark, the mercy seat and every holy vessel, and the next verse in the book says he charges the earth to guard them until the last times so that strangers may not get possession of them. In neither is the house of Yahuah (God) simply done away with. In Baruch its holy things are kept to be restored, and in Matthew the veil is opened from above, and the way back into the holiest is the way home.

cards.t_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.

cards.note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time. For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them:* (2 Baruch 51:7–8). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. Baruch speaks of people for whom the law was a hope, an understanding and a confidence, and says wonders will appear in their time and they will behold the world that is now invisible to them. These are people whose whole life was the Torah, and nothing here sets their works against the promise. It describes the covenant walk of those who kept the commandments, and the opened graves at the cross are the first glimpse of the seeing that is promised to them.

cards.note: Jeremiah 3:16 — *...they shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD): neither shall it come to mind...* — the ark passes from sight, as Baruch's earth swallows it, until its day.
cards.s_text: And he spake to the earth with a loud voice: 'Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of El Gibbor (the mighty God), And receive what I commit to thee, And guard them until the last times, So that, when thou art ordered, thou mayst restore them, So that strangers may not get possession of them.
cards.t_text: And it shall come to pass, when you be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, says Yahuah (LORD), they shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD): neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 2:8 — *Then shall Yahuah (God) shew them these things, and the glory of Yahuah (God) shall appear...* — the promised restoring of what the earth now hides.
cards.s_text: And he spake to the earth with a loud voice: 'Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of El Gibbor (the mighty God), And receive what I commit to thee, And guard them until the last times, So that, when thou art ordered, thou mayst restore them, So that strangers may not get possession of them.
cards.t_text: Then shall Yahuah (God) shew them these things, and the glory of Yahuah (God) shall appear, and the cloud also, as it was shewed under Moses, and as when Solomon desired that the place might be honourably sanctified.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 2:7 — *...As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that Yahuah (God) gather his people again together, and receive them to mercy.* — *guard them until the last times ... that thou mayst restore them*, almost word for word.
cards.s_text: And he spake to the earth with a loud voice: 'Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of El Gibbor (the mighty God), And receive what I commit to thee, And guard them until the last times, So that, when thou art ordered, thou mayst restore them, So that strangers may not get possession of them.
cards.t_text: Which when Jeremy perceived, he blamed them, saying, As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that Yahuah (God) gather his people again together, and receive them to mercy.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 2:5 — *And when Jeremy came thither, he found an hollow cave, in which he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.* — the same act: the holy things committed to the earth and sealed.
cards.s_text: And he spake to the earth with a loud voice: 'Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of El Gibbor (the mighty God), And receive what I commit to thee, And guard them until the last times, So that, when thou art ordered, thou mayst restore them, So that strangers may not get possession of them.
cards.t_text: And when Jeremy came thither, he found an hollow cave, in which he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.

cards.note: Exodus 25:17 — *And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold...* — the mercy-seat the angel takes was made to this command.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: And you shall make a mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.

cards.note: Exodus 26:33 — *And thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches ... and the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy.* — the veil and ark whose making 2 Baruch presupposes.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: And you shall hang up the vail under the taches, that you may bring in thither within the vail the ark of the testimony: and the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy.

cards.note: Matthew 27:51 — *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* — the veil of the holy place, removed again at the Messiah's death.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

cards.note: Hebrews 9:5 — *And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we can not now speak particularly.* — the mercy-seat carried off by the angel.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we can not now speak particularly.

cards.note: Hebrews 9:4 — *Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;* — the ark, the altar of incense, and the two tables, named in the same breath Baruch names them.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

cards.note: Hebrews 9:3 — *And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;* — the veil Baruch's angel first removes.
cards.s_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.
cards.t_text: And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:27 — *...lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and Yahuah (LORD) hath not done all this.* — Elohim guards His own glory against the enemy's boast, the very motive Baruch's angel voices.
cards.s_text: And after these things I heard that angel saying unto those angels who held the lamps: 'Destroy, therefore, and overthrow its wall to its foundations, lest the enemy should boast and say: "We have overthrown the wall of Zion, And we have burnt the place of El Gibbor (the mighty God)."'
cards.t_text: Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and Yahuah (LORD) has not done all this.

cards.note: Jeremiah 52:11 — *Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon...* — the same captivity attested by the prophet who lived it.
cards.s_text: And they led the people away captive and slew some of them, and bound Zedekiah the king, and sent him to the king of Babylon.
cards.t_text: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

cards.note: 2 Kings 25:7 — *...and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.* — the binding and deportation of Zedekiah Baruch records.
cards.s_text: And they led the people away captive and slew some of them, and bound Zedekiah the king, and sent him to the king of Babylon.
cards.t_text: And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.

cards.note: Ezekiel 11:23 — *And the glory of Yahuah (LORD) went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city.* — the glory leaves before the enemy enters.
cards.s_text: 'Enter, ye enemies, And come, ye adversaries; For he who kept the house has forsaken (it).'
cards.t_text: And the glory of Yahuah (LORD) went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city.

cards.note: Ezekiel 10:18 — *Then the glory of Yahuah (LORD) departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims.* — the Keeper forsakes the house, exactly as Baruch's voice declares.
cards.s_text: 'Enter, ye enemies, And come, ye adversaries; For he who kept the house has forsaken (it).'
cards.t_text: Then the glory of Yahuah (LORD) departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:10 — *The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth* — Jeremiah's own dirge of rent garments over fallen Zion.
cards.s_text: And we rent our garments, we wept, and mourned, and fasted seven days.
cards.t_text: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

cards.note: Joel 2:12 — *Therefore also now, saith Yahuah (LORD), turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning* — the same weeping-and-mourning fast Baruch and Jeremiah hold.
cards.s_text: And we rent our garments, we wept, and mourned, and fasted seven days.
cards.t_text: Therefore also now, says Yahuah (LORD), turn you even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:

cards.note: Joel 1:14 — *Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and cry unto Yahuah (LORD)* — the appointed fast over a stricken land Baruch keeps.
cards.s_text: And we rent our garments, we wept, and mourned, and fasted seven days.
cards.t_text: Sanctify you a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and cry unto Yahuah (LORD),

cards.note: Jeremiah 9:1 — *Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!* — Jeremiah's tears over Zion, the grief framing Baruch's whole lament.
cards.s_text: And you, ye virgins, who weave fine linen And silk with gold of Ophir, Take with haste all (these) things And cast (them) into the fire, That it may bear them to Him who made them, And the flame send them to Him who created them, Lest the enemy get possession of them.'
cards.t_text: Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!

cards.note: Lamentations 2:18 — *Their heart cried unto Yahuah (Lord), O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night* — Zion handed back to the LORD with weeping, Baruch's 'Guard Thy house Thyself.'
cards.s_text: Moreover, ye priests, take ye the keys of the sanctuary, And cast them into the height of heaven, And give them to Yahuah (Lord) and say: "Guard Thy house Thyself, For lo! we are found false stewards."
cards.t_text: Their heart cried unto Adonai (Lord), O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night: give thyself no rest; let not the apple of your eye cease.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:20 — *shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of Yahuah (Lord)?* — the priests of the sanctuary undone, the false-steward grief Baruch voices.
cards.s_text: Moreover, ye priests, take ye the keys of the sanctuary, And cast them into the height of heaven, And give them to Yahuah (Lord) and say: "Guard Thy house Thyself, For lo! we are found false stewards."
cards.t_text: Behold, O Yahuah (LORD), and consider to whom you have done this. Shall the women eat their fruit, and children of a span long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of Adonai (Lord)?

cards.note: Lamentations 2:20 — *Shall the women eat their fruit, and children of a span long?* — Jeremiah's horror at child and mother in the siege, the grief behind Baruch's 'bear in pain, only to bury in grief.'
cards.s_text: For why should they bear in pain, Only to bury in grief? Or why, again, should mankind have sons?
cards.t_text: Behold, O Yahuah (LORD), and consider to whom you have done this. Shall the women eat their fruit, and children of a span long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of Adonai (Lord)?

cards.note: Luke 23:29 — *they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck* — the barren counted glad over a falling Jerusalem, as Baruch's verse 14.
cards.s_text: For the barren shall above all rejoice, And those who have no sons shall be glad, And those who have sons shall have anguish.
cards.t_text: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

cards.note: Matthew 24:19 — *And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!* — the Messiah's woe over child-bearing in the day of Zion's tribulation, Baruch's lament exactly.
cards.s_text: For the barren shall above all rejoice, And those who have no sons shall be glad, And those who have sons shall have anguish.
cards.t_text: And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!

cards.note: Luke 23:29 — *For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare* — the Messiah's own lament over a doomed Jerusalem, the same blessing on the unborn.
cards.s_text: 'Blessed is he who was not born, Or he, who having been born, has died.
cards.t_text: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 4:3 — *Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun* — better never to have been, the very thought of Baruch's verse 6.
cards.s_text: But as for us who live, woe unto us, Because we see the afflictions of Zion, And what has befallen Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: Yea, better is he than both they, which has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 4:2 — *Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive* — the Preacher counting the dead happier, as Baruch does.
cards.s_text: 'Blessed is he who was not born, Or he, who having been born, has died.
cards.t_text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

cards.note: Job 3:11 — *Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?* — the same wish to have died at birth.
cards.s_text: 'Blessed is he who was not born, Or he, who having been born, has died.
cards.t_text: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

cards.note: Job 3:3 — *Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived* — Job's curse on his birthday, the root of Baruch's cry.
cards.s_text: 'Blessed is he who was not born, Or he, who having been born, has died.
cards.t_text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.

cards.note: Proverbs 14:32 — *the righteous hath hope in his death* — the fathers who 'went to rest without grief' do not rest in nothing but in hope, guarding Baruch's lament from despair.
cards.s_text: Our fathers went to rest without grief, And lo! the righteous sleep in the earth in tranquillity;
cards.t_text: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous has hope in his death.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 4:2 — *Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive* — the dead blessed above the living, Baruch's word to Sheol.
cards.s_text: "Blessed are ye more than we who live."'
cards.t_text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

cards.note: Psalm 73:17 — *Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end* — the resolution of Baruch's 'who will be judge?': their end is known before the LORD.
cards.s_text: Who will be judge regarding these things? Or to whom shall we complain regarding that which has befallen us? O Yahuah (Lord), how hast Thou borne (it)?
cards.t_text: Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end.

cards.note: Psalm 73:12 — *Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches* — the prospering wicked Baruch sees in prospering Babylon.
cards.s_text: But now, lo! the grief is infinite, And the lamentation measureless, For lo! thou art prospered And Zion desolate.
cards.t_text: Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.

cards.note: Psalm 73:3 — *For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked* — the Psalmist's grief at Babylon-like prospering, Baruch's complaint exactly.
cards.s_text: But now, lo! the grief is infinite, And the lamentation measureless, For lo! thou art prospered And Zion desolate.
cards.t_text: For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

cards.note: Psalm 39:5 — *verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity* — even at his brightest the prosperer is vanity, the lesson of the fading noonday.
cards.s_text: The noonday does not always burn, Nor do the rays of the sun constantly give light.
cards.t_text: Behold, you have made my days as an handbreadth; and my age is as nothing before you: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Selah.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 8:13 — *it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before Elohim (God)* — the prosperer's day a fleeting shadow, Baruch's noon that does not always burn.
cards.s_text: The noonday does not always burn, Nor do the rays of the sun constantly give light.
cards.t_text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he fears not before Elohim (God).

cards.note: 2 Peter 3:9 — *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward* — the 'long-suffering' that holds the wrath by reins, named by the apostle.
cards.s_text: For assuredly in its own season shall the (divine) wrath awake against thee, Which now in long-suffering is held in as it were by reins.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:35 — *their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste* — Moses' word that recompense waits its 'due time,' Baruch's wrath held by reins.
cards.s_text: For assuredly in its own season shall the (divine) wrath awake against thee, Which now in long-suffering is held in as it were by reins.
cards.t_text: To me belongs vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.

cards.note: Habakkuk 2:3 — *For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come* — the wrath that 'in its own season shall the (divine) wrath awake' the appointed delay Baruch describes.
cards.s_text: For assuredly in its own season shall the (divine) wrath awake against thee, Which now in long-suffering is held in as it were by reins.
cards.t_text: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:11 — *Beware that thou forget not Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in not keeping his commandments* — Moses' warning against forgetting the Giver, behind Baruch's 'ungrateful for the beneficence.'
cards.s_text: But now, ye peoples and nations, ye are guilty Because ye have always trodden down the earth, And used the creation unrighteously.
cards.t_text: Beware that you forget not Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command you this day:

cards.note: Romans 1:21 — *when they knew Elohim (God), they glorified him not as Elohim (God), neither were thankful* — the nations ungrateful for the benefit, Baruch's exact charge.
cards.s_text: For I have always benefited you. And ye have always been ungrateful for the beneficence.
cards.t_text: Because that, when they knew Elohim (God), they glorified him not as Elohim (God), neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:5 — *as a man chasteneth his son, so Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) chasteneth thee* — Moses' word that the affliction of His sons is fatherly discipline, not enmity.
cards.s_text: On this account he had aforetime no mercy on His own sons, But afflicted them as His enemies, because they sinned,
cards.t_text: You shall also consider in your heart, that, as a man chastens his son, so Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) chastens you.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:12 — *whom Yahuah (LORD) loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth* — the Father's chastening of His sons unto their good, Baruch's 'chastened that they might be sanctified.'
cards.s_text: Then therefore were they chastened That they might be sanctified.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (LORD) loves he corrects; even as a father the son in whom he delights.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 10:17 — *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)... regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward* — Moses' word that the LORD shows no partiality, the root of Baruch's impartial Judge.
cards.s_text: For how long? Thou wilt say to them: "Ye who have drunk the strained wine, Drink ye also of its dregs, The judgement of the Lofty One Who has no respect of persons."'
cards.t_text: For Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is Elohim (God) of gods, and Adonai (Lord) of lords, a great Elohim (God), a mighty, and a terrible, which regards not persons, nor takes reward:

cards.note: Romans 2:11 — *For there is no respect of persons with Elohim (God)* — the impartial Judge, Baruch's 'Lofty One who has no respect of persons.'
cards.s_text: For how long? Thou wilt say to them: "Ye who have drunk the strained wine, Drink ye also of its dregs, The judgement of the Lofty One Who has no respect of persons."'
cards.t_text: For there is no respect of persons with Elohim (God).

cards.note: Psalm 75:8 — *in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture... the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them* — the cup of wrath whose dregs the nations drink, Baruch's very figure.
cards.s_text: For how long? Thou wilt say to them: "Ye who have drunk the strained wine, Drink ye also of its dregs, The judgement of the Lofty One Who has no respect of persons."'
cards.t_text: For in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he pours out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them.

cards.note: Genesis 1:26 — *Let us make man in our image... and let them have dominion... over all the earth* — man set as 'administrator of Thy works,' the very stewardship Baruch names.
cards.s_text: And Thou didst say that Thou wouldst make for Thy world man as the administrator of Thy works, that it might be known that he was by no means made on account of the world, but the world on account of him.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.

cards.note: Isaiah 45:18 — *he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited* — the world made not for itself but for man's dwelling, Baruch's 'the world on account of him.'
cards.s_text: And Thou didst say that Thou wouldst make for Thy world man as the administrator of Thy works, that it might be known that he was by no means made on account of the world, but the world on account of him.
cards.t_text: For thus says Yahuah (LORD) that created the heavens; Elohim (God) himself that formed the earth and made it; he has established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am Yahuah (LORD); and there is none else.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:3 — *Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of Elohim (God)* — the works of creation framed by a spoken word, as Baruch says.
cards.s_text: When of old there was no world with its inhabitants, Thou didst devise and speak with a word, and forthwith the works of creation stood before Thee.
cards.t_text: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of Elohim (God), so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

cards.note: Psalm 33:6 — *By the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth* — creation that 'stood before Thee' at His word, Baruch's verse 17.
cards.s_text: When of old there was no world with its inhabitants, Thou didst devise and speak with a word, and forthwith the works of creation stood before Thee.
cards.t_text: By the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.

cards.note: Revelation 14:13 — *Blessed are the dead which die in Yahusha (Lord) from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.* — the righteous departing without fear, their works 'preserved in treasuries.'
cards.s_text: For the righteous justly hope for the end, and without fear depart from this habitation, because they have with Thee a store of works preserved in treasuries.
cards.t_text: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.

cards.note: 1 Peter 1:4 — *To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you* — the promised world the righteous 'hope to receive,' Baruch's treasured hope.
cards.s_text: On this account also these without fear leave this world, and trusting with joy they hope to receive the world which Thou hast promised them.
cards.t_text: To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,

cards.note: Psalm 39:5 — *mine age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity* — the fleeting breath of man's nature Baruch laments.
cards.s_text: For as the breath ascends involuntarily, and again dies, so it is with the nature of men, who depart not according to their own will, and know not what will befall them in the end.
cards.t_text: Behold, you have made my days as an handbreadth; and my age is as nothing before you: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Selah.

cards.note: Psalm 144:4 — *Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passeth away* — man made like a breath, Baruch's confession exactly.
cards.s_text: For we have all been made like a breath.
cards.t_text: Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passes away.

cards.note: Job 38:4 — *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding* — the LORD's rebuke of the creature who would search out His counsel, behind Baruch's questions.
cards.s_text: Or who will be able to think out Thy incomprehensible counsel? Or who of those that are born has ever found The beginning or end of Thy wisdom?
cards.t_text: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if you have understanding.

cards.note: Romans 11:33 — *O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of Elohim (God)! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!* — Baruch's 'who, O Yahuah (LORD), my Lord, will comprehend Thy judgement' in the apostle's very words.
cards.s_text: But who, O Yahuah (LORD), my Lord, will comprehend Thy judgement, Or who will search out the profoundness of Thy way? Or who will think out the [weight] of Thy path?
cards.t_text: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of Elohim (God)! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

cards.note: James 1:12 — *when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him* — the 'crown with great glory' promised after the labour.
cards.s_text: For this world is to them a strife and a labour with much trouble; and that accordingly which is to come, a crown with great glory.'
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that endures temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to them that love him.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 4:17 — *For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory* — this world's strife against the coming crown, Baruch's two ages.
cards.s_text: For this world is to them a strife and a labour with much trouble; and that accordingly which is to come, a crown with great glory.'
cards.t_text: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, works for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;

cards.note: Romans 7:12 — *Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good* — the law by which the knowing transgressor is justly judged, never abolished but upheld.
cards.s_text: But now, because he transgressed wittingly, yea, just on this ground that he wot (thereof), he shall be tormented.
cards.t_text: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 4:6 — *for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations* — Moses' word that the law is Israel's very understanding, behind Baruch's 'unless he had accepted the law.'
cards.s_text: Man would not rightly have understood My judgement, unless he had accepted the law, and I had instructed him in understanding.
cards.t_text: Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.

cards.note: Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple* — the law that gives understanding, the LORD's answer to Baruch.
cards.s_text: Man would not rightly have understood My judgement, unless he had accepted the law, and I had instructed him in understanding.
cards.t_text: The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.

cards.note: Psalm 90:12 — *So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom* — the wise reckoning of a 'little time,' the answer to Baruch's question.
cards.s_text: And I answered and said: 'O Yahuah (LORD), my Lord, lo! the years of this time are few and evil, and who is able in his little time to acquire that which is measureless?'
cards.t_text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

cards.note: Psalm 90:10 — *The days of our years are threescore years and ten... yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off* — man's brief and toilsome span, Baruch's 'little time.'
cards.s_text: And I answered and said: 'O Yahuah (LORD), my Lord, lo! the years of this time are few and evil, and who is able in his little time to acquire that which is measureless?'
cards.t_text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

cards.note: Genesis 47:9 — *few and evil have the days of the years of my life been* — Jacob's word to Pharaoh, the exact phrase of Baruch's 'few and evil' years.
cards.s_text: And I answered and said: 'O Yahuah (LORD), my Lord, lo! the years of this time are few and evil, and who is able in his little time to acquire that which is measureless?'
cards.t_text: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years: few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.

cards.note: Prov 6:23 — *For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life* — the commandment itself the lamp Moses lit.
cards.s_text: Or wherein did Moses suffer loss in that he lived only one hundred and twenty years, and, inasmuch as he was subject to Him who formed him, brought the law to the seed of Jacob, and lighted a lamp for the nation of Yashar'el (Israel)?'
cards.t_text: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

cards.note: Ps 119:105 — *Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path* — the law as the lamp Baruch says Moses lighted for Israel.
cards.s_text: Or wherein did Moses suffer loss in that he lived only one hundred and twenty years, and, inasmuch as he was subject to Him who formed him, brought the law to the seed of Jacob, and lighted a lamp for the nation of Yashar'el (Israel)?'
cards.t_text: Your word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

cards.note: Rom 5:14 — *Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression* — death reigning over Adam's seed, as Baruch says his years were cut off.
cards.s_text: Therefore the multitude of time that he lived did not profit him, but brought death and cut off the years of those who were born from him.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.

cards.note: Rom 5:12 — *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned* — death entering by the one man's transgression, the same root Baruch names.
cards.s_text: For what did it profit Adam that he lived nine hundred and thirty years, and transgressed that which he was commanded?
cards.t_text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

cards.note: John 1:4 — *In him was life; and the life was the light of men* — the light men have, set against the darkness of Adam.
cards.s_text: But those many whom he has lighted have taken from the darkness of Adam and have not rejoiced in the light of the lamp.'
cards.t_text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

cards.note: John 1:17 — *For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Yahusha HaMashiach* — the light that came by Moses, which Baruch says the many would not rejoice in.
cards.s_text: But those many whom he has lighted have taken from the darkness of Adam and have not rejoiced in the light of the lamp.'
cards.t_text: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).

cards.note: Prov 6:23 — *For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life* — the lamp of the law that few imitate.
cards.s_text: And I answered and said: 'He that lighted has taken from the light, and there are but few that have imitated him.
cards.t_text: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
