They make war and are overcome, for he is the one only Sovereign above every throne, and they that are with him are *called, and chosen, and faithful.*

threads.title: The waters are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues (Isaiah 8, Jeremiah 47)
threads.summary_md: *And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues* (Revelation 17:15). The angel's own interpretation rests on a settled prophetic idiom: the massed nations are floodwaters. Isaiah had said it of Assyria — *behold, Yahuah (Lord) bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks* (Isaiah 8:7) — the nation as an overflowing flood rising over every bank. And Jeremiah said it of the invaders from the north: *Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein* (Jeremiah 47:2). The many waters the whore sits upon are the peoples in just this sense — the swarming nations she rides and rules. Yet the prophets' own image carries the warning: such waters become the flood of judgment, and the city that rode the peoples is in the end overflowed by them, the very horns and nations turning to make her desolate.

threads.title: The ten horns shall hate the whore and burn her with fire — the lovers turned against the harlot (Ezekiel 16 and 23)
threads.summary_md: *And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire* (Revelation 17:16); *For Elohim (God) hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will* (17:17). The harlot's own paramours become her executioners — and this exact turn is the prophets' sentence on the unfaithful city. Ezekiel spoke it twice. *Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure... I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them* (Ezekiel 16:37) — the lovers gathered against her to strip her bare; *and they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee... and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot* (Ezekiel 16:41) — the fire that ends her harlotry. And of the second harlot-city: *they shall deal with thee hatefully, and shall take away all thy labour, and shall leave thee naked and bare* (Ezekiel 23:29), delivered into the hand of *them whom thou hatest.* The kings who fornicated with the whore turn and hate her, strip her, and burn her — exactly as the prophet foretold of the harlot-city, the lovers become haters. Against Babylon, Jeremiah summoned the instrument: *a people shall come from the north, and a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth* (Jeremiah 50:41). And the restored library names the law of her end: *The reward of your whoredom shall be in your bosom, therefore shall you receive recompence* (2 Esdras 15:55); *And you shall be cast down by them as stubble, and they shall be to you as fire* (2 Esdras 15:61). The wages of her whoredom are paid back into her own bosom; the powers Yahuah (God) raises become fire to her, and *the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth* (Revelation 17:18) is consumed as stubble — the counterfeit city fallen, set forever against the holy city that is the true bride.

threads.title: Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen — the habitation of devils (Isaiah 21, Jeremiah 50-51)
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with another angel come down from heaven, the earth lightened with his glory, crying *Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird* (Revelation 18:2). Every phrase is the prophets' own. The doubled cry is the watchman's on the tower of Isaiah: *And he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground* (Isaiah 21:9). The desolation — a haunt of unclean creatures — is Isaiah's and Jeremiah's: *But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there* (Isaiah 13:21); *Therefore the wild beasts of the desert with the wild beasts of the islands shall dwell there, and the owls shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited for ever* (Jeremiah 50:39). The suddenness is Jeremiah's: *Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed: howl for her* (Jeremiah 51:8). And the maddening cup is his too: *For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication* (Revelation 18:3), echoing *Babylon hath been a golden cup in the LORD'S hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad* (Jeremiah 51:7). The seer stands in the prophets' watchtower and sees the doomed world-system fall as the river-city by the Euphrates fell — the proud glory of kingdoms emptied of men and given over to foul spirits, never to be inhabited again.

threads.title: Come out of her, my people — the gathered seed called to separate (Jeremiah 51, Isaiah 52, Numbers 16)
threads.summary_md: *And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues* (Revelation 18:4). This is the prophets' own summons to the covenant people — *my people* — to separate from the doomed system before the judgment falls, and it is the regathering call: the same word by which Yahuah (LORD) brought the seed out of the literal Babylon, now spoken to the scattered seed living among the nations. Jeremiah cries it twice: *Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity* (Jeremiah 51:6), and *My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 51:45). Isaiah binds the coming-out to redemption and to cleanness: *Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye... Yahuah (LORD) hath redeemed his servant Jacob* (Isaiah 48:20); *Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 52:11). The pattern is as old as the wilderness, when judgment was about to swallow the rebels: *Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye be consumed in all their sins* (Numbers 16:26). And the reason the call is so urgent is the heaped-up guilt: *For her sins have reached unto heaven, and Elohim (God) hath remembered her iniquities* (Revelation 18:5), as Jeremiah said — *her judgment reacheth unto heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies* (Jeremiah 51:9). To stay is to share her sins and her plagues; to come out is to be delivered, redeemed, and made clean — the lost sheep brought home out of the system before its ruin.

threads.title: Reward her double, the cup she filled — I sit a queen and am no widow (Jeremiah 50, Psalm 137, Isaiah 47)
threads.summary_md: *Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works: in the cup which she hath filled fill to her double* (Revelation 18:6). The law of recompense is the prophets': measure for measure, her own works returned upon her head. Jeremiah twice pronounces it: *recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against Yahuah (LORD), against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Jeremiah 50:29), and *as she hath done, do unto her* (Jeremiah 50:15). The captives by the rivers sang for the day: *O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us* (Psalm 137:8). And the proud security that invites the doom is the daughter of Babylon's own boast in Isaiah: *for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow* (Revelation 18:7), echoing *thou that... sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children* (Isaiah 47:8) — the same word *I am, and there is none beside me* that the rejoicing city speaks in Zephaniah, *how is she become a desolation* (Zephaniah 2:15). The boast is answered in the suddenness Isaiah named: *these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood* (Isaiah 47:9), which the seer re-speaks — *Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) who judgeth her* (Revelation 18:8). The city that thought herself untouchable is undone in a single day, repaid in full in her own cup.

threads.title: The kings and merchants and shipmasters lament over her — the dirge over Tyre (Ezekiel 27)
threads.summary_md: The long lament of the kings, the merchants, and the shipmasters weeping over the burning city (Revelation 18:9-19) is the seer re-speaking Ezekiel's dirge over Tyre, the merchant of the peoples. The mariners' mourning is taken straight from the prophet: *And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing* (Revelation 18:19), echoing *they shall cast up dust upon their heads, they shall wallow themselves in the ashes* (Ezekiel 27:30). The astonished cry is word for word: *And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city!* (Revelation 18:18), from *they shall... lament over thee, saying, What city is like Tyrus, like the destroyed in the midst of the sea?* (Ezekiel 27:32). And the wealth she poured into the kings' laps is Ezekiel's too: *wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness* (Revelation 18:19), from *thou didst enrich the kings of the earth with the multitude of thy riches and of thy merchandise* (Ezekiel 27:33). Isaiah had already foretold the merchants' scattering: *thy merchants, from thy youth: they shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee* (Isaiah 47:15) — and so *the merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing* (Revelation 18:15). The Hebrew library knew this overturning of all commerce in the day of trouble: *He that selleth, let him be as he that fleeth away: and he that buyeth, as one that will lose* (2 Esdras 16:41); *He that occupieth merchandise, as he that has no profit by it* (2 Esdras 16:42) — the very void the seer beholds, *for no man buyeth their merchandise any more* (Revelation 18:11). The trade that fattened the kings, the gold and silk and the souls of men, is made nothing in one hour, and those who grew rich by her keep their distance and weep.

threads.title: Rejoice over her, thou heaven — Elohim (God) hath avenged you on her (Jeremiah 51, Deuteronomy 32)
threads.summary_md: Against the weeping of the kings and merchants, heaven is called to rejoice: *Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for Elohim (God) hath avenged you on her* (Revelation 18:20). The summons is Jeremiah's: when Babylon falls, *Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 51:48). And the ground of the rejoicing — the avenging of the servants' blood — is the close of the Song of Moses: *Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people* (Deuteronomy 32:43). The fall of the oppressor is the vindication of the long-waiting saints, the apostles and prophets whose blood the system shed — the ancient promise of Moses come to pass, the heavens singing because Yahuah (LORD) has at last avenged his own.

threads.title: The millstone cast into the sea — thus shall Babylon be thrown down (Jeremiah 51, Isaiah 47)
threads.summary_md: *And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all* (Revelation 18:21). The enacted sign is Jeremiah's: he commanded Seraiah, when he came to Babylon and finished reading the book of her doom, to *bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates* (Jeremiah 51:63), and to say *Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her* (Jeremiah 51:64). The angel of the Apocalypse does in the great what Seraiah did at the river: the stone cast into the water, the city sunk and never to rise. Jeremiah had seen the waters close over her — *The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof* (Jeremiah 51:42). And the silencing of the city follows: the mill that ground for proud Babylon — to which Isaiah had brought her down, *Take the millstones, and grind meal* (Isaiah 47:2) — falls forever quiet, *and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in thee* (Revelation 18:22), the music and the craftsman and the bridegroom's voice all heard no more, *and the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee... for by thy sorceries were all nations deceived* (Revelation 18:23). The Hebrew library named the same end for the city that afflicted Yahuah's (LORD's) people: *For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time* (Baruch 4:35) — the lamp put out, the city of sorceries burned and given over to the foul spirits.

threads.title: In her was found the blood of prophets and of saints (Jeremiah 51, Matthew 23)
threads.summary_md: The last word over Babylon names the reason for her doom: *And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth* (Revelation 18:24). Jeremiah had charged her with the same double guilt — the slain of the covenant people and the slain of all the earth: *As Babylon hath caused the slain of Yashar'el (Israel) to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth* (Jeremiah 51:49). And Yahusha (Jesus) had named the gathering of all righteous blood upon the system that kills the prophets: *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar* (Matthew 23:35). The doomed city is the long account of shed blood closed at last — from Abel onward, the prophets and the saints and all the slain of the earth avenged in her fall. The Babylon-system that drank the blood of Yahuah's (LORD's) servants is brought to reckoning, and the cry of the souls under the altar is answered.

threads.title: The great Alleluia — Hallelu-Yah, salvation and glory unto Yahuah (LORD) (Psalm 104 and 106)
threads.summary_md: Four times in these verses heaven cries *Alleluia* — and the word is no new coinage of the apocalypse; it is the ancient Hebrew Hallel, *Hallelu-Yah*, *Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)*, lifted straight out of the Psalms. *And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the Lord our God)* (Revelation 19:1). The first *Alleluia* in scripture stands at the close of the creation psalm, over the consuming of the wicked: *Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless thou Yahuah (LORD), O my soul. Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 104:35). The praise that opens the Hallel is the same: *Praise ye Yahuah (LORD). O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 106:1). And when the four and twenty elders and the four beasts fall down *saying, Amen; Alleluia* (Revelation 19:4), they speak the doxology that seals that psalm — *let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 106:48). The voice from the throne — *Praise our Elohim (God), all ye his servants, and ye that fear him, both small and great* (Revelation 19:5) — is the Hallel's own summons: *Praise, O ye servants of Yahuah (LORD), praise the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 113:1). And the great multitude *as the voice of many waters* cries *Alleluia: for Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) omnipotent reigneth* (Revelation 19:6) — the praise that opens the last psalms of the Psalter, *Praise Yahuah (LORD), O my soul* (Psalm 146:1), where *Yahuah (LORD) shall reign for ever* (Psalm 146:10). The second *Alleluia* is sung over the rising smoke — *And again they said, Alleluia. And her smoke rose up for ever and ever* (Revelation 19:3) — the smoke Isaiah saw over the city of Yahuah's (LORD's) curse: *the smoke thereof shall go up for ever* (Isaiah 34:10). Heaven does not invent its praise; it sings the covenant people's own *Hallelu-Yah* over the judgment of the great whore and the reign of the One.

threads.title: The marriage of the Lamb, the Bride arrayed in fine linen (Isaiah 61 and 54, Hosea 2)
threads.summary_md: *Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints* (Revelation 19:7-8). This marriage is the covenant the prophets sang for centuries. Isaiah heard the Bride rejoice: *he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels* (Isaiah 61:10) — the robe of righteousness is the very fine linen, *the righteousness of saints*, with which the wife of the Lamb is clothed; she does not weave it of herself, she is covered by the One who makes her ready. And the Bridegroom is no stranger: *thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 54:5). The Lamb who weds his Bride is her Maker and Redeemer, Yahuah (LORD) come in flesh, taking back the people he had for a small moment let go — *with great mercies will I gather thee* (Isaiah 54:7). She is the wife of Hosea's betrothal, the one who had played the harlot, brought into the wilderness and wooed back there: *I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies* (Hosea 2:19), *I will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness: and thou shalt know Yahuah (LORD)* (Hosea 2:20). The betrothal *in righteousness* is answered by the Bride arrayed in the *righteousness of saints*; the great whore is judged and the divorced house, brought into the wilderness, is betrothed again there — *I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people* (Hosea 2:23). The royal wedding-song shows her brought to the king: *the king's daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold... she shall be brought unto the king in raiment of needlework* (Psalm 45:13-14). And then the word is sealed with a blessing: *Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb* (Revelation 19:9). The betrothal in the wilderness is the road of the homecoming the prophets promised, and the called are blessed.

threads.title: Worship Elohim (God) — the angel refuses worship, the testimony of Yahusha the spirit of prophecy (Exodus 34, Deuteronomy 6)
threads.summary_md: *And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus): worship Elohim (God): for the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus) is the spirit of prophecy* (Revelation 19:10). The angel will not take the worship John offers, and the refusal rests on the first word of the covenant. *For thou shalt worship no other god: for Yahuah (LORD), whose name is Jealous, is a jealous Elohim (God)* (Exodus 34:14). Worship belongs to the One alone — not to an angel, not to a fellowservant — and the angel keeps the commandment by deflecting it straight back: *worship Elohim (God)*. The charge is the Shema's own: *Thou shalt fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and serve him, and shalt swear by his name* (Deuteronomy 6:13) — the very word Yahusha (Jesus) wielded against the tempter, that service and worship are the One's alone. This keeps the whole vision rightly ordered: on the throne sits the One who is worshipped; the Lamb is his faithful witness; the rider who is the Word of Elohim (God) is the Formed who is Yahuah (LORD) come in flesh and has a Father; and not even the mighty angel of the apocalypse will receive what is due to the One. And the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus), the angel adds, *is the spirit of prophecy* — the breath that has carried every true prophet's word, all of it bearing witness to the One worshipped and to the Lamb who is his witness. Worship the One; hold the testimony; it is the spirit by which all prophecy was ever spoken.

threads.title: The rider Faithful and True, clothed in a vesture dipped in blood — The Word of Elohim (God) (Isaiah 63 and 11)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war* (Revelation 19:11). The rider is Yahusha the Formed, drawn from the Formless — *his eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns... And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 19:12-13). Isaiah named this righteous warrior long before — the Branch out of Jesse: *with righteousness shall he judge the poor... and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked* (Isaiah 11:4), the very breath that becomes the sharp sword of his mouth. The psalm awaited his coming: *he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness* (Psalm 96:13). And the royal wedding-psalm that dressed the Bride first arms the King: *gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty... and in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness* (Psalm 45:3-4). But the vision's deepest root is Isaiah 63, the one coming from Edom with garments dyed red: *Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel... I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save* (Isaiah 63:1). Why red? *I have trodden the winepress alone* (Isaiah 63:3). The *vesture dipped in blood* is the apparel Isaiah saw; the rider treads *the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God)* (Revelation 19:15). And the blood-stained garments reach back further still, to Jacob's blessing of Yahudah (Judah): *he washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes* (Genesis 49:11) — the Lion of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah), from whom the sceptre shall not depart, come at last. The Hebrew library knew this Word as a warrior who is a sharp sword: *your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war... and brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:15-16). And Esdras saw the Son destroy the gathered nations with no weapon but his breath: *out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath* (2 Esdras 13:10). The rider called The Word of Elohim (God) is that all-powerful Word — the Formed, mighty to save, who came in flesh and rides to judge in righteousness.

threads.title: The sharp sword and the rod of iron — KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS (Isaiah 11, Psalm 2, Deuteronomy 10)
threads.summary_md: *And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God). And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS* (Revelation 19:15-16). Every word of this is the Tanakh's own. The weapon is no metal blade but the word of his mouth — *with righteousness shall he judge the poor... and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked* (Isaiah 11:4), and the servant's own confession: *he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword* (Isaiah 49:2). The rod of iron is the decree of the second psalm to the Son: *thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel* (Psalm 2:9) — and the kings who *set themselves... against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2) are the very kings gathered to war against the rider (Revelation 19:19), dashed as the psalm decreed. The winepress is Joel's valley of decision: *put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe... for the press is full, the fats overflow* (Joel 3:13). And the title on his thigh is Yahuah's (LORD's) own, declared in the Torah: *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is Elohim (God) of gods, and Lord of lords, a great Elohim (God), a mighty, and a terrible* (Deuteronomy 10:17). Even the Babylonian king confessed it — *your Elohim (God) is a Elohim (God) of gods, and a Yahuah (Lord) of kings* (Daniel 2:47) — and the Hallel sang it: *O give thanks to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:3). The rider bears the divine title because he is the Formed who is Yahuah (LORD). And the Hebrew library saw the same judgment: *this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations... and he shall destroy them without labour by the law which is like to fire* (2 Esdras 13:37-38) — the Son on mount Sion who destroys the gathered nations not by armies but by the word, the law like fire, the breath of his mouth.

threads.title: The supper of the great Elohim (God) — the sacrifice on Gog (Ezekiel 39)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great Elohim (God); That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men... and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great* (Revelation 19:17-18). This is Ezekiel's summons word for word — the prophet's vision of the fall of Gog, when the fowls and beasts are called to the sacrificial feast. *And, thou son of Adam, thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice... that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood* (Ezekiel 39:17). The fare is the same: *ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth* (Ezekiel 39:18) — the flesh of kings and captains and mighty men of the rider's supper. And the table is the same: *thus ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD)* (Ezekiel 39:20) — *the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men* (Revelation 19:18). The armies gathered *to make war against him that sat on the horse* (Revelation 19:19) become the feast at Yahuah's (LORD's) table, exactly as Ezekiel foresaw the end of Gog. The great supper of judgment is the prophet's own sacrifice come at last.

threads.title: The sea beast and the false prophet cast into the lake of fire before the reign (Daniel 7)
threads.summary_md: *And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone* (Revelation 19:20). The beast taken here is the beast out of the sea (Revelation 13:1), and the false prophet with him is the beast out of the earth (Revelation 13:11) — both cast alive into the lake before the reign begins. Daniel saw the like in his own vision: *I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame* (Daniel 7:11). Daniel's beast, whose little horn had *eyes like the eyes of man, and a mouth speaking great things* (Daniel 7:8), is slain and given to the burning flame — a witness to the same kind of end, not the key that decides who Revelation's beasts are. The sea beast and the false prophet who deceived by miracles are cast into the lake of fire burning with brimstone, while *the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth* (Revelation 19:21). The word of the rider does what no horn's great words could withstand; the proud mouths are silenced, and the two beasts are in the lake before the thousand years begin.

threads.title: The dragon, that old serpent, bound a thousand years and shut in the pit (Isaiah 24, Genesis 3)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years* (Revelation 20:1-2). The seer names the enemy by the oldest name in the book — *that old serpent* — and the whole library answers. He is the serpent of the garden: *Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had made* (Genesis 3:1), the one over whom the first promise was spoken — *I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel* (Genesis 3:15). The binding is that head-bruising worked out to its consummation. Isaiah saw its very shape: *Yahuah (LORD) shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high... And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited* (Isaiah 24:21-22) — the pit, the prison, the shutting-up, and the after-many-days visitation that the seer re-speaks: *And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up... till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season* (Revelation 20:3). He is the leviathan no man could chain — *Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?... wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?* (Job 41:1,5) — laid hold of and bound by the hand sent down from the throne. The Hebrew library carries the same architecture: the rebel powers *bind them fast... in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement* (1 Enoch 10:12), *led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13) — the binding that reserves the prisoner unto judgment, then the torment for ever, the two stages the seer names in the chaining and then the lake of fire. And the four names stacked here are the four stacked earlier when he was cast down: *the great dragon... that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world* (Revelation 12:9). The casting-down and the binding are two strokes against one adversary — the deceiver of the whole world brought at last to his chain.

threads.title: The thrones of judgment and the first resurrection (Daniel 7, Ezekiel 37, Isaiah 26)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them... and they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years... This is the first resurrection* (Revelation 20:4-5). Daniel saw the like: *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit... his throne was like the fiery flame* (Daniel 7:9), and the verdict Daniel was shown is the verdict here — *judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom* (Daniel 7:22). The ones who refused the mark of the beast out of the sea are the ones now on the thrones; as Daniel was shown the saints possessing the kingdom, so John sees them reign the thousand years — Daniel a witness, Revelation speaking for itself. And the raising of the slain is Ezekiel's valley stood up alive: *the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army* (Ezekiel 37:10), for Yahuah (LORD) had sworn, *Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves* (Ezekiel 37:12). It is the hope Isaiah sang plainest: *Thy dead men shall live... Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust... and the earth shall cast out the dead* (Isaiah 26:19). The Hebrew library names the great restoring that waits beyond the thousand years: *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her... and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them* (2 Esdras 7:32) — the earth giving back all her sleepers for the judgment, against which the first resurrection stands out as the early exception, the righteous seed raised first to reign. And it comes in ranks, as Paul taught: *every man in his own order: Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ's) at his coming* (1 Corinthians 15:23) — the first resurrection of the slain who reign, and then *the rest of the dead* who *lived not again until the thousand years were finished* (Revelation 20:5). The thrones set, the graves opened, the dust awakened — the slain of the witness raised to reign.

threads.title: Priests of Elohim (God) — the blessed and holy who reign (Exodus 19, Isaiah 61)
threads.summary_md: *Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of Elohim (God) and of Messiah (Christ), and shall reign with him a thousand years* (Revelation 20:6). The reign of the saints is a priesthood, and the priesthood is the word spoken at Sinai over the gathered people: *And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 19:6). The *blessed and holy* are that holy nation come into its calling — the kingdom of priests Sinai named, now reigning. Isaiah carried the same promise forward to the comforted of Zion: *But ye shall be named the Priests of Yahuah (LORD): men shall call you the Ministers of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 61:6) — the priestly office the restored seed bear. So those in the first resurrection, over whom *the second death hath no power,* are priests of Elohim (God) and of Messiah (Christ): not a disembodied heaven, but the gathered seed brought into the priesthood promised at the mountain and renewed by the prophet, reigning with him.

threads.title: Gog and Magog gathered, the number as the sand of the sea (Ezekiel 38, Genesis 22)
threads.summary_md: *And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea* (Revelation 20:7-8). The names are Ezekiel's own. The prophet was sent against them: *Son of Adam, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him* (Ezekiel 38:2); and he set the war in the latter days, the great host coming up *against my people of Yashar'el (Israel), as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days* (Ezekiel 38:16) — the very muster the seer sees go up *on the breadth of the earth* to compass *the camp of the saints... and the beloved city* (Revelation 20:9). Ezekiel's second oracle declares the One who stands against the host: *Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal* (Ezekiel 39:1). And the seer measures the deceived against the covenant promise itself: Abraham's seed was promised *as the sand which is upon the sea shore* (Genesis 22:17) — the blessing-number of the people of Yahuah (LORD); here that number is turned to name the enemy, *the number of whom is as the sand of the sea,* the uncountable muster of the deceived who compass the beloved city. The promise-number that counted the blessed counts the nations gathered to battle — and they are devoured.

threads.title: Fire came down from Elohim (God) out of heaven and devoured them (Ezekiel 38, 2 Kings 1, Genesis 19)
threads.summary_md: *And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, and devoured them* (Revelation 20:9). The fire that ends the Gog war is the prophet's fire. Ezekiel heard Yahuah (LORD) say of Gog's host, *I will rain upon him, and upon his bands... great hailstones, fire, and brimstone* (Ezekiel 38:22), and again, *I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am Yahuah (LORD)* (Ezekiel 39:6). The seer's fire from heaven upon Gog and Magog is the prophet's fire and brimstone upon the same gathered enemy. It is the fire that defended the man of Elohim (God) on the hill: *If I be a man of Elohim (God), then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty* (2 Kings 1:10). And it is the oldest fire-judgment in the canon, Sodom: *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven* (Genesis 19:24). The brimstone-and-fire that overthrew the cities of the plain, the fire that defended Elijah, the fire on Magog the prophet announced — all are the one fire from heaven that devours the last muster of the enemies of the people of Yahuah (LORD) about the beloved city.

threads.title: The great white throne; the earth and the heaven fled away (Daniel 2, Psalm 102, Isaiah 51)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them* (Revelation 20:11). The fleeing of earth and heaven re-speaks three Tanakh witnesses at once. When Daniel's great image was struck, the kingdoms of man were carried away *that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth* (Daniel 2:35) — the same *no place was found for them* the seer says of the old earth and heaven, while the stone-kingdom remains. The psalm sets the perishing of the heavens against the enduring of the One who sits: *all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed* (Psalm 102:26), for *thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end* (Psalm 102:27). And Isaiah saw the same: *the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment... but my salvation shall be for ever* (Isaiah 51:6). The garment-heavens pass and the aging earth flees; what abides before the great white throne is *him that sat on it* and his everlasting salvation. And this throne is no fresh and separate reckoning laid in sequence after a thousand-year box counted off on a chart; it is the same judgment the seventh trumpet already sounded — *the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints... and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth* (Revelation 11:18). Two panels, one judgment: the trumpet of chapter eleven names it, the throne of chapter twenty shows it again with the Judge in the foreground, that no eye should miss it. The Revelation does not run as a chain of separate end-events strung one after another, nor is its thousand years a stopwatch ticked off on a chart; it tells the one end from many faces, the appointed reign under symbolic measure, the same close shown and shown again until the destination is named. The earth and heaven flee; the One on the throne endures, and the dead stand before him — the one judgment of the souls of the dead toward which the whole book has been moving.

threads.title: The books were opened, and the book of life (Daniel 7 and 12, Malachi 3)
threads.summary_md: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). Daniel saw the like: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). This is the one reckoning of the dead the seventh trumpet already sounded, *the time of the dead, that they should be judged* (Revelation 11:18), shown here again in full. Daniel was told deliverance comes to *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1), and that *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2), the very division that falls at the throne, some found written in the book of life and some cast into the lake of fire. The book of the living the psalmist knew can be blotted out, *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28); names are written and never added, but they can be blotted. Malachi names the same record kept for the faithful: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). And the works are recorded and repaid, as Isaiah heard: *Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense* (Isaiah 65:6). Enoch saw the scene itself, twice. *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). And the book of life is named already in the Apocalypse: *the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world* (Revelation 13:8), the names written before the world was. The books of works and the book of life are opened together, and *And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.* (Revelation 20:15).

threads.title: Death and hell cast into the lake of fire — the second death (Hosea 13, Isaiah 25)
threads.summary_md: *And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death* (Revelation 20:14). Death and the grave that swallowed the dead are themselves swallowed up. Hosea heard Yahuah (LORD) speak death and the grave under judgment: *I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction* (Hosea 13:14). And Isaiah promised death itself undone on the mountain: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces* (Isaiah 25:8). Paul gathered both into one shout, naming the saying brought to pass at the resurrection: *then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory* (1 Corinthians 15:54), and the taunt over the beaten enemy — *O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?* (1 Corinthians 15:55), echoing Hosea's own *O death... O grave.* The bringing-to-pass is here at the throne: the sea and *death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them* (Revelation 20:13), and then death and hell themselves are cast into the lake of fire. The destruction Hosea pronounced over the grave, the victory Isaiah sang over death, the sting drawn that Paul looked for — all are this: death itself destroyed, the second death.

threads.title: A new heaven and a new earth — the renewing of creation Yahuah (LORD) promised (Isaiah 65)
threads.summary_md: John's opening vision is not a novelty but the keeping of an old promise: *And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea* (Revelation 21:1). This is the word Yahuah (LORD) spoke through Isaiah: *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind* (Isaiah 65:17). And Isaiah bound that new creation to the permanence of the covenant seed — *as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), so shall your seed and your name remain* (Isaiah 66:22): the enduring home of an enduring people, the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) not erased but kept. So the One on the throne declares, *Behold, I make all things new* (Revelation 21:5), the same *new thing* Isaiah heard — *Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert* (Isaiah 43:19) — the regathering and renewing flowering at last into the making-new of all things. *Write: for these words are true and faithful* (Revelation 21:5). The former things pass not because Yahuah (LORD) abandons the earth he formed, but because the Maker makes it new; the new heaven and new earth come down to a restored creation, the consummation of the promise, not an escape from it, and a people kept to dwell in it.

threads.title: The holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down as a bride adorned — Zion restored to her husband (Isaiah 52)
threads.summary_md: *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband* (Revelation 21:2). Every word is Isaiah's. The *holy city* is the one Isaiah called to wake: *Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean* (Isaiah 52:1) — and at the chapter's end that purity holds, *there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth* (Revelation 21:27). The *bride adorned* is the bride Isaiah sang: *he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness... as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels* (Isaiah 61:10). And the marriage was named long before: *thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 54:5). So when the angel says *Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife* (Revelation 21:9) and shows John *that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from Elohim (God)* (Revelation 21:10), the bride and the city are one: the forsaken wife of Isaiah 54, gathered with great mercies, restored to her husband. The Hebrew library prayed for this very descent from exile — *praise the everlasting King, that his tabernacle may be builded in you again with joy, and let him make joyful there in you those that are captives* (Tobit 13:10). The new Jerusalem is Yashar'el (Israel) restored to her Elohim (God), the covenant union consummated — not a new people put in her place.

threads.title: The tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men — the covenant promise consummated, the eternal Sukkot (Ezekiel 37)
threads.summary_md: This is the heart of the chapter, and it is quoted, almost word for word, out of the Tanakh. *And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and Elohim (God) himself shall be with them, and be their Elohim (God)* (Revelation 21:3). Ezekiel had already spoken it over the regathered house: *My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Ezekiel 37:27) — the everlasting covenant of peace set in the midst of his people for evermore. And it runs back further still, to the dwelling-promise of Sinai: *And I will set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you* (Leviticus 26:11), *And I will walk among you, and will be your Elohim (God), and ye shall be my people* (Leviticus 26:12). The same refrain sounds in Zechariah — *Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Zechariah 2:10), and *many nations shall be joined to Yahuah (LORD) in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee* (Zechariah 2:11) — the scattered seed gathered home from among the nations, and Yahuah (LORD) dwelling in their midst. It was the whole purpose of the first tabernacle: *And I will dwell among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and will be their Elohim (God)* (Exodus 29:45). The covenant promise — *I will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* — spoken at Sinai, repeated through every prophet, is here sealed for ever: Elohim (God) tabernacling with man, the eternal Sukkot, the dwelling that shall never be struck. The new Jerusalem is not a flight from earth to a disembodied heaven; it is Elohim (God) come DOWN to dwell with his people, the consummation of the whole covenant story.

threads.title: Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears, and there shall be no more death — the fountain of life freely (Isaiah 25)
threads.summary_md: *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4). John is quoting Isaiah's promise as accomplished fact: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it* (Isaiah 25:8). What Yahuah (LORD) pledged — to swallow up death and wipe every tear — is done in the new Jerusalem: death undone, sorrow gone, the rebuke of his people lifted for ever. Then the One on the throne renews Isaiah's open invitation: *It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely* (Revelation 21:6) — the very call of *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price* (Isaiah 55:1). The first and the last, who swallowed up death, gives the water of life without price to all who thirst and come home.

threads.title: He that overcometh shall inherit all things — I will be his Elohim (God), and he shall be my son (2 Samuel 7)
threads.summary_md: *He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his Elohim (God), and he shall be my son* (Revelation 21:7). The promise once sworn to one — David's seed — is opened to all who overcome. Yahuah (LORD) had said through Nathan, *I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men* (2 Samuel 7:14). That Davidic sonship, the everlasting throne established in David's house, widens in the new Jerusalem to the whole gathered covenant people: every overcomer made son, heir of all things, brought into the inheritance of the kingdom that has no end. *I will be his Elohim (God), and he shall be my son* — the covenant refrain in its most intimate form, the people who are his made not servants only but sons of the living Elohim (God).

threads.title: Twelve gates of the twelve tribes, twelve foundations of the twelve apostles — the one covenant people (Ezekiel 48)
threads.summary_md: The new Jerusalem is built of Yashar'el (Israel) and the apostles together — the one covenant people, the gathered seed come home. *And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Revelation 21:12); *And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb* (Revelation 21:14). The gates are Ezekiel's gates: *And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel): three gates northward; one gate of Reuben, one gate of Yahudah (Judah), one gate of Levi* (Ezekiel 48:31) — the tribes named one by one, three to each quarter, the very doors of the eternal city. And those twelve tribes are the two houses made one at last, for Ezekiel had seen Yahuah (LORD) take *the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) his fellows... even with the stick of Yahudah (Judah), and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand* (Ezekiel 37:19) — the northern house and the southern house, Ephraim and Yahudah (Judah), no more two nations but one. Ezekiel's tribal city ended with its name: *the name of the city from that day shall be, Yahuah Shammah (The LORD is there)* (Ezekiel 48:35) — and John shows why the name fits, for within this city *Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it* (Revelation 21:22). The tribes on the gates and the apostles on the foundations are not two peoples but one: Yashar'el (Israel) is not replaced by the city of Elohim (God) — her tribes are its gates, the apostles its foundations, the whole scattered seed regathered and the One who is there dwelling in the midst of them for ever.

threads.title: The city of pure gold and precious stones — the afflicted city rebuilt in gems (Isaiah 54, Tobit 13)
threads.summary_md: The jewelled city John describes is the city Yahuah (LORD) promised the storm-tossed, forsaken wife. *And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass* (Revelation 21:18); *And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones* — sapphire, emerald, beryl, and the rest (Revelation 21:19); *And the twelve gates were twelve pearls... and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass* (Revelation 21:21). This is Isaiah's comfort made fabric: *O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires* (Isaiah 54:11), *And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones* (Isaiah 54:12). The once-afflicted city is rebuilt in jewels. And the Hebrew library carried the same vision: Tobit, praying in captivity, foresaw *Jerusalem shall be built up with sapphires and emeralds, and precious stone: your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold* (Tobit 13:16), and even *the streets of Jerusalem shall be paved with beryl and carbuncle and stones of Ophir* (Tobit 13:17). The new Jerusalem John beholds is the city the prophets promised and the captives longed for — built at last in the splendour they were given to see, gold and gemstone, the work of Yahuah (LORD)'s own hand.

threads.title: No temple, no sun — Yahuah (LORD) and the Lamb the temple, the glory of Elohim (God) the light (Isaiah 60)
threads.summary_md: In the new Jerusalem the dwelling-place and the light-bearer are one and the same — Elohim (God) himself. *And I saw no temple therein: for Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it* (Revelation 21:22); *And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of Elohim (God) did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof* (Revelation 21:23). This is Isaiah's promise: *The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but Yahuah (LORD) shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy Elohim (God) thy glory* (Isaiah 60:19) — and here the One on the throne and the Lamb (the Father and the Formed Son) are together the temple and the light, the glory of Elohim (God) lightening the city and the Lamb its lamp. Then the nations walk in its light — the tribes, the company of nations promised to Jacob, *a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee* (Genesis 35:11) — as Isaiah saw: *the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it* (Revelation 21:24), fulfilling *the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising* (Isaiah 60:3); and the gates stand open as Isaiah promised — *Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought* (Isaiah 60:11) — for in the city *the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there* (Revelation 21:25). The Hebrew library knew this hidden city would one day appear: *the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth* (2 Esdras 7:26). She is shown at last — the holy Jerusalem revealed, lit by the glory of Elohim (God), her gates never shut, into which nothing unclean enters, *but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life* (Revelation 21:27).

threads.title: A pure river of water of life proceeding out of the throne (Ezekiel 47, Zechariah 14, Genesis 2)
threads.summary_md: The last vision opens with a river: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb* (Revelation 22:1). It is the oldest river in scripture come home. *A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads* (Genesis 2:10) — the garden-river lost when the man was driven out, now flowing again from the throne. It is Ezekiel's temple-river brought to its source: there *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward* (Ezekiel 47:1), and wherever they ran they gave life — *every thing shall live whither the river cometh* (Ezekiel 47:9). The seer names outright what Ezekiel saw it do: this is *water of life.* It is Zechariah's promise at its fountainhead — *living waters shall go out from Jerusalem... in summer and in winter shall it be* (Zechariah 14:8) — the unceasing stream of the restored city traced to the seat from which it pours. And it is the keeping of a word already spoken in the book: *the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters* (Revelation 7:17). The Lamb who leads the gathered to the fountains is the Lamb from whose throne the fountain flows. On the throne sit *him that sat on the throne* and the Lamb together (Revelation 22:1,3) — the Father and the Formed Son distinguished, the One from whom the water of life has always come, now giving it freely to all who thirst (Revelation 22:17).

threads.title: The tree of life, and the leaves for the healing of the nations — Eden restored (Genesis 2, Ezekiel 47, 1 Enoch 24–25, 2 Esdras 8)
threads.summary_md: The story closes where it opened, in a garden, but the garden has become a city, and the tree once guarded stands open in the street: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). This is the very tree of Eden, *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9). It stood in the midst of the garden at the first; it stands in the midst of the street at the last. After the fall the way to it was shut: *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and *Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way* were set *to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Now the guard is withdrawn and the tree is given back to the obedient (Revelation 22:14). It is Ezekiel's river-tree fulfilled, the trees by the temple-waters that bore *new fruit according to his months,* whose *fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12); the monthly fruit and the healing leaf are John's twelve manner of fruits and leaves for the healing of the nations. Enoch saw this tree and could not stop looking at it: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). He was told when it would be eaten and where it would stand: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). John is looking at the transplanting done, the tree kept till the great judgment now standing in the holy city for the righteous to eat. And 2 Esdras names the whole vision in one breath: *to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted... a city is builded* (2 Esdras 8:52), one hope and not three, Eden become the new Jerusalem. So the promise sworn at the book's opening is kept at its close: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7). The paradise of Elohim (God) is Eden restored; the overcomer eats of the tree at last, and its leaves heal the nations.

threads.title: And there shall be no more curse — the Edenic undoing (Zechariah 14, Genesis 3, 2 Esdras 8)
threads.summary_md: One short clause closes the wound the whole of scripture has carried since the third chapter of Genesis: *And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him* (Revelation 22:3). The curse fell on the ground for Adam's sake — *cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life* (Genesis 3:17). It is undone at the last. Zechariah saw the lifting of it over the restored city: *there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited* (Zechariah 14:11) — the very word for the curse of devotion-to-destruction now spoken away, the city never again given to ruin. The restored library names the same undoing from the inside: *the root of evil is sealed up from you... and corruption is fled into hell to be forgotten* (2 Esdras 8:53), and *Sorrows are passed, and in the end is shewed the treasure of immortality* (2 Esdras 8:54). The curse was the fruit of the root of evil; with the root sealed away and corruption fled, what remains is the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb, the servants serving him with the sorrow of the cursed ground forever behind them, reigning *for ever and ever* (Revelation 22:5). Eden's loss is reversed: the river returns, the tree stands open, and the curse is no more.

threads.title: They shall see his face, and his name in their foreheads (Exodus 33, Psalm 17, Numbers 6)
threads.summary_md: *And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads* (Revelation 22:4). What was denied to Moses is granted to the servants. To the one who sought the glory the word came: *Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live* (Exodus 33:20). That barrier is taken away in the restored city — the face no man could see and live is now seen by those who live for ever. David's hope is fulfilled: *I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness* (Psalm 17:15) — the waking from the dust into the open sight of Elohim (God). And both halves of the priestly blessing stand complete: *Yahuah (LORD) make his face shine upon thee* (Numbers 6:25), and *they shall put my name upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and I will bless them* (Numbers 6:27). The shining face the priests invoked is now beheld; the name laid upon the people is now written on their foreheads. That name on the forehead is the seal already set in the seventh chapter — *till we have sealed the servants of our Elohim (God) in their foreheads* (Revelation 7:3) — the mark of the living Elohim (God) set on the servants before the winds of the Day were loosed, before the sifting, the counter-sign to the mark of the beast, now seen for what it always was: the name of the One they serve, worn before the face they see.

threads.title: No night, no sun; Yahuah giveth them light, and they reign for ever (Isaiah 60, Daniel 7)
threads.summary_md: *And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever* (Revelation 22:5). Isaiah promised the restored Zion a light that is not the sun: *The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but Yahuah (LORD) shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy Elohim (God) thy glory* (Isaiah 60:19). The everlasting light is Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) himself giving light to the city — no created lamp needed where the glory of the Maker shines, as the new Jerusalem was already shown to have no need of the sun, *for the glory of Elohim (God) did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof* (Revelation 21:23), and *there shall be no night there* (Revelation 21:25). The city-vision and the garden-vision are one restored creation, lit by one light. And the reign is Daniel's vision fulfilled: *the saints of the El Elyon (most High) shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever* (Daniel 7:18), the kingdom *given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom* (Daniel 7:27). The everlasting kingdom given to the saints after the beasts are judged is the unending reign of the servants in the city of light — the same *for ever and ever,* the kingdom that shall not pass away now held by those who keep the commandments of Elohim (God).

threads.title: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last; the root and offspring of David, the morning star (Isaiah 44, Isaiah 11, Numbers 24)
threads.summary_md: The One on the throne names himself, and the names are the names of Yahuah (LORD) and of the Davidic King at once: *I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last* (Revelation 22:13), and *I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star* (Revelation 22:16). The first title is Isaiah's self-naming of Yahuah (LORD): *I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 44:6) — the redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) speaking. The Formed who speaks in the Revelation bears that divine name; the first-and-last of Isaiah and the Alpha-and-Omega of the closing vision are one — Yahusha (Jesus), the Formed drawn from the Formless, who has a Father and yet speaks in the name above every name. The second title is Isaiah's Branch: *there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots* (Isaiah 11:1), *a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek* (Isaiah 11:10). He is both root and offspring — the source from which David's line grew and the heir that grew from it, the root of Jesse lifted as the ensign for the regathering of the scattered. And he is Balaam's far-off star come near: *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 24:17) — *the bright and morning star* that announces the day. The first and the last who is also the root of David and the Star out of Jacob is the slain-yet-reigning Lamb, the Formed who shares the throne and to whom the angel will not let worship be given but says *worship Elohim* (Revelation 22:9): worship belongs to the One.

threads.title: Blessed are they that do his commandments — the tree-of-life crown (Deuteronomy 30, Malachi 4, Psalm 1, Genesis 3)
threads.summary_md: The book sets its last and highest blessing on the doers of the commandments: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). This is the third great keep-the-commandments verse of the Revelation, joined to the two before it — *the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of Elohim (God), and have the testimony of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (Revelation 12:17), and *here are they that keep the commandments of Elohim (God), and the faith of Yahusha (Jesus)* (Revelation 14:12). Three times over the saints are named by the commandments; the third naming is their crown. Moses bound the keeping of the commandments to life itself: *to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply* (Deuteronomy 30:16) — and the word is no burden, *the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it* (Deuteronomy 30:14). The last word of the prophets before the great and dreadful day was the same: *Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Yashar'el (Israel), with the statutes and judgments* (Malachi 4:4). And the first psalm drew the very figure of the tree: the blessed man whose *delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD)* is *like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither* (Psalm 1:2-3) — the man whose delight is the Torah, planted by the rivers, given right at the last to the tree of life standing by the pure river of water of life, his unwithering leaf become the leaf for the healing of the nations. The way to that tree was barred against the disobedient by *a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24); now *right* to it is given to *they that do his commandments,* and the restored library names the gift in full — *to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted... a city is builded* (2 Esdras 8:52). The disobedience that lost the tree is answered by the commandment-keeping that regains it. This is no Torah abolished and no flesh-credential earned, but the door home and the standing standard held together as one love: the commandments kept are the way back to the tree of life, and the doers of his word enter in through the gates into the city.

threads.title: The Spirit and the bride say, Come; and the warning not to add or take away (Isaiah 55, Deuteronomy 4, Proverbs 30)
threads.summary_md: The book ends with an open invitation and a sealed word. The invitation: *And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely* (Revelation 22:17). It is Isaiah's great call taken up at the close: *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat... without money and without price* (Isaiah 55:1). The free water of Isaiah is the water of life of the river from the throne (Revelation 22:1); the thirsting summoned to the waters without price are the same thirsting bidden to take the water of life freely. And the sealed word: *If any man shall add unto these things, Elohim (God) shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book* (Revelation 22:18), and *if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, Elohim (God) shall take away his part out of the book of life* (Revelation 22:19). This is the guard Moses set over the Torah: *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* (Deuteronomy 4:2), and again *What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it* (Deuteronomy 12:32). The wisdom of Agur said the same over every word of Elohim (God): *Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar* (Proverbs 30:6), for *every word of Elohim (God) is pure* (Proverbs 30:5). The words of the prophecy are kept whole as the commandments were kept whole — come freely to the water of life, and neither add to nor diminish the pure word of the One who gives it.

threads.title: The foolishness of the cross and the wisdom of Elohim (God) (Isaiah 29)
threads.summary_md: Paul sets the cross against the wisdom of the world: *the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of Elohim (God)* (1 Corinthians 1:18). And he grounds the overthrow of the world's wisdom in the prophet: *For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent* (1 Corinthians 1:19) — a verbatim citation of Yahuah (LORD)'s word in Isaiah, *I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid* (Isaiah 29:14). The destroying of the wise is no novelty of the gospel; it is the promised marvellous work of Yahuah (LORD), now accomplished in the crucified Messiah. Isaiah had named the fault of that wisdom — *their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men* (Isaiah 29:13) — and so Paul mocks it: *Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? hath not Elohim (God) made foolish the wisdom of this world?* (1 Corinthians 1:20), taking up the prophet's own taunt, *Where is the scribe? where is the receiver?* (Isaiah 33:18). The world by wisdom does not reach Elohim (God); but to the called the cross is *Messiah (Christ) the power of Elohim (God), and the wisdom of Elohim (God)* (1 Corinthians 1:24), for *the foolishness of Elohim (God) is wiser than men; and the weakness of Elohim (God) is stronger than men* (1 Corinthians 1:25). The Hebrew library had already taught where the true wisdom lies: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Sirach 1:1); *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom* (Sirach 1:14); *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). Wisdom is no flesh-credential seized by the disputer but the gift of the Father — and it is made ours in the Formed Messiah, *who of Elohim (God) is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption* (1 Corinthians 1:30). What the world calls foolish, the cross and the fear of Yahuah (LORD), is the only true wisdom.

threads.title: The world by wisdom knew not Elohim (God) — the ungodly blinded (Wisdom of Solomon 2)
threads.summary_md: *For after that in the wisdom of Elohim (God) the world by wisdom knew not Elohim (God), it pleased Elohim (God) by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe* (1 Corinthians 1:21). The world's own wisdom does not arrive at Elohim (God) — and the Hebrew library had already diagnosed exactly why. The ungodly reason *with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:1), and so they say, *let us crown ourselves with rosebuds, before they be withered* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:8). To such reasoning the cross — death undone, the One who did return from the grave — is folly: *the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of Elohim (God)* (1 Corinthians 1:18). The library names the root of this false wisdom: *Such things they did imagine, and were deceived: for their own wickedness has blinded them* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:21) — their cleverness is blindness, which is why Paul asks, *hath not Elohim (God) made foolish the wisdom of this world?* (1 Corinthians 1:20). And it names the end of it: *As for the mysteries of Yahuah (God), they knew them not* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:22) — the very thing Paul says, that the world by wisdom *knew not Elohim (God).* The knowing of Elohim (God) does not come by the disputer's wisdom, self-blinded by its own wickedness, but by the foolishness of the preached cross, the power of Elohim (God) to them that are saved.

threads.title: That no flesh should glory — let him glory in Yahuah (LORD) (Jeremiah 9)
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes on the boast that is excluded and the only boast that remains. Elohim (God) chose *the foolish things of the world to confound the wise... and base things of the world, and things which are despised* (1 Corinthians 1:27-28), *That no flesh should glory in his presence* (1 Corinthians 1:29). The calling itself passes over the flesh-credentials: *ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called* (1 Corinthians 1:26). This is the very three-fold boast Yahuah (LORD) forbade through Jeremiah: *Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches* (Jeremiah 9:23) — wisdom, might, riches, the standing of the flesh, all shut out of glorying before Elohim (God). And Paul ends with the one boast that is left, citing the prophet directly: *That, according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in Yahuah (Lord)* (1 Corinthians 1:31), from *let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am Yahuah (LORD) which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth* (Jeremiah 9:24). The boast excluded is the flesh-credential — wisdom, status, party-loyalty (*I am of Paul... of Apollos*); the boast permitted is the knowing of Yahuah (LORD) himself, who delights in lovingkindness and judgment and righteousness. The whole glory is in him, that no flesh should boast in his presence.

threads.title: The hidden wisdom ordained before the world, which the princes knew not (Wisdom of Solomon 9, Sirach 1)
threads.summary_md: Paul speaks a wisdom that is not of this age: *we speak the wisdom of Elohim (God) in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which Elohim (God) ordained before the world unto our glory: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified Yahuah (Lord) of glory* (1 Corinthians 2:7-8). The Hebrew library had already framed this exact mystery.
