From the ground itself Yahuah (LORD) had already said, *the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground* (Genesis 4:10), and that cry did not stop when Abel died. It went up as a suit for justice and it is still being heard. Hebrews knows that crying blood and sets a better word against it, for the new covenant brings *the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel* (Hebrews 12:24). And Abel does not cry alone. Under the altar the slain make the same suit: *the souls of them that were slain for the word of Elohim (God)... cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Yahuah (Lord), holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?* (Revelation 6:9-10). The blood of the righteous is kept in remembrance, and it pleads from the holding-place until the great day answers it.

threads.title: The bright spring for the righteous, the sinners set apart
threads.summary_md: The hollows are not one undivided pit. They are sorted by the way each one walked: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9), and another hollow is kept for those who died with their account unsettled: *And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.* (1 Enoch 22:10), *Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.* (1 Enoch 22:11). Abraham draws the same line for the rich man: *Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented* (Luke 16:25). The righteous are comforted at the spring and the sinner is in pain, and what divides them is the way each one kept. And the earth itself has swallowed the rebel living before — when Korah's company *go down quick into the pit* (Numbers 16:30), they *went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation* (Numbers 16:33). The division is not arbitrary. It follows the covenant. The righteous who kept the way are held at the bright spring, the transgressors are set apart in pain, and all of them alike are waiting for the great day of judgement.

threads.title: The fire that runs without resting — the fire in the west that drives the luminaries
threads.summary_md: At the western ends of the earth Enoch sees a fire that never stops: *And I saw a burning fire which ran without resting, and paused not from its course day or night but (ran) regularly.* (1 Enoch 23:2). He asks what it is, and Raguel tells him: *Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said unto me: ‘This course of fire which thou hast seen is the fire in the west which persecutes all the luminaries of heaven.’* (1 Enoch 23:4). The fire that drives the lights of heaven on their courses is no strange revelation. The canon's sun is driven the same way. Psalm 19 sees the same untiring runner: *In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun,* (Psalms 19:4), *Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.* (Psalms 19:5), *His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.* (Psalms 19:6), the very circuit to the ends of the earth that Enoch is shown. Psalm 104 says the flame is a servant of Yahuah (God), who *maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:* (Psalms 104:4) and who *appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalms 104:19). The fire does not burn loose. It runs an appointed course and it presses the luminaries to run theirs, and the sun has never once left that course. The Watchers did.

threads.title: The six portals and the chariots of the sun, moon, and stars
threads.summary_md: The fire Enoch sees at the western ends of the earth is the fire that keeps the lights of heaven moving: *Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said unto me: ‘This course of fire which thou hast seen is the fire in the west which persecutes all the luminaries of heaven.’* (1 Enoch 23:4). The book of the luminaries later shows the machinery those lights are driven through. They have gates: *And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets: and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals.* (1 Enoch 72:3). They have chariots: *The chariot on which he ascends, the wind drives, and the sun goes down from the heaven and returns through the north in order to reach the east, and is so guided that he comes to the appropriate (lit. ‘that’) portal and shines in the face of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:5), *And I saw chariots in the heaven, running in the world, above those portals in which revolve the stars that never set.* (1 Enoch 75:8). And every one of them has a keeper: *For the signs and the times and the years and the days the angel Uriel showed to me, whom Yahuah (Lord) of glory hath set for ever over all the luminaries of the heaven, in the heaven and in the world, that they should rule on the face of the heaven and be seen on the earth, and be leaders for the day and the night, i.e. the sun, moon, and stars, and all the ministering creatures which make their revolution in all the chariots of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 75:3). The portals and the chariots are the appointed gates and the appointed carriages through which the lights keep the laws Uriel showed Enoch, and the fire in the west is what will not let them rest.

threads.title: All the stars rise and set in their order — the decree that shall not pass
threads.summary_md: The fire that drives the luminaries drives them into order, and Enoch had opened his whole book on that order: *Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.* (1 Enoch 2:1). The book of the luminaries measures how exact that obedience is: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). This is the ordinance of the fourth day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). Psalm 148 commands these same obedient lights to praise, *Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.* (Psalms 148:3), and gives the reason they can be commanded at all: *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalms 148:6). Then Yahuah (God) ties that unbreakable order to the continuance of his people. He *giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night* (Jeremiah 31:35), and swears, *If those ordinances depart from before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), then the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.* (Jeremiah 31:36). Enoch turns the same comparison on his hearers: *And all His works go on thus from year to year for ever, and all the tasks which they accomplish for Him, and their tasks change not, but according as Elohim (God) hath ordained so is it done.* (1 Enoch 5:2), *But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), But ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words With your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.* (1 Enoch 5:4). The stars keeping their course is the standing pledge that the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) is never cast off, and the same stars are the standing rebuke to a people who will not keep theirs.

threads.title: The throne-mountain: the holy mountain of Elohim and the seat of the Eternal King
threads.summary_md: Enoch is led to seven magnificent mountains, and *And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne.* (1 Enoch 24:3) — and Michael unveils what it is: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). This is not a new picture. Daniel saw the same fiery seat — *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire* (Daniel 7:9). And the throne stands on the holy mountain that was Eden's first sanctuary: *thou wast upon the holy mountain of Elohim (God); thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire* (Ezekiel 28:14) — the same Eden-mountain whose covering was *every precious stone... the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created* (Ezekiel 28:13), matching the magnificent stones of Enoch's mountains. Jubilees names that very mountain among Yahuah's holy places: *For Yahuah (God) has four places on the earth, the Garden of Eden, and the Mount of the East, and this mountain on which you are this day, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion (which) will be sanctified in the new creation for a sanctification of the earth* (Jubilees 4:25). And Enoch had already glimpsed this throne-mountain on his journey: *But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Elohim (God), of alabaster, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire.* (1 Enoch 18:8). The mountain is the throne; the King who descends to it is the Creator returning to His holy place — Torah's order standing, not overturned.

threads.title: The fragrant tree of life: Eden's tree at the holy mountain
threads.summary_md: At the throne-mountain Enoch finds a tree unlike any other: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm* (1 Enoch 24:4). This is Eden's own tree, planted in the beginning: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil* (Genesis 2:9). Ezekiel saw it lining the river from the sanctuary, its undying leaf and unfailing fruit: *and by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed... and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12) — the leaves and wood that *wither not for ever.* The Spirit promises the overcomer this very tree at the end: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7); and John sees it standing in the restored city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations* (Revelation 22:2). The book of 2 Esdras names the same hope — *for to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared* (2 Esdras 8:52). One tree, from Eden's midst to the New Jerusalem; it ain't new.

threads.title: Reserved till the great judgement: the tree given to the righteous and elect
threads.summary_md: The tree is sealed until the reckoning: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). The same gate stands at the end of Scripture: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). The right to the tree belongs to those who *do his commandments*, so the Torah is still standing at the gate of the city, and the ones who keep it are the ones who were chosen, which is why they keep it. Isaiah measures the elect's portion by that same tree: *they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands* (Isaiah 65:22), the same fruit Enoch says is *for food to the elect*. And 2 Esdras describes its healing virtue laid up for the righteous: *they shall have the tree of life for an ointment of sweet savour; they shall neither labour, nor be weary* (2 Esdras 2:12), the very fragrance Enoch says will be in their bones. The tree is not for whoever reaches for it. It is given, after the judgement has separated, to a people who were chosen, the righteous and the elect, and it is carried into the holy place of Yahuah (God) where they will eat from it.

threads.title: Long life and no sorrow: the days of the fathers restored
threads.summary_md: Enoch closes with the blessing the tree secures for the elect: *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). The prophets sang the same end of sorrow: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it* (Isaiah 25:8). John saw it fulfilled in the restored creation: *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4), which is Enoch's *no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity* said again. And the curse that shortened the patriarchs' years is lifted at the throne where the tree stands: *And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him* (Revelation 22:3). The long life *such as thy fathers lived* is the span of the first fathers given back, and it is the same end the whole canon is waiting for.

threads.title: Intercede for men, not men for you — the Watchers' petition refused
threads.summary_md: Enoch is sent back to the fallen ones with a verdict, not a pardon: *And go, say to the Watchers of heaven, who have sent thee to intercede for them: "You should intercede for men, and not men for you:* (1 Enoch 15:2). The order of heaven is inverted when the guardians become the guilty — there is no mediator above them to plead their cause, for they kept not the order they were given. Jude carries this same sentence into the canon: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). Peter seals it the same way: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). The Watchers' sin is rebellion against the Creator's order, and the judgement is sure; the petition cannot stand.

threads.title: Left the holy heaven and lain with women — Genesis 6 named
threads.summary_md: The charge is laid out plainly: *Wherefore have ye left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons?* (1 Enoch 15:3); and again, *And though ye were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those also do who die and perish.* (1 Enoch 15:4). This is the canon's own Genesis 6 from the inside: *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose* (Genesis 6:2), and *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown* (Genesis 6:4). The Creator's own answer follows — *And Yahuah (LORD) said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years* (Genesis 6:3) — the same boundary on flesh that Enoch presses against the spiritual ones who lusted after it. It ain't new: the seed-war begins here.

threads.title: Prepared, created, and promised — Enoch blesses the Eternal King for what is laid up for the righteous
threads.summary_md: When Michael has finished telling Enoch what the tree is for, Enoch does the only thing left to do: *Then blessed I the Elohim (God) of Glory, the Eternal King, who hath prepared such things for the righteous, and hath created them and promised to give to them.* (1 Enoch 25:7). Three things are said in one breath, that the tree and the holy place were prepared, that they were created, and that they were promised. What was promised is what Michael had just described: *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5), *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). Isaiah blesses the same preparation in almost the same words: *For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O Elohim (God), beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him.* (Isaiah 64:4), and Paul carries Isaiah's line to the assembly: *But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which Elohim (God) hath prepared for them that love him.* (1 Corinthians 2:9). Yahusha (Jesus) says the preparing is his own work: *In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.* (John 14:2). And the tree itself is the one driven out of reach in the garden, *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24), and held out again at the end to the one who holds on: *He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). Enoch saw it already prepared, already created, and already promised, and he blessed the King who keeps his word.

threads.title: The middle of the earth and the holy mountain — Zion at the navel
threads.summary_md: Enoch is carried to the centre of the world: *And I went from thence to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place in which there were trees with branches abiding and blooming [of a dismembered tree].* (1 Enoch 26:1), *And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:2). The Tanakh sets Jerusalem in exactly that place, at the midst of the nations: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her.* (Ezekiel 5:5), and it names the regathered people as those *that dwell in the midst of the land.* (Ezekiel 38:12). The holy mountain is Zion, of whom the psalmist sings *Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.* (Psalm 48:2), the place where *Elohim (God) is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.* (Psalm 74:12). Jubilees says it most plainly of all: *And he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of Yahuah (God), and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion–the centre of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other.* (Jubilees 8:18). The blessed place at the middle of the earth with the holy mountain in it is Zion, and Enoch saw it before there was a city on it.

threads.title: The stream under the holy mountain, and the dry ravines where no tree is planted
threads.summary_md: Under the holy mountain a stream runs out to the east, and the land around it is cut by ravines: *And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:2), *And I saw towards the east another mountain higher than this, and between them a deep and narrow ravine: in it also ran a stream underneath the mountain.* (1 Enoch 26:3), *And to the west thereof there was another mountain, lower than the former and of small elevation, and a ravine deep and dry between them: and another deep and dry ravine was at the extremities of the three mountains.* (1 Enoch 26:4). Ezekiel is shown that same water coming out from under the holy mountain on the east side: *Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar.* (Ezekiel 47:1), and he sees what grows wherever it runs: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). John sees the source of it: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb.* (Revelation 22:1). Where that water runs, the trees abide and bloom, as Enoch saw at the blessed place. Where it does not, the ravines are deep and dry and *trees were not planted upon them* (1 Enoch 26:5). The man of the covenant is himself such a tree: *And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither* (Psalm 1:3). The righteous flourish where the living water of the sanctuary runs out from Zion, and nothing grows in the dry ravines beside it.

threads.title: The throne-mountain and the tree of life reserved for the great judgement
threads.summary_md: Michael unveils what the mountain and the tree truly are: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3), and of the fragrant tree: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is the tree of life of Eden, *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9) — guarded from mortal hands after the fall *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and restored at the end to the holy city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month* (Revelation 22:2), given to those who keep covenant — *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). The long life Enoch promises the elect, *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6), is Isaiah's restored Yashar'el (Israel), *for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands* (Isaiah 65:22), and John's new world where *there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain* (Revelation 21:4). The tree is withheld until the great judgement and then given to the elect, and every book that touches it says the same.

threads.title: The accursed valley beside the blessed land — where the hard-mouthed are gathered for judgement
threads.summary_md: Enoch has just seen the blessed land at the middle of the earth, and beside it something that does not fit: *Then said I: ‘For what object is this blessed land, which is entirely filled with trees, and this accursed valley between?’* (1 Enoch 27:1). Uriel tells him what the valley is for: *Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: ‘This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against Yahuah (Lord) unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.* (1 Enoch 27:2). The valley under the holy mountain is where the prophets put the judgement too. Joel hears Yahuah (God) say, *I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Yashar'el (Israel), whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.* (Joel 3:2), and again, *Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.* (Joel 3:12). Zechariah sees the ground itself opened for it: *And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south.* (Zechariah 14:4). The ones gathered there are named by what came out of their mouths, hard words against his glory, and Enoch had already said who those are: *But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), But ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words With your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.* (1 Enoch 5:4). The blessed land and the accursed valley sit side by side on purpose. The throne-mountain is where the Eternal King comes down, and the valley at its foot is where the ones who cursed him are gathered to meet him.

threads.title: The spectacle of judgement in the valley — the merciful bless the Eternal King for the lot he assigned
threads.summary_md: Uriel does not stop at the gathering. He tells Enoch what the valley becomes on the day: *In the last days there shall be upon them the spectacle of righteous judgement in the presence of the righteous for ever: here shall the merciful bless Yahuah (Lord) of glory, the Eternal King. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be the place of their habitation.* (1 Enoch 27:3), *In the days of judgement over the former, they shall bless Him for the mercy in accordance with which He has assigned them (their lot).’* (1 Enoch 27:4). Two companies stand in the same place and see the same thing, the accursed under judgement and the merciful blessing him for it. Isaiah ends his whole book on that scene: *And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.* (Isaiah 66:24). Yahusha (Jesus) takes Isaiah's words for the same valley: *And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:* (Mark 9:43), *Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.* (Mark 9:44). The hell he names there is this valley at the foot of Jerusalem, and the ones who look on are the righteous Isaiah and Enoch both saw. What Enoch does when he hears it is what the merciful will do when they see it: *Then I blessed Yahuah (Lord) of Glory and set forth His glory and lauded Him gloriously.* (1 Enoch 27:5). Judgement in the valley and blessing on the mountain are one day, and the ones who kept his word bless him for the lot he assigned.

threads.title: The elect enter the holy place — no sorrow, plague, or torment
threads.summary_md: When the tree is carried to the temple, Enoch is told what becomes of the righteous who eat of it: *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). The prophets give the elect that same homecoming. Isaiah sees the ransomed come back to the mountain with the sorrow gone out of them: *the ransomed of Yahuah (LORD) shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away* (Isaiah 35:10), and he says why: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces* (Isaiah 25:8). It is the servants who eat in that day, and the division is plain in the same breath: *Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry... behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed* (Isaiah 65:13). Those who enter the holy place and those shut out of it are two companies, and the Father is the one who knows which is which. John closes the library on the same scene Enoch opened, with nothing left to touch them: *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4).

threads.title: Water gushing in the desert — the wilderness made glad
threads.summary_md: Enoch goes east into the mountains of the desert and finds the dry place alive: *And thence I went towards the east, into the midst of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness and it was solitary, full of trees and plants. And water gushed forth from above. Rushing like a copious watercourse [which flowed] towards the north- west it caused clouds and dew to ascend on every side.* (1 Enoch 28:1-3). Farther on he comes to the valley itself: *And beyond these, I went afar to the east, and I saw another place, a valley (full) of water. And therein there was a tree, the colour (?) of fragrant trees such as the mastic.* (1 Enoch 30:1-2). This is the prophets' watered wilderness, the sign that Yahuah (LORD) has come to save His people: *The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.* (Isaiah 35:1), *for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.* (Isaiah 35:6). The same hand that opens the water also plants the fragrant trees Enoch walks among: *I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.* (Isaiah 41:18) — *I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the fir tree, and the pine, and the box tree together* (Isaiah 41:19), and the purpose is that all may *know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of Yahuah (LORD) hath done this, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel) hath created it.* (Isaiah 41:20). Enoch walks the renewed desert the prophets sing about, and he walks it before they sang.

threads.title: The tree no mortal may touch — the tree of life kept for the elect
threads.summary_md: Michael tells Enoch what the fragrant tree is for: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4) — *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). This is the tree of life of Eden, planted and then guarded: *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9), barred from fallen hands *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), so that Yahuah *placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24). Enoch sees the same tree kept until the great judgement and then given to the righteous, and that is the very promise the risen Messiah holds out to the assemblies: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7), and *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Notice who is given the fruit in both books. It is the commandment-keepers, the elect who keep the way, and never a class that chose itself. Ezekiel saw the same temple-fed fruit by the river from the sanctuary: *and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree fenced in Eden and opened again in Revelation is the tree Enoch already saw carried to the temple of the Eternal King.

threads.title: The mountain whose summit is like the throne — seen on the way, named at the tree
threads.summary_md: The throne-mountain is shown to Enoch before it is ever explained to him. On the earlier road he passes the seven mountains of stone and sees the middle one reach up: *But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Elohim (God), of alabaster, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire.* (1 Enoch 18:8). Then he comes to it again from the other side, and this time the tree stands in front of it: *And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne.* (1 Enoch 24:3). Only when he asks about the tree does Michael name the mountain: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). So the mountain Enoch saw twice is one mountain, the seat the King will take when He comes down, and the fragrant tree belongs to it. John is shown the same throne with the same tree beside it at the end of the library: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb.* (Revelation 22:1), *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). The throne, the tree, and the King who comes down to visit the earth are one vision, and it was carried whole from Enoch into the Apocalypse.

threads.title: The throne-mountain where the Eternal King comes down
threads.summary_md: Michael answers Enoch's wonder at the tree by first naming the mountain it grows on: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). The place of the throne is the place of the tree, and the King is coming down to it. Enoch had already seen that summit from the road, before the tree was in view: *And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne.* (1 Enoch 24:3). And the tree it keeps is the one set in Eden and then fenced from mortal hands: *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:* (Genesis 3:22). What Adam was barred from, the throne-mountain holds until the King comes down to visit the earth with goodness. The prophets put the same mountain at the centre of the last days: *And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD’S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.* (Isaiah 2:2). It ain't new. Enoch was shown the seat before Isaiah saw the house built on it.

threads.title: The tree of life kept until the great judgement, food for the elect
threads.summary_md: The fragrant tree is no ordinary tree, and Michael says so: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is Eden's own tree, the one Yahuah planted *pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9), and then sealed from mortal reach so that no man should *take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22). Enoch sees the same fruit given back to the elect at the end, and that is exactly the promise Yahusha (Jesus) makes to the overcomer: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). He shows it again standing in the City: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). Ezekiel saw it too, growing by the water that comes out from under the sanctuary: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree withheld since Eden is the tree given to the righteous after the judgement, and the holy place is where it is given.

threads.title: Transplanted to the temple: long life and no more sorrow
threads.summary_md: The tree's destiny is the sanctuary, and the destiny of the elect is life beside it: *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:5-6). This is the prophets' restored earth, where the days of the people are measured like the days of a tree: *They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands.* (Isaiah 65:22). The end of sorrow and plague and torment that Enoch names is the same comfort the prophets and the Revelation give: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it.* (Isaiah 25:8), unfolded at the end as *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* (Revelation 21:4). The right to enter the holy place and eat is kept for those who keep the way: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Enoch says the fathers lived such a life once; the prophets say the elect will live it again.

threads.title: The fragrant trees of the east — the chief spices
threads.summary_md: Past the valley of water Enoch walks through country that smells like the sanctuary: *And on the sides of those valleys I saw fragrant cinnamon. And beyond these I proceeded to the east.* (1 Enoch 30:3), then *And I saw other mountains, and amongst them were groves of trees, and there flowed forth from them nectar, which is named sarara and galbanum. And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain to the east of the ends of the earth, whereon were aloe-trees, and all the trees were full of stacte, being like almond-trees. And when one burnt it, it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour.* (1 Enoch 31:1-3), and north of these, *And after these fragrant odours, as I looked towards the north over the mountains I saw seven mountains full of choice nard and fragrant trees and cinnamon and pepper.* (1 Enoch 32:1). Cinnamon, nectar, galbanum, stacte, aloes, nard — these are the spices Yahuah (LORD) set apart for His own house. The incense of the holy place is compounded from the same list: *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight* (Exodus 30:34), and the anointing oil from the rest of it: *Take thou also unto thee principal spices, of pure myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty shekels, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty shekels,* (Exodus 30:23). The Song gathers them into the Bridegroom's garden: *Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:* (Song of Solomon 4:14). Enoch's eastern mountains are growing the very things the Torah later tells the priests to burn before Yahuah (LORD). The sanctuary smells like the garden because the garden came first.

threads.title: The tree of wisdom — Eden's tree of knowledge
threads.summary_md: At the Garden of Righteousness Enoch finds one tree set apart from the rest: *And I came to the Garden of Righteousness, and saw beyond those trees many large trees growing there and of goodly fragrance, large, very beautiful and glorious, and the tree of wisdom whereof they eat and know great wisdom. That tree is in height like the fir, and its leaves are like (those of) the Carob tree: and its fruit is like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful: and the fragrance of the tree penetrates afar.* (1 Enoch 32:3-4). He asks about it, and the angel names it: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). This is Eden's own tree, the one Genesis sets *in the midst of the garden*: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.* (Genesis 2:9). Enoch's phrase *they learnt wisdom* is Eve's reach for it: *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* (Genesis 3:6). And *their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked* is the fall told in Moses' own words: *And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.* (Genesis 3:7). So is the driving out: *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24). Raphael is reading Genesis 2 and 3 to Enoch, naming the tree of knowledge by its fruit and by what it cost, with the way back still guarded until the appointed day.

threads.title: The tree transplanted to the temple — fruit for the righteous
threads.summary_md: The tree withheld from Adam is not destroyed. It is kept: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:4-6). John sees the same tree replanted at the centre of the renewed city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2), and only the covenant-keepers come to it: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Ezekiel sets the same healing trees along the water that flows from the sanctuary: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree denied at the fall is carried to the temple-mountain at the judgement and its fruit goes to the elect who keep the way. That is a restoration of the covenant people at the centre, not a replacement of them, and Enoch saw it before Ezekiel or John did.

threads.title: The fragrant trees — frankincense and myrrh
threads.summary_md: East of the mountain range Enoch comes to trees that breathe the incense of worship: *And thence I went to another place in the desert, and approached to the east of this mountain range. And there I saw aromatic trees exhaling the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees also were similar to the almond tree.* (1 Enoch 29:1-2), and beyond them, *And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain to the east of the ends of the earth, whereon were aloe-trees, and all the trees were full of stacte, being like almond-trees. And when one burnt it, it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour.* (1 Enoch 31:2-3). Frankincense and myrrh are the fragrances Yahuah (LORD) reserves for His sanctuary: *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight* (Exodus 30:34). They are the same smoke that goes up around the Bridegroom as He comes out of the wilderness: *Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?* (Song of Solomon 3:6). Enoch says that when the aloe was burnt it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour, and that is a man describing incense before Moses was told how to compound it. The trees of the east were worship trees from the start.

threads.title: The tree of wisdom — eyes opened, driven from the garden
threads.summary_md: The angel names the tree for Enoch: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). This is Eden retold without a seam. Eve saw *a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof... and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat* (Genesis 3:6); then *the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked* (Genesis 3:7); and Yahuah Elohim *sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken* (Genesis 3:23). Enoch is shown the very tree Genesis names, standing where it stood, still bearing. The order Yahuah set in the garden was good; the fall was a reach for wisdom apart from the Creator's way, and the command that was broken was never the thing at fault.

threads.title: The tree reserved for the elect — transplanted to the holy place
threads.summary_md: The tree Michael shows Enoch is sealed off until the day of reckoning and then given back to the righteous: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is the Eden tree carried home to the mountain of the house. Ezekiel sees it rooted by the sanctuary stream: *shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed... because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12); Revelation sets it in the City: *the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations* (Revelation 22:2); and the way in is for those who keep the covenant: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). The vengeance falls on all who earned it, the fruit goes to the righteous and holy, and the tree is planted again at the centre. Eden, the mountain of the house, and the age to come are one story told three times.

threads.title: The tree of wisdom — Eden's tree of knowledge
threads.summary_md: Enoch is carried to the garden of righteousness in the east and shown the very tree of Eden: *Then I said: ‘How beautiful is the tree, and how attractive is its look!’ Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:5-6). This is no new tree — it is the one Genesis planted: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil* (Genesis 2:9), the same of which Yahuah commanded, *But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die* (Genesis 2:17). Enoch's 'they learnt wisdom' is Eve's reach: *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat* (Genesis 3:6); and Enoch's 'their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked' is Genesis word for word — *And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons* (Genesis 3:7). Jubilees tells the same scene the same way: *And when she had first covered her shame with fig-leaves, she gave thereof to Adam and he ate, and his eyes were opened, and he saw that he was naked* (Jubilees 3:21). It ain't new — Enoch sees the literal Eden tree and names it exactly as Moses did.

threads.title: Driven out — the tree of wisdom and the way kept
threads.summary_md: Of the tree their parents ate from Enoch is told the end of the matter: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). Genesis gives the reason for the driving out, that fallen man should not seize life for ever: *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and it names the guard set at the gate: *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Enoch, standing in the Garden of Righteousness with the tree of wisdom in front of him, is being shown that the garden is still there and the way is still kept. What Raphael says of this tree matches what Michael said of the other: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). The bar was never on wisdom itself. It was on wisdom taken against the command, and the righteous wait for the great judgement, when the way is opened again.

threads.title: The fruit given to the righteous — transplanted to the temple
threads.summary_md: At the great judgement Enoch's tree is opened to the elect and moved to the holy place: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:4-6). A tree of Eden standing in a holy place is the prophets' own picture, because Eden was always the garden of Elohim (God): *Thou hast been in Eden the garden of Elohim (God); every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created* (Ezekiel 28:13). Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same promise to the overcomer: *He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7), and Revelation sets the tree at the throne in the holy city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations* (Revelation 22:2), with its right reserved for the commandment-keepers: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). 2 Esdras hears the same opening: *For to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yes, perfect goodness and wisdom* (2 Esdras 8:52). The fruit is for the elect who keep the way, and the tree is carried to the temple of Yahuah (Lord) at the centre.

threads.title: The portals of heaven — the lights for signs and seasons
threads.summary_md: Enoch reaches the eastern edge: *And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open.* (1 Enoch 33:2) — *And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets: and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals.* (1 Enoch 72:3) This is the doorway to the Astronomical Book, and it is not new: the Creator hung the gates and set the lights at the fourth day — *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14) — the sun keeping its appointed circuit, *Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.* (Psalm 19:5) and *His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.* (Psalm 19:6) Uriel will spell out these same portals: *And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets: and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals.* (1 Enoch 72:3) And Jubilees reads the lights as the keepers of the moedim — *And Elohim (God) appointed the sun to be a great sign on the earth for days and for sabbaths and for months and for feasts and for years and for sabbaths of years and for jubilees and for all seasons of the years.* (Jubilees 2:9) The lights govern the feasts; the Torah's calendar is written into the sky.

threads.title: The stars come forth in their order — the courses Enoch wrote down
threads.summary_md: At the eastern ends of the earth Enoch watches the host come out through its gates: *And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open. And I saw how the stars of heaven come forth, and I counted the portals out of which they proceed, and wrote down all their outlets, of each individual star by itself, according to their number and their names, their courses and their positions, and their times and their months, as Uriel the holy angel who was with me showed me.* (1 Enoch 33:2-3), and *He showed all things to me and wrote them down for me: also their names he wrote for me, and their laws and their companies.* (1 Enoch 33:4). The stars have courses and times and laws, and Uriel had them written. This is the lesson Enoch opens the whole book with: *Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.* (1 Enoch 2:1). He had already seen what turns them: *I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting.* (1 Enoch 18:4). The Tanakh reads the same fidelity in the heavens: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19), and the Creator alone holds the reins of the constellations — *Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?* (Job 38:31), *Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?* (Job 38:32). The stars that never break rank are Enoch's standing rebuke to the ones that did, for he was shown their prison on the same journey: *And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:15). The heavens keep the order they were given, and rebellion against the appointed courses is where the trouble began.

threads.title: The great beasts and birds at the ends of the earth — the Creator's works kept
threads.summary_md: Before Enoch reaches the gates of heaven he passes the creatures that live at the edge of the world: *And from thence I went to the ends of the earth and saw there great beasts, and each differed from the other; and (I saw) birds also differing in appearance and beauty and voice, the one differing from the other.* (1 Enoch 33:1). Then the gates: *And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open.* (1 Enoch 33:2). Every kind differs from every other kind, and Enoch counts them as he counts the stars, each one by itself. That is Genesis speaking, every creature after its kind, and the man set over them to name them. Enoch is doing the work Adam was given, writing down names and courses and kinds under an angel's instruction. The fragrant tree he had smelt on the throne-mountain belongs to the same ordered creation: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). And the tree that wither not is the one Ezekiel sees by the sanctuary stream — *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12) — and the one John is shown at the end: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). What Enoch sees at the ends of the earth and what he smelt on the mountain are one creation, kept in order and kept for the righteous.

threads.title: The treasuries of the winds — He ordered all creation by His wisdom
threads.summary_md: Enoch is shown where the winds are kept and what they do: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-2). At the ends of the earth he sees the gates they come through: *And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. And out of one portal they blow for good: but when they blow through the other two portals, it is with violence and affliction on the earth, and they blow with violence.* (1 Enoch 34:2-3). These are the very treasuries Yahuah (LORD) set before Job out of the whirlwind — *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22) — and the prophets confess the wind drawn out of the same store: *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.* (Psalm 135:7), *When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13). Jeremiah names the wisdom behind the store in the verse before: *He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.* (Jeremiah 10:12). The world is not loose. It is furnished, founded, and ordered by the One who weighs the snow and appoints the seasons, and Enoch saw the furnishing.

threads.title: The north gates of heaven — the wind out of His treasuries
threads.summary_md: Enoch is carried to the ends of the earth and shown the gates from which the winds are loosed: *And from thence I went towards the north to the ends of the earth, and there I saw a great and glorious device at the ends of the whole earth. And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain.* (1 Enoch 34:1-2). The Tanakh keeps the very same storehouse: the wind, the rain, the frost are not stray weather but provisions Yahuah dispenses from His own treasuries — *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.* (Psalm 135:7), word for word again in *When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13). Job names the cold north-quarter Enoch saw first — *Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.* (Job 37:9) — and asks whether mortal man has ever entered those stores: *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22). It ain't new: the gated winds and the stored frost of 1 Enoch 34 are the canon's own doctrine that the Creator orders the weather from sealed treasuries no man controls.

threads.title: The four winds that bear the earth — the four quarters
threads.summary_md: Having walked north, east, south, and west, Enoch has seen the whole frame of the world at its corners, and on the earlier journey he had already seen what holds it: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2). The four winds are a fixed feature of the prophets' visions. Daniel watches them stir the nations: *Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.* (Daniel 7:2). John sees angels set over them, held back until the sealing is done: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). Enoch's own book of the luminaries names the quarters one by one: *And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the El Elyon (Most High) will descend there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever descend. And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.* (1 Enoch 77:1-2). The earth ordered to four corners, with winds held or loosed at the Creator's word, is the architecture Daniel and John take for granted, and Enoch is the one who wrote it down first.

threads.title: The winds that bear the earth — the pillars of heaven
threads.summary_md: Enoch is shown the frame of the cosmos and what holds it up: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2-3). The canon speaks the same architecture. Job knows both the hung earth and the trembling pillars: *He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.* (Job 26:7), *The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.* (Job 26:11). Isaiah sees the heavens stretched out like a tent — *It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in:* (Isaiah 40:22) — and the Psalm makes the very winds His servants: *Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:* (Psalm 104:4). Enoch's pillars and stretched-out vaults are the picture the canon already carries, a heaven the Creator hangs, spreads, and upholds, with the winds standing at their station to do it.

threads.title: The west portals and the storehouses of wind, dew, and rain
threads.summary_md: Enoch comes to the western edge and finds the same ordered gates he had seen in the east: *And from thence I went towards the west to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open such as I had seen in the east, the same number of portals, and the same number of outlets.* (1 Enoch 35:1). What comes through such gates he had just been shown on the north side: *And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. And out of one portal they blow for good: but when they blow through the other two portals, it is with violence and affliction on the earth, and they blow with violence.* (1 Enoch 34:2-3), and on the south: *And from thence I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and saw there three open portals of the heaven: and thence there come dew, rain, and wind.* (1 Enoch 36:1). The wind comes as gift and as affliction, and both are sent, not loosed. The Tanakh already keeps wind and weather in named storehouses that Yahuah (LORD) opens at His word: *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.* (Psalms 135:7); *When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13); and the same storehouses hold the frost and hail Enoch names — *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22). This is the Creator's order, and Enoch is shown it gate by gate, so that the reader can tell it apart from the disorder the Watchers brought.

threads.title: The four quarters of the earth and the four winds
threads.summary_md: From the western edge Enoch has now seen all four sides of the world, and he had already been shown what divides it: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2). The four winds and four quarters are the standard furniture of the prophets. Daniel watches them stir the nations: *Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.* (Daniel 7:2). Zechariah is told the four chariot-spirits are the same: *And the angel answered and said unto me, These are the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before Yahuah (Lord) of all the earth.* (Zechariah 6:5). John sees them held back at the corners: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). And Yahusha (Jesus) gathers the scattered seed from these same four winds at the end: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). The four quarters Enoch surveys are the compass the elect of Yashar'el (Israel) are gathered home from.

threads.title: The pillars of heaven and the stretched-out firmament
threads.summary_md: Enoch sees the winds themselves doing the structural work of holding the world up: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2-3). The Tanakh names these pillars and the firmament they bear. Job knows the heavens rest on pillars that tremble at a word: *The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.* (Job 26:11), and Hannah sings that the earth's foundations are Yahuah's own setting: *He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S, and he hath set the world upon them.* (1 Samuel 2:8). The firmament Enoch sees stretched is the firmament of the second day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.* (Genesis 1:6). And when the journey is over Enoch says plainly whose work it all is: *And as often as I saw I blessed always Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, and I continued to bless Yahuah (Lord) of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to the angels and to spirits and to men, that they might praise His work and all His creation: that they might see the work of His might and praise the great work of His hands and bless Him for ever.* (1 Enoch 36:4). The whole survey is creation kept in the Creator's order, the opposite of the disorder the Watchers brought into it.

threads.title: The portals of heaven and the four winds
threads.summary_md: Enoch finishes the circuit at the south and the east: *And from thence I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and saw there three open portals of the heaven: and thence there come dew, rain, and wind. And from thence I went to the east to the ends of the heaven, and saw here the three eastern portals of heaven open and small portals above them. Through each of these small portals pass the stars of heaven and run their course to the west on the path which is shown to them.* (1 Enoch 36:1-3). The stars run their course on a path that is shown to them, and the winds come through gates that are counted. John sees the same four-cornered order held in place in the last days: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). Job already knew the winds are weighed by the Creator's hand — *To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.* (Job 28:25) — and Enoch names the quarters himself in the book of the luminaries: *And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the El Elyon (Most High) will descend there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever descend. And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.* (1 Enoch 77:1-2). The four winds are servants under orders, not powers loose in the world.

threads.title: The winds that bear the earth — the pillars of heaven
threads.summary_md: On the earlier road Enoch had been shown what the gates of the four winds serve: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-3). Scripture speaks the same way of the world resting on the Creator's pillars: *He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S, and he hath set the world upon them.* (1 Samuel 2:8).
