The white bull is the same Formed Son named elsewhere as the Son of Adam; I do not force the title here, keeping him as the Formed Son the figure plainly is.

threads.title: The book written for the generations — preserve it, hand it on, add nothing
threads.summary_md: The Epistle opens by naming what it is and who it is for: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). The charge behind that opening was given to Methuselah earlier in the book: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father's hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1), *I have given wisdom to thee and to thy children, [And thy children that shall be to thee], That they may give it to their children for generations, This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought.* (1 Enoch 82:2). This is the Torah's own pattern for handing down the word, father to son to son's son: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* (Deuteronomy 6:6), *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* (Deuteronomy 6:7). And what is handed down is handed down whole: *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* (Deuteronomy 4:2), a fence John sets around the last book of all: *For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, Elohim (God) shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book:* (Revelation 22:18). A book written for the generations is only any use to them if it reaches them as it was written. That is why it was given to a son with the word preserve.

threads.title: Days appointed for all things — and the sinners who alter the order
threads.summary_md: Enoch tells his children not to be shaken by the times, because the times are not in the sinners' hands: *Let not your spirit be troubled on account of the times; For the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things.* (1 Enoch 92:2). He had already shown them what the sinners would do to the appointed order: *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2), *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel names the horn that sets its hand to the same thing: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). To change the times is to lay hands on the appointed feasts, and Jubilees, given on the same mountain as the Torah, says so almost word for word: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon.* (Jubilees 6:36), and *they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.* (Jubilees 6:37). The blood is the oldest line of all, from the days of Noah: *But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.* (Genesis 9:4). The sinners can confuse the calendar and hide the order from themselves. They cannot move the days the Holy and Great One appointed, and that is why Enoch says do not be troubled.

threads.title: The righteous one arises and walks in the paths of righteousness — eternal light, and sin seen no more
threads.summary_md: Against the corruption of the order Enoch sets the one who rises from sleep and walks: *And the righteous one shall arise from sleep, [Shall arise] and walk in the paths of righteousness, And all his path and conversation shall be in eternal goodness and grace.* (1 Enoch 92:3). What he is given is not a lighter way but power to walk the right one: *He will be gracious to the righteous and give him eternal uprightness, And He will give him power so that he shall be (endowed) with goodness and righteousness, And he shall walk in eternal light.* (1 Enoch 92:4), *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). The Epistle says the same blessing plainly a little further on: *But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the El Elyon (Most High), and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved.* (1 Enoch 99:10). These are the two ways Moses set before the people at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments...* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter knows the same fork in the road: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6). And the eternal light Enoch promises is the life Yahusha (Jesus) defined in his own prayer: *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom thou hast sent.* (John 17:3). The paths of righteousness are the way of life, and grace is what gives a man the power to walk them.

threads.title: A complete doctrine of wisdom — the law of the luminaries, exact and recorded
threads.summary_md: The Epistle names itself at the door: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). A great part of that wisdom is the law of the lights, which Enoch had closed out for his son a few chapters earlier: *And now, my son, I have shown thee everything, and the law of all the stars of the heaven is completed.* (1 Enoch 79:1). It was not his own reckoning. *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7), *And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.* (1 Enoch 82:9). This is the fourth day of creation spelled out: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). The seasons the lights are set for are the appointed ones, the feasts: *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* (Leviticus 23:4), and the Psalter keeps the same fixed order, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). The lights that keep their stations preach without a word: *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* (Psalm 19:1). The calendar is not an opinion a man holds. It is a law written in the sky, shown to Enoch by the angel set over it, and recorded exactly so the feasts would fall where their Maker set them.

threads.title: The leaders of the stars keep their stations — and men who err by them take them for gods
threads.summary_md: Sin has an end in this book: *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). Set beside that the ones who never sinned at all, the chiefs of the lights: *And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.* (1 Enoch 75:1). The stars keep their course; it is men who go wrong by them: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5), and the error ends in idolatry: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel shows the other end of the same sky, where the ones who keep and teach the order are made to shine like the lights they kept: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). Over those who fear the Name the true light rises: *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* (Malachi 4:2). The heavens keep telling it: *Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.* (Psalm 19:2). The lights never led anyone astray. The ones who hide the order and teach men to worship the lights are the ones whose sin perishes in the dark.

threads.title: The plant of uprightness and the elect of the world — what Enoch learned from the tablets
threads.summary_md: Enoch opens the recounting with the ones it is about: *And Enoch said: 'Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world, And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things, Yea, I Enoch will declare (them) unto you, my sons: According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision, And which I have known through the word of the holy angels, And have learnt from the heavenly tablets.'* (1 Enoch 93:2). What follows is the planting itself: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), and the enclosure built around it: *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is the man elected, his seed the plant, Sinai the law and the fence. And at the far end the charge to the sons is the same one Moses gave the plant at the Jordan: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). Moses said it this way: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same fork: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), and Yahusha (Jesus) gives it its narrow gate: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13). Sirach says it in one breath, *Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:17). The choice is set before a particular plant, the seed of the man who was elected, and it is the seed who are told to choose life so that they may be multiplied on the earth.

threads.title: The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence — all who walk in unrighteousness shall perish
threads.summary_md: Enoch's own count of the weeks begins with a warning about where the wrong road ends: *And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness, And deceit shall have sprung up; And in it there shall be the first end. And in it a man shall be saved; And after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up, And a law shall be made for the sinners.* (1 Enoch 93:4). The flood was the first end, and Noah the man saved out of it. Just before the recounting he had set the two roads before his sons in so many words: *And now I tell you, my sons, and show you The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. Yea, I will show them to you again That ye may know what will come to pass.* (1 Enoch 91:18), *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19). The Psalter's first song ends on the same verdict: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). Solomon draws the two roads as light against dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.* (Proverbs 4:18), *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) says which of the two has life at the end of it: *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.* (Matthew 7:14). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the ungodly say it themselves on the day: *We wearied ourselves in the way of wickedness and destruction: yes, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of Yahuah (God), we have not known it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:7). The way of violence is not struck down by some arbitrary hand. It has no way in it, and the ones who walk it perish on it.

threads.title: The apostate generation, and the elect righteous chosen for sevenfold instruction
threads.summary_md: The seventh week is the one Enoch's sons live in: *And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise, And many shall be its deeds, And all its deeds shall be apostate.* (1 Enoch 93:9). And out of that generation, at its close, a company is chosen: *And at its close shall be elected The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation.* (1 Enoch 93:10). What the elect are instructed in is nothing other than the way the fathers walked, and the fathers named it as the two commandments. Jubilees has Noah charge his sons' sons *to bless their Creator, and honour father and mother, and love their neighbour* (Jubilees 7:20), and Abraham charge his house *that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour* (Jubilees 20:2). Moses gave the first of those its full weight: *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* (Deuteronomy 6:5), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the two side by side as the whole of it: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* (Matthew 22:37), *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). An apostate generation is one that has let go of both. The elect righteous at the close of it are the plant of righteousness coming back to the instruction the plant was given at the start. It ain't new. The same love of Elohim (God) and neighbour runs from Enoch to Noah to Abraham to the one who called it the first and second commandment.

threads.title: The plant of righteousness, the law, and the enclosure — judgment and righteousness as the way
threads.summary_md: The third and fourth weeks are the planting and the fencing: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is elected as a plant of righteous judgment, which tells you what the plant is for, and the law given in the fourth week is the enclosure that keeps it. Micah summed up that law in a line: *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). Abraham's own house was charged with the same thing in the same words: *And he commanded them that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour, and act on this manner amongst all men; that they should each so walk with regard to them as to do judgment and righteousness on the earth.* (Jubilees 20:2). The Epistle's woes are what it looks like when the plant forgets the enclosure: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). So the two ways here are not abstract. A plant elected for righteous judgment that tramples the lowly has left its own enclosure, and the humble walk is the fence it was given.

threads.title: The two ways — choose the paths of righteousness, that ye may live
threads.summary_md: Enoch frames the whole Epistle as a choice between two roads: *And now I say unto you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein; For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.* (1 Enoch 94:1). He warns off the one road, *And now I say unto you the righteous: Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, And draw not nigh to them, lest ye be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 94:3), and sets the other in front of them: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). This is Moses' summons at the edge of the land: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). Jeremiah had the same two roads in his mouth: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD); Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death* (Jeremiah 21:8). The Psalter opens on it: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish* (Psalm 1:6), and Proverbs paints the two in light and dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day* (Proverbs 4:18) against *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) set the same fork before the crowds: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat* (Matthew 7:13), *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it* (Matthew 7:14). It is one summons from Sinai to Enoch to the mount where he sat down and taught. Walk the way that has life at the end of it.

threads.title: Woe to you who trust in your riches — they will not deliver in the day of affliction
threads.summary_md: The woe is not on having money. It is on what the heart leaned on while the money was there: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Epistle says later what that trust is worth when the day comes: *And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.* (1 Enoch 100:6). The Psalter had already weighed it: *They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches* (Psalm 49:6), and found that *None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him* (Psalm 49:7), because *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him* (Psalm 49:17). Yahusha (Jesus) told the story of one such man and let him speak for himself: *Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* (Luke 12:19), and then the answer, *Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). James says the same over the same departing wealth: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the rich say it themselves when it is too late: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8). The riches depart and the man who did not remember the Most High in the good days has nothing left to remember him by in the bad ones.

threads.title: Your riches shall not endure — the sinner's glory withers and goes into the furnace
threads.summary_md: Enoch lets the rich man make his boast in full before he answers it: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer is in the next breath: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And in the woes before it the house itself goes: *Woe to those who build their houses with sin; For from all their foundations shall they be overthrown, And by the sword shall they fall. [And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish.]* (1 Enoch 94:7). The end of the splendour is the furnace: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). Ben Sira had mocked the hoarder's plan long before: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). The Psalter's picture of the wicked's end is the grass: *For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb* (Psalm 37:2), and *the wicked shall perish... into smoke shall they consume away* (Psalm 37:20). James sets the rust on the hoard as a witness of fire: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Granaries full as with water, and lies that flow away like water. Enoch chose the same word for both on purpose.

threads.title: Woe to you who feast in luxury and tread upon the poor
threads.summary_md: The woes turn on the ones whose table is laid on other men's backs: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and in the plainest picture of it, *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Isaiah had the same woe against the same appetite: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8), *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink* (Isaiah 5:22). Amos drew the very bowl: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph* (Amos 6:6). Yahusha (Jesus) set the woe right beside the blessings: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger* (Luke 6:25), which is the Epistle's own sentence on the ones who spread harm to their neighbours: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). And James closes it: *Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter* (James 5:5). The lowly trodden under foot are the ones the Lord of the whole thing is going to answer for, and the feast built on their backs is what gets overthrown.

threads.title: Woe to those who pervert the words of uprightness and transgress the eternal law
threads.summary_md: Enoch weeps before he pronounces anything: *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), *Who has permitted you to practise reproaches and wickedness? And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners.* (1 Enoch 95:2). The woes that follow fall on the systems of deceit, and the sharpest of them is kept for the ones who rewrite the standard itself: *Woe to you who work godlessness, And glory in lying and extol them: Ye shall perish, and no happy life shall be yours.* (1 Enoch 99:1), *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Isaiah's woes name the same inversion: *Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!* (Isaiah 5:20), *Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!* (Isaiah 5:21). Yahusha (Jesus) turned the same word on the self-satisfied of his day: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24). Notice what Enoch calls the thing they pervert. It is the eternal law, and the ones who alter it do not become something new and better. They transform themselves into what they were not, which is sinners, and they write their own sentence in the act.

threads.title: Woe to the lying witnesses, the false weights, and those who persecute the righteous
threads.summary_md: The heart of the chapter is a run of woes on the ways men wrong one another: *Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 95:5), *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish.* (1 Enoch 95:6), *Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous; For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.* (1 Enoch 95:7). The false balance and the false witness are the Torah's own list, and Amos saw both at work in the market: *Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?* (Amos 8:5). Amos pronounced the same sentence on the ones at ease who did the weighing: *Woe to them that are at ease in Zion... That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph. Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive* (Amos 6:1,6,7). The Epistle keeps the gold in the same hands: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8). James carries the cry of the defrauded into the last days: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). Riches weighed out with a false measure cannot stand, *for he that getteth riches, and not by right... at his end shall be a fool.* (Jeremiah 17:11). Requited according to your works is the whole of it. The measure a man uses on his neighbour is the measure that comes back on him.

threads.title: Where are your riches now? — the rich man's wealth perishes
threads.summary_md: Enoch's tears open the chapter, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and the Epistle goes on to stage the reckoning those tears are for: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). The Parables let the mighty say what they see when it is gone: *For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, [nor glorified our Lord] But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory.* (1 Enoch 63:7), *Now they shall say unto themselves: 'Our souls are full of unrighteous gain, but it does not prevent us from descending from the midst thereof into the burden of Sheol.'* (1 Enoch 63:10), which is the Epistle's own woe: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). Yahusha (Jesus) told the scene as a story: *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:19-20). That is the boast of the full granaries answered by the night of demand. And the Wisdom of Solomon puts the confession in the mouths of the proud when they have perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8-9). Unrighteous gain fills the soul and does nothing at all to keep it out of Sheol.

threads.title: Fear not the sinners, ye righteous — the two paths and the way that lives
threads.summary_md: Enoch's woes are spoken through tears, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and in the middle of them he turns to the righteous: *Fear not the sinners, ye righteous; For again will Yahuah (Lord) deliver them into your hands, That ye may execute judgement upon them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 95:3). The choice that governs the whole Epistle was set out before the woes began: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' covenant charge, life set against death with the seed's blessing hanging on it: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly... For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:1,6), and Proverbs lights the difference: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day. The way of the wicked is as darkness* (Proverbs 4:18-19). The way of violence perishes for ever, and the ones who walk the other road are told not to be afraid of the ones on it.

threads.title: Woe to those who tread on the lowly with their might
threads.summary_md: The first woe in the chapter is on the ones whose money makes them look like the righteous: *Woe unto you, ye sinners, for your riches make you appear like the righteous, But your hearts convict you of being sinners, And this fact shall be a testimony against you for a memorial of (your) evil deeds.* (1 Enoch 96:4), and the next is on what that money was built on: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). The prophets had already named the crime. Amos: *Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.* (Amos 5:11), and *they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.* (Amos 5:12). Isaiah carries it to the rulers who ate the vineyard: *Yahuah (LORD) will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.* (Isaiah 3:14), *What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) of hosts.* (Isaiah 3:15). And the Torah's own protection of the afflicted stands behind every one of these woes: *Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:* (Proverbs 22:22), because *Yahuah (LORD) will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.* (Proverbs 22:23). Riches can make a man look righteous. The one who treads the lowly under foot has a heart that convicts him, and Enoch says that heart is the memorial that will be read.

threads.title: Woe to the mighty who oppress the righteous — the day of your destruction is coming
threads.summary_md: Enoch's woes are bracketed by comfort to the ones being trodden on. He begins, *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), and *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). Then the woe on the strong: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8), and on the ones who forsook the only fountain, *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Yahusha (Jesus) spoke the same reversal in almost the same words: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.* (Luke 6:25). James says it over the hoard: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the mighty confess it afterward: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), *All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by;* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:9). The day of the mighty man's destruction and the good days of the righteous are the same day. That is why the righteous are told to be hopeful and the mighty are told woe.

threads.title: Gold gotten in unrighteousness — the boast of full granaries
threads.summary_md: Enoch mocks the boast of the unjust rich: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8) — *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.’ And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9) Yahusha's parable of the rich fool answers that very swagger — *And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.* (Luke 12:18) — *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* (Luke 12:19) — yet *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20) Amos exposes how the brimming granaries were filled — by cheating the needy — *Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?* (Amos 8:5) — *That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes; yea, and sell the refuse of the wheat?* (Amos 8:6) It ain't new: full barns built on fraud are condemned from Amos to Enoch to the Gospel.

threads.title: The mighty who oppress the righteous, and the furnace at the end of their splendour
threads.summary_md: The last woe of the chapter is on strength used against the righteous: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8). The Epistle tells where that strength ends: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). James hears the cry of the ones whose labour paid for the purple: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4), and names the end of the oppression, *Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.* (James 5:6). Ben Sira calls the withheld wage what it is: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). And the Wisdom of Solomon watches the proud blow away: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). Poured out as water, and gone like smoke. The righteous they oppressed get their many and good days on the very day the mighty are judged.

threads.title: Be hopeful, ye righteous — the two paths and the fountain of life
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens on hope for the ones on the right road: *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). The other road is named by what it drinks from: *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Enoch had set the two roads before his sons at the start of the Epistle: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' charge at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The forsaken fountain is the one Jeremiah wept over: *For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.* (Jeremiah 2:13). And the Psalter sets the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). One road drinks from every fountain and withers. The other is told to be hopeful, because healing and light and rest are its portion.

threads.title: We have become rich — the riches that testify against the rich
threads.summary_md: Enoch lets the unrighteous rich make their speech, and the speech is the evidence: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer turns their own picture on them: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And the day it is all read out: *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). James hears the hoard itself give testimony: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). Habakkuk had raised the taunt already: *Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!* (Habakkuk 2:6). Yahusha (Jesus) calls it what it is on the night it is exposed: *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). And the proverb gives the verdict Enoch is pronouncing: *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* (Proverbs 11:4). The woe is on the acquiring in unrighteousness, not on possessing. The wealth gathered that way keeps a record of how it was gathered, and the record is read.

threads.title: The prayer of the righteous reaches the Lord — and the days of your judgement come
threads.summary_md: The sinners are asked a question they cannot answer: *What will ye do, ye sinners, And whither will ye flee on that day of judgement, When ye hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?* (1 Enoch 97:3), *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5), *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). The ones praying are the ones the Epistle has just shown trodden under foot: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Amos drew that table, the couch, the feast, the bowl of wine, with the poor uncared for in the next room: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.* (Amos 6:6). Isaiah ties the strong drinker to the cry of the oppressed: *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:* (Isaiah 5:22), having already wept that the vineyard yielded *oppression... a cry* instead of judgement (Isaiah 5:7). James gives the cry a voice and an address: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The reapers' cry enters the ears of the Lord of hosts. Enoch calls it the prayer of the righteous reaching him, and says the day it arrives is the day the judgement of the ones at the table begins.

threads.title: The sinners will become a shame and perish — the end of the splendour
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with a word to the righteous to believe what they cannot yet see: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1), *Be it known unto you (ye sinners) that the El Elyon (Most High) is mindful of your destruction, And the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction.* (1 Enoch 97:2). The Epistle has already described the splendour that goes into the fire: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). And the woe that stands behind it: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Wisdom of Solomon puts the lament in the mouths of the perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), and likens what they hoped in to dust: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). The purple and the grandeur are real while they last. Enoch's point is that the righteous should believe the end of them before it arrives, because the Most High is already mindful of it.

threads.title: The prayer of the righteous reaches him, and the riches of the unrighteous flow away like water
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens on the day the woes come due, and Enoch sets the two ends side by side so the righteous can hold on: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1). What turns that day is not the strength of the righteous but their prayer, which is heard: *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5). The men who built their lives on gathered silver hear the same verdict James will preach centuries later: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), and then the answer, *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). James heard the same cry rising from the reaped fields: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The Psalm had already drawn the two roads, the one that prospers and the one that perishes: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). The righteous do not win the day by force. They pray, the prayer is heard, and what was gathered in unrighteousness runs off like water.

threads.title: The luxury that perishes — woe to the adorned and the rich
threads.summary_md: Enoch opens the woe by swearing to wise and foolish alike and describing the doomed splendour of the oppressor: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water* (1 Enoch 98:2), whose end is that *they shall perish thereby together with their possessions* (1 Enoch 98:3). This is not a new complaint — it is the prophets' and James' woe on systems of injustice. James pronounces it on the hoarders: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1), for *your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Yahusha tells it as a parable against the man whose barns are full: *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). Enoch's own next woes name the same crowd — *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8) — and Ben Sira mocks the same false rest: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). The judgement falls on the structure of plunder, not on flesh as such.

threads.title: Sin was not sent — man made it himself
threads.summary_md: Against any plea that wickedness is fate, Enoch swears the opposite: *as a mountain has not become a slave, And a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, Even so sin has not been sent upon the earth, But man of himself has created it, And under a great curse shall they fall who commit it* (1 Enoch 98:4). The curse is not Torah but the self-made fruit of breaking it — exactly the two-ways covenant Moses set before the people: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15), with the charge, *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The choice is real; the death is chosen, not decreed. The prophets say it of Israel's idols too: *They have set up kings, but not by me... of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off* (Hosea 8:4) — the people fashion the very thing that destroys them. Torah stands as the way of life throughout; man, not the law, manufactures his own ruin.

threads.title: All your deeds are written down in heaven
threads.summary_md: Enoch takes away the one thing the oppressor counts on, that nobody sees. *I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, by the Holy Great One, That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden.* (1 Enoch 98:6). He will not let them talk themselves out of it either: *And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that ye do not know and that ye do not see that every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the El Elyon (Most High).* (1 Enoch 98:7), *From henceforth ye know that all your oppression wherewith ye oppress is written down every day till the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 98:8). The canon keeps the same ledger, and it records both sides of the page. Malachi saw the righteous written in: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). Later in the same book Enoch answers the sinner who says the record will never be kept: *And, although ye sinners say: “All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down,” nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day.* (1 Enoch 104:7). James says the fraud of the rich is already in the ears of heaven: *the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4). Nothing done to the poor is lost. It is written the day it is done, and the book waits for the day of judgement.

threads.title: Woe to the obstinate who eat blood
threads.summary_md: The woe turns on those who profane the table of the oppressed: *Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart, who work wickedness and eat blood: Whence have ye good things to eat and to drink and to be filled? From all the good things which Yahuah (Lord) the El Elyon (Most High) has placed in abundance on the earth; therefore ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 98:11). Eating blood is no minor matter; it is the covenant boundary set from Noah onward: *But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat* (Genesis 9:4), and Torah makes it a cutting-off sin: *whatsoever man there be of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)... that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people* (Leviticus 17:10), *for the life of the flesh is in the blood* (Leviticus 17:11). Torah stands; the oppressor who devours the Creator's abundance while trampling the poor breaks the law of life itself, and so has no peace.

threads.title: Woe to those who write down lying and godless words
threads.summary_md: The chapter's sharpest woe falls on the corrupters of the text itself: *Woe to you who write down lying and godless words; for they write down their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly towards (their) neighbour. Therefore they shall have no peace but die a sudden death.* (1 Enoch 98:15-16), set beside *Woe to you who set at nought the words of the righteous; For ye shall have no hope of life* (1 Enoch 98:14). The prophets already aimed this at the scribes who falsify what is written: *How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of Yahuah (LORD) is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain* (Jeremiah 8:8) — the lying pen perverts Torah. Isaiah's woe binds folly to inversion: *Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness* (Isaiah 5:20), *Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!* (Isaiah 5:21) — which is exactly Enoch's *ye fools... ye transgress against the wise* (1 Enoch 98:9). And Isaiah's woe on those who legislate injustice in writing fits the godless scribe precisely: *Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed* (Isaiah 10:1). Enoch himself names the crime again in the next chapter: *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law* (1 Enoch 99:2) — the eternal law (Torah) stands, and those who falsify it die a sudden death.

threads.title: Woe to those who transgress the eternal law
threads.summary_md: Enoch's woe falls on the lawbreaker: *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2) — the law here is *eternal*, the way of life, and the judgement is for trampling it, never the law itself being a curse. Isaiah names the same crime against the same Torah: *because they have cast away the law of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and despised the word of the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 5:24). Enoch's curse on those who lead others astray echoes Sinai's own amen-bound curse: *Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. And all the people shall say, Amen.* (Deuteronomy 27:18) Set against this is the everlasting plant-line's inheritance, marked by the boundary the fathers laid down: *Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.* (Proverbs 22:28) The eternal law stands; those who transform it perish.

threads.title: They worship a stone, and in an instant shall perish
threads.summary_md: The woe turns to idolatry: *And they who worship stones, and grave images of gold and silver and wood [and stone] and clay, And those who worship impure spirits and demons, And all kinds of idols not according to knowledge, shall get no manner of help from them.* (1 Enoch 99:7) — the idols are dumb, dead, breathless, exactly as Jeremiah names them: *Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.* (Jeremiah 10:14) — *They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.* (Jeremiah 10:15) Habakkuk's own woe mocks the same trust in a breathless thing overlaid with gold and silver: *Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.* (Habakkuk 2:19) And the last book carries the woe to its end, where idol-worship under the beast brings unceasing torment with no rest: *And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.* (Revelation 14:11) The stone gives no help; *in an instant shall they perish.*

threads.title: Blessed are they who walk in the path of His righteousness
threads.summary_md: Against the woes Enoch sets the blessing — the two ways laid side by side: *But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the El Elyon (Most High), and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved.* (1 Enoch 99:10) This is the Deuteronomic choice itself, life set against death: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15) — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two ways with the very word Enoch uses: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful* (Psalm 1:1) — *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish* (Psalm 1:6). To walk the path of His righteousness is the way of life; Torah is never the curse, only the road of the saved.

threads.title: Woe to the false measure and the house built on others' toil
threads.summary_md: The woes fall on the systems of injustice — false weights, houses built on stolen labor, the bloodshed of neighbours: *Woe to you who make deceitful and false measures, And (to them) who cause bitterness on the earth; For they shall thereby be utterly consumed.* (1 Enoch 99:12) — *Woe to you who build your houses through the grievous toil of others, And all their building materials are the bricks and stones of sin; I tell you ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 99:13) Amos names the same falsified balance and the swallowing of the needy: *making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit* (Amos 8:5) — *That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes* (Amos 8:6). James lays the whole woe on the rich whose wealth was built by defrauding the laborer: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4) — *Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you* (James 5:6). And Ben Sira makes the equation Enoch makes, defrauding the laborer is bloodshed: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). The judgement dismantles the unjust system; the righteous keep the measure.

threads.title: The prayers of the righteous as a memorial before the Most High
threads.summary_md: Before the judgement Enoch charges the righteous to lift up their prayers as a witness: *In those days make ready, ye righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial, And place them as a testimony before the angels, That they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the El Elyon (Most High).* (1 Enoch 99:3) John sees that very scene at the altar, the saints' prayers carried up by an angel: *And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne* (Revelation 8:3) — *And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before Elohim (God) out of the angel's hand* (Revelation 8:4). And the day Enoch points to is the day the righteous dead are vindicated and shine, while the godless are repaid — the resurrection parallel that runs through the Epistle: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7) — *But the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken Yahuah (God)* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:10). Election runs through the memorial: the names of the righteous stand before the Most High, the sin of the sinners stored for the day of judgement.

threads.title: The blood to the horse's breast — the day of slaughter
threads.summary_md: Enoch sees the day of judgement run with blood: *And the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners, And the chariot shall be submerged to its height.* (1 Enoch 100:3) — the kindred fall on one another from dawn till sunset until *the streams flow with their blood.* (1 Enoch 100:1) John sees the very same winepress at the end: *And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs.* (Revelation 14:20) — blood to the bridle, the exact measure Enoch gives. Joel had already set the harvest and the place: *Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.* (Joel 3:13) — and named the place of reckoning: *Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of Yahuah (LORD) is near in the valley of decision.* (Joel 3:14) Isaiah saw the same slaughter-mountains: *Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.* (Isaiah 34:3) It ain't new — the day Enoch foresaw is the day the prophets and the Revelation alike measure by blood.

threads.title: The Most High arises — the supper of the great Elohim
threads.summary_md: When the slaughter is full, judgement comes from above: *In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin, And the El Elyon (Most High) will arise on that day of judgement To execute great judgement amongst sinners.* (1 Enoch 100:4) The same gathering-angel stands in Revelation, summoning the carrion-feast over the fallen: *And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great Elohim (God);* (Revelation 19:17) — *That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great.* (Revelation 19:18) Zephaniah had already pronounced the day on the same terms: *And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against Yahuah (LORD): and their blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung.* (Zephaniah 1:17) — and Isaiah named the sentence the angels carry down: *For the indignation of Yahuah (LORD) is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.* (Isaiah 34:2) The judgement falls on the systems of sin gathered into one place, not on a scattered conscience — the Most High rises to break the unrighteous order He has long borne.

threads.title: Guardians for the righteous — kept as the apple of an eye
threads.summary_md: In the day of slaughter the righteous are not abandoned: *And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels To guard them as the apple of an eye, Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin, And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear.* (1 Enoch 100:5) The phrase is Moses' own picture of Yahuah's covenant care: *He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.* (Deuteronomy 32:10) — and the prophet's warning that to touch the elect is to touch Him: *For thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.* (Zechariah 2:8) The angelic charge is the Psalm's promise: *For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.* (Psalm 91:11) And the long sleep with nought to fear is no annihilation but a guarded rest the dead will wake from — the same hope the apocrypha holds: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1) The elect are a guarded people, kept through the judgement, never a self-selected class.

threads.title: Woe to the rich oppressor — riches shall not save
threads.summary_md: The children of the earth will see plainly that wealth is no refuge: *And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.* (1 Enoch 100:6) — and the woe falls on those who burned the righteous: *Woe to you, Sinners, on the day of strong anguish, Ye who afflict the righteous and burn them with fire: Ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 100:7) James pronounces the identical woe on the hoarding rich: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1) — *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3) Isaiah's woe is the same indictment of the land-engrossers: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8) — and Yahusha (Jesus) speaks it from the mountain: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24) Zephaniah seals it: *Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD'S wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy* (Zephaniah 1:18) — and Wisdom asks the empty question: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8) The woes fall on the system of oppression and the riches built on it, not on persons as such — dismantle the injustice; requital is according to works.

threads.title: Heaven testifies — the rain and dew withheld
threads.summary_md: Enoch declares that the very lights and waters will testify against the sinners: *And now, know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous.* (1 Enoch 100:10) — and the sky itself becomes a witness and a plague: *And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain; for they shall all be withheld because of you from descending upon you, and they shall be mindful of your sins.* (1 Enoch 100:11) The covenant curse spoke this long before: *And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron.* (Deuteronomy 28:23) — *Yahuah (LORD) shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.* (Deuteronomy 28:24) Leviticus binds the same sentence to broken covenant: *And I will break the pride of your power; and I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass:* (Leviticus 26:19) The withheld rain is no arbitrary wrath but the Torah's own curse for the covenant broken against the righteous — the bribe Enoch mocks (presents to the rain, gold and silver to buy the dew, 100:12) cannot reverse it. Torah stands; the heavens keep its terms.

threads.title: Fear not, ye souls of the righteous — wait for the day of judgement
threads.summary_md: When the fire comes, Enoch asks the sinners a question they cannot answer: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). The whole creation shakes before that word, *And ye sinners shall be cursed for ever, And ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 102:3). Then he turns to the dead who died keeping the covenant, and the tone changes entirely: *Fear ye not, ye souls of the righteous, And be hopeful ye that have died in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 102:4), *And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief, And that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness, But wait for the day of the judgement of sinners And for the day of cursing and chastisement.* (1 Enoch 102:5). Wisdom says the same thing about the same souls: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The world reads their death wrong — *In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2) — *but they are in peace* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:3), *their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). The righteous dead are not forgotten in Sheol; they are told to wait, because a day is coming that settles the account. Daniel names who comes out of it: *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). They were written before they died. The day only reveals it.

threads.title: As we die, so die the righteous — the sinners' taunt over the dead, and its answer
threads.summary_md: Enoch lets the sinners say their piece over the graves of the righteous, and it is the oldest taunt there is: *And yet when ye die the sinners speak over you: ‘As we die, so die the righteous, And what benefit do they reap for their deeds?* (1 Enoch 102:6), *Behold, even as we, so do they die in grief and darkness, And what have they more than we? From henceforth we are equal.* (1 Enoch 102:7), *And what will they receive and what will they see for ever? Behold, they too have died, And henceforth for ever shall they see no light.’* (1 Enoch 102:8). The whole argument rests on the grave being the end, and the canon answers it at the grave itself. Daniel was shown the awakening: *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the same shining at the harvest: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom stages the very scene Enoch records, with the mockers now watching the man they mocked: *This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:3), *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4), *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). Malachi heard the same complaint in his own day, *It is vain to serve Elohim (God)* (Malachi 3:14), and showed the book that settles it: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16). The sinners counted themselves equal with the righteous dead because both went into the ground. The book of remembrance says otherwise, and the day of awakening reads it out.

threads.title: Woe to the strong in unrighteousness who tread the poor — the eternal law unbroken
threads.summary_md: Enoch turns the woes against the systems of injustice, not the persons caught in them: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5) and *Woe to you who acquire gold and silver in unrighteousness* (102:13). This is the prophets' own indictment of luxury wrung from the oppressed. Isaiah: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place* (Isaiah 5:8), and *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink* (Isaiah 5:22) — the vineyard owner who *looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry* (Isaiah 5:7). Amos names the same banquet: *That drink wine in bowls... but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.* (Amos 6:6). And the apostle Yahaqov carries it whole into the last days: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), for *the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth* (James 5:4). The woe falls on the fraud, the hoarding, the trampling — the perversion of the eternal law — never on the poor, and never on Torah, which is the way of life the oppressor abandoned.

threads.title: Content to eat and drink and acquire wealth — whither will ye flee from the fire?
threads.summary_md: Enoch puts one question to the men who lived for their table and their takings: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). He describes their life without any ornament: *I tell you, ye sinners, ye are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin, and strip men naked, and acquire wealth and see good days.* (1 Enoch 102:9).
