threads.summary_md: *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour* (1 Peter 5:8). The adversary who *walketh about* is the very Satan of Job: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered Yahuah (LORD), and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it* (Job 1:7). The one *going to and fro in the earth,* prowling among men, is the *adversary* who *walketh about* — and the saints are to be sober and watchful against him. His likeness as a *roaring lion* is the image of the psalm of the suffering righteous one: *They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion* (Psalm 22:13). The lion that gaped upon David's anointed is the adversary the scattered must *resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world* (1 Peter 5:9). The enemy roars and prowls, but he is a defeated prowler before Yahuah (LORD); the watchful and steadfast withstand him, and the Elohim (God) of all grace stablishes them after they have suffered a while.

threads.title: His holy arm hath gotten him the victory — the new song of the bared arm
threads.summary_md: The enthronement psalm opens with a new song for a marvellous victory: *O sing unto Yahuah (LORD) a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory* (Psalm 98:1). Isaiah gives the verbatim twin and names the arm's work: *Yahuah (LORD) hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 52:10) — the holy arm BARED is the salvation SEEN by all. And Isaiah asks who that arm is: *Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of Yahuah (LORD) revealed?* (Isaiah 53:1) — the suffering servant, *wounded for our transgressions* (53:5). Read through the Formed and the Formless: the holy arm of Yahuah, His own strength bared and revealed, is the Formed Son in whom the victory is gotten and the salvation made known — he is Yahuah's arm, and he has a Father. And the new song the psalm calls for is sung in heaven by the redeemed of that very arm: *And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to Elohim (God) by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation* (Revelation 5:9). The new song of the marvellous victory is the song of the Lamb — the bared arm who redeemed a people out of every nation.

threads.title: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation — toward the house of Yashar'el first, and the nations seeing
threads.summary_md: *Yahuah (LORD) hath made known his salvation: his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen. He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Yashar'el (Israel): all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our Elohim (God)* (Psalm 98:2-3). The order is exact and never to be inverted: the mercy is *toward the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* FIRST — the covenant people remembered, never replaced (*Hath Elohim cast away his people? Elohim forbid*, Romans 11:1-2) — AND the ends of the earth see. Simeon holds the salvation in his arms: *For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Yashar'el (Israel)* (Luke 2:30-32) — the very pairing of the psalm: salvation that is BOTH a light to the nations AND the glory of the house of Israel. And the Baptist's herald-cry seals the universal sight: *And all flesh shall see the salvation of Elohim (God)* (Luke 3:6). This is the two-house ingathering plus the nations seeing — the made-known salvation set before every eye, the house remembered and the ends of the earth beholding, never the house cast off.

threads.title: With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before Yahuah, the King
threads.summary_md: The psalm summons the whole earth to acclaim the King with sound: *Make a joyful noise unto Yahuah (LORD), all the earth: make a loud noise, and rejoice, and sing praise. Sing unto Yahuah (LORD) with the harp; with the harp, and the voice of a psalm. With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before Yahuah (LORD), the King* (Psalm 98:4-6). The trumpet-blast before the King is the Torah's own appointed-times acclamation. The Feast of Trumpets stands as a statute for ever: *In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation* (Leviticus 23:24). And the solemn-day trumpet is commanded for a memorial: *Also in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings... that they may be to you for a memorial before your Elohim (God): I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* (Numbers 10:10). The cornet acclaiming Yahuah the King in the psalm is the appointed-times trumpet of the assembly — the feast that is never abolished, sounding the enthronement of the King who comes.

threads.title: He cometh to judge the earth — the Judge ordained as a man
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes with all creation summoned to acclaim the coming Judge: *Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein. Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together Before Yahuah (LORD); for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity* (Psalm 98:7-9). This is the twin of the sister enthronement-psalm — *for he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness, and the people with his truth* (Psalm 96:13). The coming Judge who judges in righteousness is the rider on the white horse: *And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war* (Revelation 19:11), whose *name is called The Word of Elohim (God)* (19:13) — the Formed Son. And Paul names him plainly as the Man ordained to judge: *Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead* (Acts 17:31). The One who cometh to judge the world with righteousness is the Formed Son, ordained as a man and raised from the dead — Yahuah's own arm bared to judge, and he has a Father.

threads.title: He sitteth between the cherubims — the enthroned Presence over the mercy seat
threads.summary_md: The enthronement psalm opens at the throne: *Yahuah (LORD) reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved* (Psalm 99:1). That throne is the mercy seat over the ark, where Yahuah Himself promised to meet His people: *And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony* (Exodus 25:22). It is the title Yashar'el (Israel) carried in her memory of the ark — *the ark of the covenant of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), which dwelleth between the cherubims* (1 Samuel 4:4) — and the title Hezekiah prayed to in his distress: *O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth* (Isaiah 37:16). The One enthroned above the mercy seat is the visible, Formed Presence — Yahuah who met His people and spoke from between the cherubims, *high above all the people* and *great in Zion* (99:2). His reign is *judgment and righteousness in Jacob* (99:4): the King over His own covenant people, the two-house seed of Yashar'el (Israel), never a throne over a replacement nation but over the very people He gathered to Himself.

threads.title: Holy, holy, holy — the thrice-holy of the throne; the One Isaiah saw is the Formed Son
threads.summary_md: Three times the psalm sounds the throne's holiness: *Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy* (Psalm 99:3); *Exalt ye Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), and worship at his footstool; for he is holy* (99:5); *Exalt Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), and worship at his holy hill; for Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is holy* (99:9). This threefold *holy* is the cry of the throne-vision. Isaiah, brought before the throne, hears it from the seraphim: *And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): the whole earth is full of his glory* (Isaiah 6:3). And in the Spirit's final vision the living creatures cry it without rest: *they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come* (Revelation 4:8). The One Isaiah saw upon the throne, *high and lifted up* (Isaiah 6:1), is named by the Spirit as the Formed Son: *These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him* (John 12:41). So the Holy One the psalm enthrones — He who *sitteth between the cherubims* (99:1) and whose name is *holy* — is Yahuah the Former, the expressed Word drawn from the Formless, who took flesh. He is Yahuah, and he has a Father: no co-equal-persons grammar, no modalist collapse, but the Son enthroned in the holiness the whole canon cries.

threads.title: He spake in the cloudy pillar — the great intercessors, and the testimonies kept
threads.summary_md: The psalm turns to those who called upon the Name and were answered: *Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name; they called upon Yahuah (LORD), and he answered them* (Psalm 99:6). The pairing of Moses and Samuel is Yashar'el (Israel)'s very standard of intercession — *Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people* (Jeremiah 15:1): the two men who stood before Yahuah for the people. And the manner of His speaking is the cloudy pillar: *He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them* (99:7). This is the scene of Exodus — *as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and Yahuah (LORD) talked with Moses* (Exodus 33:9). The Presence who spoke from the pillar, who led Yashar'el (Israel) through the wilderness, is the Formed Son, the visible Glory. And the center of the verse is the Torah kept, not abolished: *they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them* — the faithful kept His commandments (the filter of *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar*, 1 John 2:3-4). The God who spoke from the pillar both pardoned and corrected His own: *Thou answeredst them, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God): thou wast a Elohim (God) that forgavest them, though thou tookest vengeance of their inventions* (99:8) — covenant mercy and covenant discipline together, never the curse on the Torah itself.

threads.title: Worship at his footstool — the earth his footstool, the ark his footstool
threads.summary_md: Twice the psalm calls the people to bow at the holy place: *Exalt ye Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), and worship at his footstool; for he is holy* (Psalm 99:5); *Exalt Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), and worship at his holy hill; for Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is holy* (99:9). The footstool is His own: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest?* (Isaiah 66:1) — the enthroned One whose throne is between the cherubims (99:1) is the One whose footstool is the earth itself. And David named the ark, the throne between the cherubims, the footstool of God: *I had in mine heart to build an house of rest for the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD), and for the footstool of our Elohim (God)* (1 Chronicles 28:2). So to worship at His footstool is to bow before the place of the enthroned Presence — the ark over which He dwells, the *holy hill* of Zion where *Yahuah (LORD) is great* (99:2). The footstool and the throne and the holy hill are one holy place, and the call is the same: exalt Him, worship, *for he is holy*.

threads.title: We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture — the flock and the Shepherd
threads.summary_md: The heart of the psalm is a confession: *Know ye that Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God): it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture* (Psalm 100:3). Read through the Formed and the Formless, the Maker who made us is the Shepherd who feeds us. Ezekiel gives the near-exact twin — *ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your Elohim (God)* (Ezekiel 34:31) — in the chapter where Yahuah, against the false shepherds who let the flock be scattered, declares *I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out* (34:11) and *I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd* (34:23): ONE shepherd over the regathered house, Yahuah Himself in the person of the Formed Son, the Davidic Shepherd — never a replacement people, but the lost sheep of Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah) gathered home and fed. Psalm 95, the enthronement-collection twin, sings it the same way — *he is our Elohim (God); and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand* (95:7) — and Psalm 23 makes it the single soul's confession — *Yahuah Ra'ah (The LORD is my shepherd); I shall not want* (23:1). And the Formed Son claims the title in flesh: *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep* (John 10:11); *I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine* (John 10:14); *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me* (John 10:27). The Maker who *hath made us, and not we ourselves* is the Shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep he made; he is Yahuah, the Former, and he has a Father.

threads.title: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving — the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of the lips
threads.summary_md: The congregation is called to the house: *Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name* (Psalm 100:4). The thanksgiving brought into the gates and courts is taken FORWARD as the continual offering of the redeemed — *By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to Elohim (God) continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name* (Hebrews 13:15) — not a setting-aside of the Tabernacle worship but its very heart, the thank-offering of the lips that bless His name. The psalter gives the lateral, the same thanksgiving in the same place: *I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 116:17), offered *In the courts of the LORD'S house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem. Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)* (116:19). The gates and courts of Psalm 100:4 are the courts of the LORD'S house where the vows are paid, the Name is blessed, and the sacrifice of thanksgiving — the fruit of the lips — rises continually.

threads.title: For Yahuah is good; his mercy is everlasting — the covenant-refrain of the psalter
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes on the great covenant-refrain: *For Yahuah (LORD) is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations* (Psalm 100:5). This antiphon — His goodness and His everlasting mercy (chesed) — runs the whole psalter. It opens Book V: *O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD), for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 107:1). It is sung six-and-twenty times, once for every line, in the great hymn of creation and the exodus: *O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:1). And it has its home in David's ark-psalm, first set in Israel's mouth when the ark came up to Jerusalem: *O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever* (1 Chronicles 16:34). The everlasting mercy and the truth that *endureth to all generations* are the steadfast covenant-faithfulness of Yahuah — the unchanging ground from which all the joyful noise of Psalm 100 rises, and the refrain the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) sings on.

threads.title: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way — the just ruler the Branch fulfills
threads.summary_md: Psalm 101 is David's vow of integrity, the righteous king's pledge of a perfect reign: *I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O Yahuah (LORD), will I sing. I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. O when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart* (Psalm 101:1-2). This is the ideal the throne of David requires — and it is the ideal that only the Messiah, the Formed Son, the Branch, perfectly fulfills. David's own last words name the standard: *He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of Elohim (God)* (2 Samuel 23:3). Isaiah unfolds the Branch who meets that standard without fail: *with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked* (Isaiah 11:4); *And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins* (Isaiah 11:5). The *perfect heart* and *perfect way* David vows are the Messiah's by nature; the integrity the king pledges is the integrity the Branch wears as his very girding. And the plaintive cry *O when wilt thou come unto me?* (101:2) is the throne's longing for the Presence — the king reaching for the One whose perfect rule his own vow can only foreshadow. David's vow of a just reign is the shadow; the just King is the substance.

threads.title: An high look and a proud heart will not I suffer — the proud abased
threads.summary_md: The righteous king will not tolerate pride or slander in his court: *Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer* (Psalm 101:5). The king hates what Yahuah hates. The catalogue of the abominable opens with these very things: *These six things doth Yahuah (LORD) hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood* (Proverbs 6:16-17) — the proud look and the lying tongue heading the list, the same two the king cuts off. And Proverbs names the high look as sin in itself: *An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin* (Proverbs 21:4). The just throne is conformed to the heart of the One it serves: the slanderer's tongue and the proud heart are abominations to Yahuah, and so the king will not suffer them near him.

threads.title: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land — gathered to dwell with the king
threads.summary_md: Over against the proud cut off, the king gathers the faithful to himself: *Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me* (Psalm 101:6). The ones fit to dwell with the king are the ones fit to dwell with Yahuah — the very question the psalter poses of Yahuah's own holy hill: *Yahuah (LORD), who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill? He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart* (Psalm 15:1-2). The *perfect way* of the king's servant (101:6) is the upright walk of the one who abides in the tabernacle; the same integrity admits a man to the king's table and to Yahuah's hill. And the inverse stands: *He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house: he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight* (101:7) — the deceitful are shut out, only the upright dwell with him.

threads.title: I will cut off all wicked doers from the city of Yahuah — the purged holy city
threads.summary_md: The king's vow ends with the cleansing of the city: *I will early destroy all the wicked of the land; that I may cut off all wicked doers from the city of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 101:8). David purges his city of every wicked doer — and this is the foreshadow of the New Jerusalem, the holy city from which all that defileth is shut out forever. *And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life* (Revelation 21:27); *For without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie* (Revelation 22:15) — the wicked doers cut off from the city are those left outside its gates. Isaiah sings the same purging of the city by name: *put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean* (Isaiah 52:1). And the Son of Adam does the cutting off the king vowed: *The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity* (Matthew 13:41). David's vow to purge his city is the King's purging of the whole kingdom; the city of Yahuah cleansed of every wicked doer is the New Jerusalem, the holy city made pure.

threads.title: Reuben's confession — he defiled his father's bed
threads.summary_md: Reuben opens his deathbed testament by confessing the very sin Genesis records against him: that in the ignorance of youth he defiled the bed of his father Jacob, and was smitten in his loins until Jacob's prayer spared him. It ain't new — the testament only owns aloud what Moses already wrote, and the firstborn's forfeited excellency.

threads.title: The spirits of error — fornication, the belly, anger, pride, lying, injustice
threads.summary_md: Reuben catalogues the spirits of error that darken a young man's mind from the truth — fornication, insatiableness, fighting, pride, lying, injustice. The list is no new psychology: it is the Proverbs' seven abominations and the works of the flesh, the lust that conceives and brings forth death. It ain't new — the prophets and the apostles name the same vices and the same cure: love the truth.

threads.title: Pay no heed to the face of a woman — Bilhah and the lust that conceives
threads.summary_md: Reuben warns his sons to give no heed to a woman's beauty, telling how the sight of Bilhah uncovered would not let him sleep until he had wrought the abominable thing. This is James' anatomy of sin and Solomon's warning against the strange woman's eyelids, lived out. It ain't new — lust conceived in the eye and brought to deed is the oldest pattern, and the law and the gospel both forewarn it.

threads.title: Joseph guarded himself from a woman
threads.summary_md: Reuben holds up Joseph as the foil to his own fall: how Joseph guarded himself from the Egyptian woman, purged his thoughts of fornication, and so found favour with God and men. The testament reaches straight for the Genesis account of the temptation refused. It ain't new — single-mindedness in the fear of Yahuah, and a way of escape from temptation, are the law and the gospel's own counsel.

threads.title: The Watchers who fell through women before the flood
threads.summary_md: Reuben warns against the wiles of women by recalling how the Watchers before the flood lusted after them, took the shape of men, and the women bare giants reaching even unto heaven. This is no fable of his own: it is Genesis 6 read as Enoch read it, the sons of Elohim and the daughters of men, the angels reserved in chains. It ain't new — Moses recorded it, Enoch named the Watchers, and Jude preached the same judgment.

threads.title: Hearken to Levi — the anointed High Priest of whom Yahuah spake
threads.summary_md: Reuben charges his sons not to be jealous of the sons of Levi but to draw near in humbleness, for to Levi God gave the sovereignty: he shall know the law, give ordinances for judgment, and sacrifice for all Israel as the anointed High Priest. The hope is the priest-king foretold by Moses and the prophets, a priest upon his throne. It ain't new — the everlasting priesthood after Melchizedek and the counsel of peace between priest and king were spoken long before.

threads.title: Bow before his seed — an eternal king who dies in wars on our behalf
threads.summary_md: Reuben bids his sons bow before Levi's seed, for on Israel's behalf it will die in wars visible and invisible and be an eternal king among them. Beneath the legend the testament reaches for the Star out of Jacob and the Sceptre out of Israel, the gathering of the people to Shiloh, the priest-king who lays down his life. It ain't new — Balaam saw the Star, Jacob saw the Sceptre, and the whole hope is of one anointed from Levi and Judah.

threads.title: Do truth and love, each one to his brother
threads.summary_md: Reuben adjures his sons by the God of heaven to do truth each one unto his neighbour and to entertain love each one for his brother. This is the royal law itself, the second great commandment, spoken at a patriarch's deathbed. It ain't new — to love thy neighbour as thyself is Moses' word that all the law and the prophets hang upon.

threads.title: Simeon's confession — the spirit of jealousy against Joseph
threads.summary_md: Simeon owns the sin Moses records plainly: the brothers loved Joseph less because their father loved him more, and the jealousy that festered into a plot to destroy him. Genesis names the envy; the testament names the spirit behind it; the Prophets and apostles name what envy does to the one who harbours it. It ain't new — the rottenness of the bones Solomon warned of is the very thing Simeon confesses on his deathbed.

threads.title: Judah sold him — and the withered hand restrained
threads.summary_md: The testament recalls Genesis exactly: it was Judah who counselled selling Joseph to the Ishmaelites, and Reuben who grieved, having meant to restore him to his father. Simeon's wrath against Judah is checked by the Lord, his hand half-withered until he repents and weeps. It ain't new — the hand restrained from violence and the heart turned to repentance are the Torah's own discipline upon a brother who hated.

threads.title: Envy ruleth the mind and wastes the envier
threads.summary_md: Simeon describes envy not as a passing mood but as a ruler over the whole mind — it will neither eat nor drink nor do good, but only labours to destroy the one envied, and while the envied flourishes the envier fades away. It ain't new — Solomon and James say the same: envy rots the bones, and where envying is, there is every evil work.

threads.title: Deliverance from envy by the fear of the Lord
threads.summary_md: Simeon learns the cure for envy by fasting and the fear of the Lord: if a man flee to the Lord, the evil spirit runs away and his mind is lightened. It ain't new — Solomon already called the fear of the Lord a fountain of life, drawing a man away from the snares of death; the patriarch only walks the road Proverbs laid down.

threads.title: Joseph the good man — bearing no malice, repaying evil with good
threads.summary_md: Simeon names Joseph a good man with the Spirit of God within him, who bore no malice but loved his brothers as his own soul and never reproached them for what they did. This is Moses' own portrait of Joseph at the last: "ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good." It ain't new — Joseph forgiving the brothers who sold him is the Messiah-type the Gospel will fill full, the man who repays evil with good.

threads.title: Walk in singleness of heart — love each his brother
threads.summary_md: Simeon's charge to his sons is the heart of the whole Torah ethic: walk in singleness of heart and love each one his brother with a good heart, and the spirit of envy will withdraw. He warns that envy makes savage the soul and destroys the body. It ain't new — to love thy neighbour is the law fulfilled, and the apostles trace hatred of a brother straight to murder and death.

threads.title: Beware of fornication — the writing of Enoch
threads.summary_md: Simeon warns that fornication is the mother of all evils, separating from God and bringing near to Beliar, and he names the source he read it in: the writing of Enoch. That writing tells how the Watchers committed fornication and corrupted all flesh, the corruption Moses records in Genesis. It ain't new — the patriarch's warning reaches back to Enoch and to the days of Noah, when fornication first filled the earth with violence.

threads.title: Levi shall prevail — divided in Levi and Judah
threads.summary_md: Simeon foresees that none of his own seed shall hold sovereignty; the rule is divided to Levi and Judah, even as Jacob prophesied in his blessings. This is the testament's quiet bow to the two tribes from whom salvation will arise — the priest of Levi and the sceptre of Judah. It ain't new — the sceptre belongs to Judah by Jacob's word and Balaam's, and Simeon yields his place to the joined hope of the priest-king.

threads.title: The Lord shall appear on earth and save the sons of men
threads.summary_md: Simeon's closing prophecy: the Mighty One of Israel shall glorify Shem, the Lord God shall appear on earth and save the sons of men, the spirits of deceit shall be trodden under foot, and he himself shall rise in joy. The prophets foretold the same coming — the Lord suddenly coming to his temple, his feet standing on the mount, the King over all the earth — and the apostles the same crushing of the powers of darkness. It ain't new — the appearing Simeon awaits is the day the prophets named, when the Lord comes and his saints rule over wicked spirits. (The bracketed clause that God "took a body and ate with men" is a later gloss; the genuine root is the prophesied coming of the Lord to save.)

threads.title: My bones shall flourish — and I shall rise in joy
threads.summary_md: Simeon promises that if his sons remove their envy his bones shall flourish like a rose in Israel, his branches stretching afar, and at the last he himself shall arise in joy to bless the Most High. The flourishing of dry bones and the rising of the patriarchs in gladness are the prophets' own hope of resurrection. It ain't new — Israel's bones living again and the dead rising in joy is the word of Ezekiel and Isaiah long before Simeon.

threads.title: Obey Levi and Judah — from them the salvation of God
threads.summary_md: Here is Simeon's keystone: obey Levi and Judah, for from these two tribes shall arise the salvation of God — the Lord raising up from Levi a High-priest and from Judah a King, to save all the race of Israel. This is the Formed Son, the Father's Anointed: the priest-king foretold in Balaam's Star and Sceptre, in Zechariah's counsel of peace between the two offices, in David's priest for ever after Melchizedek, and opened in Hebrews. It ain't new — the joined hope of Levi's priesthood and Judah's throne is the whole testimony of Moses and the Prophets, and the Messiah is both.

threads.title: Command your children to observe these throughout their generations
threads.summary_md: Simeon closes by binding his commands on the generations to come: that his sons command their children to observe them always. This is the Torah's own pattern of teaching the commandments to the children diligently. It ain't new — the deathbed charge to keep and pass on the words is the very rhythm of Moses.

threads.title: His bones taken up — and the bones of Joseph
threads.summary_md: Simeon is laid in a wooden coffin, his bones to be carried up to Hebron, while Joseph's bones the Egyptians guard, for the sorcerers warned that their departure would bring darkness and an exceeding great plague. Moses records the oath Joseph laid on Israel to carry up his bones, the plague of darkness on Egypt, and the day Moses took those bones at the Exodus and Israel buried them in the land. It ain't new — the carrying up of the patriarchs' bones is the Torah's own pledge that God would surely visit his people and bring them home.

threads.title: The heavens opened — Levi's ascent through the heavens
threads.summary_md: Levi, grieving the corruption of men, prays to be saved, and a sleep falls upon him: the heavens are opened, an angel bids him enter, and he ascends from heaven to heaven toward the throne. The prophets and apostles know this same opening of heaven — Ezekiel by the river, Paul caught to the third heaven, the heavens torn at the Jordan. It ain't new — the opened heaven and the throne-vision Levi sees are the same Most High the seers of Israel beheld.

threads.title: Thou shalt stand near the Lord and be His minister
threads.summary_md: The angel tells Levi that when he ascends he shall stand near the Lord, be His minister, declare His mysteries, and proclaim the One who shall redeem Israel — and that by Levi and by Judah the Lord shall appear among men. This is the joined hope of the two tribes, the priest of Levi and the king of Judah, from whom salvation arises. It ain't new — the Star of Jacob and the priest who stands before the Lord are already spoken in Moses and the Prophets.

threads.title: The Great Glory above all the heavens, and the throne
threads.summary_md: The angel expounds the heavens to Levi: in the highest dwells the Great Glory far above all holiness, with thrones and dominions offering ceaseless praise, and the archangels who make a bloodless offering before the Lord. When the Lord looks forth, heaven and earth and the abysses are shaken. The prophets and the seer of Patmos beheld this same throne and the unceasing 'Holy, holy, holy.' It ain't new — the throne-room Levi is shown is the throne Isaiah, Ezekiel, and John saw.

threads.title: The day of judgment — the rocks rent, the sun quenched
threads.summary_md: The angel foretells the day the Lord judges men: the rocks rent, the sun quenched, the waters dried, all creation troubled, and Hades despoiled by the visitation of the Most High. The prophets paint the same Day — the sun darkened, the heavens shaken. It ain't new — the day of the Lord Levi is shown is the day Joel and Isaiah and the Gospel proclaim.

threads.title: The light of knowledge in Jacob, the sun to all Israel's seed
threads.summary_md: Because the Most High heard Levi's prayer, he is set apart to be a son and minister of His presence, to light the light of knowledge in Jacob and be as the sun to all the seed of Israel, with a blessing to his seed until the Lord visits all the Gentiles in mercy. The blessing of light to Jacob and mercy to the nations is already Moses' and the Prophets' word. It ain't new — they that bless the Lord are blessed, as Israel's own blessing declares.

threads.title: I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood
threads.summary_md: The angel opens the gates of heaven, Levi sees the holy temple and the Most High on the throne of glory, and the Lord gives him the blessings of the priesthood until He come and sojourn in the midst of Israel. This is the priesthood Moses ordained for Levi and the temple where the Lord dwells with His people. It ain't new — the priest's office given to Levi and the Lord dwelling among them is the charge of the Torah.

threads.title: Execute vengeance on Shechem — the shield and the sword
threads.summary_md: The angel brings Levi down to earth, gives him a shield and a sword, and bids him execute vengeance on Shechem because of Dinah. This is the deed Genesis records of Simeon and Levi, who took each man his sword against the city that defiled their sister. It ain't new — the testament owns the very act Moses set down, and the angel who intercedes for Israel.

threads.title: The circumcision of Shechem, and the city smitten by the sword
threads.summary_md: Levi recounts that he counselled to bid the sons of Hamor be circumcised, then slew Shechem first while Simeon slew Hamor, and the brothers smote the city with the edge of the sword. This is the deceitful counsel and the slaughter Genesis sets down word for word. It ain't new — the testament confesses aloud the very deed Moses recorded against Simeon and Levi.

threads.title: Seven men in white robe Levi in the garments of the priesthood
threads.summary_md: In a second vision seven men in white raiment clothe Levi with the robe of the priesthood, the breastplate, the ephod, the turban, and the plate, anoint him with holy oil, wash him with pure water, feed him with bread and wine, crown him, and fill his hands with incense to serve as priest. Every garment and rite is Aaron's consecration in the Torah. It ain't new — the holy garments, the anointing oil, the washing and the filling of the hands are Moses' own ordination of the priest.

threads.title: A king shall arise in Judah and establish a new priesthood
threads.summary_md: The seven men tell Levi his seed shall be divided into three offices for a sign of the glory of the Lord who is to come, the third called by a new name, because a king shall arise in Judah and establish a new priesthood — His presence beloved as a prophet of the Most High, of the seed of Abraham. This is the joined hope: the king of Judah and the priesthood made new, a priest after a changed order. It ain't new — the priest-king after Melchizedek, of Judah's line, is sworn in the Psalms and confirmed in Hebrews.

threads.title: Jacob pays tithes of all to the Lord through Levi
threads.summary_md: Coming to Bethel, Jacob sees in a vision that Levi should be priest unto God, rises early, and pays tithes of all to the Lord through him. This is the Bethel vow of Genesis, where Jacob promised the tenth, and the tithe given to the priests of Levi in the Torah. It ain't new — the tithe through Levi the priest is Jacob's own Bethel vow brought to its appointed channel.

threads.title: The law of the priesthood — clean beasts, washing, and salt
threads.summary_md: Isaac instructs Levi continually in the law of the priesthood — to bathe before the holy place, to offer of every clean beast and bird, of first-fruits and wine, and to salt every sacrifice with salt. Each charge is the Torah's law of offerings, the difference between clean and unclean, and the covenant of salt. It ain't new — Isaac teaches Levi nothing but Moses' law of the priesthood, distinguishing clean from unclean and salting every offering.

threads.title: The veil of the temple rent, Israel scattered among the Gentiles
threads.summary_md: Levi foretells that in the end of the ages his sons will deal lawlessly, the veil of the temple shall be rent, and they shall be scattered as captives among the Gentiles for a reproach and a curse. The Gospel records that very veil rent, and Moses foretold the scattering for transgression. It ain't new — the rent veil and the dispersion among the nations are written in the Torah and fulfilled in the Gospel.

threads.title: The house the Lord shall choose, as in the book of Enoch
threads.summary_md: Levi declares that the house which the Lord shall choose shall be called Jerusalem, as is contained in the book of Enoch the righteous. The vision of Enoch indeed saw a new house built greater and loftier than the first, into which the Lord gathered all His own. It ain't new — Levi names Enoch by his book, and the chosen house of God is the very new house Enoch beheld.

threads.title: Fear the Lord with your whole heart and walk in His law
threads.summary_md: Levi commands his children to fear the Lord their God with their whole heart, walk in simplicity according to all His law, teach their children the law, and lay up righteousness as a treasure in heaven. This is the Shema and the wisdom of Proverbs and the Gospel's treasure in heaven. It ain't new — to love the Lord with the whole heart and keep His law is the first command of Moses.

threads.title: The priests rob the offerings and corrupt the covenant of Levi
threads.summary_md: Levi foretells the priests who will be puffed up over their priesthood, rob the offerings of the Lord, teach His commandments out of covetousness, and pollute the holy things — lifting themselves up against the very commands of God. Malachi names this same ruin: the priests who departed from the way and corrupted the covenant of Levi. It ain't new — the prophet's lament over the corrupted priesthood is Levi's own foresight.

threads.title: The light of the law given to lighten every man
threads.summary_md: Levi names the light of the law which was given to lighten every man, and warns the priests who teach commandments contrary to the ordinances of God will darken Israel and the Gentiles. The Gospel calls this the true Light that lighteth every man. It ain't new — the law given as a light to every man is the same Light John proclaims.

threads.title: He who reneweth the law called a deceiver — innocent blood taken
threads.summary_md: Levi foretells that they shall make void the law, persecute righteous men, and call a deceiver the very man who reneweth the law in the power of the Most High — rushing upon him to slay him, not knowing his dignity, taking innocent blood upon their heads. The Gospel records this innocent blood and the man despised and rejected. It ain't new — the rejection of the righteous one and the innocent blood are foretold by the prophet and owned at the cross.

threads.title: Until He shall again visit you and in pity receive you
threads.summary_md: After the dispersion and the curse among the Gentiles, Levi promises the Lord shall again visit Israel and in pity receive them. Moses sealed the same hope: that the Lord will turn the captivity and gather His own from all the nations. It ain't new — the visiting mercy that gathers the scattered is the restoration promised in the Torah.

threads.title: The Lord shall raise up a new priest — a priest for ever
threads.summary_md: When the old priesthood has failed, Levi prophesies the Lord shall raise up a new priest to whom all the words of the Lord shall be revealed, who shall execute righteous judgment, and to whom there shall none succeed for all generations for ever. This is the priest sworn for ever after the order of Melchizedek, the changed priesthood of an endless life. It ain't new — the new and unending priest is the oath of the Psalms and the very argument of Hebrews.

threads.title: His star shall arise, he shall shine as the sun on the earth
threads.summary_md: Levi sees the new priest's star arise in heaven as of a king, lighting the light of knowledge as the sun the day; he shall shine forth as the sun on the earth, remove all darkness, and there shall be peace in all the earth. This is Balaam's Star out of Jacob and Malachi's Sun of righteousness with healing. It ain't new — the rising star and the shining Sun are spoken by Moses and the last of the prophets.

threads.title: The heavens opened, the Father's voice, the Spirit resting on him
threads.summary_md: Levi foresees the heavens opened over the new priest, sanctification coming upon him from the temple of glory with the Father's voice, and the spirit of understanding and sanctification resting upon him in the water. This is the very scene at the Jordan — the heavens opened, the Spirit descending, the Father's voice — and the Spirit of the Lord resting upon the Branch. It ain't new — the opened heaven, the Father's voice, and the resting Spirit are foretold in Isaiah and fulfilled in the Gospel.

threads.title: He shall open the gates of paradise and give to eat of the tree of life
threads.summary_md: Levi prophesies the new priest shall open the gates of paradise, remove the threatening sword against Adam, and give the saints to eat from the tree of life. The flaming sword that barred Eden is the sword Genesis set to keep the way of the tree of life — and the Revelation promises the overcomer to eat of that tree in the paradise of God. It ain't new — the re-opened gate of Eden and the tree of life are the first promise of Genesis brought to its end in the Revelation.

threads.title: Beliar shall be bound, and power given to tread on evil spirits
threads.summary_md: Levi foresees that in the new priest's days Beliar shall be bound, and he shall give power to His children to tread upon the evil spirits, while the patriarchs Abraham and Isaac and Jacob exult and the saints clothe themselves with joy. The Gospel gives this very power to tread on serpents, and the Revelation binds the adversary. It ain't new — the binding of the adversary and the power over the spirits are the authority the Lord gives His own.

threads.title: Choose the light or the darkness — the witnesses called
threads.summary_md: Levi sets before his sons the two ways — either the light or the darkness, either the law of the Lord or the works of Beliar — and calls the Lord, His angels, himself, and his sons to witness their choice to walk according to His law. This is the very charge Moses gave: life and death set before Israel, with heaven and earth called to record. It ain't new — the two ways and the summoned witnesses are Moses' own covenant call to choose life.

threads.title: Judah — the fourth son, named for thanksgiving, blessed to be king
threads.summary_md: Judah opens his deathbed testament by recalling his birth: the fourth son of Leah, named for her thanksgiving to Yahuah, and blessed by his father that he should be a king prospering in all things. It ain't new — Moses already records Leah's praise at his naming and the dying Jacob's scepter set upon Judah's tribe.

threads.title: Er and Onan — slain for their wickedness against Tamar
threads.summary_md: Judah recounts how his firstborn Er took Tamar, was wicked, and was smitten; and how Onan, refusing to raise up seed, spilled it on the ground and likewise died. It ain't new — Moses set down both deaths word for word, and the Torah's law of raising seed to a brother stands behind the whole account.

threads.title: Tamar withheld from Shelah — not of the daughters of Canaan
threads.summary_md: Bathshua works evil against Tamar and will not give Shelah to her because she was not of the daughters of Canaan — Judah's wife clinging to the very Canaanite kindred the Torah warned against. It ain't new — the Law had already forbidden marrying into the nations whose iniquity would turn the heart away.

threads.title: The Canaanite race was wicked — wine and youth blinded the mind
threads.summary_md: Judah confesses that he knew the race of the Canaanites was wicked, yet the impulse of youth and the intoxication of wine deceived him into taking Bathshua against his father's counsel. It ain't new — the Torah named the Canaanite defilement, and Proverbs already warned that wine bewitches the eyes and the heart.

threads.title: Tamar by the gate — the staff, the girdle, and the pledge
threads.summary_md: Drunk with wine and not knowing her, Judah turns aside to Tamar veiled by the gate, gives her his staff and girdle and the diadem of his kingdom in pledge, and afterward is put to shame by his own tokens. It ain't new — Moses tells the same episode, the same pledge, and Judah's own confession that she was the more righteous.

threads.title: Drunk with wine — the root of the abomination in Israel
threads.summary_md: Judah lays the whole fall to wine: being drunk he did not recognise her, and so wrought this abomination in Israel. It ain't new — Proverbs already warned that the red wine bites like a serpent, and Scripture forbids kings to drink lest they pervert judgment.

threads.title: Keep the ordinances of Yahuah — walk not after your lusts
threads.summary_md: Judah's first command to his sons is to keep all the ordinances of Yahuah and obey the commands of Elohim, and not to walk after their lusts or glory in the strength of youth, for that too is evil in His eyes. It ain't new — the testament only echoes the Torah's charge to keep the commandments and not to follow after one's own heart.

threads.title: The wine turned aside my eyes — pleasure blinded my heart
threads.summary_md: Judah confesses that wine turned aside his eyes and pleasure blinded his heart, so that he transgressed the commandment of Yahuah and his fathers. It ain't new — Proverbs already warned that the cup beholds strange women, and the apostle warns be not drunk with wine but filled with the Spirit.

threads.title: Be not drunk with wine — it turns the mind from truth
threads.summary_md: Judah charges his children not to be drunk with wine, for wine turns the mind from the truth, inspires the passion of lust, and leads the eyes into error; the drunkard reverences no man. It ain't new — Proverbs paints the same portrait of woe and redness of eyes, and the apostle gives the same command, be not drunk with wine.

threads.title: Even a king is stripped of his kingship by fornication
threads.summary_md: Judah warns that even a king who commits fornication becomes the slave of fornication and loses his glory — his staff the stay of his tribe, his girdle his power, his diadem the glory of his kingdom, all forfeited. It ain't new — Proverbs already warns that kings who drink forget the law and pervert judgment.

threads.title: Drink in gladness with the fear of Elohim — or touch it not at all
threads.summary_md: Judah names the four evil spirits in wine, and counsels that if his sons drink in gladness they be modest with the fear of Elohim, for when that fear departs drunkenness and shamelessness steal in. It ain't new — Proverbs already warns against tarrying long at the wine and the woe it brings.

threads.title: Love not money nor the beauty of women — the twin snares
threads.summary_md: Judah's parting command is to love not money nor gaze upon the beauty of women, for by money and beauty he was led astray to Bathshua. It ain't new — the apostle names the same root, the love of money, from which men err from the faith and pierce themselves through.

threads.title: From me shall the kingdom be established — the Davidic covenant
threads.summary_md: Judah declares that Isaac and Jacob both blessed him to be king in Israel, and that from him the kingdom shall be established. It ain't new — Jacob set the scepter on Judah's tribe, and Yahuah swore to establish David's throne, of Judah's seed, for ever.

threads.title: Fornication and the love of money withdraw a man from the law
threads.summary_md: Judah warns that fornication and the love of money withdraw a man from the law of Elohim, blind the soul, teach arrogance, and suffer not a man to have compassion upon his neighbour. It ain't new — the apostle calls the love of money the root from which men err from the faith, and the Torah commands love of neighbour the covetous heart refuses.

threads.title: The love of money leadeth to idolatry
threads.summary_md: Judah warns that the love of money leads to idolatry, for men led astray by money name as gods those who are not gods. It ain't new — the apostle plainly calls covetousness idolatry, and the Master taught that no man can serve both Elohim and mammon.

threads.title: Two spirits wait upon man — the heart known to Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Judah teaches that two spirits wait upon man, the spirit of truth and the spirit of deceit, and that the works of both are written on the heart, which Yahuah knows; no work of men can be hid, for it is written before the Lord. It ain't new — Moses set life and death before Israel to choose, and Jeremiah declares that Yahuah searches the heart and tries the reins.

threads.title: Love Levi — the priesthood set higher than the kingdom
threads.summary_md: Judah commands his sons to love Levi, for to Judah Yahuah gave the kingdom and to Levi the priesthood, and He set the kingdom beneath the priesthood: as heaven is higher than earth, so is the priesthood higher than the earthly kingdom. It ain't new — Zechariah foresaw the counsel of peace between the priest and the king, the priest upon his throne, and the Master of David's line is Himself a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

threads.title: The kings as sea-monsters and the false prophets like tempests
threads.summary_md: Judah prophesies that the latter kings shall be as sea-monsters swallowing men like fishes, plundering houses and lands, and that false prophets shall rise like tempests to persecute all righteous men. It ain't new — Jeremiah names the prophets who run unsent, and the Master warns of false prophets in sheep's clothing who inwardly are ravening wolves.

threads.title: Until the salvation of Israel and the Elohim of righteousness appear
threads.summary_md: Judah foresees his kingdom brought to an end among another race until the salvation of Israel shall come, the appearing of the Elohim of righteousness, that Jacob may rest in peace — for Yahuah sware that He would not destroy the kingdom from Judah's seed for ever. It ain't new — Jacob held the scepter to Judah until Shiloh come, Isaiah promised Israel an everlasting salvation in a just God and Saviour, and Yahuah's oath established David's throne for ever.

threads.title: Scattered for sin — until Yahuah visit you when ye repent
threads.summary_md: Judah foresees famine, sword, and enslavement among the Gentiles for idolatry and lewdness, until Yahuah visit His people when with perfect heart they repent, walk in all His commandments, and He brings them up from captivity. It ain't new — Moses set the same curse and the same mercy in the Law: scattered among the heathen, yet remembered and gathered when they confess and turn with all their heart.

threads.title: A star shall arise from Jacob — the Sun of righteousness
threads.summary_md: Judah's crowning prophecy: a star shall arise from Jacob in peace, and a man from his seed like the sun of righteousness, walking with men in meekness and righteousness, in whom no sin is found. It ain't new — Balaam saw the Star out of Jacob, Malachi the Sun of righteousness arising with healing, and the bright and morning star testifies He is the root and offspring of David.

threads.title: The heavens opened upon Him — the Spirit poured out
threads.summary_md: Judah foresees the heavens opened upon Him to pour out the spirit, the blessing of the Holy Father, and that He shall pour out the spirit of grace, so that they shall be unto Him sons in truth and walk in His commandments. It ain't new — the Spirit of Yahuah rests upon the Branch of Jesse, John beheld the Spirit descending and abiding on Him, and Joel foretold the Spirit poured out upon all flesh.

threads.title: This Branch of Elohim — the Fountain giving life unto all
threads.summary_md: Judah names Him the Branch of Elohim Most High, the Fountain giving life unto all. It ain't new — Isaiah saw a Branch grow out of the roots of Jesse, and Jeremiah and Zechariah named the righteous Branch raised unto David, Yahuah's servant the BRANCH who builds His temple.

threads.title: The sceptre shall shine — a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles
threads.summary_md: Judah foretells the sceptre of his kingdom shining forth, a stem from the root and a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, to judge and save all that call upon Yahuah. It ain't new — Balaam saw the Sceptre rise out of Israel, and Isaiah's root of Jesse stands as an ensign to which the Gentiles seek.

threads.title: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob shall arise unto life
threads.summary_md: Judah's last vision: Abraham and Isaac and Jacob shall arise unto life, and the patriarchs shall be chiefs of the tribes. It ain't new — Daniel foretold that they who sleep in the dust shall awake, Isaiah that the dead men shall live and rise, and the Master proved the resurrection from the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who is not the God of the dead but of the living.

threads.title: Beliar cast into the fire for ever — one people of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Judah foresees Israel made the people of Yahuah with one tongue, with no spirit of deceit of Beliar, for he shall be cast into the fire for ever. It ain't new — Ezekiel saw the dry bones come up out of their graves into the land, and Revelation the deceiver bound and cast away that he should deceive the nations no more.

threads.title: They who died in grief shall arise in joy
threads.summary_md: Judah foretells that they who died in grief shall arise in joy, and they who were put to death for Yahuah's sake shall awake to life. It ain't new — the apostle promised that Elohim will bring with Him them that sleep, and that the dead in Messiah shall rise; and Revelation pronounces blessed they who have part in the first resurrection.

threads.title: Carried up to Hebron — buried with his fathers
threads.summary_md: Judah closes with a charge to observe all the law of Yahuah, then asks to be carried up to Hebron and falls asleep, and his sons bury him in Hebron with his fathers. It ain't new — Jacob too charged his sons and was gathered to his people in the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham, Isaac, and Leah were laid.

threads.title: Issachar the husbandman — walking in singleness of eye
threads.summary_md: Issachar describes his upright life in one phrase: he walked in singleness of eye, no busybody, no slanderer, envying no neighbour. It ain't new — this is the single eye the Master praised, the bountiful eye Proverbs blesses, and the guileless heart of an Israelite indeed.

threads.title: First-fruits offered, the poor sustained
threads.summary_md: The husbandman brought all his first-fruits through the priest to Yahuah, and out of the singleness of his heart bestowed the good things of the earth on all the poor and oppressed. It ain't new — Torah commands the first-fruits, and the prophets and apostles make liberality to the poor its sister grace.

threads.title: The portrait of the single-minded man
threads.summary_md: Issachar paints the single-minded man: he covets no gold, overreaches no neighbour, lusts not after dainties or fine apparel, but waits only for the will of God and shuns the eye made evil by the world. It ain't new — this is the single eye full of light, the heart that lays up no earthly treasure, and the spirit in whom is no guile.

threads.title: Keep the law — love the Lord and thy neighbour
threads.summary_md: Issachar reduces the whole law to two commands: love Yahuah and your neighbour, have compassion on the poor and weak. It ain't new — this is the Shema and Leviticus joined, the two commandments on which the Master says all the law and the prophets hang.

threads.title: First-fruits and the blessing of the earth
threads.summary_md: Bow your back to husbandry, Issachar charges his sons, and offer first-fruits with thanksgiving, for with the first-fruits Yahuah will bless you as He blessed all the saints from Abel until now. It ain't new — the offering of first-fruits and the blessing of the fatness of the earth are Torah's own promise to the obedient land-keeper.

threads.title: Levi and Judah — the priesthood and the kingdom
threads.summary_md: Issachar bids his sons obey Levi and Judah, for Yahuah glorified them among Jacob's sons: to Levi He gave the priesthood, and to Judah the kingdom. It ain't new — the two tribes carry the joined hope of priest and king, the sceptre of Judah and the counsel of peace between the two offices the prophets foresaw fulfilled in the priest-king of David's and Levi's line.

threads.title: Dispersed among the Gentiles, brought back to their land
threads.summary_md: Issachar foresees his sons forsaking singleness and the commandments, dispersed among the Gentiles and serving their enemies — yet if they return, the merciful One will deliver them and bring them back into their land. It ain't new — this is the Torah's own cycle of scattering for sin and gathering for repentance, the two-house hope the prophets confirm.

threads.title: Guile arose not in my heart
threads.summary_md: At the last Issachar reckons his days: he knew no woman but his wife, drank no wine to be led astray, coveted nothing of his neighbour's — guile arose not in his heart, a lie passed not through his lips. It ain't new — this is the blessed man in whose spirit is no guile, the Israelite indeed the Master saw, the pure heart that shares its bread with the poor.

threads.title: I loved the Lord, and every man with all my heart
threads.summary_md: Issachar's final confession is the whole law lived out: I loved Yahuah, and likewise every man with all my heart; I shared my bread with the poor and joined my sighs with the distressed. It ain't new — this is the Shema and the love of neighbour fused, the love of God proven by the love of the brother.

threads.title: Zebulun adjures his brethren not to slay Joseph
threads.summary_md: Zebulun confesses he knew of no sin save the silence he kept over Joseph; he wept in secret and, when his brethren would have killed Joseph, he adjured them with tears not to be guilty of that sin. It ain't new — this is the very deliverance Reuben sought in Genesis, the inward grief over a brother's blood that Torah and Proverbs both forbid.

threads.title: Pity me, shed no innocent blood — the pit
threads.summary_md: Joseph pleads with his brothers to have mercy and lay not their hands upon him to shed innocent blood, and Reuben turns them from murder to the dry pit. It ain't new — Genesis tells the same restraint, and Moses and the Prophets set the guilt of innocent blood at the head of the things Yahuah hates.

threads.title: The loosed sandal — the writing of the law of Moses
threads.summary_md: Zebulun reads the brothers' fate by Torah: they bought sandals with the price of their brother's blood, and because they would not let their brother live, Yahuah loosed the sandal from them, and they were spit upon before Pharaoh. It ain't new — Zebulun cites the writing of the law of Moses by name, the levirate sandal that shames the man who will not raise up his brother.

threads.title: The coat, the kid of the goats, and Joseph sold
threads.summary_md: While the brothers ate by the pit, Zebulun and Judah fasted for pity of Joseph; then Joseph was sold, stripped of his coat, and the coat was dipped in the blood of a slain kid and sent to deceive Jacob. It ain't new — every detail here retells the bare Genesis account, the stripped coat and the kid of the goats that lied to a grieving father.

threads.title: Keep the commands and show mercy to thy neighbour
threads.summary_md: Zebulun's first charge is to keep the commands of Yahuah and to have compassion on every man — for as a man does to his neighbour, so will Yahuah do to him. It ain't new — this is Torah's love of neighbour, Wisdom's pity on the poor, and the measure with which the Master says we shall be measured.

threads.title: Compassion toward all — not toward men only, but beasts
threads.summary_md: Zebulun widens mercy to the whole creation: have compassion not toward men only but also toward beasts; for this thing Yahuah blessed and kept him from sickness. It ain't new — Torah's righteous man regards the life of his beast, and the prophets weigh mercy above sacrifice.

threads.title: He shared his catch with every stranger
threads.summary_md: Zebulun the fisherman boiled and dressed his fish and offered them to every stranger, sick, and aged as each had need, grieving with them in compassion. It ain't new — Torah and the Wisdom of the fathers command an open hand to the poor and the stranger, and the Master receives such kindness as done to himself.

threads.title: He that shareth with his neighbour receiveth manifold more
threads.summary_md: Because Zebulun shared, Yahuah satisfied him with abundance of fish — for he that shares with his neighbour receives manifold more from Yahuah. It ain't new — this is the scattering that yet increases, the watering soul that is itself watered, the storehouse of alms the fathers commend.

threads.title: He clothed the naked man in winter
threads.summary_md: Zebulun saw a man in distress through nakedness in the winter-time, had compassion, and gave him a garment; and where his hand found nothing to give, he wept with the needy and his bowels yearned in compassion. It ain't new — clothing the naked is the mercy the Master counts to himself, and pity itself is reckoned where the hand is empty.

threads.title: Have compassion, that Yahuah may have compassion on you
threads.summary_md: Have compassion toward every man with mercy, says Zebulun, that Yahuah also may have mercy on you; for in the last days Elohim sends his compassion, and wheresoever he finds bowels of mercy he dwells therein. It ain't new — the merciful obtain mercy, and the Father's own mercy is the measure he sets his children.

threads.title: Joseph bore no malice — love one another
threads.summary_md: When they went down into Egypt Joseph bore no malice; so, says Zebulun, approve yourselves without malice and love one another, setting down no evil against a brother, for malice breaks unity. It ain't new — Joseph forgiving the evil meant against him is the Genesis pattern, and the apostle bids the same kindness, forgiving one another.

threads.title: Be not divided into two heads — the two kingdoms
threads.summary_md: Zebulun warns that as waters divided into many streams are swallowed up, so Israel shall be divided and follow two kings and work every abomination. It ain't new — this is the very rending of the kingdom the prophets foretold, and the two sticks Ezekiel saw joined again into one in Yahuah's hand.

threads.title: Led captive among the Gentiles, then He shall have mercy
threads.summary_md: For their division Israel's enemies shall lead them captive among the Gentiles; but afterward they shall remember Yahuah and repent, and He shall have mercy, for He is merciful and compassionate. It ain't new — Moses set this very turning before them, that when they call their captivity to mind and return, Yahuah will have compassion and gather them.

threads.title: Yahuah Himself, the light of righteousness, and ye shall return
threads.summary_md: Then shall arise unto you Yahuah Himself, the light of righteousness, and ye shall return unto your own land and see Him in Jerusalem for His name's sake. It ain't new — this is the Sun of righteousness that arises with healing, the great light upon them that walked in darkness, the glory risen upon Zion when her scattered sons are gathered home.

threads.title: Grieve not — I shall rise again in the midst of you
threads.summary_md: Zebulun bids his sons not grieve at his death, for he shall rise again in the midst of them as a ruler among his sons and rejoice in his tribe, as many as keep the law of Yahuah. It ain't new — the dead shall awake from the dust, the sleepers shall arise and sing, and the patriarch is laid with his fathers in Hebron.

threads.title: Truth pleases God; lying and anger teach all wickedness
threads.summary_md: Dan's opening confession sets the whole testament's frame: truth with just dealing pleases God, while lying and anger are the twin evils that teach a man every wickedness. The apostles say nothing different — put away lying and speak truth, and be angry without sinning. It ain't new: the choice between the spirit of truth and the spirit of lying runs straight back through Moses and the Prophets.

threads.title: The spirit of Beliar stirs up the sword against Joseph
threads.summary_md: Dan confesses that a spirit of Beliar put a sword in his heart against Joseph the true and good man — but the God of his fathers would not suffer it, sparing a second tribe from destruction in Israel. The Gospel names this prompter: the devil, a murderer and the father of lies from the beginning. It ain't new — envy that reaches for a brother's blood is the old serpent's work, restrained by the God who keeps His own.

threads.title: Anger is blindness; love truth and longsuffering
threads.summary_md: Dying Dan presses one charge home: keep yourselves from lying and anger and love truth and longsuffering, or you perish, for anger is a blindness that lets a man see no father, brother, prophet, or friend, and ends in hatred and envy. The apostles preach the cure in the same breath — be swift to hear, slow to wrath, longsuffering, putting away bitterness. It ain't new: wrath blinds, but the slow-to-anger walk in great understanding.

threads.title: Wrath joined to lying — and the Lord departs, Beliar rules
threads.summary_md: Dan draws the line to its end: wrath joined with lying is a twofold mischief that keeps the heart in turmoil, and when the soul is continually disturbed the Lord departs from it and Beliar rules over it. The Gospel names the same exchange — when truth is forsaken the father of lies takes the house, and Paul says give no place to the devil. It ain't new: where wrath and falsehood dwell, the Lord will not, and the enemy moves in.

threads.title: Salvation of the Lord arises from Judah and Levi; Beliar's war ended
threads.summary_md: Dan's great prophecy: out of the tribe of Judah and of Levi shall arise the salvation of the Lord, who shall make war against Beliar, take the captivity from him, turn disobedient hearts to the Lord, and give eternal peace. This is the priest-king of David's and Levi's joined hope — the Branch who is both king and priest, the Star out of Jacob. It ain't new: the counsel of peace between throne and altar is Zechariah's and Balaam's word, fulfilled in the Anointed who binds the enemy and brings His people home.

threads.title: He shall make war against Beliar — the dragon bound
threads.summary_md: The salvation from Judah and Levi makes war against Beliar and takes from him the captivity of the souls of the saints. John sees the same triumph: an angel lays hold on the dragon, the old serpent, and binds him. It ain't new — the enemy who held Israel captive is the serpent of Eden, and the Anointed comes to bind him and set the captives free.

threads.title: The saints rest in Eden; the righteous rejoice in the New Jerusalem
threads.summary_md: Dan's hope rises to its height: the saints shall rest in Eden, and in the New Jerusalem the righteous shall rejoice, to the glory of God for ever. John sees the holy city come down and the tree and river of Eden restored within it; Isaiah hears God create new heavens and a Jerusalem of rejoicing. It ain't new — the garden lost in Genesis is the city gained in Revelation, and Dan names both in one breath.

threads.title: Return to the Lord and be gathered; no more captivity
threads.summary_md: Dan foresees Israel led into captivity for sin, then returning to the Lord to obtain mercy, brought into His sanctuary, and Jerusalem no longer left desolate nor Israel led captive, for the Lord shall be in the midst of it. This is the two-house gathering Moses and Ezekiel promised: scattered for sin, gathered through repentance, made one nation under one shepherd. It ain't new — the Lord who scatters is the Lord who gathers and dwells among His people.

threads.title: Draw near to the mediator between God and man
threads.summary_md: Dan bids his sons draw near to God and to the one who intercedes for them — a mediator between God and man who stands up for Israel's peace against the kingdom of the enemy. Paul names one mediator between God and men, the man Messiah Yahusha, who ever lives to make intercession. It ain't new: the appointed Anointed who stands between God and His people, pleading their peace, is the priest-king of Levi and Judah's hope.

threads.title: When Israel repents, the kingdom of the enemy is ended
threads.summary_md: Dan foretells that on the day Israel repents, the kingdom of the enemy is brought to an end, the Lord will not depart but transform them into a nation that does His will, and His name shall be in every place of Israel and among the Gentiles. This is Moses' promise of return and gathering, and Ezekiel's of a cleansed people the Lord saves and dwells among. It ain't new — repentance ends the enemy's reign and the Lord makes His scattered people His own again.

threads.title: Born of Bilhah upon Rachel's knees — Naphtali and Joseph
threads.summary_md: Naphtali opens his deathbed testament by confessing his birth: he was born of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid, upon Rachel's knees, and Rachel longed for a true brother of her own womb — whence Joseph was like unto him. The patriarch only retells what Moses already wrote. It ain't new — Genesis records that Bilhah bore Jacob a second son whom Rachel named Naphtali, and that Rachel's own sons were Joseph and Benjamin.

threads.title: As the potter knoweth the vessel — Yahuah forms body and spirit
threads.summary_md: Naphtali likens the Maker to a potter who knows how much each vessel will hold and brings clay accordingly: so Yahuah forms the body after the likeness of the spirit, and knows every inclination and thought, for He created every man after His own image. The figure is not Naphtali's invention. It ain't new — Isaiah and Jeremiah called Yahuah the potter and Israel the clay, and the psalmist confessed he was fearfully and wonderfully made, his frame searched and known.

threads.title: God made all things good in their order — do nothing disorderly
threads.summary_md: Naphtali marvels at the ordered frame of the body — the senses set in their places, each member to its work — and concludes that as God made all things good in their order, so His children should do all their works in order and in the fear of God, doing nothing disorderly or out of its due season. The order is borrowed from creation itself. It ain't new — God divided light from darkness and saw that every thing He had made was very good.

threads.title: Sun, moon and stars change not their order — change not the law of God
threads.summary_md: Naphtali points to the firmament: sun and moon and stars change not their order, and bids his children likewise not change the law of God in the disorderliness of their doings — recognising in heaven, earth and sea the LORD who made all things. The witness of the ordered heavens is no new argument. It ain't new — Moses set the lights in the firmament for signs and seasons, the psalmist heard the heavens declare the glory of God, and Paul read His eternal power in the things that are made.

threads.title: Sodom and the Watchers changed the order of nature
threads.summary_md: Naphtali warns his children not to become as Sodom, which changed the order of nature, nor as the Watchers who likewise changed the order of their nature, whom Yahuah (the LORD) cursed at the flood. The Gentiles forsook their Maker and served stocks and stones; the children of Elohim (God) must not. It ain't new — Genesis tells of Sodom and of the sons of Elohim (God) who took wives of the daughters of men, Enoch tells how the Watchers left their own high place and corrupted the earth, and Jude sets both side by side as a warning of the vengeance reserved for them: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* (Jude 1:6).

threads.title: Captivity for sin, then mercy — a man working righteousness to those near and far off
threads.summary_md: Reading in the writing of Enoch, Naphtali foresees Israel departing after the lawlessness of the Gentiles, brought into captivity, then made few, returning to acknowledge the LORD their God who brings them back according to His abundant mercy — until the compassion of the LORD shall come, a man working righteousness and mercy unto them that are afar off and them that are near. This is the long-foretold shape of the scattering and gathering. It ain't new — Moses promised that the LORD would gather Israel from the outmost parts of heaven, Ezekiel that He would make the two houses one, and the apostle that peace is preached to them afar off and to them that are near.

threads.title: Levi laid hold of the sun, Judah seized the moon — the joined hope
threads.summary_md: In a vision on the Mount of Olives Naphtali sees the sun and moon standing still; Levi lays hold of the sun and Judah seizes the moon, and both are lifted up — Levi shining as a sun with twelve branches of palm, Judah bright as the moon with twelve rays beneath their feet. Beneath the dream-figure is the one settled hope of the Testaments: salvation from Levi and Judah together, the priest and the king. It ain't new — the sun and moon of dream are Joseph's own vision, and the Star out of Jacob is the anointed of the joined tribes.

threads.title: A holy writing — the nations shall possess the twelve tribes in captivity
threads.summary_md: The vision closes with a bull that Joseph alone seizes and carries up on high, and a holy writing declaring that Assyrians, Medes, Persians and Syrians shall possess the twelve tribes of Israel in captivity. The foretelling of the scattering is no novelty. It ain't new — Moses warned of captivity among the nations, and Ezekiel foresaw the gathering of the scattered house that follows.

threads.title: The ship of Jacob — scattered to the ends of the earth, gathered in peace
threads.summary_md: In a second dream the ship of Jacob is broken up in a tempest and all the sons are scattered unto the ends of the earth — yet Levi and Judah are together, Levi prays in sackcloth for them all, and when the storm ceases the ship reaches land in peace and the father returns and all rejoice. The figure is the scattering and gathering of Israel, kept by the joined priest and king. It ain't new — Moses foretold the driving to the outmost parts of heaven and the gathering home, and Ezekiel the reuniting of the two houses into one.

threads.title: Be united to Levi and to Judah — through them salvation arises
threads.summary_md: Naphtali charges his children to be united to Levi and to Judah, for through them shall salvation arise unto Israel and in them shall Jacob be blessed. This is the spine of all twelve Testaments: the priest of Levi and the king of Judah joined in one anointed hope. It ain't new — Balaam saw the Star out of Jacob, Zechariah the priest upon his throne with the counsel of peace between the two, and the blessing of Jacob rested the sceptre upon Judah.

threads.title: God shall appear, dwelling among men, to save Israel and gather the Gentiles
threads.summary_md: Through the tribes of Levi and Judah, Naphtali prophesies, God shall appear, dwelling among men on earth, to save the race of Israel and to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles. The Father made Himself manifest in the Anointed of the joined tribes — come to dwell, to save His people, and to draw the nations in. It ain't new — Zechariah heard the LORD say He would dwell in the midst of Zion and many nations be joined to Him; the prophet set up an ensign for the nations and gathered the outcasts; and the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us, Immanuel, God with us.

threads.title: The commandments of the law are twofold — kept in due order and prudence
threads.summary_md: Naphtali closes by teaching that the commandments of the law are twofold and must be fulfilled through prudence and in due order — a season to embrace and a season to abstain for prayer — that the LORD may love them. The law is honoured, not loosed; it is to be understood and kept wisely. It ain't new — there is a season to every purpose under heaven, and the wise lay hold of the order of God's commandments.

threads.title: Gad and the brothers — Joseph's report to their father
