threads.title: Thou hast made me the head of the heathen — the dominion over the nations
threads.summary_md: The warrior-king is set over the nations: *Thou hast delivered me from the strivings of the people; and thou hast made me the head of the heathen: a people whom I have not known shall serve me. As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me: the strangers shall submit themselves unto me* (Psalm 18:43-44). The twin song sings it again — *thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me* (2 Samuel 22:44). And it reaches back to Moses' song, where the nations are drawn in to provoke Yashar'el (Israel) to jealousy: *I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation* (Deuteronomy 32:21). The dominion of the Davidic king over the nations is no replacement of the people but the gathering of the heathen to the throne of the seed — resolved in the psalm's close, where David gives thanks *among the heathen* and the nations sing WITH his people.

threads.title: Thanks among the heathen, and mercy to his seed for evermore — Paul quotes the close
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes with the nations and the seed: *Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O Yahuah (LORD), among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name. Great deliverance giveth he to his king; and sheweth mercy to his anointed, to David, and to his seed for evermore* (Psalm 18:49-50). Paul lifts verse 49 word for word into his proof that the nations glorify Elohim WITH His people: *that the Gentiles might glorify Elohim (God) for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name* (Romans 15:9). This is the ingathering, never a replacement — the heathen join David's praise, they do not supplant Yashar'el (Israel) (the Rom 11:1-2 guard). The twin song carries the same close (2 Samuel 22:50). And the mercy *to David, and to his seed for evermore* (18:50) rests on Nathan's covenant — *I will set up thy seed after thee... and I will establish his kingdom* (2 Samuel 7:12), *I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever* (2 Samuel 7:13) — fulfilled in the One given *the throne of his father David* who *shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end* (Luke 1:32-33). The seed for evermore is the Messiah enthroned, and the nations sing His praise WITH the restored house.

threads.title: The name of the Elohim of Jacob defend thee — help and strength out of Zion
threads.summary_md: Psalm 20 is the congregation's intercession over the anointed king before battle: *Yahuah (LORD) hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the Elohim (God) of Jacob defend thee; Send thee help from the sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion* (Psalm 20:1-2). The king's defence is not his own arm but the Name of the covenant-keeping Elohim of the patriarch Jacob, and the strength sent *out of Zion*. That strength out of Zion is the rod the Davidic King receives: *Yahuah (LORD) shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies* (Psalm 110:2). And the people's posture is the psalter's own confession: *Our soul waiteth for Yahuah (LORD): he is our help and our shield* (Psalm 33:20). The petitions rise — *Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfil all thy counsel* (20:4), *in the name of our Elohim (God) we will set up our banners* (20:5) — and the psalm closes where it began, with the cry over the king: *Save, Yahuah (LORD): let the king hear us when we call* (20:9). The whole intercession rests on the Name: the Elohim of Jacob, who sends help from the sanctuary and strength out of Zion, is the king's defence.

threads.title: Yahuah saveth his anointed — the Mashiach saved from the holy heaven, the King at the right hand
threads.summary_md: The hinge of the psalm: *Now know I that Yahuah (LORD) saveth his anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven with the saving strength of his right hand* (Psalm 20:6). His anointed is his Mashiach. The psalter sets the same word against the raging kings: *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2), and Yahuah answers *Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion* (Psalm 2:6). The *saving strength of his right hand* is the seat the King is given: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool* (Psalm 110:1). The restored assembly reads Psalm 2 of the Anointed by name: *The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against Yahuah (Lord), and against his Messiah (Christ)* (Acts 4:26), *against thy holy child Yahusha (Jesus), whom thou hast anointed* (Acts 4:27); and names the right hand of the psalm as his exaltation — *being by the right hand of Elohim (God) exalted, and having received of the Father the promise of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* (Acts 2:33). Read through the Formed and the Formless: Yahuah saves his Anointed, hears him from his holy heaven, sets him at his own right hand. The Anointed is Yahuah's own, and he has a Father; he received from the Father, and was exalted by the right hand that saved him.

threads.title: Some trust in chariots — but we will remember the name (the name-trust against the arm of flesh)
threads.summary_md: The keystone of the psalm: *Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)* (Psalm 20:7). This is the spine of the prophets' rebuke of the arm of flesh. Isaiah pronounces the woe on Egypt-trust: *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!* (Isaiah 31:1), and gives the reason — *the Egyptians are men, and not Elohim (God); and their horses flesh, and not spirit* (Isaiah 31:3). Zechariah names it as Spirit-not-strength: *Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Zechariah 4:6). The proverb gives the plain maxim: *The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 21:31). And the psalter says it without the figure: *There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength. An horse is a vain thing for safety* (Psalm 33:16-17). The outcome is the psalm's own verdict: the chariot-trusters *are brought down and fallen: but we are risen, and stand upright* (Psalm 20:8). The arm of flesh fails together; those who remember the Name stand. The whole battle is decided by the Name of Yahuah, never by the chariot and the horse.

threads.title: Thou settest a crown of pure gold on his head — the king crowned with glory and majesty
threads.summary_md: Psalm 21 is the answered companion to Psalm 20: where Psalm 20 petitioned — *Grant thee according to thine own heart... Yahuah (LORD) fulfil all thy petitions* (Psalm 20:4-5) — Psalm 21 receives. The king rejoices in Yahuah's salvation (21:1), and is crowned: *For thou preventest him with the blessings of goodness: thou settest a crown of pure gold on his head* (Psalm 21:3); *His glory is great in thy salvation: honour and majesty hast thou laid upon him* (Psalm 21:5); *thou hast made him most blessed for ever* (Psalm 21:6). Read FORWARD to the Formed Son crowned in flesh: *we see Yahusha (Jesus), who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of Elohim (God) should taste death for every man* (Hebrews 2:9) — the very *honour and majesty* Yahuah lays on the king is the *glory and honour* with which the King who tasted death is crowned. And the crowning is consummated in the apocalypse: *on his head were many crowns* (Revelation 19:12) — the one crown of pure gold multiplied into the diadems of the One who judges in righteousness; *upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown* (Revelation 14:14) — the gold of the psalm on the head of the seed-of-Adam King come to reap. The Father (Yahuah, the Formless) crowns; the Son (the Formed) is crowned, and he has a Father.

threads.title: He asked life of thee, and thou gavest it him — length of days for ever and ever
threads.summary_md: The keystone of the psalm: *He asked life of thee, and thou gavest it him, even length of days for ever and ever* (Psalm 21:4). The king asks LIFE — and is given not a long reign but *length of days for ever and ever*, the resurrection and endless life of the King. Peter reads David's own psalm of the risen One: *Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption* (Acts 2:27); *Thou hast made known to me the ways of life; thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance* (Acts 2:28) — the life asked and given, the King *not left in hell*, *full of joy with thy countenance* answering the psalm's own *thou hast made him exceeding glad with thy countenance* (21:6). Hebrews names the order of that life: the priest *made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life* (Hebrews 7:16) — the *length of days for ever and ever* is the indestructible life of the priest-King after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek). And the king who ASKS and is GIVEN is the begotten King of Psalm 2: *Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance* (Psalm 2:8). The Formed Son asks life of the Father and receives it for ever; he is Yahuah, and he has a Father who gives.

threads.title: Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven — the day that burns as an oven, the winepress of wrath
threads.summary_md: The judgment side of the King's reign closes the psalm. Against those who *intended evil against thee* and *imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform* (Psalm 21:11): *Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: Yahuah (LORD) shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them* (Psalm 21:9), *Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men* (Psalm 21:10). This is conduct-within-the-covenant judgment, the rout of the rebel device, never ethnic enmity. Malachi names the same oven as the Day itself: *For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), that it shall leave them neither root nor branch* (Malachi 4:1) — the *fiery oven in the time of thine anger* is the burning Day of Yahuah that leaves *neither root nor branch*, even as the psalm destroys *their fruit... and their seed*. And the apocalypse shows the crowned King treading it: *out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations... and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God)* (Revelation 19:15) — the wrath that swallows up the proud is the winepress the King treads.

threads.title: Walking in truth, as we received commandment from the Father (Psalm 86 / Psalm 119)
threads.summary_md: *I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father* (2 John 4). To walk in truth is the psalmist's prayer and the psalmist's blessing: *teach me thy way, O Yahuah (LORD); I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name* (Psalm 86:11), and *blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 119:1). The truth John's children walk in is the commandment received from the Father — Yahuah's taught way, the undefiled path of the Torah, kept with an undivided heart. Walking *in truth* and walking *in the law* are one walk.

threads.title: Abide in the doctrine; whosoever transgresseth (anomia) hath not Elohim (Deuteronomy 13 / Psalm 1)
threads.summary_md: *Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Messiah (Christ), hath not Elohim (God)... If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house* (2 John 9-10). The word *transgresseth* is the same anomia — law-breaking — that the elder's first letter defines: *sin is the transgression of the law* (1 John 3:4). To leave the doctrine is to break the Torah. And the refusal to harbour the false teacher is Moses' own: when even the nearest *entice thee secretly... thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him... neither shalt thou conceal him* (Deuteronomy 13:6,8). The blessed man *walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor... sitteth in the seat of the scornful* (Psalm 1:1) — he keeps his footing in the doctrine and does not sit down with the one who would lead the assembly astray. The doctrine and the law are of one piece.

threads.title: Deceivers who confess not Yahusha come in the flesh = antichrist (Deuteronomy 13 / Isaiah 8)
threads.summary_md: *For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist* (2 John 7). The Torah gave the test of the false prophet long before: he is not proved by a sign or wonder but by whether he turns the people toward or away from Yahuah — *thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet... for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) proveth you* (Deuteronomy 13:1,3), and the one who *hath spoken to turn you away from Yahuah... shall be put to death* (Deuteronomy 13:5). The presumptuous prophet who speaks a word Yahuah has not commanded *shall die* (Deuteronomy 18:20), and is known when *the thing follow not* (Deuteronomy 18:22). The measuring-line is Isaiah's: *to the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them* (Isaiah 8:20). The elder's first letter says the same — *try the spirits* (1 John 4:1), for *every spirit that confesseth not that Yahusha... is come in the flesh... is that spirit of antichrist* (1 John 4:3). The deceiver is tried by the law and the testimony, not believed for his signs.

threads.title: The commandment from the beginning: love is to walk after His commandments (Deuteronomy 6 / Leviticus 19)
threads.summary_md: 2 John's center: *not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another. And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it* (2 John 5-6). The elder EXPRESSLY denies a new law — the commandment is *that which we had from the beginning,* and love itself is defined as walking after His commandments. The root is the Shema and the love-command of the Torah: *thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart* (Deuteronomy 6:5), *these words... shall be in thine heart* (Deuteronomy 6:6), *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself* (Leviticus 19:18), *ye shall walk in all the ways which Yahuah... hath commanded you* (Deuteronomy 5:33), *to walk in all his ways, and to love him* (Deuteronomy 10:12). The second-Temple sages had already fused the two: *they that love him will keep his ways* (Sirach 2:15), *they that love him shall be filled with the law* (Sirach 2:16). And the elder's own first letter says it twice over — *an old commandment which ye had from the beginning* (1 John 2:7), *this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments* (1 John 5:3). Love is not a sentiment that replaces the Torah; love IS walking after His commandments. The commandment is old, from the beginning, the Torah — and it stands.

threads.title: Follow not evil but good — he that doeth good is of Elohim: the Two-Ways test (Psalm 34, 37; Isaiah 1; Amos 5)
threads.summary_md: The framework center of the whole letter stands here: *Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of Elohim (God): but he that doeth evil hath not seen Elohim (God)* (3 John 11). This is the Two-Ways test — conduct is the proof of belonging to Yahuah (LORD), the same evidentiary master-filter as John's first letter, where knowing Him is shown by the deed. The two ways are set at the very root of the Torah: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15) — the choice in every deed. The Psalms carry the charge twice over: *Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it* (Psalm 34:14), and *Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore* (Psalm 37:27), binding the doing of good to abiding with Yahuah (LORD) for ever. Isaiah gives both halves of the test in order — *cease to do evil; learn to do well* (Isaiah 1:16-17), filling out the good with justice to the oppressed, the fatherless, the widow. Amos sharpens it into the affections and joins it to life and to Yahuah's (LORD's) presence: *Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live... Hate the evil, and love the good* (Amos 5:14-15). And wisdom binds it to the fear of Yahuah (LORD): *fear Yahuah (LORD), and depart from evil* (Proverbs 3:7). John's own first letter speaks the test almost word for word — *he that doeth righteousness is righteous* (1 John 3:7), and *whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of Elohim (God), neither he that loveth not his brother* (1 John 3:10): the deed makes manifest whose children men are. There is no replacement here and no law-against-grace: doing good and turning from evil is the Torah's own measure, the standard by which a man is shown to be of Elohim (God). Conduct is the proof.

threads.title: Walking in the truth (Psalm 86, 119; 1 Kings 2; 2 Kings 20)
threads.summary_md: John's joy over Gaius is a Tanakh joy: *I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth* (3 John 3-4). To walk in the truth is an ancient path. David prays it: *Teach me thy way, O Yahuah (LORD); I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name* (Psalm 86:11). The long psalm of the Torah names its blessing: *Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 119:1) — for to walk in the truth is to walk in His law, His undefiled way. It is the covenant condition David charged upon Solomon: *to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul* (1 Kings 2:4); and the plea Hezekiah made on his bed: *remember now how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight* (2 Kings 20:3) — joining, in one breath, walking in truth and doing good, the two notes of this whole letter. And the sister-letter opens with the identical phrase and the identical joy: *I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father* (2 John 4). The truth walked in is Yahuah's (LORD's) own way, kept with the whole heart — not merely held, but done.

threads.title: Receiving the brethren, fellowhelpers to the truth — love the stranger (Genesis 18; Leviticus 19; Deuteronomy 10; Isaiah 58)
threads.summary_md: John praises Gaius for the open door: *Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers... We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth* (3 John 5,8). The receiving of the sent ones is no new ethic but the keeping of the Torah's love-the-stranger. The pattern begins with Abraham at the tent door: *And he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door* (Genesis 18:2), setting butter and milk and the dressed calf before them (Genesis 18:8) — and *thereby some have entertained angels unawares* (Hebrews 13:2). The law commands it outright: *the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt* (Leviticus 19:34); and again, *Love ye therefore the stranger: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt* (Deuteronomy 10:19) — for Yahuah (LORD) Himself *loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment* (Deuteronomy 10:18), and those who are His imitate Him. It is the fast Yahuah (LORD) chooses: *to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house... and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh* (Isaiah 58:7). The restored library teaches the same hand to the needy — *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked* (Tobit 4:16); *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected* (Sirach 7:32). And the King makes it a receiving of Himself: *I was a stranger, and ye took me in* (Matthew 25:35); so the apostolic word, *given to hospitality* (Romans 12:13). To receive the brethren *for his name's sake* (3 John 7) is to keep the Torah's love of the stranger and to become a fellowhelper to the truth.

threads.title: Enoch the seventh from Adam prophesied — Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 by name (1 Enoch 1; Deuteronomy 33, Zechariah 14)
threads.summary_md: An apostle, the brother of James, quotes Enoch by name, and the words he quotes are on the page of the book the Reformation cut out. *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him* (Jude 1:14-15). This is a direct quotation of 1 Enoch 1:9 — *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9). Word for word: the ten thousands, the judgment upon all, the conviction of all flesh of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him. Jude names the prophet — *Enoch, the seventh from Adam* — and the genealogy of the Torah proves the title: Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, Jared, *and he begat Enoch* (Genesis 5:18), the seventh, who *walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him* (Genesis 5:24). And the word Enoch prophesied is itself rooted in the Tanakh both he and Jude draw on: *Yahuah (LORD) came from Sinai... and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them* (Deuteronomy 33:2), and *Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God) shall come, and all the saints with thee* (Zechariah 14:5). One coming, foretold from Sinai to Enoch to Zechariah, and cited by an apostle as prophecy. The library is one; it ain't new. Jude wields the seventh from Adam's prophecy against the ungodly who turn grace into lasciviousness — the Master cometh with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment, and grace is no escape from that day.

threads.title: The angels which kept not their first estate — the Watchers reserved in everlasting chains (Genesis 6; 1 Enoch 10, 13, 21; Jubilees 5; 1 Peter 3, 2 Peter 2)
threads.summary_md: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). These are the Watchers — the *sons of Elohim (God)* of Genesis 6 who *saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives,* and *there were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:1-4). They left their own habitation and broke the bound order, and the library tells in full what Jude names in brief. Yahuah (God) commanded, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness... on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire* (1 Enoch 10:4-6). For Semjaza and his company the order was the same, with the term of it fixed: *And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.* (1 Enoch 10:12), and then to be *led off to the abyss of fire... the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13). Enoch was sent to pronounce the sentence already gone forth: *Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds* (1 Enoch 13:1); and on his journeys he was shown the place itself: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees says the same: the angels are *bound in the depths of the earth... for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:6,10). This is the third canonical pass over the Watchers — Peter wrote it twice: the *spirits in prison... in the days of Noah* to whom the Formed Son preached (1 Peter 3:19-20), and *the angels that sinned... delivered into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). Jude, Peter, Genesis, 1 Enoch, and Jubilees hold one settled witness: the everlasting chains, the darkness, the judgment of the great day. The faith once delivered names the Watchers as Jude names them; the antinomians who left the faith are warned by the angels who left their estate.

threads.title: Michael disputing about the body of Moses — the Master rebuke thee (the Assumption of Moses; Zechariah 3, Deuteronomy 34, Daniel 10)
threads.summary_md: *Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, Yahuah (Lord) rebuke thee* (Jude 1:9). Jude draws this scene from the Assumption of Moses — the lost ending of that work, which told how Michael contended with the devil over the body of the servant of Yahuah (LORD). No clean witness of the Assumption of Moses survives in the restored editions of the library, but its roots run straight through the Tanakh. The Torah closes Moses' story with a hidden grave: *he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab... but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day* (Deuteronomy 34:6) — the unknown sepulchre is the very point of the dispute. The words Michael speaks are Zechariah's: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto Satan, Yahuah (LORD) rebuke thee, O Satan... is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?* (Zechariah 3:2), where the angel of Yahuah (LORD) stands against the accuser and leaves the rebuke to Yahuah (LORD) alone. And the Michael who contends is Daniel's: *Michael, one of the chief princes* (Daniel 10:13), *Michael your prince* (Daniel 10:21), who *shall stand up... for the children of thy people* (Daniel 12:1) — the guardian of Yashar'el (Israel). Peter states the principle Jude shows: *angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before Yahuah (Lord)* (2 Peter 2:11). Even the archangel does not rail against the devil but yields the rebuke to the Master; how much less may the filthy dreamers who *speak evil of dignities* (Jude 1:8). The library and the canon hold one testimony, and the apostle reads the Assumption of Moses as the witness it is.

threads.title: The way of Cain, the error of Balaam, the gainsaying of Korah — three rebels of the Torah (Genesis 4, Numbers 16, Numbers 22-31; Wisdom 10, Sirach 45; 1 John 3, 2 Peter 2)
threads.summary_md: *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core (Korah)* (Jude 1:11). Jude marshals three judgments of the Torah against the ungodly. The way of Cain: *Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him* (Genesis 4:8) — the way of envy that hates and murders the righteous; the library reads him the same, *he perished also in the fury with which he murdered his brother* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3), and so does John, *not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother... because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous* (1 John 3:12). The error of Balaam: the prophet who *loved the wages of unrighteousness* and by *the counsel of Balaam* taught Yashar'el (Israel) to trespass at Peor (Numbers 31:16) — *ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward,* the same path Peter names, *following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness* (2 Peter 2:15). The gainsaying of Korah: who rose against the order Yahuah (LORD) appointed, until *the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up... they went down alive into the pit* (Numbers 16:32-33); Sirach remembers *the congregation of Core (Korah)... in his wrathful indignation were they consumed... with the fiery flame* (Sirach 45:18-19). Envy, hire, and rebellion — three roads to ruin, every one a witness that Yahuah judges the lawless, and the antinomians who turn grace into lasciviousness walk all three.

threads.title: The Master saved a people, and afterward destroyed them that believed not (Numbers 14, Psalm 95, 1 Corinthians 10)
threads.summary_md: *I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that Yahuah (Lord), having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not* (Jude 1:5). The first of Jude's judgment-witnesses, and the sharpest against presumption: the same people Yahuah (Lord) brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand he afterward destroyed in the wilderness for unbelief. *Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness... which have murmured against me* (Numbers 14:29); *in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die* (Numbers 14:35). The Psalm holds it up as the standing warning: *Harden not your heart, as in the provocation... Unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest* (Psalm 95:8,11). And Paul wields it exactly as Jude does: *they were overthrown in the wilderness... Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples... Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall* (1 Corinthians 10:5,11-12), with the murmurers *destroyed of the destroyer* (1 Corinthians 10:10) — the very murmurers Jude marks (Jude 1:16). Salvation out of Egypt did not exempt the faithless from judgment; the redeemed who fall into unbelief fall under the same sentence. Grace is no licence, and the deliverance is no charm against the judgment of the great day.

threads.title: Sodom and Gomorrha set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire (Genesis 19; Wisdom 10; 2 Peter 2)
threads.summary_md: *Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire* (Jude 1:7). The third judgment-witness, set deliberately beside the Watchers of the verse before: the *going after strange flesh* of Sodom parallels the angels who left their habitation — the same transgression of the bound order. The men of the city *compassed the house round... bring them out unto us, that we may know them* (Genesis 19:4-5), seeking to know the two angels who came to Lot; and *Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven; And he overthrew those cities* (Genesis 19:24-25). The library remembers the same fire — *the fire which fell down upon the five cities,* the smoking waste a *testimony,* the pillar of salt *a monument of an unbelieving soul* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:6-7). And Peter sets it as the ensample Jude does: *the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes... an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly* (2 Peter 2:6). The burned cities stand up beside the Watchers and the wilderness generation as one witness: Yahuah (Lord) judges the ungodly, and the example is written in brimstone.

threads.title: Clouds without water, wandering stars, the blackness of darkness reserved for ever (1 Enoch 18, 21; Proverbs 25, Isaiah 57; 2 Peter 2)
threads.summary_md: *These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds... Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever* (Jude 1:12-13). Jude paints the ungodly with images drawn from nature and from Enoch. The *clouds... without water* are Solomon's empty boaster: *Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain* (Proverbs 25:14). The *raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame* are Isaiah's wicked: *the wicked are like the troubled sea... whose waters cast up mire and dirt* (Isaiah 57:20). But the *wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever* are Enoch's vision: the *I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:13-14), *the stars which roll over the fire... which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God)... because they did not come forth at their appointed times* (1 Enoch 18:14 / 21:6), bound till their guilt should be consummated. The stars that would not keep their course are the figure for the lawless who keep not the faith once delivered. Peter writes the same indictment in the same words: *wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever* (2 Peter 2:17). Empty, restless, off-course — and the blackness of darkness reserved.

threads.title: Able to keep you from falling — the only wise Elohim our Saviour (Psalm 121, Deuteronomy 32, Isaiah 45)
threads.summary_md: *Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise Elohim (God) our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen* (Jude 1:24-25). The letter that has named the fallen Watchers and the wandering stars ends on the One able to keep his own from falling. The keeping is the Psalm's: *He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Yashar'el (Israel) shall neither slumber nor sleep* (Psalm 121:3-4) — the Keeper of Yashar'el (Israel) who never sleeps is the One able to present the saints faultless. The One they trust is the Rock of the Song of Moses: *He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he* (Deuteronomy 32:4) — the same righteous Judge who destroyed the unbelieving is the One who keeps the faithful. And he is Isaiah's only Saviour: *a just Elohim (God) and a Saviour; there is none beside me* (Isaiah 45:21). The Father is *the only wise Elohim (God) our Saviour,* the source of salvation, beside whom there is none else; the glory and majesty, dominion and power are his *through Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) our Master.* Against every falling, the saints are kept by the Keeper who slumbers not.

threads.title: Turning the grace of our Elohim into lasciviousness — the faith once delivered to the saints (Deuteronomy 32, 2 Peter 2)
threads.summary_md: *Beloved... it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares... ungodly men, turning the grace of our Elohim (God) into lasciviousness, and denying the only Yahuah Elohim (Lord God), and our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ)* (Jude 1:3-4). Here is the whole burden of the letter: the faith was *once delivered* — settled, whole, not to be remade — and the ungodly pervert grace into a licence for the flesh. This is the anti-antinomian heart of Jude: grace is no permit to abandon the Torah; the man who makes it so is *denying* the Master who bought him. Moses named such men a *perverse and crooked generation* that *corrupted themselves* (Deuteronomy 32:5). And Peter named the same intruders: *false teachers... who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying Yahuah (Lord) that bought them* (2 Peter 2:1). Against them Jude raises the whole judgment-history of the library — the wilderness, the Watchers, Sodom, Cain, Balaam, Korah — every witness that Yahuah judges the lawless. The faith once delivered stands; grace turned into lasciviousness is the lie the apostle writes to overthrow.

threads.title: Shew me thy ways — the meek will he teach his way
threads.summary_md: The whole prayer turns on being TAUGHT: *Shew me thy ways, O Yahuah (LORD); teach me thy paths. Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the Elohim (God) of my salvation* (Psalm 25:4-5). And Yahuah teaches the lowly: *Good and upright is Yahuah (LORD): therefore will he teach sinners in the way. The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way* (Psalm 25:8-9). The way taught is His own way — His Torah — and to be taught of Yahuah is to be brought to keep it. Sirach names the fruit of such teaching plainly: *They that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways* (Sirach 2:15); *they that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law* (Sirach 2:16). The meek whom Yahuah teaches His way are the ones who keep His ways and are filled with His law; the prayer to be taught is the prayer to walk in His Torah.

threads.title: The paths of Yahuah are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant
threads.summary_md: This is the load-bearing, anti-antinomian note of the psalm. *All the paths of Yahuah (LORD) are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies* (Psalm 25:10): the mercy and truth run to those who KEEP the covenant — not to those who abolish it. *What man is he that feareth Yahuah (LORD)? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose* (25:12), and *The secret of Yahuah (LORD) is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant* (25:14): the intimate knowledge of Yahuah belongs to them that fear Him, and what He shews them is His COVENANT. The psalter says it twin — *the mercy of Yahuah (LORD) is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him... To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them* (Psalm 103:17-18). Sirach echoes it: *they that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word... and they that love him shall be filled with the law* (Sirach 2:15-16). And the NT FILTER seals it — knowing Him is inseparable from keeping His commandments: *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments. He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:3-4); *he that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me... and I will... manifest myself to him* (John 14:21). The secret of Yahuah is with the covenant-keeper; the paths of mercy and truth are to such as keep His covenant. Any reading that makes commandment-keeping irrelevant is the very lie this psalm forecloses.

threads.title: His seed shall inherit the earth — the meek shall inherit the earth
threads.summary_md: The man who fears Yahuah and is taught His way (25:9,12) is the one whose seed inherits: *His soul shall dwell at ease; and his seed shall inherit the earth* (Psalm 25:13). The psalter sings the promise again — *the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace* (Psalm 37:11); *The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever* (Psalm 37:29). And the Anointed sets it forward word for word: *Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth* (Matthew 5:5). The meek whom Yahuah teaches His way in v.9 ARE the meek who inherit the earth in the Sermon on the Mount; the seed that dwells at ease is the covenant-keeper of v.10 given his rest. This is the two-house inheritance — never a people replaced, but the covenant seed, the meek taught of Yahuah, brought into the land forever.

threads.title: Redeem Yashar'el out of all his troubles — the two-house redemption
threads.summary_md: The psalm of one man's trust closes corporate: *Redeem Yashar'el (Israel), O Elohim (God), out of all his troubles* (Psalm 25:22). The single soul that lifted itself up to Yahuah (25:1) ends pleading for the whole people. The psalter answers — *Let Yashar'el (Israel) hope in Yahuah (LORD): for with Yahuah (LORD) there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption. And he shall redeem Yashar'el (Israel) from all his iniquities* (Psalm 130:7-8) — the redemption out of all his troubles is the redemption from all his iniquities. And the Torah-promise of the gathering stands behind it: *Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee* (Deuteronomy 30:3); *If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee* (Deuteronomy 30:4). The redeemed Yashar'el is the scattered seed gathered and ransomed whole — the two-house people, divided and dispersed, brought home; never replaced, the covenant people fetched even from the outmost parts.

threads.title: Try my reins and my heart — laid open to the searcher of reins and hearts
threads.summary_md: Psalm 26 is David's plea to be examined: *Judge me, O Yahuah (LORD); for I have walked in mine integrity... Examine me, O Yahuah (LORD), and prove me; try my reins and my heart. For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes: and I have walked in thy truth* (26:1-3). He lays his inmost self open to the only One who can read it. The psalter already names Him: *the righteous Elohim (God) trieth the hearts and reins* (Psalm 7:9); and Psalm 139 makes the identical plea — *Search me, O Elohim (God), and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts* (139:23). Jeremiah gives Yahuah's own word against the deceitful heart: *The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I Yahuah (LORD) search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways* (17:9-10). And the Formed Son in glory claims that very office: *all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works* (Revelation 2:23). The searcher of reins and hearts who in the Tanakh is Yahuah Himself is the Formed Son — he is Yahuah, and he has a Father, and he judges every one by his works, the same *according to his ways* Jeremiah speaks. ONE GUARD on the whole psalm: the *integrity* David pleads is the covenant-faithful walk — *I have walked in thy truth* (26:3) — NOT sinless merit. The same lips that say *I have walked in mine integrity* (26:1) say *redeem me, and be merciful unto me* (26:11). A man who must be redeemed and shown mercy is no self-righteous boaster; he keeps the covenant walk and casts himself on the lovingkindness that is ever before his eyes.

threads.title: I have not sat with vain persons — the two ways
threads.summary_md: The upright walk is marked by the company a man will not keep: *I have not sat with vain persons, neither will I go in with dissemblers. I have hated the congregation of evil doers; and will not sit with the wicked* (Psalm 26:4-5). This is the very contrast the psalter sets at its door — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful* (Psalm 1:1) — the same threefold not-sitting, not-standing, not-walking with the wicked. The NT carries the two ways forward as the call to the covenant people: *come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith Yahuah (Lord), and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you* (2 Corinthians 6:17). The separation David keeps is conduct-within-the-covenant — refusing the congregation of evil doers, not hatred of persons; the same line that asks *Gather not my soul with sinners* (26:9) keeps a man clean of the works of the wicked because Yahuah receives the separated.

threads.title: I have loved the habitation of thy house — clean hands at the altar
threads.summary_md: David's integrity comes to the altar: *I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O Yahuah (LORD): That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works. Yahuah (LORD), I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth* (Psalm 26:6-8). The clean hands at the altar are Psalm 24's gate-liturgy: only *he that hath clean hands, and a pure heart* (24:4) may *stand in his holy place* (24:3) — and David, washed in innocency, stands at last *in an even place* (26:12), against the wicked whose *right hand is full of bribes* (26:10). The love of the house is the one bent of the upright life: *One thing have I desired of Yahuah (LORD)... that I may dwell in the house of Yahuah (LORD) all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of Yahuah (LORD), and to enquire in his temple* (Psalm 27:4); and it breaks into longing in the sons of Korah — *How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)! My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 84:1-2). The Formed Son carries that very love into flesh: *The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up* (John 2:17) — the love of the habitation where Yahuah's honour dwells, burning in the One who came to His Father's house. The psalmist's love is the Son's consuming zeal.

threads.title: Yahuah is my light and my salvation — whom shall I fear?
threads.summary_md: Psalm 27 opens with the keystone confession of confidence: *Yahuah (LORD) is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? Yahuah (LORD) is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?* (Psalm 27:1). Light, salvation, strength — and therefore no fear, though *an host should encamp against me* (27:3). The same trio is sung across the Tanakh. Isaiah lifts the Song of the Sea into a refrain of trust: *Behold, Elohim (God) is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for Yahuah (LORD) JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation* (Isaiah 12:2) — itself the echo of *Yahuah (LORD) is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation* (Exodus 15:2). And the light is named everlasting: *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:1); *Yahuah (LORD) shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy Elohim (God) thy glory* (Isaiah 60:19); *Yahuah (LORD) shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended* (Isaiah 60:20). Read FORWARD through the Formed and the Formless: Yahuah, the everlasting light and the salvation and strength of His people, is the One who came in flesh and said *I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life* (John 8:12). The Formed Son IS Yahuah's light made manifest — he is Yahuah, and he has a Father; not a second co-equal person, but the expressed light of the Most High come among His own. The one whose light is Yahuah fears nothing; the one who follows the Son walks in the light of life.

threads.title: One thing have I desired — to dwell in the house of Yahuah and behold his beauty
threads.summary_md: Out of all the heart could want, one desire: *One thing have I desired of Yahuah (LORD), that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of Yahuah (LORD) all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of Yahuah (LORD), and to enquire in his temple* (Psalm 27:4). The Davidic psalms of the sanctuary sing the same single longing. The shepherd's psalm ends there: *I will dwell in the house of Yahuah (LORD) for ever* (Psalm 23:6). The love is named: *Yahuah (LORD), I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth* (Psalm 26:8). And the pilgrim psalm carries the longing to fainting: *How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)! My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 84:1-2), weighing and settling the choice — *a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my Elohim (God), than to dwell in the tents of wickedness* (Psalm 84:10). To dwell in His house all the days of one's life, to behold His beauty, to enquire in His temple — this one thing outweighs everything outside it.

threads.title: He shall hide me in his pavilion, and set me up upon a rock
threads.summary_md: The confidence has a refuge: *For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me; he shall set me up upon a rock* (Psalm 27:5). The hiding in the secret place is the psalter's steady shelter: *Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the pride of man: thou shalt keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues* (Psalm 31:20); *He that dwelleth in the secret place of the El Elyon (most High) shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty* (Psalm 91:1). And the rock he is set upon is Yahuah Himself: *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my Elohim (God), my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower* (Psalm 18:2). Hidden in the pavilion of His presence and set high on the Rock that is Yahuah — the trouble below cannot reach the one He shelters.

threads.title: Seek ye my face — Thy face, Yahuah, will I seek
threads.summary_md: The heart answers the call: *When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Yahuah (LORD), will I seek* (Psalm 27:8). The summons the psalmist answers is the covenant-call laid on the whole people: *If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land* (2 Chronicles 7:14) — the healing of the land hangs on the seeking of His face. It is the mark of the faithful: *This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob* (Psalm 24:6). And even in the scattering it is the turning Yahuah waits for: *I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early* (Hosea 5:15). The psalmist's lone heart answers the summons the whole house is called to — and to seek His face is the turning that ends the exile of the heart.

threads.title: I believed to see the goodness of Yahuah — wait on Yahuah, be of good courage
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes where confidence lands: *I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of Yahuah (LORD) in the land of the living. Wait on Yahuah (LORD): be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 27:13-14). The strengthened heart is the prophet's very promise to the waiting: *they that wait upon Yahuah (LORD) shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint* (Isaiah 40:31) — the faint the psalmist feared (27:13) answered by the wait that renews. And the psalter twins the closing charge word for word: *Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 31:24). The one who believes to see His goodness, who waits and hopes in Him, does not faint; the strengthened heart is the gift of the wait.

threads.title: Unto thee will I cry, O Yahuah my rock — lest I go down to the pit
threads.summary_md: Psalm 28 opens with a cry to the Rock: *Unto thee will I cry, O Yahuah (LORD) my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit* (Psalm 28:1). The Rock-title is the covenant confession of the psalter and of Torah's own Song — *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer... my buckler, and the horn of my salvation* (Psalm 18:2), *who is a rock save our Elohim (God)?* (Psalm 18:31), *He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment* (Deuteronomy 32:4). Read through the Formed and the Formless, the NT names the Rock that led and watered Yashar'el (Israel): *they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Messiah (Christ)* (1 Corinthians 10:4) — the Formed Son who went before his people, the expressed Word drawn from the Formless Father; he is Yahuah, and he has a Father. And the dread of going *down into the pit* (28:1) is met by the psalter's resurrection-hope: *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit* (Psalm 30:3); *thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption* (Psalm 16:10). The Rock cried to is the refuge against the pit.

threads.title: When I lift up my hands toward thy holy oracle
threads.summary_md: *Hear the voice of my supplications, when I cry unto thee, when I lift up my hands toward thy holy oracle* (Psalm 28:2). The lifted hands directed *toward thy holy oracle* are the temple-prayer posture Solomon set at the dedication: *hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Yashar'el (Israel), when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive* (1 Kings 8:30) — prayer turned toward the holy place, heard in heaven. And it is the psalter's own call to worship: *Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 134:2). The cry of supplication and the hands lifted toward the oracle are one act of turning toward the dwelling of Yahuah, who hears.

threads.title: Give them according to their deeds — render to them their desert
threads.summary_md: David prays not to be drawn away with the wicked *which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief is in their hearts* (Psalm 28:3), asking the measure-for-measure recompense: *Give them according to their deeds, and according to the wickedness of their endeavours: give them after the work of their hands; render to them their desert* (Psalm 28:4), *Because they regard not the works of Yahuah (LORD), nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up* (Psalm 28:5). This rests on Yahuah's own justice, stated plainly in the psalter: *thou renderest to every man according to his work* (Psalm 62:12). The NT sets the same standard forward into the judgment — *Who will render to every man according to his deeds* (Romans 2:6); *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works* (Matthew 16:27). This is not Torah abolished but Torah's own justice carried whole: the workers of iniquity are rendered after their deeds.

threads.title: The saving strength of his anointed — feed thy people, and lift them up for ever
threads.summary_md: The thanksgiving turns to confession — *Blessed be Yahuah (LORD), because he hath heard the voice of my supplications. Yahuah (LORD) is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped* (Psalm 28:6-7) — echoing the psalter's steady refuge: *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock... my strength... my buckler* (Psalm 18:2), *thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head* (Psalm 3:3), *Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) is a sun and shield* (Psalm 84:11). Then the load-bearing close: *Yahuah (LORD) is their strength, and he is the saving strength of his anointed* (Psalm 28:8) — the mashiach, the same anointed the kings rage against: *the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2), which the NT quotes of the Messiah — *The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against Yahuah (Lord), and against his Messiah (Christ)* (Acts 4:26). And the prayer *Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and lift them up for ever* (Psalm 28:9) is the Shepherd-King who FEEDS his flock: *I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David... and he shall be their shepherd* (Ezekiel 34:23) — the one shepherd over the regathered two-house people; *Yahuah Ra'ah (The LORD is my shepherd); I shall not want* (Psalm 23:1); *we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture* (Psalm 100:3). It is fulfilled forward in the Formed Son: *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep* (John 10:11). The inheritance fed and carried *for ever* is Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah) regathered under the one Shepherd — never a replacement people, for the natural branches are not cast away (Romans 11:1-2), but the covenant flock saved by the strength of the anointed and lifted up for ever.

threads.title: Give unto Yahuah glory and strength — worship in the beauty of holiness
threads.summary_md: The theophany opens with a summons to the heavenly host: *Give unto Yahuah (LORD), O ye mighty, give unto Yahuah (LORD) glory and strength. Give unto Yahuah (LORD) the glory due unto his name; worship Yahuah (LORD) in the beauty of holiness* (Psalm 29:1-2). The *ye mighty* are the sons of the mighty (bene elim), the host above, bidden to ascribe to Yahuah the glory and strength that are His. The summons is sung near word for word in the psalter and in David's song before the ark: *Give unto Yahuah (LORD), O ye kindreds of the people, give unto Yahuah (LORD) glory and strength... O worship Yahuah (LORD) in the beauty of holiness* (Psalm 96:7,9); *Give unto Yahuah (LORD), ye kindreds of the people... worship Yahuah (LORD) in the beauty of holiness* (1 Chronicles 16:28-29). And the host is commanded plainly to bow: *worship him, all ye gods* (Psalm 97:7). The Letter to the Hebrews sets that very command upon the firstbegotten brought into the world: *let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him* (Hebrews 1:6). The Father summons the mighty; the worship of the whole host rises in the beauty of holiness to the Formed Son who bears the Name — and he has a Father.

threads.title: The voice of Yahuah upon the waters — the expressed Word, the Formed Son
threads.summary_md: Seven times the psalm names the *voice of Yahuah (LORD)*: *The voice of Yahuah (LORD) is upon the waters: the Elohim (God) of glory thundereth: Yahuah (LORD) is upon many waters* (29:3); *The voice of Yahuah (LORD) is powerful; the voice of Yahuah (LORD) is full of majesty* (29:4); it *breaketh the cedars* (29:5), *divideth the flames of fire* (29:7), *shaketh the wilderness* (29:8), *maketh the hinds to calve* (29:9). Read through the Formed and the Formless, the VOICE is the expressed Word — the One drawn from the Formless Source: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God)... All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made* (John 1:1-3). The Voice upon the many waters is the Formed Son's own voice — *his voice as the sound of many waters* (Revelation 1:15) — the very Glory Ezekiel saw: *his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory* (Ezekiel 43:2). And *the Elohim (God) of glory thundereth* (29:3) is the glory-voice from heaven the crowd took for thunder: *Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven... The people... said that it thundered* (John 12:28-29). The Voice that breaks the cedars and divides the fire is the Word by whom all was made; he is Yahuah, and he has a Father — no rival, no second God, the expressed Word of the One who sent him.

threads.title: Yahuah sitteth upon the flood — King for ever
threads.summary_md: After the seven thunders, the psalm enthrones the Voice: *Yahuah (LORD) sitteth upon the flood; yea, Yahuah (LORD) sitteth King for ever* (Psalm 29:10). The flood is the mabbul, the waters that drowned the world — *the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters* (Genesis 7:18) — until the King who sent the judgment stilled it: *Elohim (God) remembered Noah... and made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged* (Genesis 8:1). Sovereign to raise the flood and sovereign to abate it, Yahuah sits enthroned above the deep. And His throne has no end: the same King reigns to the consummation — *The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ); and he shall reign for ever and ever* (Revelation 11:15). The Voice that shook the many waters sits King over them for ever; the everlasting throne of the psalm is the kingdom that becomes the Lord's and his Messiah's, the reign without end.

threads.title: Yahuah will give strength unto his people, and bless them with peace
threads.summary_md: The theophany closes not in terror but in blessing: *Yahuah (LORD) will give strength unto his people; Yahuah (LORD) will bless his people with peace* (Psalm 29:11). The very strength the host ascribed to Yahuah — *give unto Yahuah (LORD) glory and strength* (29:1) — Yahuah turns and gives back to His people, and crowns it with shalom. It is the close of the priestly blessing spoken over Yashar'el (Israel): *Yahuah (LORD) lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace* (Numbers 6:26). And the Formed Son hands His people that same peace in the night he was betrayed: *Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid* (John 14:27). The peace Yahuah blesses His people with in the psalm is the peace the Formed Son gives — the strength and shalom of the covenant people, from the Voice upon the waters who is Yahuah and has a Father.

threads.title: The Inspired Reason — the mind disciplined under the Law
threads.summary_md: The book opens its thesis: *whether the Inspired Reason is supreme ruler over the passions* (4 Maccabees 1:1). But this Reason is no Stoic autonomy standing apart from the Creator; the writer names its source plainly — *This I take to be the culture acquired under the Law, through which we learn with due reverence the things of Elohim (God)* (4 Maccabees 1:4). The mind that masters lust and rage and fear is the mind trained BY the Torah. It ain't new: Paul says the same — *the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good* (Romans 7:12), and *I delight in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man* (Romans 7:22), warring against *the law of sin which is in my members* (Romans 7:23). David sang it long before — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul* (Psalm 19:7) — and Solomon weighed self-mastery higher than conquest — *he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city* (Proverbs 16:32). Moses set the whole charge near, not far off — *the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it* (Deuteronomy 30:14). The Torah-trained reason is the oldest wisdom there is.

threads.title: Reason the master-gardener — ruling, not uprooting, the passions
threads.summary_md: 4 Maccabees is careful: Reason does *not* extirpate the passions but enables us to resist them — *its action in their case is not to extirpate the passions, but to enable us to resist them successfully* (4 Maccabees 1:2). The picture is the disciplined garden: *each man's Reason as master-gardener, weeding and pruning and binding up... brings the thicket of dispositions and passions under domestication* (4 Maccabees 1:7), *For while Reason is the guide of the virtues it is master of the passions* (4 Maccabees 1:7). It ain't new: Paul names the same walk — not the killing of all desire but the Spirit's mastery over the flesh — *Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh* (Galatians 5:16), *the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh* (Galatians 5:17), with its harvest of *love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith* (Galatians 5:22). And the man who rules himself is the proverb's true conqueror — *he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city* (Proverbs 16:32). The husbandry of the heart is an old craft.

threads.title: The forbidden meats abstained from under the Law
threads.summary_md: The thesis lands at once on the dinner table: the first proof that Reason masters the body is the refusal of unclean food — *when we are tempted towards forbidden meats, how do we come to relinquish the pleasures to be derived from them? Is it not that Reason has power to repress the appetites?* (4 Maccabees 1:8), *Accordingly when we feel a desire to eat water-animals and birds and beasts and meats of every description forbidden to us under the Law, we abstain through the predominance of Reason* (4 Maccabees 1:9). The abstaining is *under the Law* — not a private scruple but the Creator's command, the same line Eleazar and the seven brothers will die for. It ain't new: the swine is named unclean from Sinai — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you* (Leviticus 11:7), *Of their flesh shall ye not eat, and their carcase shall ye not touch; they are unclean to you* (Leviticus 11:8); Moses repeats it — *Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing* (Deuteronomy 14:3). And Daniel, in a tyrant's court, set the pattern of the disciplined refusal — *Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat* (Daniel 1:8). The martyrs' table-faith is the oldest obedience there is — it ain't new.

threads.title: Joseph's Reason and the Tenth Word — Thou shalt not covet
threads.summary_md: The first proof that Reason masters every passion is Joseph: *This, certainly, is why we praise the virtuous Joseph, because by his Reason, with a mental effort, he checked the carnal impulse* (4 Maccabees 2:1), *a young man at the age when physical desire is strong, by his Reason quenched the impulse of his passions* (4 Maccabees 2:1). And the writer grounds that mastery not in Stoic willpower but in the Torah itself, quoting the Decalogue: *For the Law says, 'Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor anything that is thy neighbour's'* (4 Maccabees 2:1). It ain't new: Joseph fled the very temptation centuries before the philosophers wrote — *his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me* (Genesis 39:7), and he answered, *how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?* (Genesis 39:9), and *he left his garment in her hand, and fled* (Genesis 39:12). And the word the writer cites is the Tenth Word spoken at Sinai — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife* (Exodus 20:17), repeated by Moses — *Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife* (Deuteronomy 5:21). The Torah is what trains the reason to flee — it ain't new.

threads.title: The Law overrules greed — debt-release and gleaning for the poor
threads.summary_md: The Law does not merely restrain lust; it reaches into the purse. The writer argues that the Torah teaches even the miser and the grasping man to act against their nature: *as soon as a man orders his life according to the Law, if he is miserly he acts contrary to his nature, and lends money to the needy without interest, and at the seventh-year periods cancels the debt* (4 Maccabees 2:2), and *if he is parsimonious, he is overruled by the Law... and refrains from gleaning his stubbles or picking the last grapes from his vineyards* (4 Maccabees 2:2). It ain't new: the seventh-year release is Moses' own statute — *At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release* (Deuteronomy 15:1), *Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it... because it is called the LORD'S release* (Deuteronomy 15:2). And the law of the corner and the gleanings is from Sinai — *thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest* (Leviticus 19:9), *thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger* (Leviticus 19:10), which Moses applies to the forgotten sheaf and the olive boughs — *it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow* (Deuteronomy 24:19). The Torah's mastery over greed is the oldest charity there is — it ain't new.

threads.title: The Law governs anger — Moses at Dathan and Abiram, Jacob over Simeon and Levi
threads.summary_md: Reason ruling through the Law masters even rage. The writer reaches for two examples from Moses' own books: *Moses when he was angered against Dathan and Abiram did not give free course to his wrath, but governed his anger by his Reason* (4 Maccabees 2:4), and *our wise father Jacob blame[d] the houses of Simeon and Levi for their unreasoning slaughter of the tribe of the Shechemites, saying, 'Accursed be their anger!'* (4 Maccabees 2:4). It ain't new: when Dathan and Abiram rose against him, Moses ruled his spirit — *And they rose up before Moses... two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly* (Numbers 16:2); the defiant *We will not come up* (Numbers 16:12) did not provoke unbridled wrath but a governed appeal to Yahuah. And Jacob's curse on his sons' fury is in his blessing — *Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations* (Genesis 49:5), *Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel* (Genesis 49:7) — for *Simeon and Levi... slew all the males* of Shechem (Genesis 34:25). The Torah-trained reason that restrains rage is the patriarchs' own discipline — it ain't new.

threads.title: Elohim implanted the passions and gave the Law at creation
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes at the root of the whole argument: the Creator who made the passions also gave the Law to govern them. *For in the day when Elohim (God) created man, he implanted in him his passions and inclinations* (4 Maccabees 2:5), *and also, at the very same time, set the mind on a throne amidst the senses to be his sacred guide in all things; and to the mind he gave the Law, by the which if a man order himself, he shall reign over a kingdom that is temperate, and just, and virtuous, and brave* (4 Maccabees 2:5). The passions are not evil to be killed but a trust to be ruled — by the Law given with them at creation. It ain't new: man is the Creator's own forming — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul* (Genesis 2:7) — and set in the garden under command — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed* (Genesis 2:8). The same Lawgiver who made the heart set life and death before it — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Law is the Creator's gift to the creature he formed — it ain't new.

threads.title: David's thirst, and the water poured out as an offering
threads.summary_md: To show that Reason controls but does not extirpate desire, the writer sets forth *the case of the thirst of King David.* Burning with *an intense thirst,* David craved the water held by the enemy, and two mighty warriors *scaled the enemy's ramparts* and *drew from it a draught for the king.* But David, judging the draught *reckoned as equivalent to blood* to be *a grievous danger to his soul,* and *opposing his Reason to his desire, he poured out the water as an offering to Elohim.* The Torah-trained mind masters the appetite without destroying it. It ain't new — Samuel and the Chronicler record the very deed: the three mighty men broke through the host, and David *would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Yahuah,* saying *is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives?*

threads.title: Reason rules the appetite — the antagonist of the passions
threads.summary_md: The writer grants that *none of you is able to extirpate our natural desire,* nor anger, nor a malevolent disposition — but *Reason is not the extirpator of the passions, but their antagonist,* able to *quench the fires of desire, and to wrestle victoriously with the pangs of our bodies.* This is the Torah-trained mind ruling the appetite, not Stoic autonomy. It ain't new — Solomon weighed *he that ruleth his spirit* above *he that taketh a city,* and David sang that *the law of Yahuah is perfect, converting the soul.*

threads.title: Apollonius at the treasury — angels guard the Holy Place
threads.summary_md: A traitorous Simon informs the governor Apollonius that the Jerusalem treasury holds *many thousands of private deposits, not belonging to the temple account, and rightfully the property of King Seleucus* (4 Maccabees 4:2); Apollonius marches in to seize the moneys, but *there appeared from heaven angels, riding upon horses, with lightning flashing from their arms, and cast great fear and trembling upon them* (4 Maccabees 4:4), and he falls down half-dead and entreats the Hebrews to intercede for him. This is the very episode the sibling book tells: Simon's quarrel with the high priest, the boast of the treasury, the king's man sent to take the money, the priests' prayer, and the dread horseman from heaven who strikes him down. The deliverer-by-intercession even survives because the high priest pleads for him. It ain't new — the same hand that *defendeth* the place and *beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it* (2 Maccabees 3:39) turned back the spoiler in both tellings.

threads.title: Antiochus Epiphanes — the vile king who profanes the sanctuary
threads.summary_md: Seleucus dies and his successor is *his son Antiochus Epiphanes, an overweening terrible man* (4 Maccabees 4:9), who sells the high-priesthood, lays a gymnasium on the holy Mount, *abolished the service of the temple* (4 Maccabees 4:13), and *made a decree denouncing the penalty of death upon any who should be seen to live after the Law of our fathers* (4 Maccabees 4:16). Daniel had already drawn this king to the life: a *vile person* who comes in *by flatteries*, sets his heart *against the holy covenant*, pollutes the sanctuary, takes away the daily sacrifice, and corrupts the lawless *by flatteries* — yet the people who know their Elohim stay strong. It ain't new — the persecutor of 4 Maccabees is the very horn Daniel saw rise to *speak marvellous things against the Elohim of gods* (Daniel 11:36) before he comes to his end.

threads.title: The persecution begins — circumcision, the Law, and unclean meats
threads.summary_md: Antiochus plunders the city and turns to break the people: women *for circumcising their sons... were flung, together with their offspring, headlong from the rocks* (4 Maccabees 4:17), and he *personally tried to force by tortures each man separately to eat unclean meats and thus abjure the Yahudi (Jewish) religion* (4 Maccabees 4:18). Both sibling books tell the same assault: he comes up against Jerusalem with a great multitude after striking Egypt, plunders the sanctuary, decrees that all leave the Law, slays the women who circumcised their children, and would compel them to *eat swine's flesh, and unclean beasts*. The martyrs who fill the rest of 4 Maccabees die rather than defile themselves with forbidden food — the Creator's dietary law standing firm. It ain't new — the very crisis was already chronicled, and Israel *chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats* (1 Maccabees 1:63).

threads.title: ★ The Divine Law accepted as the Law of our country
threads.summary_md: Dragged before Antiochus and urged to the *unlawful eating of unclean meat,* the aged priest Eleazar answers for his people: *We, O Antiochus, having accepted the Divine Law as the Law of our country, do not believe any stronger necessity is laid upon us than that of our obedience to the Law.* He counts no transgression small: *the transgression of the Law, be it in small things or in great, is equally heinous; for in either case equally the Law is despised.* This is the very opposite of the law-against-grace reading — the martyr will die rather than despise one statute. It ain't new — *the law of Yahuah is perfect, converting the soul,* and Moses set it before the people as *thy life, and the length of thy days,* the word *very nigh unto thee... that thou mayest do it.*

threads.title: The Law teaches self-control, justice, and to worship the only Elohim
threads.summary_md: To the tyrant's scoff that the Yahudi philosophy is contrary to reason, Eleazar replies: *Not so, for the Law teaches us self-control, so that we are masters of all our pleasures and desires... and it teaches justice, so that with all our various dispositions we act fairly, and it teaches righteousness, so that with due reverence we worship only the Elohim (God) who is.* The Torah-trained mind is not Stoic autonomy but discipline grounded in the Law — self-control, justice, righteousness, and the worship of the one Elohim. It ain't new — Moses taught *what doth Yahuah thy Elohim require of thee, but to fear* him *and to love him,* the Decalogue opens *Thou shalt have no other gods before me,* and Paul testifies *the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.*

threads.title: ★★ The Creator-Lawgiver gave the dietary law — clean and unclean stands
threads.summary_md: Eleazar grounds the refusal of swine's flesh not in custom but in creation: *Therefore do we eat no unclean meat; for believing our Law to be given by Elohim (God), we know also that the Creator of the world, as a Lawgiver, feels for us according to our nature. He has commanded us to eat the things that will be convenient for our souls, and he has forbidden us to eat meats that would be the contrary.* The clean/unclean distinction is the Maker's own statute, given for the good of his people — the martyr dies FOR it, never against it. It ain't new — *the swine... is unclean to you... of their flesh shall ye not eat,* Moses repeats *thou shalt not eat any abominable thing,* and Daniel before him *purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself.* Eleazar of 2 Maccabees, the same man, *spit it forth* rather than taste the unlawful.

threads.title: Swine's flesh and things offered to idols — no other gods
threads.summary_md: Antiochus' decree is double: *compel them to eat swine's flesh and things offered to idols,* and any who *refuse to defile themselves with the unclean things* were to be tortured and put to death. Eleazar's refusal guards both the dietary law and the first command — for the worship of *only the Elohim (God) who is* allows no eating at the idol's table.
