And Malachi promises the day when all will see it — answering the very despair (*It is vain to serve Elohim (God)... we call the proud happy*, 3:14-15) — *Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth Elohim (God) and him that serveth him not* (Malachi 3:18). The restored wisdom of Solomon sets the two ends side by side: *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom 3:1) — they only *seemed to die* (3:2), and *in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (3:7) — while *the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken Yahuah (God)* (Wisdom 3:10). The end is the answer the sanctuary gives.

threads.title: Thou didst set them in slippery places — the sudden fall of the wicked
threads.summary_md: The end seen in the sanctuary is a fall, and a sudden one: *Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction. How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors. As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Yahuah (Lord), when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image* (Psalm 73:18-20). The very firmness Asaph envied (73:4) is revealed as footing on ice. The Formed Son told the parable of it — the man who *increase[d] in riches* (73:12) heaping goods for many years: *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). The neighbouring psalm watched it happen in real time: *I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found* (Psalm 37:35-36). And the restored wisdom names the vanishing in the same terms — *the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind... and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day* (Wisdom 5:14) — and puts the confession in the mouths of the fallen: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by* (Wisdom 5:8-9). The image of the prospering wicked does not survive the dawn.

threads.title: Thou hast holden me by my right hand — and afterward receive me to glory
threads.summary_md: The confession of his own folly — *So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee* (Psalm 73:22) — turns at once into the surest hope of the whole Psalter: *Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand. Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory* (Psalm 73:23-24). This is the answer that swallows the envy of the wicked: not better prosperity, but to be held by His right hand now and received to glory afterward — the hope that runs past death. The same Psalter sang it: *my flesh also shall rest in hope... thou wilt not leave my soul in hell... Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore* (Psalm 16:9-11); and *Elohim (God) will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me* (Psalm 49:15) — the twin theodicy psalm, where the rich man *carr[ies] nothing away* (49:17) but the upright soul is received. Paul names the end of that chain: *whom he justified, them he also glorified* (Romans 8:30). And the Formed Son made the receiving His own pledge: *I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also* (John 14:3). The being-held-now is the being-received-then; the right hand that holds is the hand that brings to glory.

threads.title: Whom have I in heaven but thee? — Elohim is my portion for ever
threads.summary_md: The hope resolves into a single desire that empties out everything the wicked clutched at: *Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee. My flesh and my heart faileth: but Elohim (God) is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever* (Psalm 73:25-26). The portion is not the riches the ungodly increase (73:12) but Yahuah Himself. Out of the deepest lament the same confession rises: *Yahuah (LORD) is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him* (Lamentations 3:24). The Psalter knew no other inheritance: *Yahuah (LORD) is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot* (Psalm 16:5). And the root of it is the priest's own lot — for Asaph was of the sanctuary singers — *Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land... I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 18:20). The Levite was given no field, because he was given Yahuah; and the man whose portion is Elohim needs none of the prosperity that fails when flesh and heart fail.

threads.title: It is good for me to draw near to Elohim
threads.summary_md: The psalm that began with the clean heart (73:1) and was solved in the sanctuary (73:17) ends where a clean heart belongs — drawn near: *But it is good for me to draw near to Elohim (God): I have put my trust in Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I may declare all thy works* (Psalm 73:28). Against the wicked who are *far from thee* and *perish* (73:27), the upright draws near. Hebrews opens the new and living way into that very nearness: *Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water* (Hebrews 10:22). And James gives the promise that meets the resolve and names the same clean-heart condition the psalm opened with: *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded* (James 4:8). The good Asaph found is the drawing-near; the drawing-near is mutual; and it is, from first verse to last, the way of the clean heart.

threads.title: The ox knoweth his owner — the covenant-lawsuit, heaven and earth as witnesses
threads.summary_md: Isaiah opens with a courtroom. The Father summons the standing witnesses of creation and lays the charge: *Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me* (Isaiah 1:2). This is the very summons of the Song of Moses — *Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth* (Deuteronomy 32:1) — the covenant-lawsuit pattern, heaven and earth called to testify against a people who broke faith. The indictment is conduct, not ethnicity, and its sting is the grief of a Father: *is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?* (Deuteronomy 32:6). Then the image that cuts deepest: *The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Yashar'el (Israel) doth not know, my people doth not consider* (Isaiah 1:3). The dumb beast knows whose stall it eats from; the covenant people do not know their Owner. And the same not-knowing met the Formed Son when he came in the flesh: *He came unto his own, and his own received him not* (John 1:11). Yet through the whole lawsuit they are still *my people* — the Owner is faithful even where the owned do not know him; this is covenant rebellion, never a casting-off.

threads.title: Though your sins be as scarlet — the cleansing made white, pardon unto obedience
threads.summary_md: At the heart of the lawsuit, the Judge holds out pardon: *Come now, and let us reason together, saith Yahuah (LORD): though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool* (Isaiah 1:18). The whole indictment bends toward this offer — the covenant call to repent and be cleansed. The blood that does the whitening is named across the library: *the blood of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) his Son cleanseth us from all sin* (1 John 1:7); *he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness* (1 John 1:9); *they... have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb* (Revelation 7:14). David sang the same plea long before: *Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow* (Psalm 51:7). But the pardon is never a charter for sin. The very next breath binds it to obedience: *If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it* (Isaiah 1:19-20). Grace is the means of return to his ways, not freedom from them. The scarlet washed white is the door home — and the home is a walk in his Torah, the willing and obedient eating the good of the land.

threads.title: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices — empty ritual rejected, not abolished
threads.summary_md: Yahuah turns from the rebels' offerings in revulsion: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams... your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth... And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood* (Isaiah 1:11-15). Read carelessly, this looks like the abolition of sacrifice, new moon, and feast. It is not. It is Yahuah's rejection of his own appointed worship when it is brought by bloody, unrepentant hands. The proof is the SAME prophet's closing word: *from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:23) — the new moons and sabbaths kept forever, by all flesh, in the restoration. The prophets speak with one voice on what Yahuah seeks behind the offering: *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* (Hosea 6:6), which the King himself quotes — *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13); *I hate, I despise your feast days... But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (Amos 5:21,24); *to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams* (1 Samuel 15:22); *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). And Isaiah names the cure in the same breath: *cease to do evil; Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow* (Isaiah 1:16-17). Mercy and obedience ABOVE heartless ritual — never instead of obedience, but as its living root. The appointed times are good and kept; what Yahuah hates is worship divorced from justice and clean hands.

threads.title: Except Yahuah had left us a remnant — the seed preserved, Sodom the type
threads.summary_md: Mercy stands in the midst of judgment: *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah* (Isaiah 1:9). Paul reaches back and quotes this verse word for word to prove the remnant kept by grace: *And as Esaias said before, Except Yahuah (Lord) of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha* (Romans 9:29). Sodom is the type of the judgment narrowly escaped — *the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all* (Luke 17:29) — and Isaiah names the rebellious rulers by that very type: *Hear the word of Yahuah (LORD), ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our Elohim (God), ye people of Gomorrah* (Isaiah 1:10). The same name carries to the end of the canon, the great city *which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified* (Revelation 11:8). The point of the lawsuit is not the destruction of a people but the naming of their sin so they might turn — and the seed left is the proof of a people not cast off, a remnant according to the election of grace.

threads.title: The faithful city become an harlot — judged and redeemed, the bride at the last
threads.summary_md: The lawsuit grieves over what the city has become: *How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers* (Isaiah 1:21). But the verdict is not extinction — it is the furnace that purges: *I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin: And I will restore thy judges as at the first... afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city* (Isaiah 1:25-26). The harlot is judged in order to be made faithful again: *Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness* (1:27). The end of the canon shows where this road runs: the harlot-city purged becomes the bride-city — *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband* (Revelation 21:2). The purging hand keeps a remnant, never abandoning a people: *Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace* (Romans 11:5). Judgment is the love that burns the dross so the faithful city can rise — Zion redeemed, the harlot made bride.

threads.title: This people draw near me with their mouth — the precept of men, not the commandment of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: At the center of Isaiah 29 stands the verse Yahusha would quote against the Pharisees: *Wherefore Yahuah (Lord) said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men* (Isaiah 29:13). The mouth draws near; the heart is removed far off; the fear of Yahuah has been replaced by *the precept of men*. Yahusha takes it up word for word: *This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men* (Matthew 15:8-9); and the twin, *This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men* (Mark 7:6-7). Hear carefully where the charge lands. It is NOT a charge against the Torah. It is a charge against the TRADITIONS and PRECEPTS OF MEN that NULLIFY the commandment of Elohim. Yahusha names it exactly: *Why do ye also transgress the commandment of Elohim (God) by your tradition?... Thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition* (Matthew 15:3,6); *For laying aside the commandment of Elohim (God), ye hold the tradition of men... Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition* (Mark 7:8,13). He even defends a specific commandment — *Honour thy father and thy mother* (Mark 7:10) — against the Corban-tradition that voided it. The fault is the removed heart and the doctrines of men; never the commandments of Yahuah. The Torah is upheld in the very breath that condemns the man-made tradition displacing it, and condemns the empty lip-worship that honours with the mouth while the heart is far away. *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:4) — the lips-far-from-heart worship is the lie this verse exposes.

threads.title: The wisdom of their wise men shall perish — Paul quotes the marvellous work
threads.summary_md: *Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid* (Isaiah 29:14). Yahuah answers the lip-worship and the precept-of-men religion of v.13 with a marvellous work that abases human wisdom. Paul quotes the verse word for word and reads the cross as that marvellous work: *For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent* (1 Corinthians 1:19). He presses it: *Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? hath not Elohim (God) made foolish the wisdom of this world?* (1:20). And he names why — *Because the foolishness of Elohim (God) is wiser than men; and the weakness of Elohim (God) is stronger than men* (1:25). The marvellous work and wonder Isaiah foretold is the foolishness of preaching that confounds the wise; the prudent men whose understanding *shall be hid* are abased before the wisdom of Yahuah, which is wiser than all the wisdom it brings to nothing.

threads.title: The spirit of deep sleep and the book that is sealed — until the Lamb opens it
threads.summary_md: Before the lip-worship is named, Isaiah names the judicial stupor it sits under: *For Yahuah (LORD) hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered* (Isaiah 29:10). And the vision itself is shut: *And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed* (29:11), *And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned* (29:12). Paul quotes the deep sleep: *Elohim (God) hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear; unto this day* (Romans 11:8). But the slumber is PARTIAL and judicial, never a casting-off — *Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid* (Romans 11:1); *there is a remnant according to the election of grace* (11:5). The same vail lies on the reading: *their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament* (2 Corinthians 3:14), *when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart* (3:15) — and it lifts: *when it shall turn to Yahuah (Lord), the vail shall be taken away* (3:16). The sealed book waits for One worthy. *And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book... sealed with seven seals* (Revelation 5:1), and *no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book* (5:3) — until *behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof* (5:5). The book is sealed UNTIL the Lamb, the Messiah, opens it; the deep sleep is lifted, and the remnant stands.

threads.title: In that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book — the reversal for the meek
threads.summary_md: The sealed book and the deep sleep are not the last word. Isaiah turns to the day of reversal: *And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. The meek also shall increase their joy in Yahuah (LORD), and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 29:18-19). The very faculties shut up in the slumber — the deaf ears, the blind eyes, the sealed book — are opened for the humble. Yahusha gives this list as his proof to John that the day has come: *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them* (Matthew 11:5). Isaiah's own twin sings it: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped* (Isaiah 35:5), for *your Elohim (God) will come and save you* (35:4). And the chapter closes on the two-house restoration the reversal serves: *Yahuah (LORD), who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed* (29:22); *they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (29:23); *They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine* (29:24). The meek of redeemed Jacob hear the words of the book at last; the sealed scroll is opened, the slumber lifted, and the humble rejoice in the Holy One of Yashar'el.

threads.title: Shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? — the potter and the clay
threads.summary_md: To the men who hide their counsel from Yahuah and say *Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?* (Isaiah 29:15), Isaiah answers with the potter and the clay: *Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?* (29:16). To esteem oneself above the Maker — to imagine the clay can deny or judge the hand that shaped it — is the turning of things upside down. Isaiah's own twin presses the same: *Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?* (Isaiah 45:9). The creature cannot arraign its Maker. The Formed One who fashioned Yashar'el is not answerable to the clay; the prudent who hide their counsel will be esteemed as the potter's clay, and the wisdom that thought itself hidden from Him shall perish.

threads.title: The furnace of affliction — I have refined thee, not cast thee off
threads.summary_md: Yahuah's lawsuit against an obstinate people does not end in their rejection but in their refining: *Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction* (Isaiah 48:10). The affliction is the assaying of the CHOSEN — the fire that proves and purifies, not the wrath that discards. Peter says it of the scattered strangers: *though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations* (1 Peter 1:6), *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 1:7). Malachi names the Refiner at his work: *he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver... that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness* (Malachi 3:3). And Zechariah names the far side of the fire — the restored two-house bond: *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined... they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Yahuah (LORD) is my Elohim (God)* (Zechariah 13:9). The restored wisdom-witnesses say it twice over: *having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5-6); *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The furnace is the love of the One who chose, refining a people he will not give up.

threads.title: I am the first, I also am the last — the title the risen Messiah claims
threads.summary_md: Yahuah calls Jacob to hearken to a self-naming: *Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel), my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last* (Isaiah 48:12) — and the same hand *laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens* (48:13). Isaiah fixes this title to Yahuah alone: *I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 44:6); *I Yahuah (LORD), the first, and with the last; I am he* (Isaiah 41:4). Then at the canon's end the title falls from the risen Messiah's own mouth: *Fear not; I am the first and the last* (Revelation 1:17); *These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive* (Revelation 2:8); *I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last* (Revelation 22:13); *I am Alpha and Omega... saith Yahuah (Lord), which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty* (Revelation 1:8). This is the Formed and the Formless. The Son who appeared and spoke as Yahuah in the Tanakh, who *was dead, and is alive*, bears the Father's own titles and Name because he IS Yahuah and HAS a Father — never co-equal trinitarian persons, never a modalist collapse of Father into Son, never an Arian creature. The First and the Last who chose Jacob in the furnace is the same One who took flesh, died, and rose; the eternal title and the empty tomb belong to one Person. And the hand that founded the earth (48:13) is the Word by whom all things were made.

threads.title: And now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me — the Sent One
threads.summary_md: In the midst of Yahuah's declaration a Speaker steps forward who has been from the beginning and yet is sent: *Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), and his Spirit, hath sent me* (Isaiah 48:16). The One who was *there* from the beginning is sent by Yahuah and his Spirit — the Formed Son sent by the Father. Yahusha says it as his own testimony: *I proceeded forth and came from Elohim (God); neither came I of myself, but he sent me* (John 8:42). The Speaker who has always been is the One sent into the world; and the Spirit in the sending is Yahuah's own breath and power, not a third co-equal person beside the Father and the Son. The eternal One is the sent One.

threads.title: O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments — the river of peace
threads.summary_md: Yahuah names himself the teacher of the way that profits, then breaks into lament: *I am Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go. O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea* (Isaiah 48:17-18) — *Thy seed also had been as the sand* (48:19). Read it plainly: peace and righteousness flow FROM hearkening to the commandments. Torah-keeping is the way that profits, the path of blessing; the loss of peace is the cost of forsaking it. This is the anti-antinomian lament — the commandments were never the curse, the curse was the abandoning of them. John holds the same filter unbroken: *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments* (1 John 2:3). And Isaiah names the wage of the road a few chapters on: *I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith Yahuah (LORD); and I will heal him* (Isaiah 57:19) — the peace that flows like a river to the two houses, far and near, when they turn and walk in his way.

threads.title: Go ye forth of Babylon — the second-exodus call to come out
threads.summary_md: The lawsuit turns to deliverance with a summons and a song: *Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth; say ye, Yahuah (LORD) hath redeemed his servant Jacob* (Isaiah 48:20) — and the redeemed are led as in the first exodus: *they thirsted not when he led them through the deserts: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them* (48:21). The call to come out of Babylon runs the length of the canon. Jeremiah sounds the same alarm over the same city: *Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity* (Jeremiah 51:6); *My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 51:45). And it is still sounding at the end over the final Babylon: *Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues* (Revelation 18:4). Paul carries the same separation-pattern forward as the receiving of the gathered: *come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith Yahuah (Lord), and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you* (2 Corinthians 6:17). The gathering home is itself a coming-out; the second exodus leads the redeemed servant Jacob out of Babylon with a voice of singing.

threads.title: There is no peace, saith Yahuah, unto the wicked — the closing refrain
threads.summary_md: The chapter seals with a verdict: *There is no peace, saith Yahuah (LORD), unto the wicked* (Isaiah 48:22). It is no throwaway line — Isaiah brackets the great middle of his book with the very same refrain, sealing chapter 57 the same way: *There is no peace, saith my Elohim (God), to the wicked* (Isaiah 57:21). The two verdicts answer the lament of 48:18: peace is *as a river* to the one who hearkens to the commandments, and there is *no peace* to the one who refuses the way. The same Yahuah who teaches the way that profits names the end of the road that turns from it. Mercy is held out — the furnace refines, Babylon is left behind, the river of peace runs for the one who turns — but for the wicked who will not turn, the refrain stands.

threads.title: Awake, awake, O arm of Yahuah — the Redeemer who cut the dragon and brings the redeemed home
threads.summary_md: The prophet calls the Arm of Yahuah to awaken: *Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of Yahuah (LORD); awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?* (Isaiah 51:9-10). The Arm is not an abstraction — Isaiah names him as a Person to be revealed: *Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of Yahuah (LORD) revealed?* (53:1); *Yahuah (LORD) hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations* (52:10). The Arm of Yahuah is the Redeemer, the Formed Son drawn from the Formless Father — the One who is Yahuah and has a Father. His ancient work was the Red Sea: *Thus Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day out of the hand of the Egyptians* (Exodus 14:30); *Who is like unto thee, O Yahuah (LORD)... glorious in holiness... doing wonders* (Exodus 15:11) — the dragon-oppressor cast into the depths, as the restored witness records: *Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss* (Jubilees 48:14). That Arm was named before the world: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days* (1 Enoch 48:2). The first exodus is the figure; the second is the substance: *Therefore the redeemed of Yahuah (LORD) shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head... sorrow and mourning shall flee away* (51:11) — word for word the ingathering of *the ransomed of Yahuah (LORD) shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away* (Isaiah 35:10). This is the two-house remnant gathered home, never a cast-off people, never replacement (Romans 11). And all sorrow ends in the city John saw: *Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying* (Revelation 21:4).

threads.title: Look unto Abraham your father — the rock ye were hewn from, the father of the faithful
threads.summary_md: To the seed that follows after righteousness the call is to look back to the source: *Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek Yahuah (LORD): look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him* (Isaiah 51:1-2). The one called alone and multiplied is the father of the faithful. Paul builds the whole seed of promise on him: *to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed... who is the father of us all* (Romans 4:16); *Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations; according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be* (Romans 4:18). Hebrews sets Abraham and Sarah side by side as 51:2 does: *Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed... Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable* (Hebrews 11:11-12). And the blessing on the called father rests on the seed of faith: *So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham* (Galatians 3:9). The rock ye were hewn from is Abraham; the seed of promise is carried by the paternal bloodline AND the covenant-word together — two-house and the grafted-in seed grown wild in the nations, never a new people by mere confession, never replacement.

threads.title: A law shall proceed from me — the unabolished righteousness that outlasts the old creation
threads.summary_md: The covenant word is not abolished — it goes forth: *Hearken unto me, my people... for a law shall proceed from me, and I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people* (Isaiah 51:4). This is the same going-forth Isaiah saw earlier: *out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Yahuah (LORD) from Jerusalem* (Isaiah 2:3). And the salvation that goes with the law is everlasting, outlasting the very heavens: *Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment... but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished* (51:6). That garment-heavens word is spoken directly OF the Son: *They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail* (Hebrews 1:11-12) — the unchanging Creator who *laid the foundation of the earth* (Heb 1:10) is the Formed Son. He says the same in his own mouth: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away* (Matthew 24:35). Peter names the same dissolution and looks past it: *the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat... Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness* (2 Peter 3:10,13); and John sees it: *I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away* (Revelation 21:1). The law proceeds, the righteousness is not abolished, and the salvation is for ever — when the garment-heavens are folded up, these stand.

threads.title: The people in whose heart is my law — the Torah written within, the new covenant
threads.summary_md: Isaiah names a people by the Torah carried inside them: *Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings* (Isaiah 51:7). This is the new covenant itself — not Torah replaced, but Torah internalized: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33), the covenant made with BOTH the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah) (31:31). Ezekiel names the heart and the Spirit that keeps it: *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you... And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:26-27) — the Spirit and the Torah are inseparable; the new heart walks in the commandments. The psalmist already knew this steadiness: *The law of his Elohim (God) is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide* (Psalm 37:31). And Paul names the same heart-written law: *Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts* (Romans 2:15), *written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living Elohim (God); not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart* (2 Corinthians 3:3). The stone tablets and the fleshy heart bear the SAME law; the Spirit writes it within. The people in whose heart is the law are the people who keep the commandments — the filter holds: *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments* (1 John 2:3).

threads.title: I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling — the wrath-cup passed to her oppressors
threads.summary_md: The afflicted city has drained the wrath to its dregs: *Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out* (Isaiah 51:17). But the cup is now taken away — and handed on: *Thus saith thy Yahuah (Lord) Yahuah (LORD), and thy Elohim (God) that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over* (51:22-23). The cup does not vanish — it passes from Zion's hand to the hand of her oppressors. John sees the same cup poured out: *The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of Elohim (God), which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone* (Revelation 14:10); *great Babylon came in remembrance before Elohim (God), to give unto her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath* (Revelation 16:19). The fierceness that once bowed Jerusalem down is poured out on the city that made her bow. The afflicted daughter is comforted; the comfort is sure because the One who *comforteth you* (51:12) pleads her cause.

threads.title: The name of Yahuah is a strong tower — the true refuge against the false
threads.summary_md: The keystone of the chapter stands at v.10, and Solomon sets it pointedly against the verse that follows: *The name of Yahuah (LORD) is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe* (Proverbs 18:10) — and then *The rich man's wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit* (18:11). Two refuges are offered, the Name and the wealth; the second is a tower only *in his own conceit*. The Name-refuge is the song of the whole Psalter — *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress... my high tower* (Psalm 18:2), repeated in David's great deliverance-song *my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour* (2 Samuel 22:3); *thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy* (Psalm 61:3); *I will say of Yahuah (LORD), He is my refuge and my fortress* (Psalm 91:2). The prophets make the Name the very place of deliverance for the gathered remnant — *whosoever shall call on the name of Yahuah (LORD) shall be delivered* (Joel 2:32); and the humbled remnant *shall trust in the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (Zephaniah 3:12), the afflicted and poor, not the proud who trust their wealth. And here the framework speaks carefully: the strong tower is the Name of the FATHER, the formless Source — and that same Name is borne by the Formed Son, who prayed *Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me* (John 17:11). So the apostles run into that one Name for salvation — *Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved* (Acts 4:12) — the Name the Father gave the Son, *a name which is above every name* (Philippians 2:9), at which *every knee should bow* (2:10). Not a second Name set beside the Father's, but the Father's own Name borne by the Son into whom the righteous run and are safe.

threads.title: Death and life are in the power of the tongue
threads.summary_md: The chapter gathers its mouth-sayings to a head at v.21: *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof* (Proverbs 18:21) — drawing up the talebearer's words *as wounds* (18:8), the fool's mouth that is *his destruction* (18:7), and the belly *satisfied with the fruit of his mouth* (18:20). The book states the double power many ways: *The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life* (10:11), yet *he that refraineth his lips is wise* (10:19); *The tongue of the just is as choice silver* (10:20); *There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health* (12:18); *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction* (13:3); *A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit* (15:4). The Formed Son raises the proverb to the day of judgment: *every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment* (Matthew 12:36); *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (12:37) — death and life in the tongue, weighed at the bar. And James draws the death-power out in full: *the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity* (3:6), *an unruly evil, full of deadly poison* (3:8). The restored witness measures it against the sword: *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17); *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (28:18). From Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witness the testimony is one — the tongue holds death and life, and a man eats the fruit of his own.

threads.title: A friend that sticketh closer than a brother
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets true friendship against a wounded brotherhood: *A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle* (Proverbs 18:19), and then *A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother* (18:24). The book defines the friend it praises — *A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity* (17:17); *Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful* (27:6); *Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not... better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off* (27:10). The history shows the friend in the flesh: *the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul* (1 Samuel 18:1), and the two *made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul* (18:3) — the king's own son loving David above his house. Ruth cleaves to Naomi past all natural claim: *whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God)* (Ruth 1:16). And the Formed Son is Himself the friend that sticks closest of all, showing the proverb's full measure: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends* (John 15:13); *I have called you friends* (15:15) — opening His Father's counsel to His own. The restored witness sings the same treasure: *A faithful friend is a strong defence... has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14); *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (6:16); *Forsake not an old friend* (9:10).

threads.title: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing — a favour of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: *Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 18:22). The good thing reaches all the way back to the garden, where the wife is Yahuah's own remedy for the single thing in creation He named *not good*: *It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him* (Genesis 2:18); *they shall be one flesh* (2:24). The favour-of-Yahuah is no figure of speech — the same book names the wife a gift, not a chance: *House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD)* (19:14); and weighs the finding above all price: *Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies* (31:10). The NT carries the one-flesh ordinance unbroken, quoting the garden — *they two shall be one flesh* (Ephesians 5:31) — and upholds it as honourable, never a concession: *Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled* (Hebrews 13:4). The restored witness keeps the same blessing: *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double* (Sirach 26:1); *A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God)* (26:3); *He that getteth a wife begins a possession, a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest* (36:24) — the very help meet of Eden. The wife found is a good thing because she is a favour apportioned by Yahuah to them that fear Him.

threads.title: Before destruction the heart is haughty — and the folly of answering before hearing
threads.summary_md: The chapter twins a law of pride with a rebuke of haste: *Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility* (Proverbs 18:12); *He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him* (18:13). The law of pride the book states plainly twice more — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall* (16:18) — and binds the path to honour to the fear of Yahuah: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility* (15:33). The way up is down; the haughty heart is the herald of its own ruin. And the hasty mouth of v.13 — answering before hearing — is rebuked whole in the NT: *let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath* (James 1:19). The proud heart and the hasty tongue run together: both refuse to hear before they speak, and both go before a fall.

threads.title: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah
threads.summary_md: The keystone of the chapter makes mercy to the poor a transaction with Yahuah Himself: *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again* (Proverbs 19:17). The gift handed to the poor is not lost; it is a loan to Yahuah, and He is no man's debtor — *that which he hath given will he pay him again*. This is the Torah's own open-hand command set as a couplet: *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother* (Deuteronomy 15:7); *Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved... Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in all thy works* (15:10); *Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy* (15:11). The same book sings the loan twice over — *he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31), *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor* (22:9), *He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack* (28:27) — and David opens it: *Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble* (Psalm 41:1). The New Testament makes the loan personal and names when it is repaid: the poor man received is Yahuah received — *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me* (Matthew 25:40); the repayment is at the last day — *call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind... thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just* (Luke 14:13-14); and the manner is glad — *he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully* (2 Corinthians 9:6), *Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver* (9:7), *he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever* (9:9). The restored witness binds the same charge to the commandment and to a treasure laid up: *defraud not the poor of his living* (Sirach 4:1), *bow down your ear to the poor* (4:8), *Help the poor for the commandment's sake* (29:9), *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction* (29:12). From Torah to Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witnesses, the testimony is one: the open hand to the poor is a loan to Yahuah, and Yahuah repays. (The poor man honoured runs the whole chapter — *Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips* (19:1), *a poor man is better than a liar* (19:22) — against a world where *Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour* (19:4).)

threads.title: A false witness shall not be unpunished — the ninth word
threads.summary_md: Twice over, almost word for word, the chapter pronounces the doom of the lying witness: *A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape* (Proverbs 19:5); *A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish* (Proverbs 19:9). This is the ninth word of the Ten carried into a proverb: *Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour* (Exodus 20:16; Deuteronomy 5:20), *Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness* (Exodus 23:1). The Torah even names the false witness's exact sentence — the judges *make diligent inquisition* (Deuteronomy 19:18), and *Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother* (19:19): the liar perishes by the very harm he meant for another, which is why he shall not escape. Proverbs numbers him among the things Yahuah hates — *A false witness that speaketh lies* (6:19) — and repeats the verdict — *a false witness deceit* (12:17), *A false witness shall perish* (21:28). The New Testament keeps the same measure, never abolishing it: false witnesses are the weapon raised against Stephen — *And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law* (Acts 6:13) — and the end of all liars is sealed at the last — *all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death* (Revelation 21:8). The restored witness agrees: *Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good* (Sirach 7:13), *A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage* (Sirach 20:25). The ninth word stands; the chapter closes on it still — *An ungodly witness scorneth judgment* (19:28).

threads.title: The counsel of Yahuah, that shall stand
threads.summary_md: Against the restless planning of the heart the chapter sets the one will that prevails: *There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of Yahuah (LORD), that shall stand* (Proverbs 19:21). Man's devising is real, but it does not govern the outcome — Yahuah's counsel does. The same book twins it: *A man's heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (16:9); *Man's goings are of Yahuah (LORD); how can a man then understand his own way?* (20:24). David sings the contrast — *Yahuah (LORD) bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought; he maketh the devices of the people of none effect. The counsel of Yahuah (LORD) standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations* (Psalm 33:10-11). Isaiah swears it as an oath and asks who could undo it: *as I have purposed, so shall it stand* (14:24), *Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) hath purposed, and who shall disannul it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?* (14:27); and Yahuah Himself speaks the proverb word for word — *My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure* (46:10). The New Testament reasons from the very same ground: Gamaliel's warning — *if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of Elohim (God), ye can not overthrow it* (Acts 5:38-39) — and Paul's confession of the One *who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will* (Ephesians 1:11). The many devices of man rise and fall; the counsel of Yahuah stands. (Even the fretting heart of *The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against Yahuah (LORD)* (19:3) cannot move it.)

threads.title: The fear of Yahuah tendeth to life
threads.summary_md: The chapter gathers the book's great motto and binds it to life itself: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil* (Proverbs 19:23). The fear of Yahuah is not a dread that shrinks life but the very fountain of it — it tends to life, satisfies, and keeps from evil. This is the refrain of the whole book: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge* (1:7); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom* (9:10); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days* (10:27); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death* (14:27); *By humility and the fear of Yahuah (LORD) are riches, and honour, and life* (22:4). The restored witness sings it most fully of all: *The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing* (Sirach 1:11); *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (1:12); and the *he shall not be visited with evil* of the proverb is its fearlessness — *Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope* (34:14). The satisfied, evil-unvisited life of the proverb is precisely the life the fear of Yahuah opens, from the first chapter of Proverbs to the restored witness that sings the same.

threads.title: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger
threads.summary_md: The chapter names forbearance a glory: *The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression* (Proverbs 19:11). To let an offence go by is not weakness but honour — and it stands opposite the man who cannot: *A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment* (19:19). The same book crowns the self-governed man above the conqueror: *He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city* (16:32). The New Testament keeps the charge whole: *let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath* (James 1:19); *Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Messiah (Christ) forgave you, so also do ye* (Colossians 3:13); and Yahusha (Jesus) sets the measure of the passing-over without limit — when Peter asks if seven times is enough, *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven* (Matthew 18:22). The discretion that defers anger and passes over a transgression is the very forbearance the whole library commends — to rule one's own spirit, and to forgive as one has been forgiven.

threads.title: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets the kept commandment as the keeping of one's own life: *He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die* (Proverbs 19:16). The Torah is no bondage; to keep it is to keep the soul, and to despise one's ways is death. The chapter circles the same truth from every side — *He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good* (19:8), *Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end* (19:20), and the guarded ear of *Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge* (19:27). It is the Torah's own promise of life: *keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply* (Deuteronomy 30:16). The same book states both halves again — *Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded* (Proverbs 13:13) — and charges the holding-fast — *Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life* (4:13). And the New Testament keeps the bond unbroken, never severing love from the commandment: *If ye love me, keep my commandments* (John 14:15); so too the restored witness — *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The kept commandment keeps the soul; the despised way is death — the anti-antinomian couplet of the chapter.

threads.title: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with the deceiving cup: *Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise* (Proverbs 20:1). The wine mocks — it promises gladness and delivers folly — and the man who trusts it is, by that trust, *not wise*. The same book unfolds the warning in full: *Who hath woe? who hath sorrow?... who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?* (Proverbs 23:29); *Look not thou upon the wine when it is red... At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder* (Proverbs 23:31-32). The deceit is in the delay — sweet at the lip, venom at the last. Isaiah lays the woe on those mastered by it: *Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink* (Isaiah 5:11), *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine* (Isaiah 5:22) — a counterfeit strength, mighty only to be deceived. Habakkuk curses the one who pours it for a neighbour: *Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink... and makest him drunken also* (Habakkuk 2:15). And the NT keeps the warning and gives its remedy — not abstinence alone but a better filling: *be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit* (Ephesians 5:18).

threads.title: Who can say, I have made my heart clean? — the heart Yahuah cleanses
threads.summary_md: The chapter's keystone is a question no son of Adam can answer Yes: *Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?* (Proverbs 20:9). The whole library presses the same verdict of universal sinfulness. The Preacher answers flat: *there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not* (Ecclesiastes 7:20). Solomon himself, who wrote the proverb, prayed it at the temple: *there is no man that sinneth not* (1 Kings 8:46). Job asked it and answered: *Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one* (Job 14:4). David traced the sin to its root: *Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me* (Psalm 51:5). Jeremiah named the unsearchable heart: *The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?* (17:9). The New Testament holds the very same measure, never raising nor lowering it: *For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God)* (Romans 3:23); *If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us* (1 John 1:8); *in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing* (Romans 7:18). But Proverbs 20:9 asks a question the covenant ANSWERS — and here is the anti-antinomian hinge against the misreading that sin is therefore permanent. The man cannot make his own heart clean; Yahuah makes it clean. David asks for it as a creation, not a feat: *Create in me a clean heart, O Elohim (God); and renew a right spirit within me* (Psalm 51:10). And Ezekiel promises the new-covenant cleansing in full: *Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean... A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you... And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:25-27). The clean heart is given, not self-made — and the heart Yahuah cleanses is the heart that KEEPS His statutes. Universal sinfulness is no license; it is the very reason the new heart, with the Torah written upon it, is needed.

threads.title: Divers weights and measures — an abomination to Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Twice in the chapter the cheating scale is condemned: *Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 20:10), and *Divers weights are an abomination unto Yahuah (LORD); and a false balance is not good* (Proverbs 20:23). This is no mere commercial counsel but the Torah's own honest-measures law set as a couplet. Moses commanded it directly: *Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard, in weight, or in measure* (Leviticus 19:35); *Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* (Leviticus 19:36) — sealed with the redeemer's Name, so that honest measures are covenant fidelity itself. Deuteronomy names the very cheat: *Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great and a small* (25:13), and ties the honest scale to long life — *a perfect and just weight... that thy days may be lengthened in the land* (25:15) — closing with the same word the proverb uses: *all that do unrighteously, are an abomination unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (25:16). The same book of Proverbs twins it — *A false balance is abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but a just weight is his delight* (11:1) — and grounds it in ownership: *A just weight and balance are the LORD’S; all the weights of the bag are his work* (16:11). To falsify the scale is to falsify what belongs to Yahuah. And Micah carries the same Torah law into the covenant lawsuit: *Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?* (6:11). The honest scale is a commandment, never abolished.

threads.title: The hearing ear, the seeing eye — Yahuah made both, and searches the heart
threads.summary_md: The chapter twins the Maker of the senses with the Searcher of the heart: *The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahuah (LORD) hath made even both of them* (Proverbs 20:12), and *The spirit of man is the candle of Yahuah (LORD), searching all the inward parts of the belly* (Proverbs 20:27). The One who MADE the eye and ear is the One who SEARCHES the man through them. Yahuah claims the making in His own words to Moses: *Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I Yahuah (LORD)?* (Exodus 4:11). The Psalmist draws the conclusion: *He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?* (Psalm 94:9) — the Maker of the senses is no blind, deaf idol, not subject to their limits. And the searching reaches every hidden chamber: *Hell and destruction are before Yahuah (LORD): how much more then the hearts of the children of men?* (Proverbs 15:11) — the candle He set in man lights all the inward parts for His eye. Sha'ul reasons from the same lamp: *what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of Elohim (God) knoweth no man, but the Spirit of Elohim (God)* (1 Corinthians 2:11). The inward lamp of the man is the figure of a searching that reaches all.

threads.title: Say not, I will recompense evil — wait on Yahuah, and he shall save thee
threads.summary_md: The chapter leaves vengeance where it belongs: *Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save thee* (Proverbs 20:22). The reason is Yahuah's own claim in the Song of Moses: *To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time* (Deuteronomy 32:35). The proverb is the Torah's love-command turned toward the one who wronged you: *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 19:18). The same book repeats it almost word for word — *Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me* (Proverbs 24:29) — and turns non-vengeance into active mercy: *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink* (Proverbs 25:21). The New Testament keeps the measure whole and grounds it by quoting the Torah by name: *avenge not yourselves... for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith Yahuah (Lord)* (Romans 12:19); *Recompense to no man evil for evil* (Romans 12:17); *See that none render evil for evil unto any man* (1 Thessalonians 5:15); *Not rendering evil for evil... but contrariwise blessing* (1 Peter 3:9). And Yahusha (Jesus) lifts it to its summit: *Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you* (Matthew 5:44) — the non-recompense fulfilled as active love, not erased. The restored witness states the danger and the way: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 28:1); *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest* (Sirach 28:2) — the one who releases vengeance is the one whose own prayer is heard; *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest* (Sirach 28:7). From Torah to prophets to Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witnesses, the word is one: do not recompense; wait on Yahuah, and He shall save.

threads.title: Man's goings are of Yahuah — how can a man understand his own way?
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets the sovereign hand over the human path: *Man’s goings are of Yahuah (LORD); how can a man then understand his own way?* (Proverbs 20:24). The man plans, but the directing is not finally his — and so the way is beyond his own understanding. The same book states it plain: *A man’s heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (Proverbs 16:9); *There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of Yahuah (LORD), that shall stand* (Proverbs 19:21). The man's devices are many; the counsel of Yahuah is the one that comes to pass. Jeremiah confesses the very truth in prayer: *O Yahuah (LORD), I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps* (Jeremiah 10:23). The Formless Source, not the son of Adam, directs the goings — which is why a man cannot fully chart his own way, and is called instead to walk it in trust.

threads.title: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah than sacrifice
threads.summary_md: The framework heavyweight of the chapter is a key, not a key to the lock of the Torah: *To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice* (Proverbs 21:3). This is obedience-and-mercy set ABOVE empty ritual — NOT the abolition of the sacrificial system. The SAME Torah commands both the justice and the offering; the prophets and Yahusha (Jesus) rebuke ritual divorced from obedience, never the appointed worship itself. Samuel set the measure first, to a king who kept the spoil and disobeyed the voice: *Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams* (1 Samuel 15:22). Hosea sang it — *For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* (6:6). Micah weighed *thousands of rams* against the requirement and found it: *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (6:8). Isaiah set the courts full of sacrifice against the un-done justice — *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?* (1:11) — and sent the people back to it: *seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow* (1:17). David named the acceptable heart-posture beneath the offering — *The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (51:17). Amos thundered it — *let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (5:24). And the same chapter gives the dark twin: *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?* (21:27) — it is the WICKED man's sacrifice, the rite in place of justice, that is loathed. The New Testament keeps the SAME measure, never abolishing it: Yahusha quotes Hosea twice — *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13; 12:7) — sending the Pharisees to *learn what that meaneth*; and the scribe who saw that love *is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices* (Mark 12:33) was answered as not far from the kingdom. The restored witness states both sides plainest: the unjust offering refused — *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous... The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked* (Sirach 34:18-19) — and the kept Torah accepted — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough* (Sirach 35:1). From Samuel to the prophets to Proverbs to Yahusha to the restored witness, the testimony is one: the justice and the offering both belong to Yahuah, and the doing of justice is the more acceptable approach — the empty offering of the unjust is the only sacrifice refused.

threads.title: The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah — He turneth it whithersoever He will
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens on the sovereignty of the Father over the highest thrones: *The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will* (Proverbs 21:1). As a man channels water, so Yahuah turns the heart even of a pagan king. The same book teaches it in plainer dress — *A man's heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (16:9); *There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of Yahuah (LORD), that shall stand* (19:21); *Man's goings are of Yahuah (LORD); how can a man then understand his own way?* (20:24). Ezra saw the proverb become history — Yahuah *turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of Elohim (God)* (6:22). Daniel sang the sovereign who *removeth kings, and setteth up kings* (2:21), before whom *none can stay his hand* (4:35). Even the conquering empire is a tool — *O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger* (Isaiah 10:5) — wielded though he *meaneth not so*. And the New Testament keeps it whole: Sha'ul charges that *there is no power but of Elohim (God): the powers that be are ordained of Elohim (God)* (Romans 13:1); the Formed Son tells Pilate, *Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above* (John 19:11); and at the cross the rulers did only *whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done* (Acts 4:28). The thrones of the earth are held in the hand that turns them whithersoever He will.

threads.title: Every way right in his own eyes — but Yahuah pondereth the hearts
threads.summary_md: Set beside the sovereign hand is the searching eye: *Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but Yahuah (LORD) pondereth the hearts* (Proverbs 21:2). What a man clears in his own court is weighed in Yahuah's, and the verdicts differ. The same book sets the couplet twice — *All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but Yahuah (LORD) weigheth the spirits* (16:2) — and warns where the self-cleared way ends: *There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death* (14:12). The pondering is the pondering that renders judgment — *doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? ... shall not he render to every man according to his works?* (24:12) — and no plea of ignorance stands before it. Yahuah sees what man cannot: *man looketh on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looketh on the heart* (1 Samuel 16:7). Yahusha (Jesus) states it flat against the self-justified — *ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but Elohim (God) knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of Elohim (God)* (Luke 16:15). The way that is right in a man's own eyes, even highly esteemed among men, is weighed by the One who pondereth the hearts.

threads.title: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
threads.summary_md: The chapter binds the heard prayer to a heard poor man: *Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard* (Proverbs 21:13). The stopped ear is answered in kind — the measure is given back. To shut the ear to the poor is to reproach Yahuah Himself — *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31) — and the same book twins the stopped ear with the hidden eye that inherits the curse: *he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse* (28:27). The Torah warned the very cry: shut not thine hand, *and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee* (Deuteronomy 15:9). Yahusha (Jesus) drew the whole law of it in the servant who would not show the mercy he had received, *delivered... to the tormentors* (Matthew 18:34); and Ya'aqob (James) states it as a verdict — *he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment* (James 2:13). The restored witness names the stopped ear as the defrauding that *make[s] the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1) and gives the exact reversal of the proverb — the stopper's cry goes unheard, but the poor man's is heard: *if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him* (Sirach 4:6). The other side of the chapter is the same mercy pursued instead of stopped — *He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour* (21:21).

threads.title: There is no wisdom against Yahuah — the horse is prepared, but safety is of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes on the sovereignty of Yahuah over every plan and every army: *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD). The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 21:30-31). No human strategy stands against Him, and no war-horse secures the victory He alone gives. The Psalms strip the horse bare — *An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength* (33:17); *Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)* (20:7). Isaiah pronounces the woe — *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots... but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (31:1) — for *their horses flesh, and not spirit* (31:3). Job names why no counsel stands against Him — *He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong* (5:13). Zechariah names where the true strength lies — *Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (4:6). And Sha'ul keeps the no-wisdom-against-Yahuah whole — *I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent* (1 Corinthians 1:19), for *the foolishness of Elohim (God) is wiser than men* (1:25) — as Gamaliel warned, *if it be of Elohim (God), ye can not overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against Elohim (God)* (Acts 5:39). The horse may be prepared; the safety, the wisdom, and the victory are Yahuah's alone.

threads.title: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with a weighing: *A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold* (Proverbs 22:1). What endures is not the silver and gold but the name and the favour a man keeps before Yahuah and before men. Qoheleth weighs it the same: *A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth* (Ecclesiastes 7:1). The loving favour set above gold is named in the book itself — *So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of Elohim (God) and man* (Proverbs 3:4) — and its endurance against the wealth that perishes: *The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot* (Proverbs 10:7). The restored witness presses the choice home: *Have regard to your name; for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold* (Sirach 41:12); *A good life has but few days: but a good name endureth for ever* (Sirach 41:13). Riches are few and the days fewer; the good name alone abides past death.

threads.title: The rich and poor meet together — Yahuah is the maker of them all
threads.summary_md: At the heart of the chapter's poor-cluster stands the levelling truth: *The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all* (Proverbs 22:2). Because ONE Maker formed both, the treatment of the poor is bound directly to the honour of Yahuah: *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31); *Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker* (17:5); *The poor and the deceitful man meet together: Yahuah (LORD) lighteneth both their eyes* (29:13). Job grounds it in the womb, as the ground of justice to his servant: *Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?* (31:15); and Elihu draws the verdict: Yahuah *accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands* (34:19). The chapter's own couplets turn on this: *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor* (22:9), and *He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches... shall surely come to want* (22:16). The NT makes the one-Maker truth the law's own measure: *if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors* (James 2:9); *Hath not Elohim (God) chosen the poor of this world rich in faith* (James 2:5); *Of a truth I perceive that Elohim (God) is no respecter of persons* (Acts 10:34). And the restored witness: *poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 11:14). The rich and the poor meet on one ground — the one Maker who shows no partiality.

threads.title: By humility and the fear of Yahuah are riches, and honour, and life
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets the true wealth in its proper soil: *By humility and the fear of Yahuah (LORD) are riches, and honour, and life* (Proverbs 22:4). Not silver and gold but the lowly, Yahuah-fearing heart inherits the lasting riches. The fear-of-Yahuah motto runs the whole book — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction* (1:7) — and it is twinned with humility just as here: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility* (15:33); *Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility* (18:12). The order is fixed: humility goes before honour, never after. The NT keeps the same measure unbroken: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10). The lifting is Yahuah's to give, and He gives it to the humble who fear Him.

threads.title: Train up a child in the way he should go — the covenant handed down
threads.summary_md: The chapter carries the generational covenant charge: *Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it* (Proverbs 22:6). The *way he should go* is not generic parenting but the covenant way — the way of Yahuah, the Torah handed down father to son.
