This is the coming he guards — the ark set into the most holy place: *And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD) unto his place, to the oracle of the house, into the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims* (2 Chronicles 5:7). Holiness has been graded by the ark's presence from the first: *And the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy* (Exodus 26:33). And the ark carries a holiness that cannot be treated lightly: *they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die* (Numbers 4:15). Solomon honours that same weight. Where the ark of Yahuah has come, the ground is no longer common; the king orders his own household around the holiness of the place.

threads.title: The queen of Sheba — and "a greater than Solomon is here"
threads.summary_md: A foreign queen hears the fame of Solomon and *came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones* (2 Chronicles 9:1) — Kings adds it was *the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD)* that drew her (1 Kings 10:1). Solomon answers everything: *there was nothing hid from Solomon which he told her not* (9:2), and she breaks: *the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me: for thou exceedest the fame that I heard* (9:6), the same confession Kings keeps — *the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard* (1 Kings 10:7). She lays out her gold and spices (9:9), enacting the royal psalm — *The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts* (Psalm 72:10) — and the prophet's vision: *all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 60:6). The countries marvelled at the king (Ecclesiasticus 47:17). All of it is shadow. The Messiah lifts her up as a witness against his own generation: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment... for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42; Luke 11:31). The queen from the south and the wise men from the east who open their treasures of *gold, and frankincense, and myrrh* (Matthew 2:11) are the same magnet — the nations drawn across the earth to the wisdom and glory Yahuah gives the Davidic king.

threads.title: "To be king for Yahuah" — the throne of Yahuah, to do judgment and justice
threads.summary_md: The queen's blessing reaches past the king to the One who set him there: *Blessed be Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): because thy Elohim (God) loved Yashar'el (Israel), to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice* (2 Chronicles 9:8). The seat is named without ambiguity: *Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahuah (LORD) as king instead of David his father* (1 Chronicles 29:23). It is Yahuah's throne; the king reigns FOR him, never in his own right, and the charge is *judgment and justice*. The royal psalm prays for exactly that gift — *Give the king thy judgments, O Elohim (God), and thy righteousness unto the king's son* (Psalm 72:1); *He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment* (Psalm 72:2). Righteous rule is Yahuah's judgments lent to his vicegerent. What Solomon does in figure, the promised Branch will do in truth and for ever: *I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth* (Jeremiah 23:5).

threads.title: All the kings of the earth sought the wisdom Yahuah put in his heart
threads.summary_md: *And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that Elohim (God) had put in his heart* (2 Chronicles 9:23). Kings records the same draw word for word — *all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which Elohim (God) had put in his heart* (1 Kings 10:24) — and both fix the source: the wisdom was PUT in his heart by Elohim; the nations sought a gift, not a self-made greatness. The restored praise of Solomon sings the reach of it: *Your name went far to the islands; and for your peace you were beloved* (Ecclesiasticus 47:16); *The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations* (Ecclesiasticus 47:17). The kings of the earth marvelling at the wisdom Yahuah gave the Davidic king is the very magnet the greater Son of David inherits — the nations streaming to the wisdom of the King.

threads.title: The gold passing all kings — the wealth added to the wisdom given
threads.summary_md: The chapter heaps up Solomon's glory: six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold in one year (9:13), targets and shields of beaten gold, the great throne of ivory overlaid with pure gold and twelve lions on its six steps (9:17-19), drinking vessels all of gold so that *silver was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon* (9:20). The summary fixes how to read it: *And king Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom* (2 Chronicles 9:22) — the same word Kings keeps, *So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom* (1 Kings 10:23). Riches and wisdom are named together; the wealth is the blessing ADDED to the wisdom, never sought apart from it. The king himself weighed it so in his restored meditation: *All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:11) — the riches came WITH wisdom, in her train — and *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). The gold that filled his house was nothing beside the wisdom Yahuah gave that drew the nations.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The kingdom divides: the two houses begin
threads.summary_md: Here is the wound that runs the rest of the canon. When *all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel)* (10:16), and *Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day* (10:19). The ten northern tribes — Israel, Ephraim, Joseph — tear away from the southern house of Yahudah (Judah) and the throne of David. The parallel says it the same: *to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel)... So Yashar'el (Israel) departed unto their tents* (1 Kings 12:16). The number was prophesied: *Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). Yet a remnant is kept — *I will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake* (1 Kings 11:13) — and so *Rehoboam reigned over* the children of Yashar'el in the cities of Yahudah (10:17). This is the origin of the TWO houses. The division is real history, the judgment on Solomon's idolatry; it is NEVER one house replacing the other. And it is the very breach the prophets swear to heal: *I will take the stick of Joseph... and the stick of Yahudah (Judah), and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand* (Ezekiel 37:19); *they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all* (Ezekiel 37:22); *the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head* (Hosea 1:11); *the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north* (Jeremiah 3:18). The split is the history; the regathering is the hope.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The cause was of Elohim: Ahijah's word performed
threads.summary_md: Rehoboam's hardness is not blind chance. *So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of Elohim (God), that Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat* (10:15). The word came years earlier in a field: *the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field* (1 Kings 11:29), and rending the garment he said, *Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). The folly of the young men is the instrument; the judgment is Yahuah's — exile-grade discipline for Solomon's idolatry, never the Torah itself failing. And even as ten tribes are torn away, the covenant lamp is kept: *I will give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there* (1 Kings 11:36). The throne is wounded but not extinguished — the lamp the Branch will one day fill.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — Rehoboam forsakes the old men's counsel
threads.summary_md: The Chronicler shows the human folly that the divine word rode upon. The old men counseled mercy — *If thou be kind to this people... they will be thy servants for ever* (10:7) — *but he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him* (10:8), who boasted *My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins* (10:10). *The king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men* (10:13). Wisdom had named this ruin in advance: *Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety* (Proverbs 11:14); *Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established* (Proverbs 15:22); *The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise* (Proverbs 12:15); *Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom* (Proverbs 13:10). Pride answering roughly, folly right in its own eyes, counsel forsaken — and a kingdom torn in two.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The heavy yoke and the easy yoke
threads.summary_md: Rehoboam's threat was to crush: *For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions* (10:11), and again *My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto* (10:14). The tyranny of the false shepherd drove Yashar'el away. Against him stands the true King, whose call is the opposite: *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest* (Matthew 11:28); *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls* (Matthew 11:29). Where the proud son of David's line laded the people heavier and scattered them, the meek and lowly Son — the Formed One of David's house — lifts the load and gives the soul rest, gathering what tyranny scattered.

threads.title: This Thing Is Done of Me: Fight Not Against Your Brethren
threads.summary_md:
Rehoboam gathers a hundred and fourscore thousand chosen warriors *to fight against Yashar'el (Israel), that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam* (2 Chronicles 11:1). But the word of Yahuah stops him through Shemaiah: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of Yahuah (LORD), and returned from going against Jeroboam* (2 Chronicles 11:4).

Two things are settled in that one sentence. First, the division is Yahuah's own doing — *for this thing is done of me*. The parallel record says it plainly: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel): return every man to his house; for this thing is from me* (1 Kings 12:24), and the chapter before names the cause — *for the cause was of Elohim (God), that Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat* (2 Chronicles 10:15). The tearing of the kingdom was a prophesied judgment, not an accident to be reversed by the sword.

Second, the two houses are *brethren*. The same word that splits them forbids them to war, because they remain one blood. It is the ground Abram took with Lot: *Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren* (Genesis 13:8). Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) are divided, but they are not made two peoples to destroy each other — they are one people to be regathered.

threads.title: Jeroboam's Calves and Devils: The Counterfeit Worship
threads.summary_md:
When the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared the people's hearts would turn back if they kept going up to Jerusalem, so he built a rival worship: *the priests and the Levites that were in all Yashar'el (Israel) resorted to him* — that is, fled to Rehoboam — *for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto Yahuah (LORD): And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made* (2 Chronicles 11:13-15).

Every piece of it is a counterfeit. The calves are the old wilderness idol resurrected: *he made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28) — word for word the sin at Sinai, *they have made them a molten calf... and said, These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (Exodus 32:8). The priesthood is a counterfeit: *he made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi* (1 Kings 12:31), having cast off the true Levites. And the *devils* are the very thing the Torah forbade for ever: *they shall no more offer their sacrifices unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring. This shall be a statute for ever unto them throughout their generations* (Leviticus 17:7).

The restored witness names the whole apparatus before it ever happened: *And they will make to themselves high places and groves and graven images, and they will worship, each his own (graven image), so as to go astray, and they will sacrifice their children to demons, and to all the works of the error of their hearts* (Jubilees 1:10). The system is the enemy here, not the people — they are the prey it was built to capture, kept from the house Yahuah chose by a king's fear.

threads.title: The Heart-Remnant of the North Seek Yahuah at Jerusalem
threads.summary_md:
The calf-cult did not capture everyone. After the Levites came south, the text adds: *And after them out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) such as set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers* — and *so they strengthened the kingdom of Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 11:16-17). A heart-remnant out of the northern tribes refuses Jeroboam's high places and turns toward the house Yahuah chose.

They are doing exactly what the Torah commanded: *unto the place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come* (Deuteronomy 12:5). The same movement runs again generations later under Hezekiah — *divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:11). And it is the same remnant Yahuah names to Elijah when all the north seemed lost: *Yet I have left me seven thousand in Yashar'el (Israel), all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him* (1 Kings 19:18).

This is the two-house pattern in miniature: the houses are divided, but across the divide there are always those who *set their hearts to seek Yahuah* and gather to true worship. The faithful are never wholly swept away with the counterfeit, and the seeking remnant is the seed of the regathering to come.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:1 — Strengthened, He Forsook the Law of Yahuah (Prosperity Breeds Apostasy)
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler states the tragedy in one sentence: *And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of Yahuah (LORD), and all Yashar'el (Israel) with him* (2 Chronicles 12:1). Strength is the occasion of the forsaking — and the thing forsaken is named exactly: *the law of Yahuah*. The Torah is not the curse here; it is the covenant inheritance abandoned the moment the king felt secure.

Moses had foretold this very mechanism in the wilderness. *Beware that thou forget not Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day* (Deuteronomy 8:11) — and the trigger he named was fullness: *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage* (Deuteronomy 8:14). Rehoboam is the lifted-up heart of the full man, and Yahuah's discipline comes fittingly by the hand of Egypt — the house of bondage he forgot.

The Song of Moses had carved it into an image: *But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked... then he forsook Elohim (God) which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation* (Deuteronomy 32:15). And Hosea names the same disease in the northern house — *they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me* (Hosea 13:6). Fullness, an exalted heart, then forgetting: one apostasy that fells both houses. The warning stands over every season of strength — it is precisely when we are strengthened that we are most apt to forsake the very instruction that made us.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:6-8 — They Humbled Themselves: "Yahuah Is Righteous" (Mercy, and the Servitude That Teaches)
threads.summary_md:
Shishak comes up because *they had transgressed against Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 12:2), and Shemaiah delivers the sentence in the covenant's own grammar: *Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak* (2 Chronicles 12:5). But the response turns the judgment: *Whereupon the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous* (2 Chronicles 12:6).

That confession is the heartbeat of the whole canon's history. To say *Yahuah is righteous* is to justify the chastening and accuse oneself — exactly Daniel's plea, *Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice* (Daniel 9:14), and the Levites' return-prayer, *thou art just in all that is brought upon us; for thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly* (Nehemiah 9:33). It is the formula Solomon was given at this very house: *If my people... shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face... then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin* (2 Chronicles 7:14).

And Yahuah answers in kind: *when Yahuah (LORD) saw that they humbled themselves... I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance* (2 Chronicles 12:7) — the not-consuming mercy Jeremiah sings from the ruins, *It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not* (Lamentations 3:22). Yet mercy is not the cancelling of discipline: *Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries* (2 Chronicles 12:8). The servitude is pedagogy — they will learn by contrast the difference between serving Yahuah and serving the nations. The apostolic word names the unchanging law beneath it all: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10).

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:14 — He Prepared Not His Heart to Seek Yahuah (the Root Diagnosis)
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler closes Rehoboam's reign with a single, piercing diagnosis: *And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 12:14). The evil is traced not to circumstance but to the heart — the heart that was never set, never prepared, to seek. This is the religion of the inward man: not ritual, not lineage, but the heart turned to seek.

The canon supplies the exact inverse as its standing portrait. *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments* (Ezra 7:10) — the prepared heart seeks the Torah, does it, and teaches it; Rehoboam's unprepared heart did none. Samuel had named this as the very condition of deliverance: *prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD), and serve him only: and he will deliver you* (1 Samuel 7:3). The Chronicler himself sets up Jehoshaphat as the deliberate foil — *thou hast... prepared thine heart to seek Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 19:3) — measuring two kings by the single ruler of the prepared heart.

Hezekiah's intercession reveals how heavily Yahuah weighs it, even above ceremonial purity: he pleads pardon for everyone *that prepareth his heart to seek Elohim (God), Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary* (2 Chronicles 30:19). And Asaph's history-psalm warns the children not to become *a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with Elohim (God)* (Psalm 78:8). Rehoboam is that fathers' generation in one man: the unprepared heart is the seedbed of the evil.

threads.title: The Kingdom to David For Ever — by a Covenant of Salt
threads.summary_md: Standing on mount Zemaraim, Abijah grounds the whole war not in his own right but in a sworn covenant: *Ought ye not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?* (2 Chronicles 13:5). The phrase reaches straight back to Nathan's oracle — *I will set up thy seed after thee... and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever... thy throne shall be established for ever* (2 Samuel 7:12-16). "Covenant of salt" is Torah's own idiom for a bond that cannot spoil or lapse: the priesthood was given *by a covenant of salt for ever* (Numbers 18:19), and *the salt of the covenant of thy Elohim (God)* was laid on every offering (Leviticus 2:13) — salt that preserves, a covenant that does not fail. The psalmist sings the same oath: *I have sworn unto David my servant, Thy seed will I establish for ever* (Psalm 89:3-4), and Yahuah swears *My covenant will I not break... I will not lie unto David* (Psalm 89:34-35). The second-Temple witnesses remember it identically — *he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Sirach 47:11), a *root to David* that abides (Sirach 47:22), the kingdom *to his posterity alone* (Sirach 45:25). And it all comes to rest on the Formed Son: *Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end* (Luke 1:32-33). Note that Abijah pleads with the north as brethren — *O children of Yashar'el (Israel), fight ye not against Yahuah Elohim of your fathers* — both houses are still Yashar'el; the salt covenant is the throne under which the two will one day be one.

threads.title: The Golden Calves — the Counterfeit Against the Charge of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Abijah's indictment of the north is precise: *ye be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods. Have ye not cast out the priests of Yahuah (LORD), the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations* (2 Chronicles 13:8-9). The calves are no innovation — Jeroboam *made two calves of gold, and said... behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28), reviving the very wilderness lie: *These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel)... they have made them a molten calf* (Exodus 32:4,8). Over against the counterfeit, Abijah sets the kept charge: *as for us, Yahuah (LORD) is our Elohim (God), and we have not forsaken him... they burn unto Yahuah every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense... for we keep the charge of Yahuah Eloheinu* (2 Chronicles 13:10-11). That charge is Torah's own appointment — *two lambs... day by day, for a continual burnt offering... in the morning... at even* (Numbers 28:3-4), and *sweet incense every morning... a perpetual incense* with the lamps (Exodus 30:7-8). So when Abijah cries *Elohim (God) himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Yashar'el (Israel), fight ye not against Yahuah Elohim of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper* (2 Chronicles 13:12), he is preaching the war-Torah of Deuteronomy — *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is he that goeth with you, to fight for you* (Deuteronomy 20:1,4) — and standing in David's confidence against Goliath, *the battle is the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 17:45-47). The system is the enemy, not the people: Jeroboam built the calf-cult, and the northern brethren are its victims, kept from Jerusalem by a king's counterfeit.

threads.title: Judah Prevailed — Because They Relied Upon Yahuah
threads.summary_md: The battle turns on a single thing. Judah, outnumbered two to one and caught in an ambush before and behind, does not trust to arms: *they cried unto Yahuah (LORD), and the priests sounded with the trumpets. Then the men of Yahudah (Judah) gave a shout: and as the men of Yahudah (Judah) shouted, it came to pass, that Elohim (God) smote Jeroboam* (2 Chronicles 13:14-15). The chronicler names the cause plainly: *the children of Yahudah (Judah) prevailed, because they relied upon Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers* (2 Chronicles 13:18). This is the dependent faith the whole book teaches. Abijah's own son Asa would pray it next: *help us, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God); for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude* (2 Chronicles 14:11). The psalmist draws the line: *Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)* (Psalm 20:7). Wisdom commands it: *Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding* (Proverbs 3:5). And Hezekiah would later voice the same contrast against an even greater host: *With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) to help us, and to fight our battles* (2 Chronicles 32:8). The larger army is the arm of flesh; the victory is to those who lean on the Name.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 14 — Asa's reform: seek Yahuah, and do the law
threads.summary_md: Asa *did that which was good and right in the eyes of Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)* (14:2), and his reform has three motions that are one. First he tears down: *he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves* (14:3) — the very command of the Torah obeyed, *ye shall overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire; and ye shall hew down the graven images of their gods* (Deuteronomy 12:3), the same purge Hezekiah will make, who *removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves* (2 Kings 18:4). Then he turns the heart: he *commanded Yahudah (Judah) to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment* (14:4) — to *love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart* (Deuteronomy 6:5), to *fear Yahuah... to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve* him with the whole heart (Deuteronomy 10:12). The law is not the curse here; it is the substance of true reform — *Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart* (Psalm 119:2). Removing the idols, seeking Yahuah, and DOING THE LAW are not three competing things but one whole-hearted return; the Torah is what the broken images make room for.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 14 — The land had rest: the fruit of seeking
threads.summary_md: The rest is not luck; it is harvest. *The land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because Yahuah (LORD) had given him rest* (14:6), and Asa names the cause plainly: *because we have sought Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered* (14:7). This is the promised blessing on the whole-hearted seeker — *Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart* (Psalm 119:2). And it grows straight out of the obedience just before it: because Yahudah first tore down the strange altars as the Torah commands — *ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations... served their gods* (Deuteronomy 12:2) — and sought Yahuah, the land was given rest. The peace, the building, the prospering are the fruit; the root is the Torah kept and the heart turned. Where Yahuah is sought, rest is given on every side.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 14 — Asa's cry: Yahuah saves not by many or by few
threads.summary_md: Zerah the Ethiopian comes against Yahudah *with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots* (14:9) — an army no muster could match. And Asa does the one thing the framework holds as the heart of faith: he stops counting his own strength and rests on Yahuah. *And Asa cried unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and said, Yahuah (LORD), it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God); for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our Elohim (God); let not man prevail against thee* (14:11). This is the cry that runs through the whole canon: *there is no restraint to Yahuah (LORD) to save by many or by few* (1 Samuel 14:6); *Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 17:47); *Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)* (Psalm 20:7); *There is no king saved by the multitude of an host* (Psalm 33:16); *Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Zechariah 4:6). It is the same reliance that gave his father Abijah victory — Yahudah *prevailed, because they relied upon Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers* (2 Chronicles 13:18) — and the same prayer Jehoshaphat will pray, *we have no might... but our eyes are upon thee* (2 Chronicles 20:12). And so it is answered: *So Yahuah (LORD) smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Yahudah (Judah); and the Ethiopians fled* (14:12). The deliverance is given not by the arm of flesh but by the Name on which they rested.

threads.title: If Ye Seek Him, He Will Be Found; If Ye Forsake Him, He Will Forsake You
threads.summary_md:
The Spirit of Elohim comes upon Azariah, and he meets king Asa with the heart of the whole covenant in a single sentence: *Hear ye me, Asa, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin; Yahuah (LORD) is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you* (2 Chronicles 15:2). This is the seek/forsake principle — Yahuah is found by the seeking heart and lost to the forsaking one. It is not lineage alone and not a confession alone; it is the heart that actually turns and seeks.

It is no new word. David spoke its verbatim twin over Solomon: *for Yahuah (LORD) searcheth all hearts... if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever* (1 Chronicles 28:9). And it is rooted in the Torah itself: *if from thence thou shalt seek Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul* (Deuteronomy 4:29). The prophets carry it forward — *ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart* (Jeremiah 29:13); *Seek ye Yahuah (LORD) while he may be found* (Isaiah 55:6).

The principle cuts both ways, and the same book proves the dark edge of it. When a later generation forsook, the Spirit came on another prophet with the same word: *because ye have forsaken Yahuah (LORD), he hath also forsaken you* (2 Chronicles 24:20). And the promise side is sealed in the mouth of the Formed Son himself: *seek, and ye shall find* (Matthew 7:7), and in the apostolic word, *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you* (James 4:8). The restored wisdom-witness asks it as a question that answers itself: *did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?* (Ecclesiasticus 2:10). None who truly sought were ever forsaken.

threads.title: Without the True Elohim, Without a Teaching Priest, Without Law
threads.summary_md:
Azariah names Israel's long desolation by what it lacked: *Now for a long season Yashar'el (Israel) hath been without the true Elohim (God), and without a teaching priest, and without law* (2 Chronicles 15:3). The desolation is not the Torah set aside — it is the Torah withheld and unsought, a people stripped of true worship, the teaching priest gone silent, the law unread.

The prophets call this a famine. *Behold, the days come, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahuah (LORD)* (Amos 8:11) — and the famine bites when men *run to and fro to seek the word of Yahuah (LORD), and shall not find it* (Amos 8:12). Hosea sets the same catalogue of absence over the northern house: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim* (Hosea 3:4). The lack of the Torah and the true priesthood IS the judgment — never their abolition.

But the desolation is not the end of the story, because the seeking heart still finds. *But when they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and sought him, he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:4). Hosea writes the same return: *Afterward shall the children of Yashar'el (Israel) return, and seek Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God)... in the latter days* (Hosea 3:5). The Torah foretold the turning-in-trouble: *When thou art in tribulation... if thou turn to Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt be obedient unto his voice* (Deuteronomy 4:30). And the restored witness traces the captive people who *in the land of their captivities... shall remember themselves* (Baruch 2:30) and are brought back. Trouble drives the turn; the turn ends the famine.

threads.title: Be Ye Strong: Your Work Shall Be Rewarded
threads.summary_md:
Azariah closes his prophecy with a charge to courage and a promise of recompence: *Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded* (2 Chronicles 15:7). The hands that do not slacken in the work of Yahuah have their reward secured — faithful obedience is never spent in vain.

The New Testament holds out the same recompence to the same kind of unwearied hands. *Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward* (Hebrews 10:35). *And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not* (Galatians 6:9) — the very weak hands Azariah warns against. *Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of Yahuah (Lord), forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in Yahuah (Lord)* (1 Corinthians 15:58).

The restored wisdom-witness sets the same promise beside the same call to fear and trust: *You that fear Yahuah (God), believe him; and your reward shall not fail* (Ecclesiasticus 2:8). This is reward for faithful work, the living obedient faith that does not let its hands grow weak — never works hoarded as merit, but the recompence Yahuah keeps for those who keep their strength in his service.

threads.title: A Covenant to Seek Yahuah With All the Heart: The Northern Remnant Join
threads.summary_md:
Asa heard the prophecy and acted: he *put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin... and renewed the altar of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 15:8). Then the gathering widens beyond the south — *he gathered all Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Yashar'el (Israel) in abundance, when they saw that Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) was with him* (2 Chronicles 15:9). The faithful of the NORTHERN tribes come south in abundance — the two-house remnant gathering to true worship across the divide, drawn by the LORD's presence with Judah. This is never replacement; it is the seeking remnant of one people regathering.

There they bind themselves by covenant: *they entered into a covenant to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul... And they sware unto Yahuah (LORD) with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets... and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and Yahuah (LORD) gave them rest round about* (2 Chronicles 15:12-15). The wholehearted seeking is the Shema lived: *thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might* (Deuteronomy 6:5).

This is the covenant-renewal pattern that recurs at every true reform. Joshua sealed it at the founding: *So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem* (Joshua 24:25). The returned remnant under Nehemiah did the same — *we make a sure covenant, and write it; and our princes, Levites, and priests, seal unto it* (Nehemiah 9:38) — entering *into an oath, to walk in Elohim's (God's) law, which was given by Moses... and to observe and do all the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)* (Nehemiah 10:29). To covenant to SEEK Yahuah is to covenant to KEEP his Torah; the two are one. And the promise meets the seeking exactly as Jeremiah foretold — *ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart* (Jeremiah 29:13) — for *he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:15).

threads.title: The eyes of Yahuah run to and fro, seeking the perfect heart to strengthen
threads.summary_md: When Asa relies on Syria instead of Yahuah, the seer Hanani lays bare the doctrine of the searching gaze: *For the eyes of Yahuah (LORD) run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him* (2 Chronicles 16:9). The eyes do not range the earth to find the strong but to STRENGTHEN the wholehearted. Zechariah, prophesying to the returned remnant, sees the very same eyes: *they are the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), which run to and fro through the whole earth* (Zechariah 4:10). The wisdom writers fix the doctrine plainly — *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good* (Proverbs 15:3) — and Elihu: *For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings* (Job 34:21). David sings the gracious side: *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry* (Psalm 34:15), which Kepha (Peter) carries straight forward into the assembly: *For the eyes of Yahuah (Lord) are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of Yahuah (Lord) is against them that do evil* (1 Peter 3:12). The doctrine never moved across the whole canon: Yahuah's strength is pledged to the perfect heart and withdrawn from the heart that departs. Asa, who once rested wholly on Yahuah, forfeited that resting the day he leaned on the arm of flesh.

threads.title: Asa hires Syria — the arm of flesh where once was faith
threads.summary_md: Threatened by Baasha king of Yashar'el (Israel), Asa *brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of Yahuah (LORD) and of the king's house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria* (2 Chronicles 16:2), buying a foreign alliance against his brother-house. The tragedy is measured against the same king's earlier faith: against the vast Ethiopian host he had *cried unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)... for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude* (2 Chronicles 14:11) — and was delivered. Azariah had already set the covenant terms: *if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you* (2 Chronicles 15:2). Hanani now collects the debt: *Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand* (2 Chronicles 16:7). To lean on the arm of flesh was to forsake the One who would have been found of him — and the very host he hired escaped his grasp.

threads.title: Trust not in man — cursed be the arm of flesh
threads.summary_md: Asa's whole failure is the textbook case of a curse Jeremiah would later name: *Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 17:5). For Asa *relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (2 Chronicles 16:7) — flesh made his arm, the heart departed. The psalmist forbids the very transaction: *Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of Adam, in whom there is no help* (Psalm 146:3); the help Asa purchased from a foreign prince slipped through his fingers, for in the son of Adam there was no help. Against this stands Hanani's promise that Yahuah *shew[s] himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him* (2 Chronicles 16:9), and Ben Sira's appeal to the whole record of the fathers: *did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?* (Sirach 2:10). None who trusted was ever confounded — Asa was confounded only when he stopped trusting.

threads.title: Diseased in his feet — he sought not Yahuah but the physicians
threads.summary_md: The same self-reliance that hired Syria follows Asa to his sickbed: *Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12). The indictment is not that he consulted physicians but that he *sought not to Yahuah* — the heart that departed in v.7 does not turn back even under affliction. The northern king Ahaziah shows the same sin in starker dress: in his sickness he sends *to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron* (2 Kings 1:2), and the angel of Yahuah answers, *Is it not because there is not a Elohim (God) in Yashar'el (Israel), that ye go to enquire?* (2 Kings 1:3). Ben Sira guards the reading against any condemnation of medicine: the order is to *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole* (Sirach 38:9) FIRST, and THEN *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him* (Sirach 38:12) — both, in order, the heart turned first to its Maker. The physician is Yahuah's own creation, honourably consulted; the wrong is to seek him INSTEAD of Yahuah. So the proverb that frames Asa's end is exact: *He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician* (Sirach 38:15) — to fall into that hand ALONE, having forsaken Yahuah, is the judgment on the heart that departs.

threads.title: He walked in his commandments, and his heart was lifted up in the ways of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat is the Torah-faithful king drawn in life: *And Yahuah (LORD) was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim; But sought to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 17:3-4). This is the Torah's own charge kept — *Ye shall walk in all the ways which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you, that ye may live... and that ye may prolong your days* (Deuteronomy 5:33) — and the warning not to turn aside obeyed: *ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left* (Deuteronomy 5:32). When *his heart was lifted up in the ways of Yahuah (LORD): moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Yahudah (Judah)* (17:6), he is Joshua's king, the one charged *turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper* (Joshua 1:7) and *thou shalt meditate therein day and night... for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous* (Joshua 1:8). He is Psalm 1 walked out: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly* (Psalm 1:1), whose *delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night* (Psalm 1:2), and who therefore *shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water... and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper* (Psalm 1:3) — answered in *Therefore Yahuah (LORD) stablished the kingdom in his hand... and he had riches and honour in abundance* (17:5). The Torah is not the king's burden; it is the spring of his strength.

threads.title: They taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of Yahuah with them
threads.summary_md: The heart of Jehoshaphat's revival is the itinerant teaching of the Torah to the whole people: *he sent to his princes... to teach in the cities of Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 17:7), *and with them he sent Levites... and... priests* (17:8), *And they taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yahudah (Judah), and taught the people* (17:9). This is the household command of Deuteronomy widened to a kingdom — *thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou... walkest by the way* (Deuteronomy 6:7) — and the Levitical office Moses blessed: *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) thy law* (Deuteronomy 33:10). It is the priestly charge of Malachi: *the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Malachi 2:7), and the grant Ben Sira sets on Aaron — *that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws* (Ecclesiasticus 45:17). Ezra walks the same threefold path, *prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 7:10), and the Levites of Nehemiah finish it: not bare reading but the Torah made understood, *gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading* (Nehemiah 8:8). The pattern runs straight into the Great Commission — *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway* (Matthew 28:20). The Torah is taught and kept, never abolished; this teaching, understood by all the people, is the very substance of true revival.

threads.title: The fear of Yahuah fell upon all the kingdoms round about
threads.summary_md: The fruit of the Torah-faithful, Torah-teaching reign is peace: *And the fear of Yahuah (LORD) fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Yahudah (Judah), so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat* (2 Chronicles 17:10), *And Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly* (17:12). This is the covenant blessing of Deuteronomy 28 made visible — *if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to observe and to do all his commandments... Yahuah Elohayka will set thee on high above all nations* (Deuteronomy 28:1), and *all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of Yahuah (LORD); and they shall be afraid of thee* (Deuteronomy 28:10). The proverb proves the same law in a single reign: *When a man’s ways please Yahuah (LORD), he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him* (Proverbs 16:7). The nations make no war not because Judah is mighty in the field but because Judah's king walks in and teaches the commandments — the fear of Yahuah on the heathen is the overflow of a people who keep his ways.

threads.title: The Unequal Yoke: The Good King Joined to the House of Ahab
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat the righteous king of Yahudah (Judah) *had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab* (2 Chronicles 18:1), the wicked king of the northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) — and at Ahab's feast he bound himself to Ahab's war: *I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war* (2 Chronicles 18:3). This is the unequal yoke Sha'ul forbids: *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* (2 Corinthians 6:14), and against which Yahuah summons his own, *come out from among them, and be ye separate* (2 Corinthians 6:17). The next chapter names the entanglement for what it is: *Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate Yahuah (LORD)? therefore is wrath upon thee from before Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 19:2). It is the blessed man's first warning lived out backward — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners* (Psalm 1:1) — the danger is not the wicked's hatred but the righteous man's willingness to sit at his table and take his cause.

threads.title: Enquire at the Word of Yahuah: The One True Prophet vs the Four Hundred
threads.summary_md: Before the war Jehoshaphat insists, *Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of Yahuah (LORD) to day* (2 Chronicles 18:4). Ahab gathers four hundred prophets who say with one voice *Go up; for Elohim (God) will deliver it* (2 Chronicles 18:5) — yet Jehoshaphat is not satisfied with the crowd: *Is there not here a prophet of Yahuah (LORD) besides, that we might enquire of him?* (2 Chronicles 18:6). The parallel preserves the same instinct: *Is there not here a prophet of Yahuah (LORD) besides, that we might enquire of him?* (1 Kings 22:7). The multitude is no measure of the word. This is the Torah's own test: *If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder* (Deuteronomy 13:1), Yahuah *proveth you, to know whether ye love Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) with all your heart* (Deuteronomy 13:3). Ahab fails the test in advance, hating the one true prophet for the truth itself: *I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil: the same is Micaiah the son of Imla* (2 Chronicles 18:7).

threads.title: The Lying Spirit in the Mouth of the Prophets: Strong Delusion
threads.summary_md: Micaiah unveils the throne-room: *I saw Yahuah (LORD) sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left* (2 Chronicles 18:18). Yahuah asks who will entice Ahab to his fall, and *there came out a spirit... and said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets* (2 Chronicles 18:21), and is permitted: *Now therefore, behold, Yahuah (LORD) hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of these thy prophets, and Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken evil against thee* (2 Chronicles 18:22). The lie is not Yahuah deceiving the innocent — it is judgment given to a king who has already chosen the flattering word over the true. The prophets confirm it: *I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied* (Jeremiah 23:21); *they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 23:16); *The prophets prophesy lies in my name... the deceit of their heart* (Jeremiah 14:14); *They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, Yahuah (LORD) saith: and Yahuah (LORD) hath not sent them* (Ezekiel 13:6). Sha'ul names the same righteousness: *for this cause Elohim (God) shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie* (2 Thessalonians 2:11) — sent to those who *received not the love of the truth*. Therefore the apostolic charge: *believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of Elohim (God): because many false prophets are gone out into the world* (1 John 4:1). Micaiah is smitten on the cheek and cast into prison on bread and water of affliction for the true word (2 Chronicles 18:23-26) — the cost of standing against the flattering majority.

threads.title: The True Word Stands: No Disguise Escapes the Arrow Drawn at a Venture
threads.summary_md: Ahab tries to outwit the prophecy: *I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes* (2 Chronicles 18:29). But no stratagem hides a man from the word Yahuah has spoken — *be sure your sin will find you out* (Numbers 32:23). *And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness* (2 Chronicles 18:33): an arrow loosed at random finds the one unguarded seam, for *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 21:30). The parallel records the same arrow at a venture (1 Kings 22:34), and Ahab dies *about the time of the sun going down* (2 Chronicles 18:34) exactly as Micaiah foretold: *If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not Yahuah (LORD) spoken by me* (2 Chronicles 18:27). The four hundred who promised victory are proven liars, the one true prophet is vindicated, and the despised word stands — the disguise was no escape, and the venture-arrow no accident.

threads.title: Shouldest thou help the ungodly? — the unequal yoke rebuked, yet good things found
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat returns from the Ahab alliance to a seer's rebuke: *Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate Yahuah (LORD)? therefore is wrath upon thee from before Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 19:2). This is the unequal yoke named for what it is — *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* (2 Corinthians 6:14), with its remedy, *come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith Yahuah (Lord)* (2 Corinthians 6:17). David had already drawn the line the king blurred: *Do not I hate them, O Yahuah (LORD), that hate thee?* (Psalm 139:21). Yet the verdict is mixed, not crushing: *Nevertheless there are good things found in thee, in that thou hast taken away the groves out of the land, and hast prepared thine heart to seek Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 19:3) — the very pattern Messiah uses with Ephesus, *I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience* (Revelation 2:2), and then *Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love* (Revelation 2:4). The commendation never cancels the correction.

threads.title: Ye judge not for man, but for Yahuah — no respect of persons, no taking of gifts
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat sets judges *in all the fenced cities of Yahudah (Judah), city by city*, and charges them: *Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for Yahuah (LORD), who is with you in the judgment. Wherefore now let the fear of Yahuah (LORD) be upon you... for there is no iniquity with Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts* (2 Chronicles 19:6-7). The charge is pure Torah, re-issued. Moses charged his judges, *Ye shall not respect persons in judgment... for the judgment is Elohim's (God's)* (Deuteronomy 1:17); commanded, *Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates... and they shall judge the people with just judgment* (Deuteronomy 16:18), *Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise* (Deuteronomy 16:19); grounded it in Yahuah's own character, *which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward* (Deuteronomy 10:17); and forbade partiality both ways, *thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty* (Leviticus 19:15). This standard never lapses: *there is no respect of persons with Elohim (God)* (Romans 2:11); *Of a truth I perceive that Elohim (God) is no respecter of persons* (Acts 10:34); *he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons* (Colossians 3:25). The judge's rule and the Judge's rule are one.

threads.title: The priests, the Levites, for the judgment of Yahuah — the higher court of Deuteronomy 17
threads.summary_md: Beyond the city gates Jehoshaphat re-establishes the supreme tribunal: *Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), for the judgment of Yahuah (LORD), and for controversies* (2 Chronicles 19:8). This is precisely the court Moses appointed for the cases too hard for the local judge — *If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood... then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose* (Deuteronomy 17:8); *And thou shalt come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days... and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment* (Deuteronomy 17:9). The king names the same docket — *between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments* (2 Chronicles 19:10) — the very matters Deuteronomy sends up, *And thou shalt do according to the sentence... thou shalt observe to do according to all that they inform thee* (Deuteronomy 17:10), *According to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee... thou shalt not decline from the sentence... to the right hand, nor to the left* (Deuteronomy 17:11). And so Jehoshaphat seats Amariah the chief priest over them and bids the bench, *Deal courageously, and Yahuah (LORD) shall be with the good* (2 Chronicles 19:11) — the Torah's teaching-court, courageously kept.

threads.title: Our eyes are upon thee: the prayer of utter dependence
threads.summary_md: When a great multitude of Moab, Ammon, and mount Seir came against him, Jehoshaphat *feared, and set himself to seek Yahuah (LORD), and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 20:3), and stood before the house to pray. His prayer ends at the bottom of all human resource: *O our Elohim (God)... we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee* (2 Chronicles 20:12). This is faith's posture — the lifted, fixed eye. *I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from Yahuah (LORD), which made heaven and earth* (Psalm 121:1-2). *As the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters... so our eyes wait upon Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God), until that he have mercy upon us* (Psalm 123:2). *Mine eyes are ever toward Yahuah (LORD); for he shall pluck my feet out of the net* (Psalm 25:15). The posture is inherited: his father Asa had prayed *it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power... for we rest on thee* (2 Chronicles 14:11). And Paul names the same school of dependence — *we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in Elohim (God) which raiseth the dead* (2 Corinthians 1:9). The end of self-might is the doorway into Yahuah's deliverance.

threads.title: The battle is not yours, but Elohim's: stand still and see the salvation
threads.summary_md: The Spirit of Yahuah came upon Jahaziel the Levite in the midst of the congregation, and the answer to Jehoshaphat's prayer was the oldest deliverance word in Israel: *Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but Elohim's (God's)* (2 Chronicles 20:15), and *Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD) with you... for Yahuah (LORD) will be with you* (2 Chronicles 20:17). This is the Red Sea pattern carried into the monarchy word for word: *Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day* (Exodus 14:13); *Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace* (Exodus 14:14). David named the same truth against Goliath — *the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands* (1 Samuel 17:47) — and the Torah's own war-law had promised it: *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you* (Deuteronomy 20:4). The people's only work is to cease their own striving: *Be still, and know that I am Elohim (God): I will be exalted among the heathen* (Psalm 46:10). Yahuah fights; Israel stands still and sees.

threads.title: Believe in Yahuah, so shall ye be established
threads.summary_md: As they went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood and charged the people: *Believe in Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper* (2 Chronicles 20:20). The wordplay is Isaiah's — faith and standing are the same root — and it answers the warning once given to faithless Ahaz: *If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established* (Isaiah 7:9). This is living covenant-faith, the faith by which the righteous LIVE — *the just shall live by his faith* (Habakkuk 2:4) — never a bare confession set against the covenant, but the trust that rests wholly on Yahuah and is therefore made to stand. Hezekiah would call Judah to the same rest against Sennacherib: *with us is Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) to help us, and to fight our battles. And the people rested themselves upon the words of Hezekiah* (2 Chronicles 32:8). And the prophets believed lead at last to the Prophet believed: *these are written, that ye might believe that Yahusha (Jesus) is the Messiah (Christ), the Son of Elohim (God); and that believing ye might have life through his name* (John 20:31).

threads.title: When they began to praise, Yahuah set the ambush
threads.summary_md: Then came the strangest battle order in Scripture: *he appointed singers unto Yahuah (LORD), and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise Yahuah (LORD); for his mercy endureth for ever* (2 Chronicles 20:21). The choir, not the soldiers, went first — *And when they began to sing and to praise, Yahuah (LORD) set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir... and they were smitten* (2 Chronicles 20:22). Praise itself was the weapon. The psalm had named the mechanism: *Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger* (Psalm 8:2) — which Yahusha sealed: *have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?* (Matthew 21:16). The very song they sang — *Praise Yahuah (LORD); for his mercy endureth for ever* — is the temple praise that once drew down the Glory: *...for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: that then the house was filled with a cloud* (2 Chronicles 5:13). As Jericho's wall fell to the shout — *the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat* (Joshua 6:20) — so the enemy fell to the song, for *the high praises of Elohim (God)* are *a twoedged sword in their hand* (Psalm 149:6).

threads.title: The valley of Berachah and the rest round about
threads.summary_md: The enemy destroyed itself, and the spoil was so great they *were three days in gathering* it (2 Chronicles 20:25). Then the people did what the faith-victory called for: *on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they blessed Yahuah (LORD): therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah* (2 Chronicles 20:26) — Berachah is blessing. And the chapter closes in covenant rest: *So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his Elohim (God) gave him rest round about* (2 Chronicles 20:30). This is the rest that follows the seeking. His grandfather Asa knew it: *the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because Yahuah (LORD) had given him rest* (2 Chronicles 14:6), *because we have sought Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)... and he hath given us rest on every side* (2 Chronicles 14:7). Seek Yahuah, trust him, praise him — and the realm is quiet round about.

threads.title: They loathed this light bread — and tempted the Formed Son
threads.summary_md: At the edge of Edom *the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way* (Numbers 21:4), and they *spake against Elohim (God), and against Moses... our soul loatheth this light bread* (Numbers 21:5) — the manna of heaven despised. Asaph sings the charge back: *they spake against Elohim (God); they said, Can Elohim (God) furnish a table in the wilderness?* (Psalm 78:19). Sha'ul reads the whole scene as written for us, and names whom they provoked: *Neither let us tempt Messiah (Christ), as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents* (1 Corinthians 10:9), *Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer* (1 Corinthians 10:10). The One they tempted in the wilderness was the Formed Son who led them; the fiery serpents were the destroyer's answer to the despising of heaven's bread.

threads.title: The serpent of brass lifted up — beheld, and they lived
threads.summary_md: When the fiery serpents bit the people, Yahuah (LORD) said, *Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live* (Numbers 21:8), and *Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole... when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived* (Numbers 21:9). Yahusha (Jesus) takes this very sign as the figure of His own cross: *And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Adam be lifted up* (John 3:14), *That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life* (John 3:15). The bare look that healed the venom prefigures the believing look that gives life. Yet the sign was never the Saviour: when Yashar'el (Israel) burned incense to it, Hezekiah *brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made... and he called it Nehushtan* (2 Kings 18:4) — a piece of bronze. The lifted-up sign points beyond itself to the Formed Son; to worship the bronze is to lose the healing it once carried.

threads.title: Spring up, O well — the water springing up unto everlasting life
threads.summary_md: At Beer Yahuah (LORD) gave water, and *Yashar'el (Israel) sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it* (Numbers 21:17), the well *digged... by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves* (Numbers 21:18). Isaiah makes that song the song of the redeemed: *Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation* (Isaiah 12:3). And Yahusha (Jesus) fills the figure to the brim: *the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14), and at the feast, *out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water* (John 7:38) — the Spirit poured out. The well Yahuah (LORD) opened in the wilderness sings forward to the living water that never fails.

threads.title: Sihon and Og delivered into the hand of Yashar'el (Israel)
threads.summary_md: Sihon king of the Amorites *would not suffer Yashar'el (Israel) to pass through his border* (Numbers 21:23) and fell by the edge of the sword, and when Og king of Bashan came out, *Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand* (Numbers 21:34). Moses' own retelling seals the cause: *Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people* (Deuteronomy 2:33) — the deliverance was Yahuah (LORD)'s doing. The psalms gather both kings into His praise: He *smote great nations, and slew mighty kings... Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan* (Psalm 135:10-11), and the great Hallel rehearses each by name — *Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:19), *And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:20). The victory was covenant mercy toward His people, not the sword alone.

threads.title: Thou Shalt Not Curse, For They Are Blessed
threads.summary_md: Balak the son of Zippor, terrified of a people *many* and victorious, sends to hire a curse: *Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me... for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed* (Numbers 22:6). But the verdict is already sealed in heaven. Elohim answers Balaam plainly: *Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed* (Numbers 22:12). The blessing on Yashar'el (Israel) is not Balaam's to revoke — it stands on the oath to the fathers: *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed* (Genesis 12:3). The very curse Balak hires recoils on the one who hires it. Paul gathers the whole scene into one question: *What shall we then say to these things? If Elohim (God) be for us, who can be against us?* (Romans 8:31) — and answers it: *Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Elohim's (God's) elect? It is Elohim (God) that justifieth* (Romans 8:33). Moab and its diviner are *against* a people Yahuah is *for*; the accusation for hire cannot stick. These are victims of a king's fear, not enemies to be destroyed — and Yahuah turns the whole assault into blessing.

threads.title: The Way of Balaam — Who Loved the Wages of Unrighteousness
threads.summary_md: Balak refuses Balaam's first no and sends again — *princes, more, and more honourable than they* — with a sweeter purse: *For I will promote thee unto very great honour, and I will do whatsoever thou sayest unto me: come therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people* (Numbers 22:17). Balaam's reply sounds devout — *If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God), to do less or more* (Numbers 22:18) — yet he tarries to ask Yahuah again, his eye on the reward. The apostles read his heart exactly. Peter: *Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness* (2 Peter 2:15). Jude: *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core* (Jude 1:11). The sin is named: a prophet who knows the word of Yahuah yet lets covetousness pull him toward a curse he has been forbidden to speak.

threads.title: The Angel With the Drawn Sword and the Mouth of the Ass
threads.summary_md: On the road, *Elohim's (God's) anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of Yahuah (LORD) stood in the way for an adversary against him... and his sword drawn in his hand* (Numbers 22:22-23). This is the Angel of Yahuah who bears the Name — the Formed Son who appeared, spoke, and stood across Yashar'el's path before — now barring the diviner's way with a sword drawn. The beast beneath Balaam sees what the seer-for-hire is blind to, turning aside three times and beaten three times, until *Yahuah (LORD) opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?* (Numbers 22:28). Only then does Yahuah open Balaam's own eyes, and he falls flat before the Angel who says *thy way is perverse before me* (Numbers 22:32). Peter seals the shame: *But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet* (2 Peter 2:16). A dumb beast saw the Angel and obeyed; the prophet had to be reproved by the creature he rode.

threads.title: The Word That Elohim Putteth In My Mouth, That Shall I Speak
threads.summary_md: Balaam comes at last to Balak, but with a warning that quietly undoes the whole hire: *Lo, I am come unto thee: have I now any power at all to say any thing? the word that Elohim (God) putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak* (Numbers 22:38). The diviner has no command over his own tongue. The next chapter shows the promise kept and the king enraged: *And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether* (Numbers 23:11) — and Balaam can only answer, *Must I not take heed to speak that which Yahuah (LORD) hath put in my mouth?* (Numbers 23:12). The bought curse turns to blessing in the very mouth hired to utter it. Yahuah overrules the hostile prophet and makes him a herald of the blessing on His people.

threads.title: The People Shall Dwell Alone — Not Reckoned Among the Nations
threads.summary_md: Balak hired the seer *to curse me Jacob, and come, defy Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 23:7), but from the top of the rocks Balaam can only confess what Yahuah sees: *lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations* (Numbers 23:9). This is election, not isolation — the covenant people set apart, the dust of Jacob beyond counting (23:10). Moses had blessed them in these very words: *Yashar'el (Israel) then shall dwell in safety alone* (Deuteronomy 33:28). And the dwelling-apart runs forward to the *peculiar people* redeemed unto Yahuah — *purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works* (Titus 2:14) — the *chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people* (1 Peter 2:9), the two-house people who were *not a people* and are now the people of Elohim (God), restored and never replaced. No wonder the hireling cries, *let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!* (Numbers 23:10) — he covets a portion he cannot purchase.

threads.title: The Bound Word — All That Yahuah Speaketh, That I Must Do
threads.summary_md: When the first oracle blessed instead of cursing, Balak protested: *What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether* (Numbers 23:11). Balaam's answer is the seal on his whole errand: *Must I not take heed to speak that which Yahuah (LORD) hath put in my mouth?* (Numbers 23:12). He had said the same before he ever climbed the altars — *the word that Elohim (God) putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak* (Numbers 22:38). So Balak drags him to *another place* and builds seven fresh altars (23:13-14), still grasping: *What hath Yahuah (LORD) spoken?* (23:17). But a new vantage and a new sacrifice cannot loose a mouth Yahuah has bound. The hired curse is impossible; the word is not for sale.

threads.title: Elohim Is Not a Man That He Should Lie — He Hath Blessed, and I Cannot Reverse It
threads.summary_md: The second oracle opens with the axiom that anchors the whole covenant: *Elohim (God) is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of Adam, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?* (Numbers 23:19). Therefore the blessing stands fixed: *I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it* (Numbers 23:20). Samuel turned the same word into Yashar'el's warrant — *the Strength of Yashar'el (Israel) will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent* (1 Samuel 15:29) — and Malachi made it the reason Jacob endures: *For I am Yahuah (LORD), I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed* (Malachi 3:6). The New Testament rests every promise here: *the gifts and calling of Elohim (God) are without repentance* (Romans 11:29) — Paul's charter that Yahuah has not cast away his people; *eternal life, which Elohim (God), that cannot lie, promised before the world began* (Titus 1:2); and the oath to Abraham, *two immutable things, in which it was impossible for Elohim (God) to lie* (Hebrews 6:18). A hired curse cannot reverse what the unchanging One has spoken to bless.

threads.title: He Hath Not Beheld Iniquity in Jacob — The Shout of a King Is Among Them
threads.summary_md: The oracle declares the blessed people uncondemnable: *He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither hath he seen perverseness in Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) is with him, and the shout of a king is among them* (Numbers 23:21). Not that the people are sinless, but that their sin is covered — David sings the very blessedness: *Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered* (Psalm 32:1); *Blessed is the man unto whom Yahuah (LORD) imputeth not iniquity* (Psalm 32:2). Because of this, no hostile word can prosper: *Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 23:23). Paul carries the defence to its end — *Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Elohim's (God's) elect? It is Elohim (God) that justifieth* (Romans 8:33); *Who is he that condemneth? It is Messiah (Christ) that died... who also maketh intercession for us* (Romans 8:34). The *shout of a king* among the people is answered: the King intercedes, and the hired curse falls to the ground.

threads.title: How goodly are thy tents — blessed is he that blesseth thee
threads.summary_md: The hireling seer, hired by Balak to curse, is overruled by the Ruach: *And when Balaam saw that it pleased Yahuah (LORD) to bless Yashar'el (Israel), he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments... and the spirit of Elohim (God) came upon him* (Numbers 24:1-2). He can only bless — and his blessing pours out: *How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Yashar'el (Israel)! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river's side... He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee* (24:5-9). That last line is the Abrahamic seed-word repeated verbatim — *I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed* (Genesis 12:3). The promise spoken to Abram is so fixed that a Moabite diviner is forced to mouth it; the blessing and the curse cleave to the seed, unmoved by a king's gold. And the couched lion none dares rouse is Yahudah's own emblem from Jacob's deathbed blessing: *Yahudah (Judah) is a lion's whelp... he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?* (Genesis 49:9) — the sceptre-tribe, pointing straight to the Star and Sceptre the seer is about to name.

threads.title: There shall come a Star out of Jacob — the Messiah-King foreseen by a pagan seer
