And the work is finished at Shiloh by the same hands: *These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes... divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Yahuah (LORD)... So they made an end of dividing the country* (Joshua 19:51). The stewards named here are the stewards who complete the division.

threads.title: The Forty-Eight Levite Cities — Scattered to Serve
threads.summary_md: Yahuah (LORD) commands that the priestly tribe receive no land-block but cities scattered through every tribe's inheritance: *Command the children of Yashar'el (Israel), that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in* (Numbers 35:2), *So all the cities which ye shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities* (Numbers 35:7). Joshua records the command fulfilled: *All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were forty and eight cities with their suburbs* (Joshua 21:41). And the dispersion itself fulfils Jacob's old word over Levi — *Cursed be their anger... I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Genesis 49:7). The curse of scattering is turned to priestly portion: the tribe with no territory of its own becomes the tribe present in every territory, dwelling among all Yashar'el (Israel).

threads.title: The Six Cities of Refuge — Fled for Refuge to Lay Hold on Hope
threads.summary_md: Among the Levite cities, six are set apart as refuge for the manslayer who *killeth any person at unawares* (Numbers 35:11): *they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment* (Numbers 35:12). The refuge is wide — *both for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them* (Numbers 35:15). Moses presses the same statute home before the crossing — *Thou shalt separate three cities for thee in the midst of thy land* (Deuteronomy 19:2) — and Joshua executes it in the land, *Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses* (Joshua 20:2). The writer to the Hebrews reads our hope through this very picture: *we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us* (Hebrews 6:18). The appointed city is the type; the hope set before us is the fulfilment.

threads.title: Murder and the Mouth of Witnesses — The Distinction Yahuah Draws
threads.summary_md: The Torah sharply distinguishes the murderer from the manslayer. He who smites *with an instrument of iron... a stone... an hand weapon of wood* (Numbers 35:16-18), or *thrust him of hatred, or hurl at him by laying of wait* (Numbers 35:20), *is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death* (Numbers 35:16), and *the revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer* (Numbers 35:19). But he who *thrust him suddenly without enmity... seeing him not... and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm* (Numbers 35:22-23) the congregation delivers to the refuge. And the conviction is guarded: *the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die* (Numbers 35:30) — the same evidentiary safeguard Deuteronomy fixes, *At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses... but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death* (Deuteronomy 17:6). The verdict on deliberate bloodshed rests on the oldest covenant ground: *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man* (Genesis 9:6).

threads.title: Until the Death of the High Priest — The Death That Sets Free
threads.summary_md: The manslayer in the refuge is not loosed by a fine, nor by the passing of years, but by one death: *he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil* (Numbers 35:25), and *after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession* (Numbers 35:28). It is the death of the anointed one that liberates and restores the inheritance. The writer to the Hebrews carries the type forward: *he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death... they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance* (Hebrews 9:15), for *where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator* (Hebrews 9:16). And the death that frees is not repeated: *Messiah (Christ) being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him* (Romans 6:9). The risen High Priest dies no more, and the one set free walks home without fear of the avenger.

threads.title: Blood Defiles the Land — Cleansed Only by Blood
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes on the gravest principle: *ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it* (Numbers 35:33). The reason is the dwelling of Yahuah (LORD) himself: *Defile not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I Yahuah (LORD) dwell among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 35:34). Blood demands blood — this is the floor under the whole sacrificial order: *without shedding of blood is no remission* (Hebrews 9:22). It reaches back to the first murder, *the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground* (Genesis 4:10), and the curse that followed, *cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood* (Genesis 4:11); and it stands on the Noahic charge, *for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man* (Genesis 9:6). Messiah (Christ) gathers the reckoning into one indictment — *all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel* (Matthew 23:35) — and the land where Yahuah dwells is purged of unsolved blood only by appointed rite, *lay not innocent blood unto thy people of Yashar'el's (Israel's) charge. And the blood shall be forgiven them* (Deuteronomy 21:8). Innocent blood is never forgotten; it accumulates until it is required.

threads.title: The Inheritance Kept Within the Tribe
threads.summary_md:
The close of Numbers completes the statute it began nine chapters earlier. The chief fathers of Gilead come with a real worry: if Zelophehad's daughters marry outside their tribe, *then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers, and shall be put to the inheritance of the tribe whereunto they are received* (Numbers 36:3). Yahuah's (the LORD's) answer guards the gift: *only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry. So shall not the inheritance of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers* (Numbers 36:6-7).

This is the completion of the Numbers 27 statute — *The daughters of Zelophehad speak right... thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them* (Numbers 27:7) — now sealed so the gift cannot bleed away. And the reason runs deeper than property: *The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me* (Leviticus 25:23). The tribal portion is covenant trust, held of Yahuah (the LORD), kept whole and undiminished. So Naboth, generations later, keeps this very law unto death: *Yahuah (LORD) forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee* (1 Kings 21:3). And the apostle carries the same logic forward to the inheritance that can never be lost — *an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you* (1 Peter 1:4). The portion of Yahuah's people is kept.

threads.title: The Daughters Obeyed the Word
threads.summary_md:
The statute is not left as theory. *Even as Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad* (Numbers 36:10). Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah marry their father's brothers' sons, *into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father* (Numbers 36:11-12).

The word first spoken to them in chapter 27 — *thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them* (Numbers 27:7) — is now obeyed to the letter. The same women who once stood and asked rightly for their portion now keep the commandment that guards it; the obedient keeping of the word holds the inheritance exactly where Yahuah (the LORD) set it.

threads.title: The Book Sealed at Jordan
threads.summary_md:
Numbers ends with its colophon — the seal of the book at the very threshold of the land: *These are the commandments and the judgments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded by the hand of Moses unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho* (Numbers 36:13). It is the twin of the seal that closed Leviticus — *These are the commandments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in mount Sinai* (Leviticus 27:34). One continuous Torah, given by the hand of the one mediator, sealed first at the mountain and now at the river.

And the place is not incidental. Where Numbers seals, Deuteronomy opens: *On this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this law, saying* (Deuteronomy 1:5). The book is sealed at Jordan and the exposition begins on the same ground — the people stand at the edge of the inheritance, the commandments and judgments gathered and confirmed, ready to cross over.

threads.title: As Long As He Sought Yahuah, He Prospered
threads.summary_md:
The whole arc of Uzziah's reign hangs on one clause: *And he sought Elohim (God) in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of Elohim (God): and as long as he sought Yahuah (LORD), Elohim (God) made him to prosper* (2 Chronicles 26:5). Not *because* he was a great builder, not *because* he was marvellously helped — the prospering tracks the seeking, and only *as long as* it lasts. This is the Chronicler's law, spoken to Asa and standing over every king: *Yahuah (LORD) is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you* (2 Chronicles 15:2).

It is no prosperity-formula a king can work; it is the fruit of being rooted in Yahuah and his word. Of Hezekiah the same is written: *in every work that he began in the service of the house of Elohim (God), and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his Elohim (God), he did it with all his heart, and prospered* (2 Chronicles 31:21) — the seeking bound to *the law, and the commandments*. The charge to Joshua names the same way: *thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous* (Joshua 1:8). And the Psalm draws the picture: the man whose delight is in the Torah is *like a tree planted by the rivers of water... and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper* (Psalm 1:3). Yahusha (Jesus) gives the order plainly: *seek ye first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you* (Matthew 6:33). Uzziah's helping and might were the *added* things — and when he forgot the order and trusted the strength, the same chapter turns to his ruin.

threads.title: When He Was Strong, His Heart Was Lifted Up to His Destruction
threads.summary_md:
The hinge of the chapter is the word *strong*. Uzziah was *marvellously helped, till he was strong* (2 Chronicles 26:15) — and then the gift turns to poison: *But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense* (2 Chronicles 26:16). The strength Yahuah gave became the occasion to forget Yahuah. This is the peril Moses named before the land was ever entered: *Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses... Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Deuteronomy 8:12-14). Uzziah is that warning come true.

Proverbs gives the law of it in seven words: *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall* (Proverbs 16:18) — and the Chronicler binds *lifted up* and *destruction* into the same breath. He uses the very phrase again of Hezekiah: *his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him* (2 Chronicles 32:25); and Daniel uses it of Nebuchadnezzar: *when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne* (Daniel 5:20). Paul guards even the elder against it: *lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil* (1 Timothy 3:6). And Ben Sira reads the Chronicler exactly: *pride is the beginning of sin... and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). Uzziah's strange calamity was leprosy in the forehead of a king — the proud heart cast down by the very hand that had raised him up.

threads.title: It Appertaineth Not Unto Thee — The King May Not Usurp the Priest, Until the Melek Tsadiq
threads.summary_md:
Uzziah's pride drives him into the holy place: he *went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense* (2 Chronicles 26:16). Eighty priests of Yahuah withstand him and speak the Torah back to his face: *It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed* (2 Chronicles 26:18). The boundary is not theirs to invent; Yahuah set it. *That no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before Yahuah (LORD); that he be not as Korah* (Numbers 16:40); *the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death* (Numbers 18:7); the incense was Aaron's appointed act, *a perpetual incense before Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations* (Exodus 30:7-8). The office of king and the office of priest are distinct, and Yahuah guards the wall between them.

The judgment falls in the same instant: *the leprosy even rose up in his forehead* (2 Chronicles 26:19) — the same sign that struck Miriam when she presumed against Moses' standing: *Miriam became leprous, white as snow* (Numbers 12:10). Uzziah is *a leper unto the day of his death... cut off from the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 26:21). The New Testament states the principle plainly: *no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of Elohim (God), as was Aaron* (Hebrews 5:4). And here the threads of the whole canon converge: there is One — and only One — who is rightly both King and Priest. Zechariah foresaw him: *he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both* (Zechariah 6:13). Yahuah swore it to David's Lord: *Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek)* (Psalm 110:4). Hebrews names the order: *this Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), king of Salem, priest of the El Elyon (most high God)... King of righteousness... King of peace* (Hebrews 7:1-2). What the strong king grasped for and was struck leprous for, the Messiah holds by Yahuah's own oath — King and Priest in one, lawfully, where Uzziah could only trespass.

threads.title: He entered not into the temple: the priestly boundary kept
threads.summary_md: Jotham *did that which was right in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 27:2). That little word *howbeit* is the whole point: Jotham imitates his father's good, but not his fatal trespass. For Uzziah, *when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense* (2 Chronicles 26:16). The priests withstood him: *It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed* (2 Chronicles 26:18) — a boundary Torah set between throne and altar, and a leprous forehead enforced. Jotham learned from the father's sin. The righteous son keeps the line his father broke; he does the good Uzziah did and refuses the presumption that destroyed him.

threads.title: Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before Yahuah
threads.summary_md: *So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)* (2 Chronicles 27:6). The chronicler states the cause plainly: the building of the high gate, the cities and castles, the victory over Ammon (2 Chronicles 27:3-5) — all of it is the fruit of one ordered, prepared walk. The verdict has an exact inverse a few chapters back: Rehoboam *did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 12:14). The same hinge word — *prepared* — sorts might from ruin. And the rest of Scripture unfolds what preparing one's ways means. It is the disciplined path of wisdom: *Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established* (Proverbs 4:26). It is the deliberate turn toward the covenant word: *I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies* (Psalm 119:59). It is Samuel's charge to the whole house: *prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD), and serve him only* (1 Samuel 7:3). It is Ezra's aim, naming what the prepared heart is for: *Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments* (Ezra 7:10). Yet the preparing is never autonomous striving: *A man's heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (Proverbs 16:9). The man orders his ways toward Yahuah's testimonies; Yahuah gives the might. That is why Jotham became mighty.

threads.title: He Burnt His Children in the Fire: The Abomination Torah Forbids
threads.summary_md: Ahaz *did not that which was right in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), like David his father* (2 Chronicles 28:1); instead *he walked in the ways of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), and made also molten images for Baalim* (2 Chronicles 28:2), and descended to the depth of apostasy: *he burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom Yahuah (LORD) had cast out before the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 28:3). The parallel account names the same horror: *made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen* (2 Kings 16:3). This is the very thing Torah forbids in advance: *thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy Elohim (God)* (Leviticus 18:21) — a capital crime, *he shall surely be put to death* (Leviticus 20:2) — *because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name* (Leviticus 20:3). It is the abomination that defines the heathen: *for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods* (Deuteronomy 12:31). The same valley of Hinnom becomes Jeremiah's Tophet: *to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart* (Jeremiah 7:31). And the Psalm that sings the history names it plainly: *they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils* (Psalm 106:37), *and shed innocent blood... and the land was polluted with blood* (Psalm 106:38). Ahaz takes up the very practice for which Yahuah cast the nations out before Israel — and the judgment of the chapter follows the polluting of the land.

threads.title: The Prophet Oded: Are There Not With You, Even With You, Sins?
threads.summary_md: Yahuah delivers Ahaz into the hand of Syria and of the north, and Pekah slays *an hundred and twenty thousand in one day* of Judah, and the northern host carries away *two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters* of their brethren captive to Samaria (2 Chronicles 28:5-8). But Yahuah sends a prophet to the north: *a prophet of Yahuah (LORD) was there, whose name was Oded* (2 Chronicles 28:9), who goes out before the victorious army and pierces their triumph — *ye have slain them in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven*, and then the searching word: *are there not with you, even with you, sins against Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)?* (2 Chronicles 28:10). The north is no less guilty than the south; the conqueror must first see his own sin, as Yahusha (Jesus) will say: *why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?* (Matthew 7:3). Oded calls them not to triumph but to mercy: *deliver the captives again, which ye have taken captive of your brethren* (2 Chronicles 28:11) — for Yahuah *desired mercy, and not sacrifice* (Hosea 6:6). To enslave the brother is to hate him, and Torah forbids it: *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour* (Leviticus 19:17); to forbear deliverance is the sin: *If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death* (Proverbs 24:11). Violence against the brother is the very crime for which Edom falls: *For thy violence against thy brother Yaaqob (Jacob) shame shall cover thee* (Obadiah 1:10). The two houses are brethren, and the prophet's word is that mercy, not bondage, must answer the day of wrath.

threads.title: The Men of Ephraim Clothed the Naked: The Foreshadow of the Good Samaritan
threads.summary_md: The men of the northern house heed the prophet. *Certain of the heads of the children of Ephraim... stood up against them that came from the war* (2 Chronicles 28:12), refusing to add the captives to their trespass — *whereas we have offended against Yahuah (LORD) already, ye intend to add more to our sins* (2 Chronicles 28:13) — and the armed men leave the captives before the princes. Then comes one of the most tender pictures in all the Tanakh: *the men which were expressed by name rose up, and took the captives, and with the spoil clothed all that were naked among them, and arrayed them, and shod them, and gave them to eat and to drink, and anointed them, and carried all the feeble of them upon asses, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren* (2 Chronicles 28:15). It is the good Samaritan before the parable was told. The Samaritan is a northerner — of this same Ephraim — and the acts are the same acts: *when he saw him, he had compassion on him* (Luke 10:33), *pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him* (Luke 10:34); even the road runs to the same Jericho. These are the works the King will own at the last: *Naked, and ye clothed me* (Matthew 25:36), *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink* (Matthew 25:35) — the fast Yahuah chose: *when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh* (Isaiah 58:7). Armies met that morning, yet mercy answered war, *if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink* (Romans 12:20). The captives were *their brethren* (2 Chronicles 28:15) — the divided houses of Yahudah (Judah) and Ephraim shown as one flesh, mercy bridging the divide, and the Samaritan-pattern foreshadowed centuries before.

threads.title: Ahaz Sacrificed to the Gods That Smote Him: The Hardening in Trouble
threads.summary_md: Distress should drive a king to repentance, but Ahaz hardens instead. Beset by Edom, the Philistines, and Assyria, *in the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against Yahuah (LORD): this is that king Ahaz* (2 Chronicles 28:22). He sacrifices to the very gods that defeated him: *he sacrificed unto the gods of Damascus, which smote him... Because the gods of the kings of Syria help them, therefore will I sacrifice to them, that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him* (2 Chronicles 28:23). He *shut up the doors of the house of Yahuah (LORD), and he made him altars in every corner of Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 28:24). The contrast with his own grandson is the lesson: Manasseh, far wickeder, *when he was in affliction, he besought Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and humbled himself greatly* (2 Chronicles 33:12), and *Manasseh knew that Yahuah (LORD) he was Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 33:13). The same affliction that breaks one man's pride only hardens the other's. Isaiah, prophet to Ahaz's Jerusalem, names the sickness: *Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint* (Isaiah 1:5). And shutting the house of Yahuah to build altars in every corner is Jeremiah's two evils made visible: *they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water* (Jeremiah 2:13). Trouble is a summons; Ahaz answers it by digging deeper into the cisterns that cannot hold.

threads.title: Sanctify Now Yourselves: The House and the Ministers Cleansed
threads.summary_md: In the first month of his reign Hezekiah *opened the doors of the house of Yahuah (LORD), and repaired them* (2 Chronicles 29:3), reversing in a single act what his father Ahaz had done when he *shut up the doors of the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 28:24). Then he gathers the priests and Levites and charges them: *sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place* (2 Chronicles 29:5), for *our fathers have trespassed... and have turned away their faces from the habitation of Yahuah (LORD), and turned their backs* (2 Chronicles 29:6); *also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps* (2 Chronicles 29:7). The neglected house is the same one Haggai must later rouse: *build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Haggai 1:8). And the cleansing of the ministers is the prophetic pattern: *he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness* (Malachi 3:3). The charge is sealed with election: *My sons, be not now negligent: for Yahuah (LORD) hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him* (2 Chronicles 29:11). Carried forward, this is the cleansing of the living temple — *let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of Elohim (God)* (2 Corinthians 7:1) — and the priesthood it makes ready: *ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood* (1 Peter 2:5), *a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people* (1 Peter 2:9). The doors thrown open, the filthiness carried out, the ministers chosen to serve — this is the worship the framework upholds, reconsecrated.

threads.title: It Is In Mine Heart To Make a Covenant: Wrath Turned Away by Renewal
threads.summary_md: Before a single bullock is killed, Hezekiah names the heart of his reform: *Now it is in mine heart to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that his fierce wrath may turn away from us* (2 Chronicles 29:10). The wrath had fallen for covenant-breaking — *Wherefore the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) was upon Yahudah (Judah) and Jerusalem... our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity* (2 Chronicles 29:8-9) — and the turning of it is not bought but covenanted. Hezekiah walks the road his father Asa cut: *And they entered into a covenant to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul* (2 Chronicles 15:12), binding the whole house so that *whosoever would not seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) should be put to death, whether small or great* (2 Chronicles 15:13). It is the same renewal Josiah will make: *the king... made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD), to walk after Yahuah (LORD), and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book* (2 Kings 23:3). The covenant is never a new instrument — it is the Torah-covenant of the fathers taken up again, the people returning to the statutes they had forsaken, and so the fierce wrath turns away.

threads.title: The Sin Offering and the Blood: Atonement Made for All Yashar'el
threads.summary_md: With the house cleansed, Hezekiah brings *seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 29:21). The priests *received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar* (2 Chronicles 29:22), and *made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 29:24). This is the Torah's own appointed remedy: the sin offering by which *the priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them* (Leviticus 4:20), and the Day of Atonement promise, *for on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 16:30). The sprinkled blood is the law's unbroken testimony — *almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission* (Hebrews 9:22) — and the atonement *for all Yashar'el (Israel)* points beyond the bullocks and goats to the blood of the Messiah, the one offering every sin offering foreshadowed. The cleansing of the holy place and the cleansing of the people meet at the altar where the blood makes all Yashar'el (Israel) clean before Yahuah.

threads.title: The Song of Yahuah Began Also: The Appointed Worship Restored
threads.summary_md: When the altar is purified and the offering laid on, the worship of the house rises with it. Hezekiah *set the Levites in the house of Yahuah (LORD) with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet: for so was the commandment of Yahuah (LORD) by his prophets* (2 Chronicles 29:25). The order is no innovation — it is the very service David appointed, when he *separated to the service of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals* (1 Chronicles 25:1), the same standing rule Solomon kept, *according to the order of David his father... to praise and minister... for so had David the man of Elohim (God) commanded* (2 Chronicles 8:14). *And when the burnt offering began, the song of Yahuah (LORD) began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 29:27), *and all the congregation worshipped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded* (2 Chronicles 29:28). This is the company of praise the Psalter commands — *Praise Elohim (God) in his sanctuary... praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp* (Psalm 150:1, 3) — and where his people sing it, there he dwells: *thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Psalm 22:3). Carried forward, *the words of David, and of Asaph the seer* (2 Chronicles 29:30) are still the songs of his assembly: *speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to Yahuah (Lord)* (Ephesians 5:19). The song the framework upholds is restored with the offering, and the people worship.

threads.title: Hezekiah keeps the Passover for the whole people
threads.summary_md:
Hezekiah does not invent a rite; he restores the appointed feast. *And Hezekiah sent to all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 30:1). The Passover is the feast of the exodus — *it is the LORD'S passover* (Exodus 12:11) — and the whole people is summoned back to it, *from Beer-sheba even to Dan... for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written* (2 Chronicles 30:5).

That it falls in the second month is no deviation but the Torah's own provision: *If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Numbers 9:10) — *the fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it* (Numbers 9:11), the very day 2 Chronicles names (30:15). The provision was given for a people scattered and afar; Hezekiah reaches the northern remnant by it. And the whole congregation is gathered to the rejoicing Moses commanded — *thou shalt rejoice in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter... and the stranger* (Deuteronomy 16:14). The appointed times are not abolished; here they are recovered for both houses, kept *according to the law of Moses the man of Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 30:16).

threads.title: Turn again unto Yahuah — the scattered remnant called home
threads.summary_md:
The posts carry a gathering call to the divided people: *So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah)... saying, Ye children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria* (2 Chronicles 30:6). This is the northern house — Ephraim, Manasseh, the tribes scattered through Assyria — summoned home; and the promise hangs on returning: *if ye turn again unto Yahuah (LORD), your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him* (2 Chronicles 30:9).

This is the word Moses foretold — *and shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)... with all thine heart* (Deuteronomy 30:2); *then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations* (Deuteronomy 30:3). It is the prophets' cry to the very same northern house: *Come, and let us return unto Yahuah (LORD): for he hath torn, and he will heal us* (Hosea 6:1); *O Yashar'el (Israel), return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Hosea 14:1); *Return, thou backsliding Yashar'el (Israel)... for I am merciful* (Jeremiah 3:12) — aimed *toward the north*, as the posts pass *through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun* (2 Chronicles 30:10). The whole covenant motion is here: *Turn ye unto me, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and I will turn unto you* (Zechariah 1:3).

Hezekiah's Passover is the two-house gathering in miniature — Yahudah summoning Ephraim to the one house of Yahuah — a foretaste of the day Yahuah says *Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side* (Ezekiel 37:21), the two sticks made one. Not all came — *they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them* (2 Chronicles 30:10) — yet *divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:11), for *the hand of Elohim (God) was to give them one heart to do the commandment* (2 Chronicles 30:12). And the heart of it is the running Father: *when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him* (Luke 15:20). The returning son is the scattered house; the houses remain brethren, never replaced — gathered home.

threads.title: Yahuah pardon every one that prepareth his heart
threads.summary_md:
When many came to the table unready in the letter of the law, the king did not bar them — he prayed for them. *For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Yahuah (LORD) pardon every one that prepareth his heart to seek Elohim (God), Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary* (2 Chronicles 30:18-19). And the answer came: *And Yahuah (LORD) hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people* (2 Chronicles 30:20).

This is not antinomian license — they were keeping the feast, gathered to Yahuah's house, seeking him at his appointed time. It is Yahuah honoring the prepared heart where ceremonial purity fell short. He is the One who *seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looketh on the heart* (1 Samuel 16:7); who declares *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* (Hosea 6:6); who will not despise *a broken and a contrite heart* (Psalm 51:17). The Formed Son names the very principle the Chronicler lived — *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13) — and defends those who keep the appointed time with right hearts against those who would condemn them on the form: *if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless* (Matthew 12:7). The heart that seeks him within the keeping of his feast is the heart he receives.

threads.title: Great joy in Jerusalem — the restored feast
threads.summary_md:
The restored feast breaks out in gladness so great it doubles itself. *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness* (2 Chronicles 30:21); then *the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness* (2 Chronicles 30:23). This is the Torah's own command poured out full: *Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which Yahuah (LORD) shall choose... therefore thou shalt surely rejoice* (Deuteronomy 16:15).

The joy is the joy of a people come home, unmatched in living memory: *So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Yashar'el (Israel) there was not the like in Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:26) — the same gladness that would crown the later restoration of the feast, *for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) done so. And there was very great gladness* (Nehemiah 8:17). And it ends as Yahuah ordained his people be blessed: *Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to his holy dwelling place, even unto heaven* (2 Chronicles 30:27) — the Aaronic blessing fulfilled, *Yahuah (LORD) bless thee, and keep thee* (Numbers 6:24), rising from the restored feast and heard in heaven.

threads.title: The Tithe — the Portion of the Ministry, Brought in Abundance per the Torah
threads.summary_md: Hezekiah commands the people *to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 31:4), and the response overflows: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly* (2 Chronicles 31:5). This is not a fresh fundraising scheme but a return to the Torah's own provision for the ministry. The tenth was never the people's to keep: *all the tithe of the land... is the LORD'S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 27:30). It is the Levites' inheritance precisely because they hold no land — *I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve* (Numbers 18:21); *the tithes... I have given to the Levites to inherit* (Numbers 18:24). The Torah even names the same firstfruits Hezekiah's people brought — *thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed* (Deuteronomy 14:22) — and ties it to the same end Hezekiah seeks: *that thou mayest learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always* (Deuteronomy 14:23). The Second-Temple wisdom keeps the same measure: *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands* (Ecclesiasticus 35:8). The willing tithe upholds the ministry so the law of Yahuah may stand — the support of those who serve at his house, given whole, never diminished.

threads.title: Since the People Began to Bring — Yahuah Blessed His People
threads.summary_md: When Hezekiah and the princes saw the heaps, *they blessed Yahuah (LORD), and his people Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 31:8), and the chief priest gave the reckoning: *Since the people began to bring the offerings into the house of Yahuah (LORD), we have had enough to eat, and have left plenty: for Yahuah (LORD) hath blessed his people; and that which is left is this great store* (2 Chronicles 31:10). The blessing follows the bringing — exactly the order Yahuah later puts to a people who had robbed him: *Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it* (Malachi 3:10); *and I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes* (Malachi 3:11). The proverb names the same posture and the same outcome: *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: so shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine* (Proverbs 3:9-10). This is no prosperity-bargain by which the giver compels Yahuah; it is Yahuah's faithfulness to the willing, glad giver — *In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness* (Ecclesiasticus 35:9). The apostle carries it forward to its right end: *Elohim (God) is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work* (2 Corinthians 9:8) — the sufficiency given so the giving may overflow into the service, not back into the self.

threads.title: With All His Heart — In the Law and in the Commandments, and Prospered
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes on the measure of the man: *And thus did Hezekiah throughout all Yahudah (Judah), and wrought that which was good and right and truth before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God). And in every work that he began in the service of the house of Elohim (God), and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his Elohim (God), he did it with all his heart, and prospered* (2 Chronicles 31:20-21). The whole heart, the law and the commandments, the prospering — three threads of the Torah's own promise braided into one life. The great command set it: *thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might* (Deuteronomy 6:5). The prospering is no accident but the pledged fruit of keeping the law without turning: *that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law... turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest* (Joshua 1:7); *thou shalt meditate therein day and night... for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous* (Joshua 1:8). It is the Chronicler's own standard, set elsewhere against a faithless king: *the eyes of Yahuah (LORD) run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him* (2 Chronicles 16:9). The wisdom call is the same — *Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might* (Ecclesiastes 9:10) — and the apostle carries the posture into every labour: *what soever ye do, do it heartily, as to Yahuah (Lord), and not unto men* (Colossians 3:23). Hezekiah's prospering is the fruit of seeking Yahuah with an undivided heart, in the Torah, with the whole strength of the hand.

threads.title: With Him Is an Arm of Flesh; But With Us Is Yahuah
threads.summary_md: When Sennacherib came up against the fenced cities, Hezekiah set captains over the people and *spake comfortably to them*: *Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him: With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) to help us, and to fight our battles* (2 Chronicles 32:7-8). This is the great contrast of trust running through the whole canon. Jeremiah names the curse on the other side of it: *Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 17:5). The psalm sings the wager: *Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God)* (Psalm 20:7). Elisha had opened a servant's eyes to the unseen host — *they that be with us are more than they that be with them* (2 Kings 6:16) — the same arithmetic Hezekiah preaches. Jehoshaphat heard it in the same Chronicles: *the battle is not yours, but Elohim's (God's)* (2 Chronicles 20:15). And it carries forward whole: *If Elohim (God) be for us, who can be against us?* (Romans 8:31), for *greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world* (1 John 4:4). The arm of flesh withers; the help is greater.

threads.title: The Blasphemy of the Living Elohim Against the No-Gods
threads.summary_md: Sennacherib's servants set the living Elohim among the carved gods of the nations he had conquered: *Who was there among all the gods of those nations that my fathers utterly destroyed, that could deliver his people out of mine hand, that your Elohim (God) should be able to deliver you out of mine hand?* (2 Chronicles 32:14). He *wrote also letters to rail on Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 32:17), and *they spake against the Elohim (God) of Jerusalem, as against the gods of the people of the earth, which were the work of the hands of man* (2 Chronicles 32:19). Isaiah, the prophet of this very siege, names the offence: *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed?... even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 37:23) — and the Kings account answers in the same words (2 Kings 19:22). The psalm lays the reproach before Yahuah: *Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Yahuah (LORD), and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name* (Psalm 74:18). And the second psalm shows heaven's posture toward such raging: *Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?* (Psalm 2:1) — *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: Yahuah (Lord) shall have them in derision* (Psalm 2:4). The living Elohim is no work of men's hands to be counted among the no-gods; to revile Him is to imagine a vain thing.

threads.title: The Angel of Yahuah, and the Blasphemer Cut Down
threads.summary_md: The deliverance comes not by sword of Yahudah (Judah) but by prayer answered from heaven: *And for this cause Hezekiah the king, and the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz, prayed and cried to heaven. And Yahuah (LORD) sent an angel, which cut off all the mighty men of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. And when he was come into the house of his god, they that came forth of his own bowels slew him there with the sword* (2 Chronicles 32:20-21). Kings and Isaiah count what Chronicles tells in sum: *the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand* (2 Kings 19:35; Isaiah 37:36). This is the same delivering Presence the psalm sings: *The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them* (Psalm 34:7). And Psalm 76 sings the very camp of Assyria fallen: *The stouthearted are spoiled, they have slept their sleep: and none of the men of might have found their hands* (Psalm 76:5); *At thy rebuke, O Elohim (God) of Jacob, both the chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep* (Psalm 76:6); *Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?* (Psalm 76:7). The blasphemer who said no god could deliver was cut down in the house of his own god — and Yahuah saved Jerusalem.

threads.title: Elohim Left Him, to Try Him, to Know What Was in His Heart
threads.summary_md: The same Hezekiah who trusted Yahuah against Assyria is then tested in his strength. Sick to death he prayed and was given a sign, *But Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him* (2 Chronicles 32:25). Then *Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart... so that the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah* (2 Chronicles 32:26). And in the matter of the Babylonian envoys the purpose is named plainly: *Elohim (God) left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart* (2 Chronicles 32:31). The Torah had set this purpose for the testing: *to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no* (Deuteronomy 8:2), the proving that is *to do thee good at thy latter end* (Deuteronomy 8:16). Uzziah stands as the warning Hezekiah nearly becomes: *when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction* (2 Chronicles 26:16). And the law of it carries forward: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10). The test does not make the heart — it reveals it.

threads.title: The Worst King: The Host of Heaven and the Forbidden Abominations
threads.summary_md: Manasseh 'did that which was evil in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), like unto the abominations of the heathen' (33:2), and the chapter lists them: he *reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven* (33:3); he *caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards* (33:6). This is not random wickedness — it is the Torah's abomination list run in full. The host of heaven was forbidden from the start: 'either the sun, or moon, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded' (Deuteronomy 17:3). The crafts were forbidden by name: 'There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination... or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard' (Deuteronomy 18:10-11), 'for all that do these things are an abomination unto Yahuah (LORD): and because of these abominations Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) doth drive them out from before thee' (Deuteronomy 18:12). Leviticus set the seed-to-Molech and the familiar-spirit under death and cutting-off (Leviticus 20:2, 20:6). The parallel in 2 Kings 21:3 records the same provocations, and Jeremiah, a century later, names this king as the reason the kingdom finally fell — 'because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Yahudah (Judah), for that which he did in Jerusalem' (Jeremiah 15:4). So *Manasseh made Yahudah (Judah)... to err, and to do worse than the heathen* (33:9): a king set to guard the covenant instead leading the covenant people into the very abominations they had inherited the land for renouncing.

threads.title: Manasseh Humbled Himself Greatly, and Yahuah Was Intreated
threads.summary_md: This is the deepest mercy in the chronicle of the kings. The worst man to sit on the throne of Yahudah — who filled Jerusalem with idols and made his own children pass through the fire — is brought low: 'Yahuah (LORD) brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon' (33:11). And there the impossible turn: 'And when he was in affliction, he besought Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and HUMBLED HIMSELF GREATLY before the Elohim (God) of his fathers, And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that Yahuah (LORD) he was Elohim (God)' (33:12-13). This is the doctrine of repentance proved in the worst possible case. The sacrifice Yahuah will not refuse is 'a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise' (Psalm 51:17). The prophet had promised it: 'Let the wicked forsake his way... and let him return unto Yahuah (LORD), and he will have mercy upon him; and to our Elohim (God), for he will abundantly pardon' (Isaiah 55:7). The law of the turning soul stood for him: 'if the wicked will turn from all his sins... he shall surely live, he shall not die' (Ezekiel 18:21), for Yahuah has 'no pleasure at all that the wicked should die... and not that he should return from his ways, and live?' (Ezekiel 18:23). Joel's call is the very shape of his prayer: 'rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem... for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger' (Joel 2:13). And the promise spoken at the dedication of this very house was claimed by its greatest defiler: 'If my people... shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin' (2 Chronicles 7:14). The whole forward weave is here too: the prodigal arises and goes to the Father, 'and when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran' (Luke 15:18-20); and the chief of sinners obtains mercy 'for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe' (1 Timothy 1:15-16). The restored library preserves the inside of the verse — the prayer attributed to Manasseh himself: 'Now therefore I bow the knee of my heart, beseeching you of grace... For you are Yahuah (God), even Yahuah (God) of them that repent' (Prayer of Manasseh 1:11,13). The lesson stands forever: no one is beyond mercy who humbles himself and turns. Even the worst king was heard.

threads.title: The Fruit of Repentance: The Strange Gods Cast Out
threads.summary_md: True turning is proved by the hands, not by feeling alone. Restored to his kingdom, Manasseh *took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of Yahuah (LORD), and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of Yahuah (LORD), and in Jerusalem, and cast them out of the city* (33:15); 'And he repaired the altar of Yahuah (LORD), and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Yahudah (Judah) to serve Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)' (33:16). The king who had *made Yahudah (Judah)... to err* (33:9) now commands Yahudah to serve — the wicked way reversed in public, the very things he had built torn down by the same hands. This is the obedience Ezekiel attaches to the turning soul: the wicked who turns must 'keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right' (Ezekiel 18:21). It is the healing 2 Chronicles 7:14 promised those who 'turn from their wicked ways.' And it shows the character Joel preached — Yahuah 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness' (Joel 2:13) — the kindness that lets the worst king begin again. (The note that 'the people did sacrifice still in the high places, yet unto Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) only' [33:17] shows the reform was real but not yet complete — the deeper cleansing would wait for his great-grandson Josiah.)

threads.title: Amon Humbled Not Himself: The Son Who Would Not Turn
threads.summary_md: The chapter ends with a deliberate contrast that sharpens the whole lesson. Amon 'did that which was evil in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), as did Manasseh his father: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them' (33:22) — he revived the very idols his repentant father had cast out. But the one thing he did not inherit is named exactly: 'And humbled NOT himself before Yahuah (LORD), as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more' (33:23). The mercy that found Manasseh was open to Amon too — the difference was not the size of the sin but the bowing of the heart. Ezekiel's law cuts the other way for him: 'when the righteous turneth away... and committeth iniquity... in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die' (Ezekiel 18:24). The parallel in 2 Kings 21:21-22 says it plainly — he 'forsook Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his fathers, and walked not in the way of Yahuah (LORD).' And he handed the sin forward: the carved images he served are the very evil Jeremiah said the land would be exiled for, 'because of Manasseh... for that which he did in Jerusalem' (Jeremiah 15:4). The father took up the sin and then laid it down in repentance; the son took it back up and would not bow. One was heard; the other was slain. The throne is never beyond mercy — but mercy is only for the knee that bends.

threads.title: Josiah seeks Yahuah and purges Judah and the northern tribes
threads.summary_md:
The young king does that which is right and *declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left* (2 Chronicles 34:2) — and the engine of his reign is named at once: *in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the Elohim (God) of David his father* (2 Chronicles 34:3). This is the prophet's promise made flesh: *if ye seek him, he will be found of you* (2 Chronicles 15:2). To seek Yahuah is to find him, and Josiah's finding becomes a purging.

The cleansing is obedience to the written word he has not yet recovered: *ye shall overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire; and ye shall hew down the graven images* (Deuteronomy 12:3) — and so *they brake down the altars of Baalim in his presence... and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images, he brake in pieces, and made dust of them* (2 Chronicles 34:4). And the reform does not stop at Yahudah's border. *So did he in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon, even unto Naphtali* (2 Chronicles 34:6) — reaching into the scattered northern house, the two-house scope of the cleansing. This is the deed prophesied by name three hundred years before: *Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places... and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee* (1 Kings 13:2), fulfilled when *he burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars* (2 Chronicles 34:5). No king matched this turning: *like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to Yahuah (LORD) with all his heart... according to all the law of Moses* (2 Kings 23:25) — the very law he is about to find.

threads.title: The book of the law found — the king rends his clothes
threads.summary_md:
In the work of repairing the house — *the men did the work faithfully* (2 Chronicles 34:12) — the lost Word is uncovered: *Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) given by Moses* (2 Chronicles 34:14). The parallel records the same moment: *I have found the book of the law in the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Kings 22:8). This is the very book Moses had laid up — *Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant... that it may be there for a witness against thee* (Deuteronomy 31:26) — a witness buried under generations of idolatry and now found again.

And at once the witness witnesses. *Shaphan read it before the king* (2 Chronicles 34:18), and *when the king had heard the words of the law, that he rent his clothes* (2 Chronicles 34:19; cf. 2 Kings 22:11). The recovered Torah does not flatter; it pierces. Josiah sends to enquire of Yahuah, *for great is the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) that is poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of Yahuah (LORD), to do after all that is written in this book* (2 Chronicles 34:21). This is the law working the knowledge of sin — *I had not known sin, but by the law* (Romans 7:7) — not the Torah as curse, but the mirror that shows the breach. It is the living Word that cuts: *quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword... a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart* (Hebrews 4:12).

The recovery of the Word is the framework's celebration, never its abolition. What Shaphan does before the king, Ezra later does before the whole people — *they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel)* (Nehemiah 8:1) — the same restoration turning on the public reading of the Word that had been laid aside. The lost Torah, found and read, convicts and calls home.

threads.title: Thine heart was tender — the contrite who trembles at the Word
threads.summary_md:
Huldah the prophetess returns the word of Yahuah: the judgment is sure for the broken covenant — *I will bring evil upon this place... even all the curses that are written in the book* (2 Chronicles 34:24) — yet to the king himself comes mercy, and the reason is his heart. *Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before Elohim (God), when thou heardest his words against this place... and didst rend thy clothes, and weep before me; I have even heard thee also, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 34:27; cf. 2 Kings 22:19). The tender heart that hears the Word is heard in turn.

This is the very heart Yahuah declares he regards: *to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word* (Isaiah 66:2). Josiah brings no offering to turn the wrath; he brings the sacrifice Yahuah will not despise — *a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (Psalm 51:17). And so the ancient promise to Solomon is fulfilled: *if my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven* (2 Chronicles 7:14). The king humbled himself, and Yahuah heard. The heart that trembles at the recovered Word is the heart Yahuah looks to.

threads.title: A covenant to keep his commandments with all the heart
threads.summary_md:
The recovered Torah is not shelved; it is read aloud and sworn to. The king gathers all the people, *and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 34:30). Then he binds himself: *the king stood in his place, and made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD), to walk after Yahuah (LORD), and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant which are written in this book* (2 Chronicles 34:31), and *caused all that were present... to stand to it* (2 Chronicles 34:32; cf. 2 Kings 23:3). This is the anti-antinomian keystone of the recovered Word: the Torah read, understood, and covenanted.

The covenant Josiah swears is the heart of the Torah itself — *thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might* (Deuteronomy 6:5) — wholehearted love expressed as commandment-keeping. It renews Sinai, where *he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient* (Exodus 24:7); and it takes up the pattern of Joshua, who *made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem* (Joshua 24:25). And it points beyond outward reform to the promise Jeremiah — prophesying in Josiah's very days — held out: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33). The new covenant is not a new law but this same Torah made inward. The recovered Word is never abolished; it is read, sworn, kept — and at last graven on the heart.

threads.title: Josiah Kept the Passover As It Is Written in the Book of Moses
threads.summary_md: Josiah's reformation reaches its summit at the appointed feast: *Moreover Josiah kept a passover unto Yahuah (LORD) in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month* (2 Chronicles 35:1). This is no innovation — it is the Torah's own passover kept to the letter. Yahuah set the day in Egypt: *And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall kill it in the evening* (Exodus 12:6), and stamped it an everlasting feast: *ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever* (Exodus 12:14). The same fourteenth-day passover stands in the calendar of the feasts: *In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the LORD'S passover* (Leviticus 23:5), and Moses bound it to the chosen place: *Thou shalt therefore sacrifice the passover unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)... in the place which Yahuah (LORD) shall choose to place his name there* (Deuteronomy 16:2). Josiah charges the Levites to keep it *according to the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the hand of Moses* (2 Chronicles 35:6), and twice the chronicler stamps the obedience: they offered *as it is written in the book of Moses* (2 Chronicles 35:12). The parallel record agrees: *Keep the passover unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), as it is written in the book of this covenant* (2 Kings 23:21), and crowns it as unequalled — *there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges* (2 Kings 23:22). The restored chronicle of 1 Esdras tells the same scene: *And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem to his Elohim (God), and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month* (1 Esdras 1:1), kept *according to the commandment of Yahuah (God), which was given to Moses* (1 Esdras 1:6), and remembered as without equal *since the time of the prophet Samuel* (1 Esdras 1:20). Ben Sira sets Josiah's memory among the sweetest of the fathers: *The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume... it is sweet as honey in all mouths* (Ecclesiasticus 49:1), for *he directed his heart to Yahuah (God), and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of Yahuah (God)* (Ecclesiasticus 49:3). The appointed time was not abolished; it was restored in fullness, kept exactly as Yahuah wrote it.

threads.title: No Passover Like It — Messiah Our Passover
threads.summary_md: The chronicler sets Josiah's feast at the summit of the whole monarchy: *And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept* (2 Chronicles 35:18); *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present kept the passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days* (2 Chronicles 35:17). The unrivalled feast was not the end of the matter — it was a shadow pointing forward to the Lamb it always testified of. The apostle names that fulfilment: *For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us* (1 Corinthians 5:7), and he does not abolish the feast but commands it kept: *Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven... but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth* (1 Corinthians 5:8). The Messiah himself longed for this same appointed meal: *With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer* (Luke 22:15). Josiah's great passover was the greatest the kings ever kept; the Messiah our Passover is the One it was reaching toward — the feast not done away but filled, the lamb of Egypt and of Jerusalem gathered at last around the One Yahuah always meant.

threads.title: Josiah Fell at Megiddo and Jeremiah Lamented
threads.summary_md: The great Passover is followed by the great grief. *After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple, Necho king of Egypt came up to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates: and Josiah went out against him* (2 Chronicles 35:20); though Necho claimed a word *from the mouth of Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 35:22), Josiah *would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself... and came to fight in the valley of Megiddo*, where the archers struck him and *all Yahudah (Judah) and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah* (2 Chronicles 35:24). The parallel record tells the same fall: *king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo* (2 Kings 23:29), and *his servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem* (2 Kings 23:30). The restored chronicle preserves it too: *Pharaoh the king of Egypt came to raise war at Carchamis upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him* (1 Esdras 1:25), and *joined battle with him in the plain of Magiddo* (1 Esdras 1:29). Above all, the prophet himself wept: *And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah: and all the singing men and the singing women spake of Josiah in their lamentations to this day* (2 Chronicles 35:25) — a grief 1 Esdras carries word for word: *Jeremy the prophet lamented for Josias, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him to this day* (1 Esdras 1:32). So deep was the mourning at Megiddo that the prophet Zechariah made it the measure of the nation's future weeping for the pierced One: *In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon* (Zechariah 12:11). The death of the righteous king became the very byword for the deepest lament Yashar'el (Israel) would ever raise.

threads.title: He sent his messengers, but they mocked, till there was no remedy
threads.summary_md:
The whole tragedy of the kingdom is gathered into two verses, and the heart of them is the long patience of Yahuah. *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place: But they mocked the messengers of Elohim (God), and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) arose against his people, till there was no remedy* (2 Chronicles 36:15-16). Judgment falls only after compassion is exhausted — and even then it is the people's refusal, not Yahuah's coldness, that brings it.

This *rising up betimes* is Jeremiah's own refrain: *I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them* (Jeremiah 7:25); *Yahuah (LORD) hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened* (Jeremiah 25:4). The Chronicler had shown the pattern earlier — *Yet he sent prophets to them, to bring them again unto Yahuah (LORD)... but they would not give ear* (2 Chronicles 24:19) — and Nehemiah confesses the crime by name: *they... slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee* (Nehemiah 9:26). The prophets sent to TURN them were the prophets they killed. Zedekiah's hardened neck (36:13) is the proverb come true: *He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy* (Proverbs 29:1).

This is the indictment of a SPECIFIC generation's sin — never a blanket curse on the people. For the same Yahuah who *had compassion on his people* is the One who, in the flesh of the Formed Son, weeps: *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets... how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37; Luke 13:34). The longing behind every sending was always to gather. And the parable of the vineyard tells this very history — *the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another* (Matthew 21:35) — the householder's patience and the violence done to all he sent, one story across the ages.

threads.title: They burnt the house of Elohim — the fall of Jerusalem
threads.summary_md:
The wrath that *arose... till there was no remedy* falls in fire and sword. *Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age* (2 Chronicles 36:17); *And they burnt the house of Elohim (God), and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof* (2 Chronicles 36:19).

The parallel records weep the same ruin. *And burned the house of Yahuah (LORD), and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem... burned he with fire* (Jeremiah 52:13); *And he burnt the house of Yahuah (LORD), and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire* (2 Kings 25:9). Lamentations gives the fire its meaning: *Yahuah (LORD) hath accomplished his fury; he hath poured out his fierce anger, and hath kindled a fire in Zion, and it hath devoured the foundations thereof* (Lamentations 4:11).

Yet even the destroyer is a rod in the hand of Yahuah, foretold by the prophet: *Behold, I will send and take all the families of the north... and Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will bring them against this land... and make them... perpetual desolations* (Jeremiah 25:9). The Chaldean does what Yahuah ordained, when the covenant-patience is spent — *he gave them all into his hand* (2 Chronicles 36:17). The fall is judgment, named long before by the very prophet whose word the chapter goes on to say was fulfilled.

threads.title: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths — the seventy years
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler reads the seventy-year exile not as the bare end of a nation but as the land taking back the rest it was denied. *And them that had escaped from the sword carried he away to Babylon... To fulfil the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years* (2 Chronicles 36:20-21). The desolation is the unkept sabbatical years repaid — Torah's land-sabbath vindicated, not the Torah cast off as a curse.

The Torah itself wrote this sentence in advance. *Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths, as long as it lieth desolate, and ye be in your enemies' land; even then shall the land rest, and enjoy her sabbaths* (Leviticus 26:34); *As long as it lieth desolate it shall rest; because it did not rest in your sabbaths, when ye dwelt upon it* (Leviticus 26:35); *The land also shall be left of them, and shall enjoy her sabbaths, while she lieth desolate without them... because they despised my judgments, and because their soul abhorred my statutes* (Leviticus 26:43) — the very despising the Chronicler records (*they... despised his words*, 36:16). And the land-sabbath despised is the one Moses gave: *in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 25:4).

The number was Jeremiah's: *these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years* (Jeremiah 25:11) — and the same word held the promise of its end, *after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place* (Jeremiah 29:10). Daniel searched it out in the books: *I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of Yahuah (LORD) came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem* (Daniel 9:2). The exile is the sabbath-law reckoned to the day — and its expiry is the hinge to the return.

threads.title: Yahuah stirred up the spirit of Cyrus — the decree and the door home
threads.summary_md:
The book of Chronicles — and, in the Hebrew order, the whole Tanakh — does not end in exile. It ends on the open door home. *Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of Yahuah (LORD) spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, Yahuah (LORD) stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom... Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem... Who is there among you of all his people? Yahuah Elohav (The LORD his God) be with him, and let him go up* (2 Chronicles 36:22-23). The last word of the canon is a summons to GO UP.

These closing words are the opening words of Ezra, almost letter for letter — *Yahuah (LORD) stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation* (Ezra 1:1) — and the call goes out: *Who is there among you of all his people? his Elohim (God) be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem... and build the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 1:3). What the Chaldees plundered, the decree restores: *let the golden and silver vessels of the house of Elohim (God), which Nebuchadnezzar took forth out of the temple... be restored, and brought again unto the temple which is at Jerusalem* (Ezra 6:5).

And it is all the fulfilment of a promise: *after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you... in causing you to return to this place* (Jeremiah 29:10). The mechanism is the sovereign hand on a pagan heart — *The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will* (Proverbs 21:1). Yahuah turned the heart of an emperor like a watercourse to bring his people home. The gathering is begun; the exile is not the last word.

threads.title: Thou shalt be built — Cyrus my shepherd, mine anointed
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler closes on a king Isaiah had named generations before he was born. *Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 36:23) — and long before, Yahuah had said it through the prophet: *That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid* (Isaiah 44:28). The shepherd Yahuah appointed speaks to Jerusalem exactly the word Yahuah put in his mouth.
